paper_title: Algorithmic Semi-algebraic Geometry and Topology -- Recent Progress and Open Problems
context_brief: All Betti numbers in single-exponential time
original_question: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^k described by s polynomials of degree at most d. The Betti numbers b_i(S) are the dimensions of the homology or cohomology groups of S, equivalently the numbers of independent i-dimensional holes in the relevant dimensions. Does there exist an algorithm whose running time is single exponential in k for computing all Betti numbers of S? Known single-exponential algorithms compute only b_0(S), ..., b_ell(S) when ell is fixed in advance.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ be a semi-algebraic set described by a Boolean combination of sign conditions on $s$ polynomials in $\mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k]$, each of degree at most $d$. For each integer $i \ge 0$, let $b_i(S) = \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_i(S;\mathbb{Q})$ be the $i$-th Betti number of $S$ (the dimension of its $i$-th singular homology group with rational coefficients); equivalently, $b_i(S)$ counts the number of independent $i$-dimensional holes of $S$.

Does there exist an algorithm that, given such a description of $S$, computes all the Betti numbers $b_0(S), b_1(S), \dots, b_k(S)$ in time bounded by $(sd)^{k^{O(1)}}$ (i.e., singly exponential in $k$)?

Remark on the state of knowledge: algorithms of complexity singly exponential in $k$ are known for computing $b_0(S),\dots,b_\ell(S)$ when $\ell$ is fixed in advance, as well as for the Euler–Poincaré characteristic; the question asks whether such a complexity can be achieved for all Betti numbers simultaneously.
status_search_result: The problem remains open. Singly exponential algorithms are known for the Euler–Poincaré characteristic, for $b_0$ and $b_1$, and more generally for the first $\ell+1$ Betti numbers with complexity $(sd)^{k^{O(\ell)}}$ when $\ell$ is fixed (Basu and collaborators). Computing all Betti numbers (especially middle ones) in single exponential time in $k$ is still considered a major open question in algorithmic real algebraic geometry; obstacles include the lack of a singly exponential triangulation algorithm.

paper_title: Algorithmic Semi-algebraic Geometry and Topology -- Recent Progress and Open Problems
original_question: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^k defined by ell quadratic inequalities. Existing algorithms decide emptiness, compute sample points in every connected component, and compute the Euler-Poincare characteristic of such sets with complexity k^{O(ell)}, while the best known way to count connected components via computing all Betti numbers has complexity k^{2^{O(ell)}}. Is there a more efficient algorithm, with complexity k^{O(ell)} or even k^{O(ell^2)}, for counting the connected components of S, equivalently computing b_0(S)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^k$ be a semi-algebraic set defined by a finite conjunction (or, more generally, a Boolean combination) of $\ell$ inequalities of the form $P_i(x_1,\dots,x_k) \le 0$ (or $<0$, $=0$), where each $P_i \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_k]$ has total degree at most $2$. Let $b_0(S)$ denote the number of connected components of $S$ (equivalently, the rank of $H_0(S;\mathbb{Q})$).

It is known that emptiness of $S$, computation of a set of sample points meeting every connected component of $S$, and computation of the Euler–Poincaré characteristic of $S$ can each be performed by deterministic algorithms whose arithmetic complexity (number of operations over the coefficient ring of the $P_i$) is bounded by $k^{O(\ell)}$. On the other hand, the best known algorithm for computing $b_0(S)$ proceeds by computing all Betti numbers of $S$ and has complexity $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given the polynomials $P_1,\dots,P_\ell$ of degree at most $2$ describing $S \subset \mathbb{R}^k$, computes $b_0(S)$ with arithmetic complexity bounded by $k^{O(\ell)}$, or at least by $k^{O(\ell^2)}$?
status_search_result: Searches surface the existing $k^{2^{O(\ell)}}$ bound via Betti-number computation and related work on top Betti numbers and projections of sets defined by quadratic inequalities, but do not reveal a published algorithm achieving $k^{O(\ell)}$ or $k^{O(\ell^2)}$ complexity for $b_0$ in this setting. The current status appears unresolved based on the available sources.

paper_title: Algorithmic Semi-algebraic Geometry and Topology -- Recent Progress and Open Problems
context_brief: Quantifier elimination for projected quadratic systems
original_question: Let S be a closed and bounded semi-algebraic subset of R^{k+m} defined by a fixed number ell of quadratic inequalities P_1 >= 0, ..., P_ell >= 0, where each P_i has degree at most 2, and let pi: R^{k+m} -> R^m be the projection onto the last m coordinates. Because pi(S) is semi-algebraic, quantifier elimination asks for a quantifier-free semi-algebraic description of pi(S). For fixed ell, can quantifier elimination for this class be performed efficiently, in particular in time polynomial in k and m?
self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer $\ell$. Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^{k+m}$ be a closed and bounded semi-algebraic set defined by
$$P_1 \ge 0,\; P_2 \ge 0,\; \dots,\; P_\ell \ge 0,$$
where each $P_i \in \mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k,Y_1,\dots,Y_m]$ has total degree at most $2$. Let $\pi : \mathbb{R}^{k+m} \to \mathbb{R}^m$ denote the projection onto the last $m$ coordinates $(Y_1,\dots,Y_m)$. By the Tarski–Seidenberg theorem, the image $\pi(S)$ is again a semi-algebraic subset of $\mathbb{R}^m$, so there exists a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial inequalities in $Y_1,\dots,Y_m$ describing $\pi(S)$.

Question: For every fixed $\ell$, does there exist an algorithm which, given the polynomials $P_1,\dots,P_\ell$, computes a quantifier-free semi-algebraic description of $\pi(S)$ in time polynomial in $k$ and $m$?
status_search_result: Partial results are known: Basu and others have given polynomial-time algorithms (for fixed ℓ) for computing the top Betti numbers and bounding the Betti numbers of projections of semi-algebraic sets defined by a constant number of quadratic inequalities, and Barvinok gave polynomial-time feasibility algorithms for systems of quadratic equations with a fixed number of equations. However, no algorithm is known that produces a quantifier-free description of π(S) in time polynomial in k and m, even for fixed ℓ; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Matching of correlators in AdS3/CFT2
original_question: Can the relation between supergravity holographic renormalization and the string-theory computation of AdS3/CFT2 correlators be made systematic, so that the volume renormalization that renders string correlators finite and the map between worldsheet vertex operators and CFT operators are understood as precisely as the corresponding bulk-field boundary-condition dictionary in supergravity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider type IIB string theory on AdS_3 × S^3 × M (with M either T^4 or K3) with NS-NS flux, dual via the AdS_3/CFT_2 correspondence to a two-dimensional superconformal field theory on the boundary. On the bulk side, two complementary frameworks compute boundary correlation functions:

(a) Supergravity holographic renormalization. One regularizes the on-shell supergravity action by cutting off the asymptotically AdS region at a finite radial coordinate, adds covariant boundary counterterms determined by the asymptotic expansion of the bulk fields, and extracts CFT correlators by functional differentiation with respect to prescribed boundary data. This produces a precise dictionary in which each bulk supergravity field is identified, via its leading and subleading falloffs, with a specific source and a specific operator of definite conformal weight in the dual CFT.

(b) Worldsheet string theory on AdS_3 (described by an SL(2,R) WZW model times an internal CFT). Boundary correlators are computed as integrated worldsheet correlation functions of physical vertex operators, and require a renormalization of the divergent volume of the target AdS_3 (equivalently, a regularization of certain divergences in the moduli/spectral-flow integrals) to yield finite answers.

Formulate and prove a systematic prescription that (i) defines the volume renormalization rendering all string-theory boundary correlators finite, in a scheme-independent way comparable to holographic renormalization in supergravity, and (ii) provides an explicit, systematic map between worldsheet vertex operators (including their spectral-flow sectors and internal-CFT factors) and local operators in the dual two-dimensional CFT, such that the resulting prescription reduces, in the supergravity limit, to the standard bulk-field/boundary-operator dictionary of holographic renormalization, and agrees with it on the level of two- and three-point correlation functions.
status_search_result: The question is a research-program proposal asking for a systematic worldsheet analogue of holographic renormalization for AdS_3/CFT_2. There is substantial subsequent work on AdS_3 string correlators (e.g., Eberhardt, Dei–Eberhardt and others on the symmetric-orbifold/tensionless point), but a complete, systematic worldsheet renormalization framework matching supergravity holographic renormalization in full generality does not appear to have been definitively established. Status is best classified as unknown/open.

paper_title: Kontsevich Graphs Act on Nambu-Poisson Brackets, VI. Open Problems
original_question: Can one find a Poisson bracket P on an affine manifold and a nontrivial Kontsevich graph cocycle action whose induced infinitesimal deformation changes P in a way that is not merely a coordinate change along a vector field, thereby producing a family of inequivalent Poisson structures?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be an affine manifold and let $P$ be a Poisson bivector on $M$, i.e. a smooth bivector field $P\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$ satisfying $[P,P]=0$ in the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. Recall that to every cocycle $\gamma$ in M. Kontsevich's graph complex of finite oriented graphs (with vertices of valency $\geq 3$ and a wedge ordering on edges) one associates, via the orientation morphism, a bivector flow $\dot P=\mathcal{O}r(\gamma)(P)$ that is automatically tangent to the variety of Poisson structures, so that $P_t=P+t\,\mathcal{O}r(\gamma)(P)+O(t^2)$ is an infinitesimal deformation of $P$ through Poisson bivectors. The flow is called trivial at $P$ if there exists a vector field $X$ on $M$ such that $\mathcal{O}r(\gamma)(P)=[P,X]$ (i.e. the deformation is generated by a coordinate change), and nontrivial otherwise. The known nontrivial graph cocycles include the tetrahedron $\gamma_3$ and an infinite family $\gamma_5,\gamma_7,\dots$ of "good" wheel-type cocycles.

Problem. Exhibit an affine manifold $M$, a Poisson bivector $P$ on $M$, and a graph cocycle $\gamma\in\{\gamma_3,\gamma_5,\gamma_7,\dots\}$ such that the induced flow $\mathcal{O}r(\gamma)(P)$ is not of the form $[P,X]$ for any vector field $X$ on $M$, thereby producing a one-parameter family of Poisson structures on $M$ that are pairwise inequivalent under diffeomorphisms of $M$.
category_tag: Kontsevich graph complex and Poisson deformations
status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2025) on the action of Kontsevich graph cocycles on Nambu–Poisson brackets show that for the tetrahedron $\gamma_3$ on Nambu brackets in low dimensions ($2\le d\le 4$) the induced flow is a Poisson coboundary, i.e. realized by a vector field. No published example of a Poisson bracket on an affine manifold for which a graph cocycle (tetrahedron or higher wheel) produces a deformation that is not a coordinate-change coboundary appears to exist; the problem is explicitly stated as open in the cited series.

paper_title: Kontsevich Graphs Act on Nambu-Poisson Brackets, VI. Open Problems
original_question: Assume that the tetrahedral Kontsevich graph flow on a Nambu-Poisson bracket in dimension d + 1 is trivial, so that Q_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P tensor 4) can be written as the Poisson coboundary [[P, X_{gamma_3}^{d+1}(P tensor 3)]]. Is the trivializing vector field X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} always expressible as a linear combination of the (d + 1)-dimensional descendants of the two-dimensional sunflower graph X_{gamma_3} = (0, 1; 1, 3; 1, 2) + 2(0, 2; 1, 3; 1, 2), where descendants are produced in the dimensional step by adjoining the new Casimir and applying the stated Leibniz-rule expansion?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 2$ and consider an affine manifold of dimension $d+1$ equipped with a Nambu–Poisson bracket
$$P(f_1,\dots,f_{d+1}) \;=\; \varrho \cdot \det\!\Big(\tfrac{\partial f_i}{\partial x^j}\Big)\quad\text{(after fixing $d-1$ Casimirs),}$$
so that $P$ is the rank-2 Poisson bivector obtained from a top-degree multivector by contraction with $d-1$ Casimir functions $a_1,\dots,a_{d-1}$.

Let $\gamma_3$ denote the tetrahedron, the unoriented graph cocycle on four vertices with six edges that gives the smallest nontrivial class in Kontsevich's graph complex, and let $Q_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{\otimes 4})$ denote the bivector obtained by orienting $\gamma_3$ in all admissible ways and inserting four copies of $P$ at the vertices, evaluated on a $(d+1)$-dimensional Nambu–Poisson bracket.

Assume that the tetrahedral flow is trivial on the class of $(d+1)$-dimensional Nambu–Poisson brackets, i.e.\ there exists a vector field $X_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{\otimes 3})$, polynomial in the components of $P$, such that
$$Q_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}\bigl(P^{\otimes 4}\bigr) \;=\; [\![\,P,\;X_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}(P^{\otimes 3})\,]\!] $$
in the Poisson cohomology sense, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ is the Schouten bracket.

In dimension $d=2$ the "sunflower" trivializing vector field is the graph
$$X_{\gamma_3} \;=\; (0,1;\,1,3;\,1,2) \;+\; 2\,(0,2;\,1,3;\,1,2),$$
with marked sink-vertex labels $(m,n)=(1,3)$, viewed as a Nambu micro-graph in 2D. A $(d+1)$-dimensional descendant of a $d$-dimensional Nambu micro-graph is any Nambu micro-graph in dimension $d+1$ obtained by adjoining one new Casimir argument and expanding via the Leibniz rule on each Nambu bracket vertex; the linear span of such descendants of the 2D sunflower is the space of "sunflower descendants" in dimension $d+1$.

Question: Is the trivializing vector field $X_{\gamma_3}^{d+1}$ always expressible as a linear combination, with constant coefficients, of the $(d+1)$-dimensional descendants of the 2D sunflower graph $X_{\gamma_3}$?
category_tag: Kontsevich graph complex and Nambu–Poisson brackets
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2025 problem-list contribution; related results show triviality of the tetrahedral flow has been established for $d=2$ (Kontsevich, 1996), $d=3$ (2020), and $d=4$ (2024), with explicit 3D solutions found as linear combinations of the ten 3D descendants of the 2D sunflower. Whether the sunflower-descendant ansatz suffices in all dimensions $d+1$ appears not to be settled.

paper_title: Kontsevich Graphs Act on Nambu-Poisson Brackets, VI. Open Problems
original_question: For the vanishing one-vector Nambu micro-graphs that are needed in the dimensional shift d -> d + 1, do all indispensable examples come from descendants of an underlying vanishing set already present over R^{d-1}, rather than from new vanishing micro-graphs whose vanishing mechanisms first appear in the higher dimension?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider the Kontsevich graph calculus specialised to Nambu–Poisson brackets on R^d, where a Nambu–Poisson bracket is given by the Jacobian determinant of d-1 Casimir functions with respect to the standard volume form. Within this calculus one works with "micro-graphs" Γ_d: oriented graphs whose internal vertices carry copies of a Nambu–Poisson structure expanded in terms of its Casimirs, with one external sink, and whose associated differential-polynomial formula φ(Γ_d) is a (multi-)vector field on R^d. A micro-graph Γ_d is called vanishing in dimension d if φ(Γ_d) ≡ 0 identically on R^d.

A natural lifting (descent) procedure produces, from any micro-graph Γ_d defined over R^d, a collection of descendants over R^{d+1}, obtained by inserting an additional Casimir into each Nambu vertex. A vanishing micro-graph Γ_{d+1} over R^{d+1} is called indispensable if removing it (and its orbit under graph symmetries) destroys the existence of a graph-level solution to the relevant cocycle/coboundary equation in dimension d+1, while its presence is required to balance non-vanishing contributions of other descendants.

Question. For the dimensional shift R^d → R^{d+1}, is it the case that every indispensable vanishing one-vector Nambu micro-graph in dimension d+1 arises as a descendant of some vanishing micro-graph already present over R^d? Equivalently, prove or disprove that no indispensable vanishing micro-graph over R^{d+1} has a vanishing mechanism (e.g., a non-trivial automorphism enforcing φ ≡ 0) that first appears strictly in dimension d+1 and is not inherited from a vanishing micro-graph over R^d via the descent operation.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the most recent installment (2025) of an ongoing series on Kontsevich graphs acting on Nambu–Poisson brackets. Companion papers (parts III–V, 2024–2025) and related theses establish the indispensable role of vanishing micro-graphs in dimensional lifts but do not resolve whether all such indispensable vanishers descend from lower-dimensional vanishing sets. No resolution was located.

paper_title: Symmetry and colorings: some results and open problems, II
context_brief: Asymptotic constant for interval symmetry numbers
original_question: Let I = [0,1] be the unit interval with Lebesgue measure and central symmetries x ↦ 2c − x. Let ms_r(I) be the maximal symmetry number for measurable r-colorings of I, meaning the largest measure guaranteed for a monochromatic measurable subset that is symmetric about some center c. In the asymptotic formula lim_{r→∞} r^2 · ms_r(I) = inf_{r∈N} r^2 · ms_r(I) = S', determine or estimate the constant S'. Decide whether S' is strictly larger than the constant S from the autoconvolution lower bound for ms_r(I).
self_contained_problem:
Let $I=[0,1]$ be the unit interval equipped with Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. For a point $c\in\mathbb{R}$, the central symmetry about $c$ is the map $\sigma_c\colon x\mapsto 2c-x$. A measurable set $A\subseteq I$ is said to be symmetric about $c$ if $\sigma_c(A\cap I)\cap I = A$ (equivalently, $A$ is invariant under $\sigma_c$ within $I$). 

Given a positive integer $r$, a measurable $r$-coloring of $I$ is a partition $I = C_1\sqcup C_2\sqcup\cdots\sqcup C_r$ into measurable sets. Define the symmetry number of such a coloring as 
$$\operatorname{ms}(C_1,\dots,C_r) \;=\; \sup_{c\in\mathbb{R}}\;\max_{1\le i\le r}\;\lambda\!\left(\{x\in C_i : 2c-x\in C_i\}\right),$$
the largest measure of a subset of one color class that is symmetric about some center $c$. Set 
$$\operatorname{ms}_r(I) \;=\; \inf_{C_1,\dots,C_r}\operatorname{ms}(C_1,\dots,C_r),$$
the infimum taken over all measurable $r$-colorings of $I$.

It is known that the limit 
$$S' \;=\; \lim_{r\to\infty} r^2\,\operatorname{ms}_r(I) \;=\; \inf_{r\in\mathbb{N}} r^2\,\operatorname{ms}_r(I)$$
exists and satisfies $S \le S' < 5/6$, where $S$ is the analogous constant arising from the autoconvolution lower bound for $\operatorname{ms}_r(I)$ (i.e., the best constant $S$ such that $\int f * f \ge S$ for all nonnegative measurable $f\colon[0,1/2]\to[0,1]$ with $\int f = 1/2$, suitably normalized).

Determine, or give nontrivial estimates for, the constant $S'$. In particular, decide whether $S' > S$.
status_search_result: No published resolution of the problem was located. Searches for the symmetry number $\operatorname{ms}_r(I)$ and the autoconvolution constant $S$ on the unit interval return only related background work; the exact value of $S$ itself is also reported as unknown, and no source establishes the value of $S'$ or the strict inequality $S'>S$. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Absolute continuity, Lyapunov exponents and rigidity I : geodesic flows
original_question: Does dynamic coherence persist under perturbations of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms? More explicitly, let f be a partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism of a compact Riemannian manifold with invariant tangent splitting into unstable, center, and stable bundles, written as E^u, E^c, and E^s. Say that f is dynamically coherent when there are f-invariant center-stable and center-unstable foliations tangent to E^c + E^s and E^c + E^u, respectively, and their intersections give an invariant center foliation W^c. If f is dynamically coherent, is every perturbation of f also dynamically coherent?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold and let $f : M \to M$ be a $C^1$ diffeomorphism. Recall that $f$ is partially hyperbolic if there is a $Df$-invariant continuous splitting $TM = E^u \oplus E^c \oplus E^s$ of the tangent bundle into nonzero subbundles, together with constants and a Riemannian metric such that vectors in $E^u$ are uniformly expanded, vectors in $E^s$ are uniformly contracted, and the expansion/contraction rates on $E^c$ are strictly dominated by those on $E^u$ and $E^s$, respectively. Such an $f$ is said to be dynamically coherent if there exist $f$-invariant foliations $W^{cs}$ and $W^{cu}$ of $M$ tangent to $E^c \oplus E^s$ and $E^c \oplus E^u$, respectively; in that case $W^c := W^{cs} \cap W^{cu}$ is an $f$-invariant center foliation tangent to $E^c$.

Question: Is dynamical coherence open in the $C^1$ topology among partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms? Equivalently, if $f$ is a dynamically coherent partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism of $M$, does there exist a $C^1$-neighborhood $\mathcal{U}$ of $f$ in $\mathrm{Diff}^1(M)$ such that every $g \in \mathcal{U}$ is partially hyperbolic and dynamically coherent?
status_search_result: The general question of whether dynamical coherence is $C^1$-open (i.e., persists under arbitrary small perturbations) among partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms appears to remain open. Examples of non-dynamically coherent partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms have been constructed (Rodriguez Hertz–Rodriguez Hertz–Ures on $\mathbb{T}^3$; Bonatti–Fisher–Frankel–Potrie on Seifert manifolds), and many positive results hold under extra assumptions (e.g., on $\mathbb{T}^3$ or for systems isotopic to Anosov on tori/nilmanifolds), but no general counterexample showing a dynamically coherent diffeomorphism with a non-coherent perturbation, nor a general proof of openness, was found in available sources.

paper_title: On two open problems about embedding of modules in free modules
original_question: For a ring R, call R a left FGF ring when each finitely generated module over R on the left side can be injected into some free left R-module. Must every left FGF ring be Quasi-Frobenius?
self_contained_problem: A ring $R$ (associative, with identity) is called a left FGF ring if every finitely generated left $R$-module embeds as a submodule of some free left $R$-module. A ring $R$ is called quasi-Frobenius (QF) if $R$ is left (equivalently, right) artinian and left (equivalently, right) self-injective. paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
original_question: Let (q)_m = product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^i), (q)_infinity = product_{i=1}^infinity (1 - q^i), and let [a choose b]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. For the A2 Rogers-Ramanujan identity (q)_infinity sum_{r1,r2>=0} q^(r1^2 - r1 r2 + r2^2)/((q)_{r1}(q)_{r2}(q)_{r1+r2}) = sum_{r1,r2>=0} q^(r1^2 - r1 r2 + r2^2)/(q)_{r1} [2r1 choose r2]_q = product_{n>=0} 1/((1 - q^(7n+1))^2 (1 - q^(7n+3)) (1 - q^(7n+4)) (1 - q^(7n+6))^2), find a partition-theoretic interpretation for the middle sum. Preferably, first rewrite the left-hand side as a q-series that is both manifestly of A2 type and manifestly coefficientwise positive, and then give a combinatorial interpretation of that positive series.
self_contained_problem:
Notation. For a non-negative integer $m$, set $(q)_m=\prod_{i=1}^m(1-q^i)$ with $(q)_0=1$, and let $(q)_\infty=\prod_{i=1}^\infty(1-q^i)$. For non-negative integers $a,b$, the Gaussian $q$-binomial coefficient is
$$\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{a}{b}_q=\begin{cases}\dfrac{(q)_a}{(q)_b\,(q)_{a-b}}&\text{if }0\le b\le a,\\[4pt]0&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

Consider the $A_2$ Rogers–Ramanujan identity
$$(q)_\infty\sum_{r_1,r_2\ge 0}\frac{q^{r_1^2-r_1r_2+r_2^2}}{(q)_{r_1}(q)_{r_2}(q)_{r_1+r_2}}\;=\;\sum_{r_1,r_2\ge 0}\frac{q^{r_1^2-r_1r_2+r_2^2}}{(q)_{r_1}}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{2r_1}{r_2}_q\;=\;\prod_{n\ge 0}\frac{1}{(1-q^{7n+1})^2(1-q^{7n+3})(1-q^{7n+4})(1-q^{7n+6})^2}.$$

Tasks:
(a) Express the left-hand side as a $q$-series that is simultaneously (i) manifestly of $A_2$ type (its summand reflects the $A_2$ root-system structure, e.g.\ involves the quadratic form $r_1^2-r_1r_2+r_2^2$ in an essential way) and (ii) manifestly coefficient-wise positive (each coefficient in the $q$-expansion is visibly a non-negative integer, with no need for cancellation).

(b) Give a partition-theoretic interpretation of the middle sum
$$\sum_{r_1,r_2\ge 0}\frac{q^{r_1^2-r_1r_2+r_2^2}}{(q)_{r_1}}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{2r_1}{r_2}_q,$$
i.e.\ exhibit a class $\mathcal P$ of partitions (or coloured/multi-partitions) together with a statistic such that the generating function of $\mathcal P$ equals this sum, and such that $\mathcal P$ is naturally in bijection with the partitions enumerated by the infinite product on the right-hand side.
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g. Tsuchioka 2025 on $A_2^{(1)}$ level-3 bipartition identities, and Andrews–Schilling–Warnaar style $A_2$ Bailey-lemma developments) provides manifestly positive Andrews–Gordon-type series and some bipartition interpretations related to $A_2$ Rogers–Ramanujan identities. However, no source clearly establishes a partition-theoretic interpretation of the specific middle sum above in a way that is simultaneously manifestly of $A_2$ type and manifestly positive. The status appears unresolved in full generality.

paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
original_question: Develop an arbitrary-rank A_{n-1} version of the Bailey-type summations that include the A1 q-binomial invariance sum and the two A2 supernomial summations used to iterate identities. In this setting S(L,k) denotes the normalized A_{n-1} supernomial with L in Z_+^{n-1}, k in Z^n, and |k|=0. The desired arbitrary-rank theorem should be strong enough to iterate identities, not merely the known weak form sum_{L in Z_+^{n-1}} q^(L C L/2) S(L,k) = q^((k1^2+...+kn^2)/2)/(q)_infinity^{n-1}, because that weak form produces a new q-series identity but cannot be iterated indefinitely.
self_contained_problem:
For each integer $n\geq 2$, the normalized $A_{n-1}$ supernomial coefficient $S(L,k)$ is a $q$-series-valued function of $L=(L_1,\dots,L_{n-1})\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}^{n-1}$ and $k=(k_1,\dots,k_n)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n}$ subject to $|k|:=k_1+\cdots+k_n=0$; for $n=2$ it reduces to the usual normalized $q$-binomial coefficient, and for $n=3$ it coincides with the $A_2$ supernomial. Let $C=(C_{ij})$ denote the Cartan matrix of $A_{n-1}$ and write $LCL = \sum_{i,j} C_{ij} L_i L_j$. The "weak" $A_{n-1}$ summation
$$\sum_{L\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}^{n-1}} q^{LCL/2}\, S(L,k) \;=\; \frac{q^{(k_1^2+\cdots+k_n^2)/2}}{(q;q)_\infty^{\,n-1}}$$
is known but is insufficient to iterate Bailey-type chains of identities.

Problem. Find and prove an arbitrary-rank $A_{n-1}$ Bailey-type summation theorem involving the supernomials $S(L,k)$ that simultaneously generalizes:
(i) the $A_1$ $q$-binomial invariance summation, and
(ii) the two known $A_2$ supernomial summations used in the Bailey iteration,
and is strong enough to admit indefinite iteration, thereby producing infinite families of Rogers–Ramanujan-type identities of higher rank rather than only the single identity yielded by the weak form above.
status_search_result: Surveys on Bailey's lemma and supernomial coefficients (Warnaar, "50 Years of Bailey's Lemma", and the supernomial survey itself) describe the iterable $A_{n-1}$ generalization of the $A_2$ supernomial Bailey summations as an open problem; only the weak (non-iterable) $A_{n-1}$ summation and the $A_2$ iterable case are known. No subsequent publication establishing the iterable arbitrary-rank version was located.

paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
original_question: For the A3 case, find a sufficiently simple closed expression for the more general summation sum_{L in Z_+^3} q^(L C L/2) S(L,k)/(q)_{M-L}, where M is an arbitrary element of Z_+^3, C is the A3 Cartan matrix, and S(L,k) is the normalized A3 supernomial. The expression should be simple enough, after any necessary extraction of common factors, to indicate how the A3 Bailey-type summation can be iterated beyond the isolated single-parameter A3 result sum_{L in Z_+^3} q^(L C L/2) S(L,k)/(q)_{M2-L2}.
self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a formal variable and use the standard $q$-Pochhammer notation $(q)_n = \prod_{j=1}^n (1-q^j)$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, with $(q)_n = 0$ for $n<0$ and the convention $1/(q)_{n}=0$ when $n<0$. For a vector $L=(L_1,L_2,L_3)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3$ and $M=(M_1,M_2,M_3)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3$, write $1/(q)_{M-L} = \prod_{i=1}^3 1/(q)_{M_i-L_i}$.

Let $C$ be the Cartan matrix of type $A_3$,
$$C=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&0\\-1&2&-1\\0&-1&2\end{pmatrix},$$
and define the quadratic form $LCL/2 = \tfrac12\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}L_iL_j$.

For $L\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3$ and $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, let $S(L,k)$ denote the normalized $A_3$ supernomial coefficient: with $|L| = L_1+2L_2+3L_3$ assumed $\equiv 0\pmod{4}$ (otherwise $S(L,k)=0$), 
$$S(L,k) = \sum_{\substack{a,b,c,d\ge 0\\ a+b=L_1,\ c+d=L_2,\\ \text{(standard }A_3\text{ supernomial constraints)}}} \prod (\text{Gaussian }q\text{-binomials})$$
i.e. the $q$-supernomial associated with the symmetric power representation of weight $(k,k,k,\dots)$ for $\mathfrak{sl}_4$, normalized so that for the rank-one truncation it reduces to the Andrews--Bressoud $q$-supernomial.

Find a closed-form evaluation, simple enough that (after extracting common factors) it can be iterated as a Bailey-type recursion, of the multi-sum
$$F(M,k;q) \;=\; \sum_{L\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3} \frac{q^{LCL/2}\, S(L,k)}{(q)_{M_1-L_1}(q)_{M_2-L_2}(q)_{M_3-L_3}}, \qquad M=(M_1,M_2,M_3)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3.$$

The known case in which the denominator contains only the single factor $(q)_{M_2-L_2}$ (with no restriction on $L_1$ or $L_3$) admits a closed form; the problem is to obtain the analogous closed form for the full three-parameter sum above.
status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific A3 three-parameter Bailey-type summation involving the normalized A3 supernomial appears to be available; the question is posed as an open problem in the survey context, and a literature search did not turn up a subsequent paper providing the desired closed form.

paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
original_question: Prove the cylindric-partition-motivated identity involving the product T''(L,M,k,k') = product_{i=1}^n [M+L-k_i+k'_i choose L-k_i]_q for L,M in Z_+ and zero-sum integer vectors k,k'. For p>=n, show that the signed A_{n-1} sum over |k|=0 and sigma in S_n of q^{phi_{p,k,sigma}} T''(L,M, p k - sigma + rho, (p-1)k - sigma + rho) equals the corresponding mu-sum with exponent mu(C^{-1} tensor C)mu/2, the q-binomial factor [M+nL - sum_b C^{-1}_{1,b} mu^{(b)}_1 choose nL]_q, and the factor [mu+eta choose mu]_q, where eta=nL(C^{-1}e_1 tensor e_1) - (C^{-1} tensor C)mu and the mu-sum uses the same integrality restriction as the supernomial hierarchy. The case p=n+1 is known from the cited Gessel-Krattenthaler identity; the open problem is the general conjecture supported by computer checks.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers $n\ge 2$ and $p\ge n$. Let $C$ denote the Cartan matrix of type $A_{n-1}$, with inverse $C^{-1}$. Let $\rho=(n-1,n-2,\dots,1,0)\in\mathbb Z^n$, and let $e_1=(1,0,\dots,0)\in\mathbb Z^n$. For a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$ let $\ell(\sigma)$ denote its length, and write $\sigma\cdot v$ for the natural action of $S_n$ on $\mathbb Z^n$ by coordinate permutation.

For $L,M\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ and zero–sum vectors $k=(k_1,\dots,k_n),\ k'=(k'_1,\dots,k'_n)\in\mathbb Z^n$ with $\sum_i k_i=\sum_i k'_i=0$, define
$$T''(L,M,k,k')\ :=\ \prod_{i=1}^{n}\binom{M+L-k_i+k'_i}{L-k_i}_q,$$
where $\binom{a}{b}_q=\frac{(q)_a}{(q)_b(q)_{a-b}}$ when $0\le b\le a$ and zero otherwise, with $(q)_m=\prod_{j=1}^m(1-q^j)$.

For each $k\in\mathbb Z^n$ with $|k|:=\sum_i k_i=0$ and $\sigma\in S_n$, define an integer exponent $\phi_{p,k,\sigma}$ by
$$\phi_{p,k,\sigma}\ =\ \tfrac{p(p-1)}{2}\,k\cdot C\,k\ -\ k\cdot(p\rho-(p-1)\sigma\cdot\rho)\ +\ \ell(\sigma).$$

On the other side, let $\mu=(\mu^{(1)},\dots,\mu^{(n-1)})$ range over tuples of compositions (with the usual integrality/length restriction of the $A_{n-1}$ supernomial hierarchy: $\mu^{(b)}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}^{N}$ for a fixed large $N$, satisfying the standard congruence conditions making all subsequent $q$-binomials nonzero). Put
$$\eta\ :=\ nL\,(C^{-1}e_1\otimes e_1)\ -\ (C^{-1}\otimes C)\,\mu,$$
and define
$$\binom{\mu+\eta}{\mu}_q\ :=\ \prod_{b=1}^{n-1}\prod_{j\ge 1}\binom{\mu^{(b)}_j+\eta^{(b)}_j}{\mu^{(b)}_j}_q.$$

Conjecture (to be proved). For all $L,M\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ and all $p\ge n$,
$$\sum_{\substack{k\in\mathbb Z^n\\ |k|=0}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}(-1)^{\ell(\sigma)}q^{\phi_{p,k,\sigma}}\,T''\!\bigl(L,M,\,pk-\sigma\cdot\rho+\rho,\,(p-1)k-\sigma\cdot\rho+\rho\bigr)$$
$$=\ \sum_{\mu}q^{\,\tfrac12\,\mu\,(C^{-1}\otimes C)\,\mu}\ \binom{M+nL-\sum_{b=1}^{n-1}C^{-1}_{1,b}\mu^{(b)}_1}{nL}_q\ \binom{\mu+\eta}{\mu}_q.$$

Prove this identity. (The case $p=n+1$ is known from a Gessel–Krattenthaler-type cylindric-partition identity; establish the general case.)
status_search_result: The conjecture is stated as a computer-checked open problem in the survey by Schilling and Warnaar on supernomial coefficients and Bailey's lemma. Subsequent work on the A_{n-1} Bailey lemma and on cylindric partitions (including the A_2 Rogers–Ramanujan revisited work and MacMahon-analysis approaches to cylindric partitions) has continued, but no source recovered in the search explicitly establishes this general p ≥ n identity beyond the known p = n+1 case. Its current status could not be conclusively verified.

paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
original_question: Does there exist a Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group G, where paratopological means that the group multiplication map G x G -> G is continuous, that is not a topological group because the full topological-group continuity requirements fail?
self_contained_problem: A paratopological group is a group $G$ endowed with a topology such that the multiplication map $G\times G\to G$, $(x,y)\mapsto xy$, is jointly continuous (no continuity assumption is made on the inversion map $x\mapsto x^{-1}$). A paratopological group is a topological group if, in addition, inversion is continuous. Working in ZFC, decide the following question: does there exist a Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group whose inversion map is discontinuous (equivalently, a Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group that is not a topological group)?
status_search_result: Under additional set-theoretic assumptions (e.g., the existence of an infinite torsion-free abelian countably compact topological group without nontrivial convergent sequences), a functionally Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group that is not a topological group has been constructed (Banakh–Ravsky, "On feebly compact paratopological groups", arXiv:1003.5343). A ZFC example does not appear to be known, so the problem is partially solved (consistent example exists; ZFC status open).

paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
original_question: Let G be a Hausdorff semitopological group, meaning that G is a group with a topology such that multiplication is separately continuous and inversion is continuous. If the underlying topological space of G is Baire, must G be a topological group?
self_contained_problem:
Call a triple $(G,\cdot,\tau)$ a Hausdorff semitopological group with continuous inversion if $G$ is a group, $\tau$ is a Hausdorff topology on $G$, the multiplication map $G\times G\to G$, $(x,y)\mapsto x\cdot y$, is separately continuous (i.e., continuous in each variable when the other is fixed), and the inversion map $G\to G$, $x\mapsto x^{-1}$, is continuous. Recall that a topological space is Baire if the intersection of any countable family of dense open subsets is dense, and that $(G,\cdot,\tau)$ is a topological group if, in addition to continuous inversion, the multiplication map is jointly continuous as a map $G\times G\to G$.

Question: Must every Hausdorff semitopological group with continuous inversion whose underlying topological space is Baire be a topological group?
status_search_result: Searches reveal an active line of research giving partial positive results (e.g., every Čech-analytic Baire semitopological group is a topological group; metrizable Baire and various Bouziad-type conditions imply the conclusion) and counterexamples in weaker settings (a separable Baire semi-metric semitopological group that is not paratopological), but no source clearly settles the general question for Hausdorff semitopological groups with continuous inversion that are Baire. The problem appears to still be considered open.

paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
original_question: Given any paratopological group (G, tau), where tau is a Hausdorff topology making multiplication continuous, does there always exist a coarser or equal group topology tau' <= tau such that (G, tau') is a topological group?
self_contained_problem:
A paratopological group is a pair $(G,\tau)$ consisting of a group $G$ equipped with a topology $\tau$ such that the multiplication map $G\times G\to G$, $(x,y)\mapsto xy$, is jointly continuous (inversion is not required to be continuous). A topological group is a paratopological group $(G,\tau')$ in which, additionally, the inversion map $x\mapsto x^{-1}$ is continuous.

Question: Let $(G,\tau)$ be an arbitrary paratopological group whose topology $\tau$ is Hausdorff. Does there always exist a group topology $\tau'$ on $G$ with $\tau'\subseteq\tau$ (i.e., $\tau'$ is coarser than or equal to $\tau$) such that $(G,\tau')$ is a topological group?
status_search_result: Web searches surface considerable activity on related questions (e.g., when a Hausdorff/first-countable paratopological group admits a coarser (separable) metrizable group topology, regularity vs. complete regularity of paratopological groups), but no source found directly resolves the general question of whether every Hausdorff paratopological group admits a coarser group topology making it a topological group. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
original_question: For a zero-dimensional topological space X, is the free topological inverse semigroup I(X) over X also zero-dimensional?
self_contained_problem:
An inverse semigroup is a semigroup S in which, for every element a ∈ S, there exists a unique element a⁻¹ ∈ S (called the inverse of a) such that a·a⁻¹·a = a and a⁻¹·a·a⁻¹ = a⁻¹. A topological inverse semigroup is an inverse semigroup endowed with a Hausdorff topology making both the multiplication S × S → S and the inversion S → S, a ↦ a⁻¹, continuous.

Given a topological space X, the free topological inverse semigroup over X is a topological inverse semigroup I(X) together with a continuous map η : X → I(X) such that for every continuous map f : X → T into a topological inverse semigroup T there is a unique continuous inverse-semigroup homomorphism f̄ : I(X) → T with f̄ ∘ η = f.

Recall that a topological space is called zero-dimensional if it is a T₁ space possessing a base consisting of clopen (simultaneously closed and open) sets.

Question: If X is a zero-dimensional topological space, is the free topological inverse semigroup I(X) over X necessarily zero-dimensional?

paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
original_question: Let S be a topological inverse semigroup, let E(S) be the subsemigroup of idempotents of S, and let H = {H(e) | e in E(S)} be the family of maximal subgroups of S. Given topological properties P_1 and P_2, if E(S) has property P_1 and each maximal subgroup H(e) has property P_2, what topological properties must the whole semigroup S have?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a topological inverse semigroup, that is, a Hausdorff topological space equipped with a continuous associative multiplication $S\times S\to S$ such that every element $s\in S$ has a unique inverse $s^{-1}$ satisfying $ss^{-1}s=s$ and $s^{-1}ss^{-1}=s^{-1}$, with the inversion map $s\mapsto s^{-1}$ continuous. Let
$$E(S)=\{e\in S:e^2=e\}$$
be the subsemigroup of idempotents of $S$, endowed with the subspace topology, and for each $e\in E(S)$ let
$$H(e)=\{s\in S:ss^{-1}=s^{-1}s=e,\ \exists\,t\in S\text{ with }st=ts=e\}$$
denote the maximal subgroup of $S$ at $e$, again with the subspace topology. The family $\mathcal{H}=\{H(e):e\in E(S)\}$ partitions the set of group-like elements of $S$.

Given two topological properties $P_1$ and $P_2$ (for example: compactness, local compactness, metrizability, separability, Lindelöf property, $\sigma$-compactness, paracompactness, completeness, pseudocompactness, countable tightness, etc.), determine which topological properties $Q$ must necessarily hold for $S$ under the assumption that $E(S)$ has property $P_1$ and every maximal subgroup $H(e)$, $e\in E(S)$, has property $P_2$.

More precisely: characterize, for each pair $(P_1,P_2)$, the strongest topological property $Q=Q(P_1,P_2)$ such that whenever $E(S)$ satisfies $P_1$ and all $H(e)$ satisfy $P_2$, the topological inverse semigroup $S$ must satisfy $Q$.
status_search_result: The question is a broad meta-problem asking, for arbitrary pairs of topological properties $(P_1,P_2)$, what is inherited by a topological inverse semigroup $S$ from its idempotent subsemigroup $E(S)$ and its maximal subgroups $H(e)$. Searches reveal active research on related special cases (e.g., locally compact shift-continuous topologies on simple inverse $\omega$-semigroups with compact maximal subgroups), but no comprehensive resolution of the general transfer problem. The overall status appears open/unresolved in its full generality.

paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
context_brief: Taylor expansions in several quaternionic variables
original_question: For regular functions of several quaternionic variables, can one prove an analogue of the one-variable Taylor expansion theorem? Here H denotes the quaternion algebra; a regular function of n quaternionic variables is a differentiable function f: H^n -> H satisfying the left Cauchy-Fueter equation d f / d bar(q_i) = 0 in every variable. The one-variable theory uses homogeneous regular polynomials P_nu and the Cauchy-Kowalewski (C-K) product, which multiplies entire regular functions while staying regular; no analogous C-K product is known in several variables, and this absence blocks a Taylor series theory.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of real quaternions with standard basis $1, i, j, k$, and write a quaternion as $q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k$. For a differentiable function $f : \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{H}$, define the left Cauchy–Fueter operator by
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial \bar{q}} = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_0} + i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1} + j\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_2} + k\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_3}.$$
A differentiable function $f : \mathbb{H}^n \to \mathbb{H}$ in variables $q_1, \dots, q_n \in \mathbb{H}$ is called (left) regular if it satisfies the Cauchy–Fueter equation in each variable separately, i.e.
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial \bar{q}_i} = 0, \qquad i = 1, \dots, n.$$
In the one-variable case ($n = 1$), Fueter's theorem states that every regular function $f$ defined on a suitable neighborhood of the origin admits a Taylor-type expansion
$$f(q) = \sum_{\nu} P_\nu(q)\, a_\nu,$$
where $\{P_\nu\}$ is the family of homogeneous regular polynomials in $q$ and $a_\nu \in \mathbb{H}$. A key ingredient enabling the construction and multiplication of regular functions in this one-variable theory is the Cauchy–Kowalewski (C–K) product, which assigns to two entire regular functions a new entire regular function and which restricts to the usual product on the subspace $\{q : x_0 = 0\}$.

Problem. Establish, or refute, an analogue of the Taylor expansion theorem for regular functions of several quaternionic variables: namely, prove that every regular function $f : \Omega \subseteq \mathbb{H}^n \to \mathbb{H}$, with $\Omega$ a suitable neighborhood of the origin, can be expanded as a convergent series
$$f(q_1, \dots, q_n) = \sum_{\nu} P_\nu(q_1, \dots, q_n)\, a_\nu, \qquad a_\nu \in \mathbb{H},$$
in terms of a natural family of homogeneous regular polynomials $P_\nu$ on $\mathbb{H}^n$. Equivalently, construct a multivariable analogue of the Cauchy–Kowalewski product on entire regular functions of $n$ quaternionic variables that allows such a Taylor theory to be developed.
status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a known proof of a multivariable Taylor expansion theorem for regular functions on $\mathbb{H}^n$, nor a construction of a multivariable Cauchy–Kowalewski product. Available surveys on the Cauchy–Fueter system in several variables continue to treat the absence of such a product as an obstruction, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
original_question: In the free resolution of the Cauchy-Fueter module M_n from Theorem 3.2, prove or refute that every matrix in the resolution except P_2 has entries that are degree-one polynomials. The problem also asks for the analytic meaning of this observed linearity, since the authors report seeing it in computed examples but not knowing how to prove it in general.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the quaternions with basis $1,i,j,k$. For $n\geq 1$ and quaternionic variables $q_\ell = x_{\ell,0}+ix_{\ell,1}+jx_{\ell,2}+kx_{\ell,3}$, $\ell=1,\dots,n$, the Cauchy–Fueter operator in the $\ell$-th variable is
$$\partial_{\bar q_\ell} = \partial_{x_{\ell,0}} + i\,\partial_{x_{\ell,1}} + j\,\partial_{x_{\ell,2}} + k\,\partial_{x_{\ell,3}}.$$
After identifying $\mathbb{H}\cong\mathbb{C}^2$, the operator $\partial_{\bar q_\ell}$ corresponds to a $2\times 2$ matrix of first-order constant-coefficient differential operators with polynomial symbol $P_\ell\in \operatorname{Mat}_{2\times 2}(R)$, where $R = \mathbb{C}[z_{\ell,\alpha}\colon \ell=1,\dots,n,\ \alpha=1,2,3,4]$ is a polynomial ring with $4n$ indeterminates corresponding to the Fourier symbols of the $4n$ real partial derivatives.

Let $P\in \operatorname{Mat}_{2n\times 2}(R)$ be the column matrix obtained by stacking $P_1,\dots,P_n$, and let $M_n = \operatorname{coker}(P^T\colon R^{2n}\to R^{2})^{\vee}$ be the associated Cauchy–Fueter module (viewed as the $R$-module whose minimal free resolution computes the syzygies of $P$). There exists a minimal graded free resolution
$$0\to R^{b_N}\xrightarrow{P_N}\cdots\xrightarrow{P_3} R^{b_2}\xrightarrow{P_2} R^{b_1}\xrightarrow{P_1} R^{b_0}\to M_n\to 0.$$

Prove or disprove: for every $n\geq 2$ and every $i\in\{1,3,4,\dots,N\}$ (that is, for every matrix in the resolution other than $P_2$), all nonzero entries of the matrix $P_i$ are homogeneous polynomials of degree exactly one in $R$.

In addition, provide an analytic interpretation of this linearity in terms of the Cauchy–Fueter complex.
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any paper that explicitly proves or disproves the linearity of all matrices (other than the second) in the minimal free resolution of the Cauchy–Fueter module $M_n$, nor any work giving an analytic interpretation of this phenomenon. The status appears unverified from publicly available sources.

paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
original_question: Find a (2n+1)-dimensional variety S inside H^n = R^(4n) for which the local cohomology of the sheaf R of Cauchy-Fueter regular functions with support in S vanishes in every degree j different from 2n-1 and is nonzero in degree 2n-1. This is intended as a quaternionic analogue of the classical pure n-codimensionality theorem for R^n inside C^n with respect to the sheaf O of holomorphic functions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}^n \cong \mathbb{R}^{4n}$ denote the space of $n$-tuples of quaternions, and let $\mathcal{R}$ be the sheaf on $\mathbb{H}^n$ of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions, i.e. functions $f:\mathbb{H}^n\to\mathbb{H}$ that are annihilated coordinate-wise by the Cauchy–Fueter operator $\partial_{\bar q_i}=\partial_{x_i^0}+i\,\partial_{x_i^1}+j\,\partial_{x_i^2}+k\,\partial_{x_i^3}$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. For a closed subset $S\subset\mathbb{H}^n$, let $\mathcal{H}^j_S(\mathbb{H}^n,\mathcal{R})$ denote the $j$-th local cohomology of $\mathcal{R}$ with support in $S$.

Construct a real-analytic (or semi-analytic) subvariety $S\subset\mathbb{H}^n$ of real dimension $2n+1$ such that
$$\mathcal{H}^j_S(\mathbb{H}^n,\mathcal{R}) = 0 \quad \text{for all } j\neq 2n-1, \qquad \mathcal{H}^{2n-1}_S(\mathbb{H}^n,\mathcal{R}) \neq 0.$$

This is the quaternionic analogue of the classical purity result stating that $\mathbb{R}^n\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ is purely $n$-codimensional with respect to the sheaf $\mathcal{O}$ of holomorphic functions.
status_search_result: The case $n=2$ (i.e. 5-dimensional varieties in $\mathbb{H}^2$) has been addressed by Colombo–Damiano–Sabadini–Struppa, who constructed quaternionic hyperfunctions on certain 5-dimensional varieties in $\mathbb{H}^2$ realizing the expected pure codimensionality with respect to $\mathcal{R}$. The general case for arbitrary $n$ — producing $(2n+1)$-dimensional varieties in $\mathbb{H}^n$ with local cohomology concentrated in degree $2n-1$ — does not appear to have a complete published resolution.

paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
original_question: For the Cauchy-Fueter system P(D)f = 0, give a geometric characterization of the open sets that are P-convex. In the source, P-convexity is the weaker hypothesis that replaces ordinary convexity in the Ehrenpreis-Palamodov exactness theorem for systems of linear constant-coefficient differential operators, and it should express an appropriate relation between the system P and the topology of the open set.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions and consider the Cauchy–Fueter operator in $n$ variables. For a quaternionic variable $q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k$, define
$$\bar\partial_{CF} = \frac{\partial}{\partial x_0} + i\frac{\partial}{\partial x_1} + j\frac{\partial}{\partial x_2} + k\frac{\partial}{\partial x_3}.$$
For $n$ quaternionic variables $q_1,\dots,q_n$, let $P(D)$ be the linear constant-coefficient differential operator (with values in a suitable free $\mathbb{H}$-module) whose components are $\bar\partial_{CF,\ell}$ ($\ell=1,\dots,n$), so that the homogeneous system $P(D)f = 0$ on an open set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{4n}$ characterizes regular (Fueter-regular) functions of several quaternionic variables.

Recall that, in the Ehrenpreis–Palamodov theory of systems of linear partial differential operators with constant coefficients, an open set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is called $P$-convex (for the system $P$) if the cohomology of the associated complex on $\Omega$ vanishes in the appropriate degrees—equivalently, the exactness theorem that holds for convex $\Omega$ continues to hold for $\Omega$. $P$-convexity is strictly weaker than ordinary convexity and is expected to reflect a compatibility between the system $P$ and the topology/geometry of $\Omega$.

Problem. Give a purely geometric characterization of the open sets $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{4n}$ that are $P$-convex for the Cauchy–Fueter system in $n$ quaternionic variables.
status_search_result: A complete geometric characterization of P-convex open sets is known only in restricted settings (e.g., scalar principal-type operators in ℝ³ with C²-boundary). For general systems, and in particular for the Cauchy–Fueter system in several quaternionic variables, no such geometric characterization appears in the literature, and the problem is still regarded as open.

paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
original_question: Prove a Paley-Wiener theorem for the Fourier transform of compactly supported H-hyperfunctions, where H denotes the quaternion algebra and H-hyperfunctions are built from boundary values of quaternionic regular functions. The relevant Fourier transform should use the regular quaternionic exponential defined through the homogeneous regular polynomials P_nu, and the theorem should identify compact support with an appropriate space of entire functions of exponential type.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions, and let $f:\mathbb{H}\to\mathbb{H}$ be (left) regular in the sense of Cauchy–Fueter, i.e. it satisfies
$$\overline{D}f := \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_0} + i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_1} + j\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_2} + k\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_3} = 0.$$
For each multi-index $\nu$, let $P_\nu(q)$ denote the Fueter homogeneous regular polynomials (the symmetrized products of the Fueter variables $\zeta_\ell = x_\ell - x_0 e_\ell$, $\ell=1,2,3$), and let
$$E(q,\xi) := \sum_{\nu} P_\nu(q)\,\frac{(i\xi)^{|\nu|}}{|\nu|!}\cdot(\text{coefficients})$$
be the regular quaternionic exponential built from the $P_\nu$. The space of $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions on an open set $U\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ is defined as boundary values, modulo regular functions, of Cauchy–Fueter regular functions on appropriate complex neighbourhoods, yielding a sheaf analogous to Sato's hyperfunctions but built from the kernel of $\overline{D}$.

Define the regular Fourier transform $\widehat{T}(\xi)$ of a compactly supported $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunction $T$ by
$$\widehat{T}(\xi) := \langle T_q, E(q,\xi)\rangle,\qquad \xi\in\mathbb{H}.$$

Problem. Establish a Paley–Wiener theorem characterizing the image of the space of compactly supported $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions under this regular Fourier transform: namely, identify $\widehat{T}$ with an explicitly described space of $\mathbb{H}$-valued entire functions on $\mathbb{H}_{\mathbb{C}}$ of exponential type, with the type bounded by the radius of a ball containing the support of $T$, together with appropriate growth conditions on the real axis reflecting that $T$ is a hyperfunction (rather than a distribution).
status_search_result: Searches reveal active development of Paley–Wiener-type theorems in quaternionic settings (quaternion Fourier transform, slice regular functions, Dirac operators of Riesz–Feller type), but no source explicitly establishes a Paley–Wiener theorem for compactly supported $\mathbb{H}$-hyperfunctions in the Cauchy–Fueter sense using the regular exponential built from the $P_\nu$. The status of this specific problem could not be confirmed.

paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
original_question: Given a hypercomplex algebra, study all possible families of operators that linearize the wave operator. This problem sits in the setting of hypercomplex operators that linearize ultrahyperbolic or wave-type operators, including operators related to Maxwell's system for biquaternion-valued functions and operators linearizing the Klein-Gordon equation using octonions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a hypercomplex algebra, i.e., a finite-dimensional unital real algebra equipped with a basis $\{e_0=1,e_1,\dots,e_{n}\}$ satisfying prescribed multiplication relations (examples include the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$, the biquaternions $\mathbb{H}\otimes\mathbb{C}$, and the octonions $\mathbb{O}$). For functions $f:\mathbb{R}^{p,q}	o A$ on a (possibly indefinite) real space, consider first-order linear differential operators of the form
$$D=\sum_{j=0}^{m} a_j\,\partial_{x_j},\qquad a_j\in A,$$
or more generally finite families $(D_1,\dots,D_r)$ of such operators with coefficients in $A$. Say that such a family linearizes the wave operator $\square=\partial_{x_0}^2-\partial_{x_1}^2-\cdots-\partial_{x_m}^2$ (or, more generally, an ultrahyperbolic operator of signature $(p,q)$) if there exist operators $D_1',\dots,D_r'$ of the same form such that
$$D_i' D_j + D_j' D_i = 2\delta_{ij}\,\square\quad	ext{for all }i,j,$$
so that composing the family with its companion family reproduces the wave (or ultrahyperbolic) operator on each component.

Problem: For an arbitrary hypercomplex algebra $A$, classify all families of first-order $A$-linear differential operators that linearize the wave operator (and, more generally, ultrahyperbolic operators). In particular, describe completely the cases corresponding to (i) operators related to Maxwell's system acting on biquaternion-valued functions and (ii) operators linearizing the Klein–Gordon equation by means of octonions.
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open research direction in the context of hypercomplex analysis (Cauchy–Fueter type systems). While various individual linearizations of the wave/Klein–Gordon/Maxwell operators by quaternionic, biquaternionic, Clifford, and octonionic operators are known in the literature, a complete classification for an arbitrary hypercomplex algebra does not appear to have been achieved. No definitive resolution was found.

paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
context_brief: Several variables as one hypercomplex variable
original_question: Given a hypercomplex algebra A and a notion of A-regularity, find a hypercomplex algebra C and a corresponding notion of C-regularity such that every A-regular function of several variables appears as a special case of a C-regular function of one variable. The motivating examples are that regular functions of two quaternionic variables can be viewed as regular functions of one biquaternionic variable or one suitable Clifford variable.
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional real hypercomplex algebra (i.e., a unital associative real algebra generated by a finite set of "imaginary" units, such as the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$, the biquaternions $\mathbb{H}\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C}$, or a Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}(p,q)$). Suppose one has fixed a notion of $A$-regularity for functions $f:\Omega\subset A^n\to A$, meaning a first-order constant-coefficient linear differential operator $D_A^{(n)}$ (a Cauchy–Fueter type operator) such that the $A$-regular functions of $n$ variables are exactly the solutions of $D_A^{(n)} f=0$.

Problem. Find a hypercomplex algebra $C$ (depending on $A$ and $n$) together with a Cauchy–Fueter–type operator $D_C^{(1)}$ defining a notion of $C$-regularity for functions $g:\Omega'\subset C\to C$ of a single $C$-variable, and an embedding/identification
$$\iota:A^n \hookrightarrow C, \qquad \pi:C\to A,$$
such that every $A$-regular function $f:\Omega\to A$ of $n$ variables arises as $f = \pi\circ g\circ \iota$ for some $C$-regular function $g$ of one $C$-variable, and conversely the pullback of every $C$-regular $g$ yields an $A$-regular $f$.

As motivating instances, one requires that:
(i) when $A=\mathbb{H}$ and $n=2$, the algebra $C$ may be taken to be the biquaternions $\mathbb{H}\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{C}$, with an appropriate one-variable regularity;
(ii) alternatively, $C$ may be taken to be a suitable Clifford algebra, again with a one-variable Cauchy–Fueter–type regularity recovering the two-quaternionic-variable Fueter-regular functions.

Determine such an algebra $C$ and one-variable regularity for general $A$ and $n\ge 2$.
status_search_result: This is stated as an open research problem in hypercomplex analysis concerning Cauchy–Fueter systems in several variables. No published solution providing a general construction of such an algebra $C$ and one-variable regularity reducing $n$-variable $A$-regularity to one-variable $C$-regularity could be located; only the motivating quaternion/biquaternion/Clifford examples are known.

paper_title: Open problems in combinatorial group theory
original_question: Given a finite presentation of a hyperbolic group that is not necessarily a Dehn presentation, can one find a Dehn presentation for the group in polynomial time?
self_contained_problem:
A finitely generated group $G$ is called word hyperbolic if its Cayley graph (with respect to some, equivalently any, finite generating set) is a Gromov-hyperbolic metric space. A finite presentation $\langle X \mid R\rangle$ of $G$ is called a Dehn presentation if for every nontrivial word $w$ in $X \cup X^{-1}$ representing the identity in $G$, there exist a relator $r \in R$ (cyclically reduced) and a factorization $r = uv$ such that $w$ contains $u$ as a subword and $|v| < |u|$; equivalently, the word problem can be solved by iteratively replacing such subwords $u$ by $v^{-1}$, strictly decreasing the length at every step. It is a theorem of Gromov that a finitely presented group is word hyperbolic if and only if it admits a Dehn presentation.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input an arbitrary finite presentation $\langle X \mid R\rangle$ of a word hyperbolic group $G$ (not assumed to be a Dehn presentation), produces in time polynomial in the total length of the input a Dehn presentation for $G$?
status_search_result: No source found that resolves this problem. Related work (e.g., polynomial-time procedures that certify hyperbolicity and produce linear-time word-problem solvers when they succeed) addresses adjacent algorithmic questions but does not establish a polynomial-time algorithm to convert an arbitrary finite presentation of a hyperbolic group into a Dehn presentation. The problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Achromatic number decision problem for trees
original_question: Given a finite tree T = (V,E) and a positive integer K, does T admit a complete K-coloring, meaning a coloring of the vertices of T with colors {1,2,...,K} such that adjacent vertices receive different colors and, for every pair i,j of distinct colors, some edge of T has one endpoint colored i and the other endpoint colored j?

(i) for every edge $\{u,v\}\in E$, $c(u)\neq c(v)$ (properness); and
(ii) for every pair $i\neq j$ in $\{1,2,\dots,K\}$, there exists an edge $\{u,v\}\in E$ with $\{c(u),c(v)\}=\{i,j\}$.

paper_title: Some Recent Results and Open Problems on Sets of Lengths of Krull Monoids with Finite Class Group
context_brief: maximum distance in sets of lengths
original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group with |G| at least 3 and invariant-factor decomposition G ≅ C_{n1} ⊕ ... ⊕ C_{nr}, where C_n is a cyclic group of order n and 1 < n1 | ... | nr. For the monoid B(G) of zero-sum sequences over G, let Delta(G) denote the set of all positive gaps between consecutive lengths that occur in sets of factorization lengths of elements of B(G). Must the largest such distance satisfy max Delta(G) = max{nr - 2, -1 + sum_{i=1}^r floor(ni/2)}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|\ge 3$, and let $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ be its invariant-factor decomposition, where $C_n$ denotes the cyclic group of order $n$ and $1<n_1\mid n_2\mid\cdots\mid n_r$.

A sequence over $G$ is a finite unordered tuple $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_\ell$ of elements of $G$ (repetitions allowed), and $S$ is called a zero-sum sequence if $g_1+\cdots+g_\ell=0$ in $G$. The set $\mathcal B(G)$ of all zero-sum sequences over $G$, with concatenation as operation, forms a commutative cancellative monoid (the monoid of zero-sum sequences). An element $U\in\mathcal B(G)$ is called an atom if it cannot be written as a product of two nontrivial zero-sum sequences. For a nonzero, non-unit $B\in\mathcal B(G)$, the set of (factorization) lengths is
$$\mathsf L(B)=\{k\in\mathbb N : B=U_1\cdot\ldots\cdot U_k\text{ with each }U_i\text{ an atom of }\mathcal B(G)\}.$$
For a finite set $L=\{m_1<m_2<\cdots<m_t\}\subset\mathbb Z$ of integers, define its set of distances $\Delta(L)=\{m_{i+1}-m_i : 1\le i<t\}$. Set
$$\Delta(G)=\bigcup_{B} \Delta(\mathsf L(B)),$$
the union taken over all $B\in\mathcal B(G)$ with $|\mathsf L(B)|\ge 2$.

Question: Does the equality
$$\max\Delta(G)\;=\;\max\!\Bigl\{\,n_r-2,\ -1+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Bigl\lfloor\frac{n_i}{2}\Bigr\rfloor\Bigr\}$$
hold for every such $G$?

status_search_result: A general closed-form formula for $\max\Delta(G)$ in terms of the invariant-factor decomposition does not appear to be established in the literature; the conjectured equality is stated as a problem and surveys on sets of lengths in Krull monoids over finite abelian groups continue to list the determination of $\max\Delta(G)$ as an open question, with results known only in special cases (cyclic groups, elementary $p$-groups, rank-two groups). No source confirming a proof of the stated equality for all finite abelian groups was found.

original_question: Let G be a finite abelian group. For each subset G0 of G whose zero-sum-sequence monoid has a nonempty distance set Delta(G0), form the minimum distance min Delta(G0), and let Delta*(G) be the set of all such minima. Does there exist a finite abelian group G for which Delta*(G) is an interval and exp(G) >= 2r(G) + 2, where r(G) is the rank of G and exp(G) is the exponent of G in its invariant-factor decomposition?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, written in invariant-factor form $G \cong \mathbb{Z}/n_1\mathbb{Z} \oplus \cdots \oplus \mathbb{Z}/n_r\mathbb{Z}$ with $1 < n_1 \mid n_2 \mid \cdots \mid n_r$; set $r(G) = r$ (the rank) and $\exp(G) = n_r$ (the exponent). For a subset $G_0 \subseteq G$, let $\mathcal{B}(G_0)$ denote the monoid of zero-sum sequences over $G_0$ (the finitely generated submonoid of the free abelian monoid $\mathcal{F}(G_0)$ consisting of all sequences $S = g_1 \cdots g_\ell$ with $g_1 + \cdots + g_\ell = 0$ in $G$). For a zero-sum sequence $S \in \mathcal{B}(G_0)$, let $\mathsf{L}(S) \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be its set of lengths, i.e., the set of all $k$ such that $S$ can be written as a product of $k$ atoms (irreducible elements) of $\mathcal{B}(G_0)$. Define
$$\Delta(G_0) = \bigcup_{S \in \mathcal{B}(G_0),\, |\mathsf{L}(S)| \ge 2} \{\, \ell_{i+1} - \ell_i : \mathsf{L}(S) = \{\ell_1 < \ell_2 < \cdots\}\,\},$$
the distance set of $G_0$. Define
$$\Delta^{*}(G) = \{\, \min \Delta(G_0) : G_0 \subseteq G \text{ with } \Delta(G_0) \ne \emptyset \,\}.$$
A subset of $\mathbb{N}$ is called an interval if it equals $\{a, a+1, \dots, b\}$ for some $a \le b$.

Question: Does there exist a finite abelian group $G$ such that $\Delta^{*}(G)$ is an interval and $\exp(G) \ge 2\, r(G) + 2$?

paper_title: Open problems concerning the Hőlder continuity of the direction of vorticity for the Navier-Stokes equations.
context_brief: Navier-Stokes velocity integrability from vorticity-direction Hölder regularity
original_question: Let u be a Leray-Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional evolution Navier-Stokes equations in the whole space R^3 on the time interval (0,T), and let its vorticity be ω = ∇×u. For θ(x,y,t) equal to the angle between ω(x,t) and ω(y,t), assume the direction of vorticity is β-Hölder in the sense that sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x-y|^β on R^3×R^3×(0,T) for some β < 1/2. Let $u$ be a Leray–Hopf weak solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
\[
\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \Delta u + \nabla p = 0,\qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,
\]
on $\mathbb{R}^3 \times (0,T)$, and let its vorticity be $\omega = \nabla\times u$. For points $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^3$ and $t\in(0,T)$, let $\theta(x,y,t)$ denote the angle between the vectors $\omega(x,t)$ and $\omega(y,t)$. Assume that the direction of vorticity is $\beta$-Hölder continuous in space in the sense that there exist constants $c>0$ and $\beta\in(0,1/2)$ such that
\[
\sin\theta(x,y,t) \le c\,|x-y|^{\beta} \qquad \text{for all } (x,y,t)\in\mathbb{R}^3\times\mathbb{R}^3\times(0,T).
\]
For exponents $s,q\in[1,\infty]$, set $\lambda(s,q) = \tfrac{2}{s} + \tfrac{3}{q}$.

Question: Under the above hypothesis with some $\beta<1/2$, must there exist exponents $s$ and $q$ such that
\[
u \in L^s\bigl(0,T;\,L^q(\mathbb{R}^3)\bigr) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \lambda(s,q) = \tfrac{2}{s} + \tfrac{3}{q} < \tfrac{3}{2}\,?
\]
status_search_result: The strongest known result handles the borderline case β = 1/2 (Berselli–Beirão da Veiga, 2002), giving ω ∈ L^∞(L²) and hence smoothness. Extending the regularity/integrability conclusion to β < 1/2 is explicitly identified as an open problem in subsequent surveys and follow-up papers, with no full solution reported as of 2026.

paper_title: Progress on homogeneous Einstein manifolds and some open probrems
original_question: Let M = G/K be a homogeneous space, and call a G-invariant Riemannian metric Einstein when its Ricci tensor is a scalar multiple of the metric. Is Ziller's finiteness conjecture true: if the rank of G equals the rank of the isotropy subgroup, or if the isotropy representation of G/K decomposes into only non-equivalent irreducible summands, must the number of G-invariant Einstein metrics on M be finite?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M = G/K$ be a homogeneous space, where $G$ is a compact connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup of $G$. A Riemannian metric on $M$ is called $G$-invariant if $G$ acts by isometries, and is called Einstein if its Ricci tensor is a constant scalar multiple of the metric. Two $G$-invariant Einstein metrics are identified if they differ by an isometry and by a positive scaling factor.

Prove or disprove the following finiteness statement (Ziller's finiteness conjecture): the number of $G$-invariant Einstein metrics on $M = G/K$ (up to isometry and homothety) is finite whenever at least one of the following holds:

(a) $\operatorname{rank} G = \operatorname{rank} K$, or

(b) the isotropy representation of $K$ on $T_{eK}(G/K)$ decomposes into pairwise non-equivalent irreducible summands.

context_brief: Equivalent isotropy summands and Stiefel manifolds
original_question: For Stiefel manifolds such as V_k R^n = SO(n)/SO(n-k), and more generally homogeneous spaces G/K whose isotropy representation contains equivalent summands, is the set of invariant Einstein metrics finite, or can continuous one-parameter families of invariant Einstein metrics occur?

Let $G/K$ be a compact homogeneous space, where $G$ is a compact connected Lie group and $K\subset G$ is a closed subgroup, with reductive decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$ (so that $\mathrm{Ad}(K)\mathfrak{m}\subset\mathfrak{m}$). paper_title: Three Open Problems on the Wijsman Topology
original_question: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). Characterize exactly when this Wijsman hyperspace is a normal topological space.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and let $2^X$ denote the family of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$. For each $A \in 2^X$, let $d(\cdot, A): X \to \mathbb{R}$ be the distance functional $x \mapsto \inf\{d(x,a) : a \in A\}$. The Wijsman topology $\mathscr{T}_{W(d)}$ on $2^X$ is defined as the weakest topology on $2^X$ such that for every $A \in 2^X$, the map $2^X \to C(X,\mathbb{R})$ given by $B \mapsto d(\cdot, B)$ induces continuity of the evaluation, equivalently, $\mathscr{T}_{W(d)}$ is the weakest topology in which, for each $x \in X$, the functional $B \mapsto d(x,B)$ is continuous on $2^X$. The pair $(2^X, \mathscr{T}_{W(d)})$ is called the Wijsman hyperspace of $(X,d)$.

Give a complete characterization of those metric spaces $(X,d)$ for which the Wijsman hyperspace $(2^X, \mathscr{T}_{W(d)})$ is a normal topological space (i.e. $T_1$ and such that any two disjoint closed subsets can be separated by disjoint open sets).
status_search_result: The general characterization of when a Wijsman hyperspace is normal remains open. Partial results are known: every hereditarily normal Wijsman hyperspace is metrizable (Chaber–Pol type result, arXiv:1211.0043); for linear metric spaces, normality is equivalent to metrizability; and if $X$ is locally separable with weight a regular uncountable cardinal, the Wijsman hyperspace fails to be normal. A full characterization in ZFC has not been established.

original_question: Let (X, d) be a metric space. Let 2^X be the family of all non-empty closed subsets of X, and let T_W(d) be the Wijsman topology on 2^X; the Wijsman hyperspace of (X, d) is (2^X, T_W(d)). A space is strongly alpha-favorable when player alpha has a winning tactic in the strong Choquet game, and strongly Choquet when alpha has a winning strategy in that game. If X is completely metrizable, then for every metric d compatible with the topology of X, must the Wijsman hyperspace (2^X, T_W(d)) be strongly Choquet or strongly alpha-favorable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space. Denote by $2^X$ the family of all non-empty closed subsets of $X$. The Wijsman topology $\mathcal{T}_{W(d)}$ on $2^X$ is the weakest topology that makes, for every $A\in 2^X$, the distance functional $D_A: 2^X \to \mathbb{R}$, $D_A(B) = \inf\{d(b,a): a\in A\}$ (i.e. $d(\cdot,A)$ evaluated at points, lifted appropriately) continuous; equivalently $\mathcal{T}_{W(d)}$ is generated by the maps $B\mapsto d(x,B)$ for $x\in X$. Call $(2^X,\mathcal{T}_{W(d)})$ the Wijsman hyperspace of $(X,d)$.

The strong Choquet game $\mathrm{Ch}(Y)$ on a topological space $Y$ is played by two players $\alpha$ and $\beta$ in $\omega$ rounds. In round $n$, $\beta$ chooses a pair $(x_n, V_n)$ where $V_n$ is a non-empty open set in $Y$ and $x_n\in V_n$, with $V_n\subseteq U_{n-1}$ (where $U_{-1}=Y$); then $\alpha$ chooses an open set $U_n$ with $x_n\in U_n\subseteq V_n$. Player $\alpha$ wins the play if $\bigcap_{n<\omega} U_n \neq \emptyset$. original_question: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with constant density, kinematic viscosity ν > 0, divergence-free velocity field u(x,t), pressure p(x,t), no external energy input, and the usual whole-space, periodic, or no-slip bounded-domain settings, what are the most general smooth initial velocities u(x,0) that guarantee the solution exists for every positive time and remains smooth?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations for a fluid of constant density and kinematic viscosity ν > 0:

  ∂_t u + (u · ∇)u − ν Δu + ∇p = 0,   ∇ · u = 0,

where u(x,t) ∈ ℝ³ is the velocity field and p(x,t) ∈ ℝ is the pressure, posed on one of the following standard spatial domains: the whole space ℝ³ (with appropriate decay at infinity), the three-dimensional torus 𝕋³ (periodic boundary conditions), or a bounded smooth domain Ω ⊂ ℝ³ with the no-slip boundary condition u|_{∂Ω} = 0. There is no external forcing.

A smooth initial velocity is a divergence-free vector field u₀ : domain → ℝ³ belonging to C^∞ (with appropriate decay or boundary compatibility).

Determine the most general class of such smooth divergence-free initial data u(x,0) = u₀(x) for which the corresponding solution (u,p) exists globally in time (for all t > 0) and remains smooth (i.e., u(·,t) ∈ C^∞ for every t > 0).

Equivalently, characterize sharp sufficient conditions on u₀ that guarantee global-in-time smoothness of the resulting Leray solution and rule out any finite-time singularity.
status_search_result: The global regularity of 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes from general smooth initial data is one of the Clay Millennium Prize Problems and remains open. Only partial results exist (small data, axisymmetric without swirl, various conditional/regularity criteria such as Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin and Beale–Kato–Majda, and Koch–Tataru small-BMO⁻¹ data), but no general characterization is known.
