context_brief: equivalence of code families for equal-order reciprocal-style trinomials
original_question: Let t1(x) = x^n - a x^i - b and t2(x) = x^n - a' x^(n-i) - b' be trinomials over a finite field F_q with the same order, meaning Ord(t1(x)) = Ord(t2(x)). If C1 is the family of all length-n polycyclic codes over F_q associated with t1(x), and C2 is the family of all length-n polycyclic codes over F_q associated with t2(x), is there always a one-to-one correspondence between C1 and C2 such that each code in one family corresponds to an equivalent code in the other family?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, and fix integers $n \geq 2$ and $1 \leq i \leq n-1$. For a monic polynomial $f(x) \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ of degree $n$, a polycyclic code of length $n$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ associated with $f(x)$ is, by definition, an ideal of the quotient ring $\mathbb{F}_q[x]/\langle f(x)\rangle$, viewed as an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ via the natural identification $(c_0,c_1,\dots,c_{n-1}) \leftrightarrow c_0 + c_1 x + \cdots + c_{n-1} x^{n-1}$. Two linear codes $C, C' \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ are called equivalent if there exists a monomial transformation (a permutation of coordinates composed with multiplication of each coordinate by a nonzero scalar) that maps $C$ onto $C'$. For a polynomial $f(x) \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ with $f(0) \neq 0$, the order $\operatorname{Ord}(f(x))$ is the least positive integer $e$ such that $f(x) \mid x^e - 1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q[x]$.

Consider two trinomials
$$t_1(x) = x^n - a x^i - b, \qquad t_2(x) = x^n - a' x^{\,n-i} - b'$$
in $\mathbb{F}_q[x]$, with $a,b,a',b' \in \mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and assume $\operatorname{Ord}(t_1(x)) = \operatorname{Ord}(t_2(x))$. Let $\mathcal{C}_1$ denote the set of all polycyclic codes of length $n$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ associated with $t_1(x)$, and let $\mathcal{C}_2$ denote the analogous set for $t_2(x)$.

Prove or disprove: there always exists a bijection $\Phi : \mathcal{C}_1 \to \mathcal{C}_2$ such that for every $C \in \mathcal{C}_1$, the code $\Phi(C)$ is equivalent to $C$.
status_search_result: The question is stated as a conjecture in work on polycyclic codes associated with trinomials. Follow-up literature on skew polycyclic codes (e.g., a 2025 preprint on bounds and equivalence of skew polycyclic codes) discusses equivalence of trinomial-defined ambient spaces but does not appear to resolve this specific conjecture in the commutative setting. No published proof or counterexample was located, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Over the binary field F_2, let C be a polycyclic code associated with the trinomial x^n - a x^i - b and generated by a divisor g(x) of that trinomial. Is C iso-dual if and only if g(x)^2 = x^n - a x^i - b?
self_contained_problem:
Work over the binary field $\mathbb{F}_2$. Fix integers $n\ge 2$ and $0<i<n$, and elements $a,b\in\mathbb{F}_2$ with $b\ne 0$, so that $f(x)=x^n-ax^i-b\in\mathbb{F}_2[x]$ is a trinomial. For a monic divisor $g(x)\mid f(x)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x]$ of degree $k$, the polycyclic code $C$ associated with $f$ and generated by $g$ is
$$C=\{g(x)\,h(x)\bmod f(x):h(x)\in\mathbb{F}_2[x]/(f(x))\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n,$$
identifying polynomials of degree $<n$ with their coefficient vectors. The Euclidean dual $C^\perp$ is taken with respect to the standard inner product on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The code $C$ is called iso-dual if $C$ is monomially (equivalently, permutation, over $\mathbb{F}_2$) equivalent to $C^\perp$.

Prove or disprove: $C$ is iso-dual if and only if $g(x)^2=x^n-ax^i-b$.
status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture in the work introducing polycyclic codes from trinomials, published in Designs, Codes and Cryptography (2022). Subsequent literature on polycyclic codes (duality, isodual constructions from polycirculant matrices, skew polycyclic codes, and polycyclic codes over finite chain rings) discusses the framework but does not appear to settle this specific binary characterization, so it remains open.

original_question: Is a polycyclic code over a finite field F_q self-dual exactly in the following situation: its generator polynomial has the form g(x) = x^m - a, it divides a trinomial x^(2m) - b x^m - c, and the scalar a satisfies a^2 = q - 1? In addition, if such a self-dual polycyclic code exists, must its minimum distance always be 2, and must every self-dual polycyclic code of this kind in fact be constacyclic rather than genuinely more general polycyclic?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements. For a monic polynomial $f(x)\in\mathbb{F}_q[x]$ of degree $n$, a polycyclic code associated with $f$ is an ideal of the quotient ring $\mathbb{F}_q[x]/\langle f(x)\rangle$; equivalently, it is a linear subspace $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ that is closed under the linear shift induced by multiplication by $x$ modulo $f(x)$. Such a code $C$ is generated, as an ideal, by a monic divisor $g(x)$ of $f(x)$, called the generator polynomial of $C$. The code $C$ is called constacyclic if it is polycyclic with respect to a binomial $f(x)=x^n-\lambda$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_q^*$. The dual code $C^\perp$ is defined with respect to the standard Euclidean inner product on $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, and $C$ is self-dual if $C=C^\perp$.

Determine whether the following statement is true: a polycyclic code $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is self-dual if and only if there exist a positive integer $m$, elements $a,b,c\in\mathbb{F}_q$, and a trinomial $f(x)=x^{2m}-bx^m-c$ such that $C$ is the polycyclic code associated with $f$ having generator polynomial $g(x)=x^m-a$, with $g(x)\mid f(x)$ and $a^2=-1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$. Moreover, decide whether every such self-dual polycyclic code necessarily has minimum Hamming distance equal to $2$ and is in fact a constacyclic code (rather than a strictly more general polycyclic code).
status_search_result: A follow-up work "On the duality and the direction of polycyclic codes" by Alahmadi et al. discusses duality and corrections to results on polycyclic codes, but the search did not produce conclusive evidence that this specific conjecture (characterizing self-dual polycyclic codes via the divisor $x^m-a$ of a trinomial with $a^2=-1$, minimum distance 2, and constacyclicity) has been proven or disproven. Status remains unverified from available sources.

original_question: Let C be a polycyclic code whose generator polynomial g(x) divides a trinomial x^n - a x^i - b over a finite field, with n prime. Is it always true that C cannot be dual-containing?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and let $n$ be a prime number. Consider a trinomial of the form
$$f(x) = x^n - a x^i - b \in \mathbb{F}_q[x],$$
where $a, b \in \mathbb{F}_q$ and $1 \le i \le n-1$. Let $g(x) \in \mathbb{F}_q[x]$ be a monic divisor of $f(x)$, and let $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be the polycyclic code of length $n$ associated with $f(x)$ whose generator polynomial is $g(x)$; that is, $C$ is the image of the ideal $(g(x))/(f(x))$ in $\mathbb{F}_q[x]/(f(x))$ under the coordinate identification with $\mathbb{F}_q^n$. Let
$$C^{\perp} = \{ u \in \mathbb{F}_q^n : \langle u, c\rangle = 0 \text{ for all } c \in C\}$$
denote the Euclidean dual of $C$ with respect to the standard inner product. Prove or disprove: under the above hypotheses (in particular, $n$ prime), the code $C$ is never dual-containing, i.e. $C^{\perp} \not\subseteq C$ unless $C$ is trivial in the excluded sense.
status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture in the work introducing polycyclic codes associated to trinomials. Follow-up works (e.g., subsequent arXiv papers extending the theory to chain rings and studying duality of polycyclic codes) continue to investigate trinomial-based polycyclic codes but do not appear to resolve this specific conjecture. No explicit proof or counterexample is found in the literature.

original_question: Can one construct the moduli space Delta_G for a characteristic-zero local field such as Q_p?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For a perfect field $k$ of positive characteristic (with $|G|$ allowed to be divisible by $\operatorname{char} k$), one can form a moduli space (more precisely, a formal stack or ind-scheme) $\Delta_G$ over $k$ whose $B$-points, for a $k$-algebra $B$, parametrize $G$-torsors over $\operatorname{Spec} B(\!(t)\!)$ (equivalently, continuous homomorphisms from the absolute Galois group of $B(\!(t)\!)$ to $G$, up to conjugation). This moduli space plays a central role in the wild McKay correspondence, where motivic integrals over $\Delta_G$ compute stringy invariants of quotient varieties $V/G$.
 
Problem: Construct an analogous moduli space $\Delta_G$ associated to a local field of characteristic zero, such as $\mathbb{Q}_p$, that parametrizes $G$-torsors over (families of) such local fields and that is suitable for developing a motivic integration theory and a wild McKay correspondence in mixed characteristic. Specifically, define a geometric object $\Delta_G$ over an appropriate base (e.g.\ $\operatorname{Spf} \mathbb{Z}_p$ or $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{F}_p$) whose points classify $G$-torsors over $p$-adic local fields, establish its basic geometric properties (such as a stratification by ramification data, dimension, and a measure), and show that integration on $\Delta_G$ recovers the expected invariants of quotients in mixed characteristic.
category_tag: Moduli of G-torsors and wild McKay correspondence
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a collection of open problems on the wild McKay correspondence (T. Yasuda). The construction of $\Delta_G$ exists for equal-characteristic local fields (via the "moduli of formal torsors" framework), but no construction over mixed-characteristic local fields such as $\mathbb{Q}_p$ appears in the literature; recent related work on $G$-torsors over perfectoid/adic spaces over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ does not provide such a moduli object suitable for motivic integration. No resolution was located.

original_question: Can motivic integration for Deligne-Mumford stacks be developed over a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic and applied to the McKay correspondence?
self_contained_problem:
Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (for example, the ring of $p$-adic integers $\mathbb{Z}_p$), with residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and fraction field $K$ of characteristic $0$. Existing theories of motivic integration provide, for a formal scheme $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite type over $R$, a measure on the arc space (or Greenberg space) of $\mathfrak{X}$ valued in a suitable Grothendieck ring of varieties, generalizing Kontsevich's motivic integration and Sebag's extension to formal schemes. Parallel work has developed motivic integration over (possibly wild) Deligne–Mumford stacks $\mathcal{X}$ in the equal-characteristic setting, i.e., over power series rings $k[[t]]$, and used it to establish motivic forms of the McKay correspondence, including for wild quotient singularities.

Problem: Develop a theory of motivic integration for Deligne–Mumford stacks $\mathcal{X}$ that are of finite type (or formal of finite type) over a complete discrete valuation ring $R$ of mixed characteristic, including:

(a) a well-defined notion of twisted arcs / jets of $\mathcal{X}$ over $R$ and an appropriate Greenberg-type space carrying a measure with values in a localized Grothendieck ring of varieties over the residue field $k$;
(b) a change-of-variables formula along proper birational (and in particular crepant) morphisms between such stacks; and
(c) using this theory, prove a motivic McKay correspondence over $R$: for a finite group $G$ acting linearly on $\mathbb{A}^n_R$ with quotient $X = \mathbb{A}^n_R/G$ and any crepant resolution (or stacky resolution) $Y \to X$, establish an equality of stringy/motivic invariants of $Y$ with a suitable orbifold/twisted-arc motivic integral on the quotient stack $[\mathbb{A}^n_R/G]$, recovering in mixed characteristic the wild McKay correspondence known in equal characteristic.
status_search_result: Motivic integration over Deligne–Mumford stacks has been developed in equal characteristic (over power series rings $k[[t]]$), including the wild case, leading to a wild motivic McKay correspondence. While Sebag's motivic integration for formal schemes covers mixed characteristic, no published extension to Deligne–Mumford stacks over a complete DVR of mixed characteristic, together with a McKay correspondence application, appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Can the McKay correspondence be generalized at the level of derived categories to the wild case?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and let $G \subset \mathrm{GL}(V)$ be a finite subgroup whose order is divisible by $p$ (the "wild" case). Let $X = V/G$ denote the quotient variety, and let $Y \to X$ be a crepant resolution of singularities (when one exists). In characteristic zero (the tame case), the classical derived McKay correspondence asserts an equivalence of triangulated categories
$$ D^b(\mathrm{Coh}\, Y) \;\simeq\; D^b(\mathrm{Coh}^G V) $$
between the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $Y$ and the bounded derived category of $G$-equivariant coherent sheaves on $V$ (as established for finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_n$ with $n\le 3$ via the Hilbert scheme of $G$-clusters).

Problem: Formulate and prove an analogue of this derived equivalence in the wild case. Note that the naive statement above cannot hold as written, because in the wild case the category $\mathrm{Coh}^G V$ has infinite global dimension. The task is to identify the correct categorical replacement (for one or both sides) and establish a derived-categorical McKay correspondence valid when $p \mid |G|$.
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in surveys on the wild McKay correspondence. The known obstruction is that the equivariant category $\mathrm{Coh}^G V$ has infinite global dimension when $p \mid |G|$, so the classical Bridgeland–King–Reid/Kapranov–Vasserot equivalence cannot hold verbatim, and an alternative formulation is required. Existing wild McKay correspondences (e.g., via stringy invariants and p-adic measures) operate at the level of invariants, not derived categories, and no derived-category version is known.

original_question: Can one prove special cases of one of the two conjectures discussed in Section 13 from known cases of the other conjecture?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $k$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_k$.

(A) Malle's conjecture. For a finite transitive subgroup $G\subset S_n$, let
$$N_k(G;X)=\#\{K/k\ \text{(in a fixed algebraic closure)}: [K:k]=n,\ \operatorname{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{gal}}/k)\simeq G\ \text{as permutation group},\ |\operatorname{Disc}(K/k)|\le X\}.$$
Malle's conjecture predicts the existence of explicit constants $a(G)\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ and $b(k,G)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ and a positive constant $c(k,G)$ such that
$$N_k(G;X)\sim c(k,G)\,X^{a(G)}(\log X)^{b(k,G)-1}\qquad (X\to\infty),$$
where $a(G)=1/\min_{g\in G\setminus\{1\}}\operatorname{ind}(g)$ with $\operatorname{ind}(g)=n-\#\{\text{orbits of }\langle g\rangle\text{ on }\{1,\dots,n\}\}$.

(B) Batyrev–Manin conjecture (stacky form). Let $\mathcal{X}=[V/G]$ be a smooth Deligne–Mumford quotient stack over $k$ with $V$ a faithful $G$-representation, equipped with an anticanonical-type height $H\colon \mathcal{X}(k)\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ coming from the "raised line bundle" associated to the canonical sheaf. Let $U\subset\mathcal{X}$ be a suitable open substack. The Batyrev–Manin–Peyre conjecture predicts
$$\#\{x\in U(k): H(x)\le X\}\sim c_{\mathrm{Peyre}}(\mathcal{X})\,X^{\alpha(\mathcal{X})}(\log X)^{\beta(\mathcal{X})-1}\qquad (X\to\infty),$$
for explicit exponents $\alpha(\mathcal{X}),\beta(\mathcal{X})$ defined in terms of the anticanonical class and Picard group of $\mathcal{X}$, together with an explicit Peyre-type leading constant.

Conjectural relation. The two predictions are expected to coincide when $\mathcal{X}=[\mathbb{A}^n_k/G]$ with the regular permutation representation, in the sense that $k$-points of $[\mathbb{A}^n_k/G]$ counted by the canonical height correspond to $G$-extensions $K/k$ counted by absolute discriminant, and the exponents and constants on the two sides match.

Problem. Identify a nontrivial special case (a specific group $G$ and base $k$, or a specific family of stacks $\mathcal{X}$) for which one of conjectures (A) and (B) is already established, and derive from that case a previously unknown special case of the other conjecture. Equivalently: produce a rigorous implication "(A) for $(k,G)$" $\Rightarrow$ "(B) for $[\mathbb{A}^n_k/G]$", or vice versa, and verify it on at least one example beyond what is known directly.
status_search_result: The problem of bridging Malle's conjecture and the (stacky) Batyrev–Manin–Peyre conjecture via the wild McKay correspondence is the subject of ongoing research. Follow-up work (e.g., Darda–Yasuda, "The Batyrev–Manin conjecture for DM stacks," 2022, and Part II, 2025) develops the stacky framework but does not establish the requested implication in general; no source claims to have proved a special case of one conjecture by using a known case of the other along these lines. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis
context_brief: Compact intervals versus bicontinuity in posets
original_question: Let (A, ≺) be a partially ordered set equipped with its interval topology. Suppose every closed interval [a,b] = {x : a ⪯ x ⪯ b} is compact in that topology. Must (A, ≺) then be bicontinuous in the domain-theoretic sense, meaning that the way-below relation is characterized both by directed suprema and dually by filtered infima, with each upper set ↑x filtered and having infimum x? More broadly, is there an order-theoretic analogue of the spacetime result that compact causal diamonds imply causality in non-compact spacetimes of dimension greater than 2, and if so what should play the role of the dimensional hypothesis for posets, or does no such restriction arise in the purely order-theoretic setting?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(A,\preceq)$ be a partially ordered set. For $a,b\in A$, write $[a,b]=\{x\in A:a\preceq x\preceq b\}$. Equip $A$ with the interval topology, i.e.\ the topology generated by the subbasis of sets of the form $\{x: x\not\preceq a\}$ and $\{x: a\not\preceq x\}$ for $a\in A$ (equivalently, having as a subbasis of closed sets the principal up-sets ${\uparrow}a=\{x:a\preceq x\}$ and the principal down-sets ${\downarrow}a=\{x:x\preceq a\}$).

Recall the way-below relation $\ll$ on a poset: $x\ll y$ iff for every directed set $D\subseteq A$ with a supremum $\sup D$, the inequality $y\preceq \sup D$ implies $x\preceq d$ for some $d\in D$. Dually, $x\ll^{op} y$ iff for every filtered set $F\subseteq A$ with an infimum $\inf F$, $\inf F\preceq x$ implies $f\preceq y$ for some $f\in F$. The poset $(A,\preceq)$ is called bicontinuous if:

(i) for every $x\in A$, the set ${\downarrow\!\!\ll}\,x=\{a:a\ll x\}$ is directed with supremum $x$;
(ii) for every $x\in A$, the set ${\uparrow\!\!\ll}\,x=\{a:x\ll a\}$ is filtered with infimum $x$;
(iii) $a\ll b$ if and only if $a\ll^{op} b$.

Question: Suppose that every closed interval $[a,b]$ is compact in the interval topology of $(A,\preceq)$. Must $(A,\preceq)$ be bicontinuous in the above sense? 

If additionally an order-theoretic analogue is required of the result that, for spacetimes of dimension strictly greater than $2$, compactness of all causal diamonds implies (strong) causality, identify what (if any) hypothesis on $(A,\preceq)$ should replace the dimension condition; in particular, does the implication "compact intervals $\Rightarrow$ bicontinuity" hold for all posets without any such restriction?
status_search_result: A search did not surface a published resolution of this specific implication "compact intervals in the interval topology $\Rightarrow$ bicontinuity" for arbitrary posets, nor an order-theoretic analogue of the dimension-$>2$ hypothesis used in the spacetime setting. The Martin–Panangaden framework establishes the converse direction (bicontinuity plus compact intervals characterizes globally hyperbolic posets, equivalent to interval domains), but the question of whether compactness of intervals alone forces bicontinuity appears to remain open.

paper_title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis
context_brief: Recovering spacetime topology from interval domains
original_question: Can the topology of a spacetime be reconstructed in a rigorous technical way from the topology of an interval domain, as suggested by the equivalence between globally hyperbolic posets and interval domains? Relatedly, does the fact that candidate causal spacetime topologies such as the Zeeman fine topology, Göbel’s generalization, and the Hawking-King-McCarthy topology are non-metrizable reveal what kind of non-manifold topology should be regarded as the right topology for spacetime when the underlying model is order-theoretic?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A partially ordered set $(P,\le)$ is called bicontinuous if there is a way-below relation $\ll$ on $P$ such that for every $x\in P$ the sets $\{y:y\ll x\}$ and $\{y:x\ll y\}$ are directed/filtered with suprema/infima equal to $x$, and $a\ll b$ iff for every directed (resp. filtered) set with supremum (resp. infimum) $b$ (resp. $a$) the element $a$ (resp. $b$) is eventually below (resp. above) some member. The interval topology on $P$ is generated by the subbasis $\{y:a\ll y\}\cup\{y:y\ll b\}$ for $a,b\in P$. An interval domain is a continuous dcpo whose elements are pairs $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$ in some bicontinuous poset, ordered by reverse inclusion.

A globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ is a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold whose causal relation $\le$ makes $(M,\le)$ a bicontinuous poset for which the interval topology coincides with the manifold topology, and the category of such spacetimes (with suitable order-preserving maps) is equivalent to a category of interval domains.

Several candidate "causal" topologies on a spacetime $M$ have been proposed in place of the manifold topology, including:
(i) the Zeeman fine topology, the finest topology on Minkowski space inducing the Euclidean topology on every timelike line and every spacelike hyperplane;
(ii) Göbel's generalization of the Zeeman topology to arbitrary Lorentzian manifolds;
(iii) the Hawking–King–McCarthy path topology, the finest topology on $M$ inducing the manifold topology on every timelike curve.
Each of these topologies is non-metrizable.

Problem. 
(a) Given only the interval domain $\mathbf{I} M$ associated to a globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ (viewed as an abstract topological/order-theoretic object), give a rigorous procedure to reconstruct a topology on the underlying point set $M$ (identified with the maximal elements of $\mathbf{I} M$) and identify it with a naturally defined spacetime topology.
(b) Using the order-theoretic nature of interval domains, determine which non-manifold, non-metrizable topology on $M$ (such as the Zeeman, Göbel, or Hawking–King–McCarthy topology, or another order-theoretically defined topology) is canonically singled out by this reconstruction, and explain in what sense it is the "right" topology for spacetime in the order-theoretic framework.
category_tag: Causal structure and domain theory of spacetimes
status_search_result: Martin and Panangaden (Comm. Math. Phys., 2006) showed that a globally hyperbolic spacetime can be order-theoretically reconstructed as a bicontinuous poset whose interval topology equals the manifold topology, and that the category of globally hyperbolic posets is equivalent to a category of interval domains. This addresses part (a) by yielding the manifold topology from the interval domain. However, whether order-theoretic considerations single out a specific non-metrizable causal topology (such as Zeeman, Göbel, or Hawking–King–McCarthy) as the canonical "right" spacetime topology in this framework does not appear to be resolved in the literature; no definitive resolution was found.

paper_title: Open Problem: Is There an Online Learning Algorithm That Learns Whenever Online Learning Is Possible?
original_question: Consider realizable binary online learning over a nonempty instance space X with measurable target concepts f*: X → {0,1}. At each time t, after observing the past labeled examples (X_s, f*(X_s)) for s < t and the current instance X_t, an online learning algorithm predicts a label in {0,1}; its mistakes are the times when the prediction differs from f*(X_t). For a possibly random instance sequence X independent of the learner's internal randomness, weak universal consistency under X means that, for every measurable f*, the expected number of mistakes through time T is o(T), while strong universal consistency under X means that, for every measurable f*, the number of mistakes through time T is o(T) almost surely. Universal online learning is possible under X if some online learning algorithm has the corresponding universal consistency property under X. Does there exist a single optimistically universal online learning algorithm, meaning a single algorithm that is weakly, respectively strongly, universally consistent under every instance sequence X for which weak, respectively strong, universal online learning is possible under X?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a nonempty instance space equipped with a sigma-algebra. A target concept is a measurable function f*: X → {0,1}. An online learning algorithm is a sequence of (possibly randomized) measurable functions f_t: X^{t-1} × {0,1}^{t-1} × X → {0,1}, t ∈ ℕ, whose internal randomization is independent of any data sequence considered. Given a (possibly random) instance sequence X = (X_t)_{t∈ℕ} taking values in X and independent of the algorithm's internal randomness, and a target concept f*, the algorithm's prediction at time t is Ŷ_t = f_t(X_{1:(t-1)}, f*(X_{1:(t-1)}), X_t), and a mistake occurs at time t when Ŷ_t ≠ f*(X_t).

Say that the algorithm is weakly universally consistent under X if, for every measurable f*: X → {0,1},
  E[∑_{t=1}^T 1{Ŷ_t ≠ f*(X_t)}] = o(T) as T → ∞,
and strongly universally consistent under X if, for every measurable f*: X → {0,1},
  ∑_{t=1}^T 1{Ŷ_t ≠ f*(X_t)} = o(T) almost surely as T → ∞.

Say that weak (respectively strong) universal online learning is possible under X if some online learning algorithm is weakly (respectively strongly) universally consistent under X. An online learning algorithm is called optimistically weakly (respectively strongly) universal if it is weakly (respectively strongly) universally consistent under every instance sequence X for which weak (respectively strong) universal online learning is possible.

Question: Does there exist an optimistically weakly universal online learning algorithm? Does there exist an optimistically strongly universal online learning algorithm?
status_search_result: The open problem was resolved by Blanchard (2022), "Universal Online Learning: an Optimistically Universal Learning Rule" (COLT 2022 / arXiv:2201.05947), which constructs a variant of the 1-nearest-neighbor rule that is optimistically universal in both the weak and strong senses for realizable binary online learning, thereby closing the COLT 2021 open problem.

paper_title: Open Problem: Is There an Online Learning Algorithm That Learns Whenever Online Learning Is Possible?
context_brief: Strong universal online learning characterization by C_s
original_question: In realizable binary online learning with arbitrary measurable target concepts f*: X → {0,1}, say that strong universal online learning is possible under a possibly random instance sequence X if some online learning algorithm has total mistakes o(T) through time T almost surely for every measurable f*. Let C_s be the family of all possibly random sequences X = {X_t}_{t∈N} such that every disjoint sequence {A_i}_{i∈N} of measurable sets satisfies |{i ∈ N : {X_1,...,X_T} intersects A_i}| = o(T) almost surely. Is C_s exactly equal to the set of all instance sequences X such that strong universal online learning is possible under X?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a measurable space, and consider realizable binary online learning with arbitrary measurable target concepts $f^*: \mathcal{X} \to \{0,1\}$. A (possibly random) instance sequence is a stochastic process $\mathbf{X} = \{X_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ taking values in $\mathcal{X}$. An online learning algorithm is a sequence of (possibly randomized, independent of $\mathbf{X}$) measurable maps $f_t: \mathcal{X}^{t-1} \times \{0,1\}^{t-1} \times \mathcal{X} \to \{0,1\}$. The algorithm is said to be strongly universally consistent under $\mathbf{X}$ if, for every measurable $f^*: \mathcal{X} \to \{0,1\}$,
$$\sum_{t=1}^{T} \mathbf{1}\big[f_t(X_{1:t-1}, f^*(X_{1:t-1}), X_t) \neq f^*(X_t)\big] = o(T) \quad \text{almost surely.}$$
Strong universal online learning is said to be possible under $\mathbf{X}$ if some online learning algorithm is strongly universally consistent under $\mathbf{X}$.

Define $\mathcal{C}_s$ to be the family of all (possibly random) sequences $\mathbf{X} = \{X_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that, for every disjoint sequence $\{A_i\}_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of measurable subsets of $\mathcal{X}$,
$$\big|\{i \in \mathbb{N} : \{X_1, \dots, X_T\} \cap A_i \neq \emptyset\}\big| = o(T) \quad \text{almost surely.}$$

Question. Is $\mathcal{C}_s$ exactly equal to the set of all (possibly random) instance sequences $\mathbf{X}$ such that strong universal online learning is possible under $\mathbf{X}$?
status_search_result: Subsequent work by Blanchard (and collaborators) — in particular "Universal Online Learning: an Optimistically Universal Learning Rule" (2022) — gives a complete characterization of the processes admitting strong (and weak) universal online learning, and is described as closing all COLT 2021 open problems by Hanneke on universal online learning. The characterizing condition (called SMV / $C_2$) coincides with the proposed family $\mathcal{C}_s$, so $\mathcal{C}_s$ is indeed the exact set of $\mathbf{X}$ admitting strong universal online learning.

paper_title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis
context_brief: Non-stationary case: global hyperbolicity versus self-adjointness
original_question: For a general non-stationary globally hyperbolic spacetime with metric of the form g = -N^2(t, x) dt^2 + g_{Σ,ij}(t, x) dxi dxj, what precise connection, if any, holds between global hyperbolicity of the Lorentzian manifold and essential self-adjointness of the spatial Laplacian appearing in the Klein–Gordon equation? Equivalently, beyond the static, warped-product, and uniformly bounded sliced-space cases discussed in the paper, when does global hyperbolicity force geodesic completeness of the conformally transformed spatial slices (Σ_t, g̃_{Σ_t}), which is the ingredient used to prove essential self-adjointness?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian manifold of dimension $n+1$ that admits a global smooth splitting $M \cong \mathbb{R} \times \Sigma$ with metric of the form
$$ g = -N^2(t,x)\, dt^2 + g_{\Sigma,ij}(t,x)\, dx^i dx^j, $$
where $N \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}\times\Sigma, (0,\infty))$ is the lapse function and, for each $t \in \mathbb{R}$, $g_{\Sigma_t} := g_{\Sigma}(t,\cdot)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on the spacelike slice $\Sigma_t := \{t\}\times\Sigma$. Assume that $(M,g)$ is globally hyperbolic, with the slices $\Sigma_t$ being smooth Cauchy hypersurfaces.

For each $t$, define the conformally rescaled spatial metric
$$ \tilde g_{\Sigma_t} := N^{-2}(t,\cdot)\, g_{\Sigma_t}, $$
and let $\tilde \Delta_t$ denote the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator of $(\Sigma_t, \tilde g_{\Sigma_t})$, viewed as a symmetric operator on $C_c^\infty(\Sigma_t) \subset L^2(\Sigma_t, d\mathrm{vol}_{\tilde g_{\Sigma_t}})$.

It is known that:
(a) if each Riemannian manifold $(\Sigma_t, \tilde g_{\Sigma_t})$ is geodesically complete, then $\tilde\Delta_t$ is essentially self-adjoint on $C_c^\infty(\Sigma_t)$;
(b) in the special cases of static spacetimes, standard warped products $g = -N^2(t)\,dt^2 + a(t)^2 h(x)$, and spacetimes with uniformly bounded lapse and uniformly equivalent slice metrics, global hyperbolicity of $(M,g)$ is equivalent to geodesic completeness of all $(\Sigma_t, \tilde g_{\Sigma_t})$.

Problem. Determine the precise relationship between global hyperbolicity of $(M,g)$ and essential self-adjointness of the family $\{\tilde\Delta_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ on $C_c^\infty(\Sigma_t)$ for a general non-stationary metric of the form above. Equivalently, identify sharp geometric conditions on $(N, g_\Sigma)$, going beyond the three special classes (a)–(b), under which global hyperbolicity of $(M,g)$ implies geodesic completeness of $(\Sigma_t, \tilde g_{\Sigma_t})$ for every $t \in \mathbb{R}$, and conversely under which such completeness (for all $t$) implies global hyperbolicity. Either establish such an equivalence under explicit, verifiable hypotheses or construct counterexamples showing that no such implication can hold in full generality.
status_search_result: A targeted search did not reveal a definitive resolution of the general non-stationary relationship between global hyperbolicity of a Lorentzian spacetime in lapse–slicing form and essential self-adjointness of the spatial (conformally rescaled) Laplacian on Cauchy slices. Known results cover static spacetimes, warped products, and bounded-lapse settings, while the general case appears to remain unresolved in the literature.

original_question: For functions on a finite interval, can one characterize all one-parameter families of fractional derivatives that are associated with the Riemann-Liouville fractional integrals through the first fundamental theorem of fractional calculus, meaning that each derivative family acts as a left inverse of the corresponding Riemann-Liouville fractional integral on the relevant function space?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha\ge 0$ and let $I^\alpha$ denote the Riemann–Liouville fractional integral on the finite interval $[0,1]$, defined for $\alpha>0$ by
$$(I^\alpha \varphi)(x)=\frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)}\int_0^x (x-t)^{\alpha-1}\varphi(t)\,dt,\qquad x\in[0,1],$$
and $I^0=\mathrm{Id}$. A one-parameter family $\{D^\alpha\}_{\alpha\ge 0}$ of linear operators, each acting on a suitable nontrivial space of functions on $[0,1]$, is called a family of fractional derivatives associated with the Riemann–Liouville fractional integrals through the first fundamental theorem of fractional calculus if for every $\alpha\ge 0$ the operator $D^\alpha$ is a left inverse of $I^\alpha$, i.e.
$$(D^\alpha I^\alpha \varphi)(x)=\varphi(x),\qquad x\in[0,1],$$
on the chosen function space.

Known examples of such families include the Riemann–Liouville fractional derivatives, the Caputo fractional derivatives, the Hilfer fractional derivatives, and the so-called $n$th level fractional derivatives.

Problem: Provide a complete characterization (classification) of all one-parameter families $\{D^\alpha\}_{\alpha\ge 0}$ of fractional derivatives on $[0,1]$ that are associated with the Riemann–Liouville fractional integrals through the first fundamental theorem of fractional calculus in the sense above.
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g. work by Luchko and follow-ups through 2023–2024) introduces broader generic fractional derivatives left-inverse to the Riemann–Liouville integral and shows infinitely many such families exist beyond Riemann–Liouville, Caputo, Hilfer, and the nth-level derivatives, but a complete classification remains unresolved; related sub-questions (e.g., existence of such derivatives with infinite-dimensional null space, or with finite-dimensional null spaces different from the nth level derivatives) are explicitly listed as open problems.

original_question: Can the finite-interval analytical characterization problems for fractional integrals and derivatives be extended from bounded intervals to functions defined on the positive real semi-axis and on the whole real line, while preserving the same notions of admissible fractional integrals, associated fractional derivatives, and desiderata-based operator structure?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A fractional integration operator on an interval $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a one-parameter family $\{I^\alpha\}_{\alpha>0}$ of linear operators acting on a suitable space of functions $f: I \to \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies the following desiderata:

(D1) Interpolation: $I^1 f(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt$ for the natural left endpoint $a$ of $I$ (with $a=0$ when $I = [0,\infty)$ and $a=-\infty$ when $I = \mathbb{R}$).
(D2) Semigroup (index) law: $I^\alpha I^\beta = I^{\alpha+\beta}$ for all $\alpha,\beta > 0$.
(D3) Continuity: $\alpha \mapsto I^\alpha f$ is continuous in an appropriate topology, with $I^\alpha f \to f$ as $\alpha \downarrow 0$.
(D4) Linearity and a suitable form of locality/causality compatible with $I$.

An associated fractional derivative of order $\alpha \in (0,1)$ is an operator $D^\alpha$ that is a left inverse of $I^\alpha$ on an appropriate domain, satisfies $D^\alpha I^\alpha f = f$ and reduces to ordinary differentiation in the limit $\alpha \uparrow 1$.

For $I = [a,b]$ a bounded interval, an analytical characterization is known: under the desiderata (D1)–(D4), the admissible fractional integrals coincide (up to a normalization) with the Riemann–Liouville integrals
$$I^\alpha f(x) = \frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)} \int_a^x (x-t)^{\alpha-1} f(t)\,dt,$$
with corresponding fractional derivatives of Riemann–Liouville (or Caputo) type.

Problem. Determine whether the analogous characterization extends to the unbounded settings:

(a) On the positive real semi-axis $I = [0,\infty)$: characterize all one-parameter families $\{I^\alpha\}_{\alpha>0}$ of operators acting on a natural function space on $[0,\infty)$ (e.g., $L^p([0,\infty))$, $C_0([0,\infty))$, or a weighted variant) that satisfy the desiderata (D1)–(D4), and identify the associated fractional derivatives.

(b) On the whole real line $I = \mathbb{R}$: characterize all one-parameter families $\{I^\alpha\}_{\alpha>0}$ on a natural function space on $\mathbb{R}$ satisfying (D1)–(D4) (with the convention that $I^1 f(x) = \int_{-\infty}^x f(t)\,dt$ on functions decaying at $-\infty$), and identify the associated fractional derivatives.

In each case, prove that the family must coincide with the appropriate Liouville-type fractional integral, or exhibit other admissible families.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open extension of a finite-interval axiomatic characterization of fractional integrals/derivatives to the half-line and full real line. No definitive published resolution of this specific axiomatic extension was located; the status appears unresolved in the literature consulted.

original_question: Given a function kappa in C^-1(0,+infinity), what conditions are necessary and sufficient for kappa to belong to the class L1 of Sonine-kernel pairs, and how can one derive an explicit representation of the associated kernel k that satisfies the Sonine relation (kappa * k)(t) = 1 for t > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ denote the space of functions $f:(0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ that are continuous on $(0,+\infty)$ and satisfy $f(t)=t^{p}f_1(t)$ for some $p>-1$ and some $f_1\in C[0,+\infty)$. Let $C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$ be its subspace consisting of those $f\in C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ with $p<0$ (so that $f$ has at most an integrable power-type singularity at $0$). For $f,g\in C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ define the Laplace convolution
$$(f*g)(t)=\int_0^t f(t-\tau)g(\tau)\,d\tau,\qquad t>0.$$
A pair $(\kappa,k)$ of functions in $C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$ is called a Sonine pair, written $(\kappa,k)\in\mathcal{L}_1$, if it satisfies the Sonine condition
$$(\kappa*k)(t)=1\quad\text{for all } t>0.$$

Problem. Given a function $\kappa\in C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$:
(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions on $\kappa$ for the existence of $k\in C_{-1,0}(0,+\infty)$ such that $(\kappa,k)\in\mathcal{L}_1$, i.e.\ for $\kappa\in\mathcal{L}_1$.
(b) Under these conditions, derive an explicit representation formula for the associated Sonine kernel $k$.
category_tag: Sonine kernels and general fractional calculus
status_search_result: The problem of characterizing Sonine kernel pairs in the class $\mathcal{L}_1$ has been studied within Luchko's general fractional calculus framework, where partial results give sufficient conditions (e.g., kernels with integrable power-type singularities, via Laplace-transform criteria) and explicit examples (power, Mittag-Leffler-type kernels). A complete characterization in the full class $C_{-1}(0,+\infty)$ together with a general explicit representation of the associated kernel does not appear to be settled in the literature surveyed; the status is therefore unclear.

original_question: How should the notions of general fractional integrals and general fractional derivatives, originally developed on the positive real semi-axis using Sonine-type kernels and convolution formulas, be adapted to functions defined on a finite interval and on the whole real line R?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A pair of locally integrable functions $\kappa,k:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a Sonine pair if their Laplace convolution satisfies
$$(\kappa * k)(t)=\int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau)\,k(\tau)\,d\tau = 1, \qquad t>0.$$
For such a pair, the general fractional integral (GFI) and the general fractional derivative (GFD) of a function $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ are defined, on the positive real semi-axis, by
$$(\mathbb{I}_{(\kappa)} f)(t) = \int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau)\,f(\tau)\,d\tau,$$
$$(\mathbb{D}_{(k)} f)(t) = \frac{d}{dt}\int_0^t k(t-\tau)\,f(\tau)\,d\tau \qquad\text{(Riemann–Liouville type)},$$
$$({}_*\mathbb{D}_{(k)} f)(t) = \int_0^t k(t-\tau)\,f'(\tau)\,d\tau \qquad\text{(Caputo type)}.$$
The Sonine condition $(\kappa*k)(t)=1$ guarantees the fundamental identities $\mathbb{D}_{(k)}\mathbb{I}_{(\kappa)} f = f$ and analogous projector formulas. Definitions for arbitrary (non-integer) order are obtained by iterating or extending these constructions to suitable kernel classes.

Problem. Develop a consistent theory of general fractional integrals and general fractional derivatives, with Sonine-type kernels and convolution structure as above, in the following two settings, in such a way that the Sonine pairing, the fundamental theorems of fractional calculus (left- and right-inverse relations between GFI and GFD), the projector formulas, and appropriate function spaces on which the operators act, are all preserved:

(a) Functions defined on a finite interval $[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}$: define left-sided and right-sided GFIs and GFDs on $[a,b]$, identify the admissible kernel classes, and establish their mapping properties and inversion relations.

(b) Functions defined on the whole real line $\mathbb{R}$: define two-sided (left, right, and Liouville/Marchaut-type) GFIs and GFDs on $\mathbb{R}$, identify the admissible kernel classes (including Fourier-analytic characterizations of the Sonine condition), and establish their mapping properties and inversion relations.
category_tag: general fractional calculus with Sonine kernels
status_search_result: Subsequent work in general fractional calculus has introduced GFIs/GFDs on finite intervals (e.g., right-sided operators, multi-kernel approach, 1st-level GFDs) and partial extensions, but a complete, unified theory adapting the Sonine-kernel GFI/GFD framework to both finite intervals and to the whole real line (with two-sided/Liouville-type operators and full inversion theorems) does not appear to have been fully established. The problem appears to be partially addressed rather than fully solved.

original_question: How can time-fractional differential equations involving general fractional derivatives of arbitrary order be developed and analyzed so that they model processes that are intermediate between diffusion and wave propagation?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $k\in L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}_+)$ be a nonnegative locally integrable kernel. For a function $f:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}$, define the general fractional integral (GFI) with kernel $k$ by
$$ (\mathbb{I}_{(k)} f)(t)=\int_0^t k(t-\tau)f(\tau)\,d\tau, \qquad t>0. $$
For a Sonine kernel pair $(k,\kappa)$ — that is, a pair satisfying the Sonine condition $\int_0^t k(t-\tau)\kappa(\tau)\,d\tau=1$ for $t>0$ — the general fractional derivative (GFD) in the Riemann–Liouville sense is
$$ (\mathbb{D}_{(\kappa)} f)(t)=\frac{d}{dt}\int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau)f(\tau)\,d\tau, $$
and in the Caputo sense
$$ ({}_*\mathbb{D}_{(\kappa)} f)(t)=\int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau)f'(\tau)\,d\tau. $$
Suppose furthermore that a notion of GFD "of arbitrary order" greater than one has been defined via a generalized Sonine condition that produces kernels with an integrable singularity at the origin and that permits the prescription of two or more initial conditions in associated Cauchy problems.

Problem. Develop a theory of time-fractional partial differential equations of the form
$$ ({}_*\mathbb{D}_{(\kappa)} u)(x,t) = \mathcal{L}\, u(x,t), \qquad x\in\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n,\ t>0, $$
where $\mathcal{L}$ is a (possibly second-order elliptic) spatial operator and $\kappa$ is the kernel of a general fractional derivative of arbitrary order strictly between $1$ and $2$, with two initial conditions
$$ u(x,0)=\varphi(x),\qquad u_t(x,0)=\psi(x). $$
Specifically: (i) formulate the well-posed initial(-boundary) value problem; (ii) establish existence, uniqueness, and regularity of solutions; (iii) derive a fundamental solution and analyze its qualitative behaviour (positivity, asymptotics, propagation speed); and (iv) prove that the resulting evolution genuinely interpolates between the diffusive regime (single first-order initial condition) and the wave regime (two initial conditions with finite propagation speed) — that is, identify quantitative criteria on $\kappa$ under which the solutions exhibit behaviour intermediate between heat-like diffusion and undamped wave propagation.
status_search_result: A follow-up program has appeared: general fractional integrals and derivatives of arbitrary order have been defined via a generalized Sonine condition, with two fundamental theorems of fractional calculus and Cauchy problems admitting multiple initial conditions formulated. Subsequent works (e.g., on GFDs of arbitrary order in the Riemann–Liouville sense, 2022, and on multi-kernel extensions of Luchko's operational calculus, 2025) have advanced the theory. However, a complete theory of time-fractional PDEs with GFDs of arbitrary order modeling intermediate diffusion-wave processes (fundamental solutions, well-posedness, qualitative interpolation properties) remains in development and only partially settled.

original_question: Can one construct trial-function and test-function families for Petrov-Galerkin or related spectral methods that are not tailored to only one specific fractional differential equation but instead work across a broad class of problems, still guarantee rapid convergence, possibly yield even faster convergence than current constructions, and admit error analyses in stronger norms such as L^infinity rather than only L^2?
self_contained_problem:
Consider linear fractional differential equations on a bounded interval, for instance equations of the form
   D^α u(x) + L u(x) = f(x),   x ∈ (a,b),
together with appropriate initial or boundary conditions, where D^α denotes a Caputo or Riemann–Liouville fractional derivative of order α ∈ (0,1) ∪ (1,2) and L is a (possibly zero) lower-order linear operator. For such problems, a Petrov–Galerkin spectral method seeks an approximation u_N in a finite-dimensional trial space span{φ_1,…,φ_N} by imposing the weak orthogonality conditions
   ⟨D^α u_N + L u_N − f, ψ_k⟩ = 0,   k = 1,…,N,
against a finite-dimensional test space span{ψ_1,…,ψ_N}.

Construct an explicit pair of families {φ_n}_{n≥1} and {ψ_n}_{n≥1} of trial and test functions with the following properties simultaneously:

1. (Universality) The same families work for a broad class of fractional differential equations — at minimum, for all sufficiently smooth right-hand sides f and for a non-trivial range of fractional orders α and of admissible lower-order operators L — rather than being tailored to a single equation.

2. (Rapid convergence) For sufficiently regular exact solutions u, the approximations u_N converge to u at a spectral (faster than any algebraic) rate; ideally at a rate at least as fast as that achieved by existing equation-specific constructions, and if possible strictly faster.

3. (Strong-norm error analysis) The convergence and error estimates can be established in the L^∞(a,b) norm, i.e. one can prove bounds of the form
   ‖u − u_N‖_{L^∞(a,b)} ≤ C(u) η(N),   η(N) → 0 rapidly,
and not merely in the L^2(a,b) norm.

Either exhibit such families together with proofs of (1)–(3), or prove that no families satisfying all three properties simultaneously can exist.
category_tag: Spectral methods for fractional differential equations
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning the construction of universal trial/test bases for Petrov–Galerkin spectral discretizations of fractional ODEs with L^∞ error analysis. No published work appears to provide such a construction with all three properties (universality across a broad class, provable spectral convergence, and L^∞ error estimates); standard treatments (e.g., Jacobi poly-fractonomial bases of Zayernouri–Karniadakis and subsequent developments) are analyzed in weighted L^2 settings and are largely problem-specific. Status remains open to the best of available evidence.

original_question: How should temporal and spatial nonlocality be classified into mathematically distinct types such as memory, distributed lag, and distributed scaling, and which classes of operator kernels and corresponding fractional operators are able to model each type of phenomenon?
self_contained_problem:
Consider integro-differential operators of the form
\[ (K f)(t) = \int_{a}^{t} M(t,\tau)\, f(\tau)\, d\tau \quad\text{(temporal case)}, \qquad (K f)(x) = \int_{\Omega} N(x,y)\, f(y)\, dy \quad\text{(spatial case)}, \]
including, as a distinguished family, the fractional integral and derivative operators (Riemann–Liouville, Caputo, Hadamard, Erdélyi–Kober, general Sonine-kernel operators, etc.) whose kernels depend on the difference, ratio, or more general two-variable combination of their arguments.

Three qualitatively distinct types of nonlocal behavior are to be distinguished:

(i) Memory: the value of an output at the present moment depends on a weighted history of the input on a preceding interval, with the kernel acting as a fading-memory weight.

(ii) Distributed lag: the response at the present moment is produced by inputs concentrated near one or several past instants, represented by kernels that are localized (peaked, possibly multi-modal) rather than monotonically decaying.

(iii) Distributed scaling: the contribution of past (or distant) inputs is governed by a self-similar, scale-invariant weighting, i.e. kernels that are homogeneous functions of a ratio of their arguments.

Problem. Give a rigorous mathematical classification of temporal and spatial nonlocality into the three types above (memory, distributed lag, distributed scaling), formulated as precise structural conditions on the kernel $M(t,\tau)$ or $N(x,y)$ (e.g. monotonicity, support/concentration, scaling/homogeneity properties, integrability, and admissible singularities). For each class, characterize the corresponding family of admissible kernels and identify which classes of fractional/integro-differential operators (Riemann–Liouville, Caputo, Hadamard, Erdélyi–Kober, Prabhakar, general Sonine-pair, distributed-order, variable-order, tempered, etc.) realize that class, and conversely which type of nonlocal phenomenon each such operator family is capable of modeling.
status_search_result: The question is a programmatic classification problem in the theory of fractional calculus and nonlocal operators. No comprehensive classification linking kernel structural properties to memory / distributed-lag / distributed-scaling phenomena appears in the literature; surveys on general fractional calculus (Sonine kernels, Luchko, Kochubei, Tarasov) discuss partial aspects but do not provide a complete taxonomy. Status appears open.

original_question: Can one establish general fundamental theorems of fractional calculus for fractional operators with distributed lag, especially in models where memory effects and distributed lag are present simultaneously?
self_contained_problem:
Consider fractional operators with continuously distributed lag, defined as follows. For an absolutely integrable probability density M:[0,∞)→[0,∞) (the lag distribution) and a function f:[0,∞)→ℝ, define the integer-order operator with distributed lag

  (T_M f)(t) = ∫_0^t M(t−τ) f(τ) dτ,

and, for α>0, the fractional integral and fractional derivative with distributed lag as the compositions of T_M with the Riemann–Liouville fractional integral I^α and with the Riemann–Liouville (or Caputo) fractional derivative D^α, e.g.

  (I^α_M f)(t) = (T_M ∘ I^α f)(t),   (D^α_M f)(t) = (D^α ∘ T_M f)(t),

so that memory effects (captured by I^α, D^α) and distributed lag (captured by M) are simultaneously present.

Establish, in this general setting, analogs of the first and second fundamental theorems of calculus: namely, identify natural function classes 𝒳 and broad classes of admissible lag kernels M for which one has

 (i) (First FT) D^α_M I^α_M f = f for all f ∈ 𝒳;
 (ii) (Second FT) I^α_M D^α_M f = f − (boundary/initial-value terms expressible through M and f),

and prove these identities, characterizing the kernels M and the orders α for which such fundamental theorems hold.
status_search_result: Within the framework of General Fractional Calculus (Kochubei 2011; Luchko 2020 onward) based on Sonine kernel pairs, general first and second fundamental theorems have been proven, and these GFC operators include cases interpretable as derivatives/integrals with continuously distributed lag. Thus the problem is partially solved: fundamental theorems are available for broad Sonine-kernel classes, but a fully general treatment specifically for the composed fractional-plus-distributed-lag operators in the form posed has not been uniformly established.

original_question: Which mathematically consistent fractional-calculus models should be used to formulate quantum mechanics with nonlocality in space and quantum field theory with nonlocality in space-time by passing from lattices with long-range interactions to their continuum limits?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a lattice model in d-dimensional space (or space-time) whose degrees of freedom interact through long-range couplings of power-law type, i.e., interaction strengths between sites n and m decaying as |n−m|^{-(d+α)} for some parameter α > 0. By taking an appropriate continuum limit of such lattice systems (with lattice spacing tending to zero), one is led to continuum field equations that involve fractional (nonlocal) differential operators, such as the Riesz fractional Laplacian (−Δ)^{α/2} or fractional time derivatives.

Problem: Identify a mathematically consistent fractional-calculus framework — specifying (a) which classes of fractional derivatives and integrals (e.g. Riesz, Caputo, Marchaud, Grünwald–Letnikov, or generalized fractional operators on appropriate function spaces), (b) which functional-analytic setting (domains, boundary/decay conditions, distributional or Sobolev-type spaces), and (c) which quantization scheme — that:

1. Formulates a quantum mechanics with spatial nonlocality, obtained rigorously as the continuum limit of lattice Hamiltonians with power-law long-range interactions, in a way that preserves self-adjointness of the Hamiltonian, unitarity of time evolution, and the correct local limit as α → 2.

2. Extends to a quantum field theory with nonlocality in space-time, obtained as the continuum limit of lattice field theories with long-range interactions in both spatial and temporal directions, satisfying basic consistency requirements (e.g. well-defined propagators, causality or its suitable nonlocal replacement, locality recovery in a prescribed limit, and renormalizability or finiteness properties).

Determine such fractional-calculus models and rigorously justify the lattice-to-continuum limit linking them to long-range interacting lattice systems.
category_tag: Fractional calculus and nonlocal quantum field theory
status_search_result: This is posed as a future research direction rather than a precise conjecture. While various fractional Schrödinger equations (Laskin) and nonlocal field theories with fractional Laplacians have been proposed and studied, no single universally accepted, mathematically rigorous fractional-calculus framework derived from continuum limits of long-range lattice systems for both nonlocal quantum mechanics and nonlocal QFT has been established. The problem is therefore best classified as open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
original_question: Let HS = sum_{k>=0} H(k)t^k be the Hilbert series of a ring or variety, and let its unrefined Laurent expansion be HS = sum_{i>=0} gamma_i/(1-t)^(d-i), where d is the Krull dimension. What are the mathematical and physical interpretations of all Laurent coefficients gamma_i of an arbitrary Hilbert series?
self_contained_problem:
Let R be a finitely generated graded commutative algebra over a field (or, more generally, the coordinate ring of an affine variety) of Krull dimension d, and let
   HS(t) = sum_{k>=0} H(k) t^k
be its Hilbert series, where H(k) is the dimension of the k-th graded piece. Expand HS(t) as a Laurent series about t = 1 in the form
   HS(t) = sum_{i>=0} gamma_i / (1 - t)^{d-i},
defining a sequence of rational coefficients gamma_0, gamma_1, gamma_2, ... .

It is known that, in favorable cases, gamma_0 equals the degree of the underlying variety (and, when the variety is the affine cone over a Sasaki-Einstein manifold, equals a normalized volume of the base, related to central charges of an associated supersymmetric gauge theory), and that low-order coefficients gamma_0, gamma_1 can sometimes be expressed in terms of the a-invariant of R or, in the case of an invariant ring under a finite group, in terms of the group order and the number of pseudoreflections.

Problem. Provide a general mathematical interpretation, and (when the algebra arises as a Coulomb-branch / Higgs-branch / moduli-space chiral ring of a supersymmetric quiver gauge theory) a corresponding physical interpretation, of every Laurent coefficient gamma_i, i >= 0, of an arbitrary Hilbert series HS(t).
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on quiver gauge theory. While interpretations are known for the leading coefficient gamma_0 (degree of the variety; volume of the Sasaki-Einstein base in the Gorenstein case) and partial results exist for gamma_1 (related to the a-invariant or, for invariant rings, to group order and pseudoreflections), no general interpretation of all gamma_i appears in the literature, and the problem is still listed as open in subsequent work.

original_question: In 3d N = 4 theories, Higgs and Coulomb branches are related by symplectic duality, and certain phase diagrams are related by inversion. Is there a conceptual or structural relation between symplectic duality and inversion of phase diagrams?
self_contained_problem:
In three-dimensional N=4 supersymmetric gauge theories the moduli space of supersymmetric vacua decomposes into a Higgs branch and a Coulomb branch, each of which is a (singular) symplectic variety stratified by its symplectic leaves. The Hasse diagram of this stratification, with vertices labelled by elementary transverse slices (either Kleinian ADE singularities or minimal nilpotent orbit closures of simple Lie algebras), encodes the partial Higgsing/phase structure of the branch and is therefore called the phase diagram of the branch.

Two structures are defined on such theories:

1. Symplectic duality: a pairing of conical symplectic singularities (X, X^!) which, for many 3d N=4 theories, identifies X with the Higgs branch and X^! with the Coulomb branch of the same theory; equivalently it is an equivalence between certain categories O attached to X and X^!.

2. Inversion of phase diagrams: an involution on Hasse diagrams which reverses the partial order and simultaneously exchanges the labels by swapping each Kleinian ADE singularity of type g with the closure of the minimal nilpotent orbit of the simple Lie algebra of type g (and vice versa).

Problem. Determine whether there is a conceptual or structural relation between symplectic duality and inversion of phase diagrams. Concretely, formulate and prove (or disprove) precise conditions on a 3d N=4 theory T under which the phase diagrams of the Higgs and Coulomb branches of T are exchanged by the inversion involution exactly when those branches are symplectic dual, and explain the underlying mathematical mechanism (e.g. in terms of categories O, symplectic resolutions, or magnetic quivers) relating the two notions.
category_tag: Symplectic duality and 3d N=4 Coulomb/Higgs branches
status_search_result: The notion of Hasse-diagram inversion conjecturally relating Higgs and Coulomb branch phase diagrams was introduced by Grimminger–Hanany (JHEP 09 (2020) 159), and subsequent surveys (e.g. Kamnitzer 2022 on symplectic duality; the 2024 Perimeter workshop on symplectic singularities and magnetic quivers; Bourget et al. 2025 on 3d mirrors and phase diagrams) continue to discuss the relationship as conjectural, with no general conceptual identification of symplectic duality with phase-diagram inversion established. The question therefore appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
original_question: Quiver folding relates Coulomb branches of unfolded and folded quivers via finite-group actions, and Hilbert series and highest weight generating functions have been computed for certain non-simply laced quivers. Can one compute the Hilbert series and highest weight generating functions for the Higgs branches of folded theories?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A quiver is a finite directed graph whose nodes carry compact gauge groups (typically U(n), SO(n), or Sp(n)) and whose edges encode hypermultiplet matter representations. To such a quiver one associates two hyperkähler moduli spaces: the Coulomb branch and the Higgs branch. Quiver folding is the operation of identifying nodes of a simply-laced quiver related by a discrete automorphism, producing a (generally non-simply laced) folded quiver whose Coulomb branch is the fixed-point locus of the induced action on the Coulomb branch of the unfolded quiver.

For a hyperkähler cone X with an action of a global symmetry group G, the Hilbert series HS_X(t; x) is the generating function
   HS_X(t; x) = ∑_n dim(C[X]_n) χ_n(x) t^n,
where C[X]_n is the degree-n part of the coordinate ring of X and χ_n is the character of G on this graded piece. The highest weight generating function (HWG) of X repackages this information as
   HWG_X(t; μ_1, …, μ_r) = ∑_λ a_λ(t) μ^λ,
where λ ranges over dominant weights of G, μ_i are fugacities for fundamental weights, and a_λ(t) ∈ ℤ[[t]] counts (with signs) the multiplicities of the irreducible G-representation of highest weight λ in C[X].

For non-simply laced folded quivers, the Hilbert series and HWG of the Coulomb branch have been computed in many examples via a monopole-type formula adapted to folded quivers.

Problem. Develop a systematic method to compute the Hilbert series HS and highest weight generating functions HWG of the Higgs branches of folded (non-simply laced) quiver gauge theories, and carry out these computations explicitly for natural families of such theories.
status_search_result: Subsequent work, notably "Folding orthosymplectic quivers" (JHEP 12 (2021) 070), gives a magnetic-quiver realisation of certain Higgs branches of folded theories and computes both Coulomb and Higgs branch Hilbert series in cases where agreement can be verified, providing partial progress. A fully general, systematic prescription for HS and HWG of Higgs branches of arbitrary folded theories does not appear to be established in the literature, so the question remains partially solved.

original_question: The generalized s-rule can be described using dot diagrams and, for irreducible brane junctions, in terms of self-intersection numbers of the holomorphic curves wrapped by M2-branes. Can one formulate a criterion for the generalized s-rule in terms of self-intersection numbers for reducible junctions?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Consider Type IIB / M-theory configurations of (p,q) 5-brane webs (equivalently, the dual M-theory description in which BPS states arise from M2-branes wrapping holomorphic curves in a local Calabi–Yau threefold). To such a web one may attach additional brane junctions, and a fundamental consistency condition limiting how many such junctions can be simultaneously placed is known as the generalized s-rule. Two equivalent formulations are known in special cases:

(i) Dot-diagram criterion: For a web with attached 7-branes, the dot diagram records how the BPS string ends on the 7-branes, and the generalized s-rule can be stated combinatorially as a condition on allowed dot diagrams.

(ii) Self-intersection criterion (irreducible case): For an irreducible brane junction, i.e. one realized in M-theory by a single irreducible holomorphic curve C wrapped by an M2-brane in the local Calabi–Yau, the generalized s-rule is equivalent to the condition that the self-intersection number C·C (computed in the relevant surface, with appropriate boundary contributions) satisfies a definite inequality (so that C represents a genuine BPS state and the junction is supersymmetric).

A reducible junction is one whose corresponding holomorphic class decomposes as a sum C = C_1 + C_2 + … + C_k of two or more irreducible holomorphic curves, possibly with multiplicities, each wrapped by an M2-brane.

Problem. paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
context_brief: Ugly and bad theories as affine Grassmannian slices
original_question: Affine Grassmannian slices appear as Coulomb branches of framed quivers. Can one study the Coulomb branches of “ugly” and “bad” theories, in the sense of Gaiotto and Witten, as generalized affine Grassmannian slices?
self_contained_problem:
Background. To a 3-dimensional N=4 gauge theory determined by a complex reductive group G and a quaternionic representation N, Braverman–Finkelberg–Nakajima associate a Coulomb branch M_C(G,N), a (typically singular) affine symplectic variety. When the data come from a framed quiver of finite ADE type — i.e. G = ∏ GL(v_i) and N is built from the quiver arrows together with framing maps determined by dimension vectors v = (v_i) and w = (w_i) — the Coulomb branch is known to be isomorphic to a (generalized) affine Grassmannian slice attached to the corresponding pair of dominant coweights determined by w and w − Cv (where C is the Cartan matrix), provided the quiver gauge theory is "good" in the following sense of Gaiotto–Witten:

For each node i of the quiver, set
   d_i := (the number of fundamental hypermultiplets at node i) − 2·(rank at node i) + (contributions from neighbouring nodes)
       = w_i + ∑_{j∼i} v_j − 2 v_i.
The theory is called
 • good if d_i ≥ 1 for every node i,
 • ugly if d_i ≥ 0 for every node i and d_i = 0 for at least one node,
 • bad if d_i < 0 for some node i.

Equivalently in highest-weight language, with λ = ∑ w_i ω_i and μ = λ − ∑ v_i α_i, the theory is good when λ − μ is a positive sum of simple roots and μ is dominant (and "deep enough"), ugly when μ lies on a wall in a specified sense, and bad otherwise.

Problem. For framed quiver gauge theories that are ugly or bad in the above sense, give a description of the Coulomb branch M_C(G,N) as a generalized affine Grassmannian slice (or a suitable extension of that notion). More precisely:

 (i) For ugly theories, identify M_C(G,N) with a generalized slice W^{λ}_{μ} (or a related variety, e.g. a slice for a smaller group or with shifted parameters) and describe the associated geometric structures (symplectic resolution, Poisson deformation, quantization by a truncated shifted Yangian).

 (ii) For bad theories, where μ fails to be dominant and standard Gaiotto–Witten predictions break down, develop a generalized notion of affine Grassmannian slice — for instance, slices in the affine Grassmannian for shifted Yangians with arbitrary (not necessarily dominant) shift, or geometric objects naturally attached to non-dominant μ — and prove that M_C(G,N) is isomorphic to such an object, including matching of Poisson structure and quantization.

Provide a uniform construction covering both ugly and bad cases.

status_search_result: Searches turned up the foundational work of Braverman–Finkelberg–Nakajima identifying Coulomb branches of good/ugly framed ADE quiver gauge theories with (generalized) affine Grassmannian slices, plus follow-ups on shifted Yangians, Hamiltonian reduction, symplectic leaves, and Kac-Moody slices via fundamental monopole operators (through 2024). However, no paper found gives a uniform description of the Coulomb branches of ugly and especially bad theories as generalized affine Grassmannian slices in full generality; the question appears to remain open, with only partial results in special cases.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
original_question: Given a chiral ring I with associated affine variety X = Spec(I), K-stability has been proposed as a criterion for when I is the chiral ring of a superconformal field theory, but known counterexamples show the picture is incomplete. What is the precise relationship between K-stability, chiral rings, and superconformal field theories?
self_contained_problem:
Let $I$ be a finitely generated commutative graded ring over $\mathbb{C}$ (called a chiral ring) with an isolated singularity at the origin, and let $X = \mathrm{Spec}(I)$ be the associated affine variety, viewed as a (possibly Fano) cone with a chosen Reeb vector field. To such data one associates a notion of K-stability defined via test configurations and the (equivariant) Futaki invariant computed, for instance, from the Hilbert series of $I$. It has been proposed that K-stability of $(X,\xi)$ should characterize when $I$ arises as the chiral ring of a four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theory (for example, the chiral ring of a quiver gauge theory living on D3-branes probing the singularity $X$), with the Reeb vector encoding the superconformal R-symmetry obtained by $a$-maximization. However, examples are known in which the naive K-stability criterion fails to match the physical SCFT condition (e.g. when nontrivial baryonic symmetries, accidental symmetries, or further modifications of the Hilbert series numerator are required).

Problem: Formulate and prove a precise mathematical statement giving necessary and sufficient conditions, in terms of an appropriately refined notion of K-stability of the pair $(X,\xi)$ (equivalently, of the graded ring $I$ with its $\mathbb{R}$-grading), for $I$ to be realizable as the chiral ring of a four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theory. In particular, identify the correct refinement of the Futaki invariant / test-configuration framework that accounts for the known counterexamples and characterizes SCFT chiral rings exactly.
status_search_result: The precise relationship between K-stability and SCFT chiral rings remains an active research area. Foundational work (Collins–Xie–Yau) established equivalence between K-stability and existence of Ricci-flat Kähler cone metrics, and conjectured equivalence with chiral-ring stability, but recent work (e.g., 2021 JHEP "Chiral rings, Futaki invariants, plethystics, and Gröbner bases") shows that naive Hilbert-series Futaki computations must be modified (numerator corrections) to correctly diagnose SCFT chiral rings, with no complete characterization yet established. The question therefore remains open.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
original_question: Can K-stability be applied to chiral rings in dimensions other than four, such as settings related to F-theorem or c-theorem, and can K-stability accommodate accidental symmetries that emerge along renormalization-group flow?
self_contained_problem:
In four-dimensional N=1 superconformal field theories, the chiral ring (the ring of holomorphic gauge-invariant operators modulo F-term relations) of a theory dual to a Calabi–Yau cone singularity is known to be "stable" precisely when the cone admits a Ricci-flat Kähler conic metric; equivalently, the affine variety Spec of the chiral ring is K-stable as a Fano cone singularity, and the superconformal R-charge is recovered by volume minimization (the geometric counterpart of a-maximization).

(a) Develop an analogous K-stability framework for chiral rings of superconformal theories in dimensions other than four. Concretely, formulate and prove a K-stability criterion whose associated extremization principle reproduces:
  (i) the F-maximization principle that determines the superconformal R-symmetry of three-dimensional N=2 superconformal field theories (relevant for the F-theorem); and
  (ii) the c-extremization principle that determines the superconformal R-symmetry of two-dimensional N=(0,2) superconformal field theories (relevant for the c-theorem).
State the precise notion of test configuration, Donaldson–Futaki–type invariant, and the geometric objects (e.g. Sasaki–Einstein-type metrics on links of cone singularities) whose existence is equivalent to this stability.

(b) Extend the K-stability framework so that it accounts for accidental symmetries that emerge along the renormalization-group flow — i.e. U(1) symmetries which act trivially on the UV theory but mix with the superconformal R-symmetry at the infrared fixed point, so that certain chiral operators hit the unitarity bound and decouple. Determine how the set of test configurations and the extremization functional must be modified so that the stable point correctly predicts the IR superconformal R-charge in the presence of such accidental symmetries.
status_search_result: Search results indicate that the equivalence between K-stability of three-dimensional Fano cone singularities and stability of chiral rings of 4d N=1 SCFTs is established, but extensions to other dimensions (3d F-maximization, 2d c-extremization) and a systematic treatment of accidental symmetries along RG flow have not been carried out in a general K-stability framework. Recent work (e.g., on chiral rings along RG flow in 5d N=1) continues to address related questions, but no comprehensive solution to the posed problem was found.

paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
context_brief: Dualities for graded quivers with adjoints
original_question: Study dualities for m-graded quivers in the presence of adjoint fields.
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q$ be an $m$-graded quiver with potential, by which is meant a finite quiver whose arrows carry a $\mathbb{Z}/(m+1)$-grading (with arrows of degree $c$ and $m+1-c$ paired by orientation reversal) together with a superpotential of total degree $m$. Such data encode a quiver gauge theory associated to a Calabi–Yau $(m+2)$-fold, whose order-$(m+1)$ Seiberg-like dualities are realized by mutations of $Q$ at nodes that carry no adjoint fields (i.e., no loops at the mutated node).

An adjoint field at a node $i$ is an arrow from $i$ to itself (of some degree $c \in \{1,\dots,m\}$), together with its conjugate partner determined by the grading.

Problem. Develop a theory of order-$(m+1)$ dualities (equivalently, mutation rules for the underlying $m$-graded quivers with potential) at nodes that carry one or more adjoint fields. Specifically:

(a) Define a mutation operation $\mu_i$ on an $m$-graded quiver with potential $(Q,W)$ at a node $i$ possessing adjoint fields of arbitrary degrees, producing a new $m$-graded quiver with potential $(Q',W')$ that:
  (i) reduces to the standard mutation when $i$ has no adjoints;
  (ii) is compatible with the underlying Calabi–Yau $(m+2)$-fold geometry; and
  (iii) reproduces, for $m=1$, Kutasov–Schwimmer-type dualities of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories with adjoint matter.

(b) Determine the conditions on the degrees and superpotential couplings of the adjoint fields under which such a mutation is well defined, and describe the resulting transformation of ranks, arrows, and superpotential terms.
status_search_result: Searches indicate that mutations of $m$-graded quivers (equivalently, order-$(m+1)$ dualities) are currently formulated only at nodes without adjoint fields/loops, both in the physics and the higher cluster category literature. Treatment of nodes with adjoints remains incomplete; recent works on Kutasov–Schwimmer-type dualities for graded quivers (e.g., 2024 preprints) explicitly revisit this case but do not provide a complete general framework, so the question appears still open.
