original_question: Define anisotropic function spaces adapted to ideal hydrodynamics that have higher regularity along flow lines than across them, and prove existence and uniqueness theorems for Euler dynamics in those spaces in any dimension.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations for an ideal fluid on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (or on a smooth $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold), $d \ge 2$:
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla) u + \nabla p = 0,\qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
where $u(t,x)$ is the velocity field and $p(t,x)$ the pressure.

Motivated by the observation that physical fluid flows often exhibit much higher smoothness along streamlines (integral curves of $u$) than transverse to them — for example, vorticity tends to be analytic along level lines while only finitely smooth in the transverse direction — carry out the following program:

(a) Define a scale of anisotropic function spaces $X = X(\Omega)$ on a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (or on a manifold) in which regularity is measured separately in the direction tangent to the flow lines of a given divergence-free vector field $u$ and in the directions transverse to those flow lines, with strictly higher (e.g., analytic or Gevrey) regularity required tangentially and only finite (e.g., Hölder or Sobolev) regularity required transversally. Provide a precise definition of $X$ that is intrinsic, invariant under volume-preserving diffeomorphisms compatible with the flow structure, and well adapted to the transport operator $u\cdot\nabla$.

(b) Prove local-in-time existence and uniqueness theorems for the Euler system above with initial data in $X$, in any dimension $d \ge 2$, establishing that the solution map $u_0 \mapsto u(t,\cdot)$ is well-defined and continuous in the topology of $X$ on some nontrivial time interval.
status_search_result: No published resolution of this program was found. The literature contains related work on anisotropic Hölder/Sobolev spaces in fluid problems and on Lagrangian flows with anisotropic regularity, but no construction of intrinsic anisotropic function spaces with higher tangential regularity along streamlines together with corresponding existence/uniqueness theorems for the Euler equations in arbitrary dimension. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Quantify how the L2 exponential map on D_mu^s(M) fails to be Fredholm for compact Riemannian three-manifolds, for example in terms of essential spectrum or another measurement of non-compactness in the derivative of the exponential map.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian three-manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$, for $s>\tfrac{n}{2}+1=\tfrac{5}{2}$. Equip $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with the right-invariant $L^2$ (kinetic energy) metric; its geodesics correspond, via the Arnold interpretation, to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Let $\exp_e: U \subset T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M) \to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ be the associated Riemannian exponential map at the identity.

It is known that, in contrast to the two-dimensional case, $\exp_e$ generally fails to be a nonlinear Fredholm map of index zero when $\dim M = 3$: there exist explicit initial velocity fields $v_0 \in T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ along whose geodesics the derivative $d\exp_e$ is not Fredholm.

Problem: Quantify this failure of the Fredholm property. For instance, for a geodesic with initial velocity $v_0$, determine the essential spectrum of the derivative $d\exp_e|_{tv_0}$ (viewed as a bounded operator on $T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$), or otherwise provide a precise measure of its non-compactness. Specifically, decomposing $d\exp_e$ in the form $A + K_r$ where $A$ is an invertible operator and 
$$K_r w \;=\; (1-\Delta)^{-r/2}\, P_e\!\left(\iota_w\, d\,(1-\Delta)^{r/2} v_0^{\flat}\right)$$
(with $P_e$ the Hodge projection onto divergence-free fields, $\flat$ the metric musical isomorphism, and $r=0$ corresponding to the $L^2$ case), determine whether and how badly $K_0$ fails to be compact, and compute (or estimate) the essential spectrum of $d\exp_e$ along three-dimensional Euler geodesics.
status_search_result: Existing literature establishes that the L^2 exponential map on the volumorphism group is nonlinear Fredholm of index zero in dimension two but fails to be Fredholm in dimension three, with explicit non-Fredholm examples on three-manifolds (e.g., solid torus). A decomposition of the derivative into an invertible part plus a remainder K_r is available for H^r metrics with r>0, suggesting the L^2 failure is borderline, but no published work appears to quantify the failure (e.g., compute the essential spectrum) for compact Riemannian 3-manifolds. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Show that the absolute complexity C(gamma(t)) of any L2 geodesic gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M) is bounded above by an exponential function of time and initial H^s speed.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth, closed, oriented Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$, and let $\mu$ be its Riemannian volume form. For a Sobolev exponent $s > n/2 + 1$, denote by $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$. This group is a smooth infinite-dimensional Hilbert manifold, and it carries the right-invariant $L^2$ (Arnold) metric whose geodesics describe solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$.

For a curve $\gamma:[0,T]\to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$, define its absolute complexity $C(\gamma(t))$ to be the total spatial complexity accumulated by $\gamma$ up to time $t$ (for instance, measured by the growth of an appropriate geometric quantity such as the length of the image of a generic submanifold, or equivalently a measure of the intricacy of the configuration $\gamma(t)$ relative to the identity).

Prove that there exist constants $a, b > 0$, depending only on $M$ and $s$, such that for every $L^2$-geodesic $\gamma(t)$ in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with initial velocity $\dot\gamma(0)\in T_{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$,
$$ C(\gamma(t)) \;\le\; a\, \exp\!\bigl(b\, t\, \|\dot\gamma(0)\|_{H^s}\bigr) $$
for all $t$ in the interval of existence of $\gamma$.

original_question: Quantify the aging phenomenon of ideal fluids, preferably by constructing a Lyapunov function on fluid velocities that is nondecreasing along Euler evolution except on a slim exceptional set.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold, possibly with boundary (e.g.\ a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ or the periodic channel $\mathbb{T}\times(0,a)$), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving Sobolev diffeomorphisms of $M$ of class $H^s$ (with $s>n/2+1$). The tangent space at the identity may be identified with the space of divergence-free vector fields tangent to $\partial M$,
$$T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)=\{u\in H^s(M;TM):\ \operatorname{div} u=0,\ u\cdot\nu|_{\partial M}=0\},$$
on which the incompressible Euler equations
$$\partial_t u+(u\cdot\nabla)u=-\nabla p,\qquad \operatorname{div} u=0,\qquad u\cdot\nu|_{\partial M}=0 \tag{$\ast$}$$
define a (local) flow $u(t,\cdot)$.

Construct a continuous functional ("Lyapunov function") 
$$L:T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}$$
with the following two properties:

(i) For every solution $u(t,\cdot)$ of $(\ast)$, the map $t\mapsto L(u(t,\cdot))$ is monotone nondecreasing, i.e.\ $\frac{d}{dt}L(u(t,\cdot))\ge 0$ for all $t$ for which the solution is defined.

(ii) The set of velocity fields $u\in T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ at which equality $\frac{d}{dt}L(u(t,\cdot))=0$ may hold is a "slim" subset of $T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ — for instance, of infinite codimension.

Such a functional should quantify the heuristic "aging"/regularity-deterioration phenomenon for ideal incompressible fluids and, in particular, should not be supported only near $\partial M$ (i.e.\ examples with support in the interior of the fluid domain are sought). Does such a Lyapunov function exist?
status_search_result: The problem of constructing a global Lyapunov function on divergence-free velocity fields that is monotone along Euler evolution outside a slim set is listed as an open problem in the geometric-hydrodynamics open-problems survey (Khesin et al., 2022). Partial results exist: Yudovich (1970s) constructed local Lyapunov functions for flows with a rectilinear streamline, and Shnirelman extended this to arbitrary bounded domains, both implying regularity deterioration near the boundary. No interior-supported global Lyapunov function quantifying aging is known.

context_brief: Entropy notions for sets and measures
original_question: Investigate the properties and relations of the entropy quantities H_epsilon, H_{epsilon,delta}, H_tilde_epsilon, and H_tilde_{epsilon,delta} introduced for compact sets and probability measures in metric or Hilbert spaces.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space (or a Hilbert space) and let $M\subset X$ be a compact subset equipped with a Borel probability measure $\mu$ supported on $M$. For $\varepsilon>0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, consider the following entropy-type quantities.

(i) The $\varepsilon$-entropy of the set $M$:
$$H_\varepsilon(M)=\log_2 N_\varepsilon(M),$$
where $N_\varepsilon(M)$ is the minimal number of closed balls of radius $\varepsilon$ needed to cover $M$.

(ii) The measure $\varepsilon$-entropy: choose a minimal $\varepsilon$-cover of $M$ by balls and let $\{C_j\}$ be the associated partition of $M$ into measurable pieces of diameter $\le 2\varepsilon$; set
$$H_\varepsilon(\mu)=-\sum_j \mu(C_j)\log_2\mu(C_j).$$

(iii) The $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-entropy $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}(\mu)$: the logarithm (base $2$) of the minimal number of $\varepsilon$-balls needed to cover a subset of $M$ of $\mu$-measure at least $1-\delta$.

(iv) The variants $\widetilde H_\varepsilon$ and $\widetilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ in which coverings are replaced by packings (maximal collections of pairwise disjoint balls of radius $\varepsilon$ centered in $M$, with the analogous measure-restricted version for $\widetilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$).

Problem. Investigate the properties of, and establish the precise relations between, the four entropy functions $H_\varepsilon$, $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$, $\widetilde H_\varepsilon$, $\widetilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ on compact sets and probability measures in metric or Hilbert spaces. In particular, study their asymptotic behavior as $\varepsilon\to 0$, their invariance (or lack thereof) under isometries, rotations, and smooth deformations of the underlying set $M$, and determine to what extent the leading-order asymptotic
$$H_\varepsilon(\mu)\sim d\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\cdot \mu(X)$$
(observed when $M=Q^d\subset\mathbb R^d$ is the unit cube with $\mu$ the Lebesgue measure) persists when $Q^d$ is embedded and rotated inside a larger space $X^n$, $n>d$, or otherwise deformed.
category_tag: Metric entropy of sets and measures
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open investigation problem in a 2022 open-problems collection on geometric hydrodynamics. No subsequent work specifically resolving the systematic comparison of these four entropy quantities was located.

original_question: Prove that the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is non-integrable under at least one reasonable notion of infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian integrability.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation for an ideal fluid on a surface $M$ (for concreteness, take $M$ to be the two-torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or the two-sphere $S^2$), written in vorticity form as
$$\partial_t \omega + \{\psi, \omega\} = 0, \qquad \omega = \Delta \psi,$$
where $\omega: M \to \mathbb{R}$ is the vorticity, $\psi$ is the stream function, $\Delta$ is the Laplace–Beltrami operator, and $\{f,g\} = \partial_x f\,\partial_y g - \partial_y f\,\partial_x g$ is the canonical Poisson bracket on $M$. This system is an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian system on the dual of the Lie algebra $\mathrm{SVect}(M)$ of divergence-free vector fields on $M$, equipped with the Lie–Poisson structure, and its Hamiltonian is the kinetic energy $H(\omega) = \tfrac12 \int_M |\nabla \psi|^2$.

Although the system possesses an infinite family of Casimir invariants (the moments $\int_M f(\omega)\,d\mu$ for any smooth $f$) and admits a formal Lax representation arising automatically from its Euler–Poincaré structure, no Lax pair depending nontrivially on a spectral parameter is known, and the existence of such a representation (or of action–angle coordinates) is not established.

Problem. Formulate a precise reasonable notion of integrability for infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian systems—for instance, one of:
(a) algebraic-geometric integrability arising from a Lax pair with a nontrivial spectral parameter;
(b) the existence of a complete set of functionally independent Poisson-commuting first integrals giving an invariant foliation by Lagrangian tori in a suitable functional-analytic sense;
(c) integrability in the sense of meromorphic/real-analytic first integrals along a generic invariant submanifold (in the spirit of Ziglin–Morales-Ramis or Melnikov-type obstructions applied to periodic orbits and saddle separatrices of the Euler flow)—

and prove that the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is not integrable in that sense. Equivalently, exhibit a rigorous obstruction (e.g. nontrivial monodromy of variational equations along a periodic solution, a nonvanishing Melnikov integral for a heteroclinic/homoclinic connection of stationary solutions, or a differential-Galois obstruction) that rules out integrability of the 2D Euler equation.
status_search_result: The non-integrability of the 2D Euler equation is a long-standing open problem. While 2D Euler admits infinitely many Casimir invariants and a formal Lax representation coming from its Euler–Poincaré/Lie–Poisson structure, no spectral-parameter Lax pair is known, and no rigorous proof of non-integrability under any standard infinite-dimensional notion has been published. The problem is listed as open in recent problem collections on hydrodynamics and Hamiltonian PDEs.

original_question: Prove that the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equation admits wandering solutions.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian 3-manifold, and consider the incompressible Euler equation
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
for a time-dependent divergence-free vector field $u(t,\cdot)$ on $M$, tangent to $\partial M$ if any. For a fixed regularity class (e.g. $C^k$ with non-integer $k$ sufficiently large, or a suitable Sobolev space) on the space $\mathcal{X}$ of divergence-free vector fields on $M$, call a solution $u(t,\cdot)$ a wandering solution if there exists an open neighborhood $U\subset\mathcal{X}$ of the initial datum $u(0,\cdot)$ and a time $T>0$ such that $u(t,\cdot)\notin U$ for all $t\ge T$ (equivalently, the trajectory eventually leaves a neighborhood of its initial datum and never returns).

Prove that the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on some closed Riemannian 3-manifold $M$ admits a wandering solution in this sense.
status_search_result: The problem is generally regarded as open. Only partial results are available: using KAM-theoretic methods, Khesin, Kuksin and Peralta-Salas (and subsequent work) established non-mixing and non-transitivity of the 3D Euler flow in suitable C^k topologies for prescribed helicity and large energy, both globally and locally near typical steady states on S^3. These results constitute the only known progress toward the existence of wandering solutions in 3D, analogous to the 2D results of Nadirashvili and Shnirelman, but a direct construction of wandering solutions for the 3D Euler equation has not been achieved.

context_brief: Chaos on singular loci of integrable systems
original_question: For an integrable Hamiltonian system on a compact 2n-dimensional manifold, determine how complicated the dynamics can be on singular submanifolds where the n commuting first integrals lose functional independence, including whether chaotic behavior can occur on such tiny singular sets.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a compact symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $H:M\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth Hamiltonian. Assume the Hamiltonian system defined by $H$ is Liouville integrable: there exist $n$ smooth functions $f_1=H,f_2,\dots,f_n:M\to\mathbb{R}$ that pairwise Poisson-commute, $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$ for all $i,j$, and are functionally independent (i.e., $df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_n\neq 0$) on an open dense subset of $M$. Let 
$$\Sigma\;=\;\{\,x\in M\;:\;df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_n\,(x)=0\,\}$$
denote the singular set on which the integrals fail to be functionally independent. The Hamiltonian flow of $H$ preserves $\Sigma$ and each connected component of its strata.

Investigate the dynamical complexity of the Hamiltonian flow restricted to $\Sigma$:

(a) Describe what constraints Liouville integrability imposes on the dynamics on $\Sigma$ (and on its individual smooth strata).

(b) Determine whether the restricted dynamics on $\Sigma$ can exhibit chaotic behavior — for instance, positive topological entropy, a horseshoe, or a hyperbolic invariant set with a dense orbit — even when $\Sigma$ is a "tiny" (low-dimensional, measure-zero) submanifold of $M$.

(c) If chaos is possible, exhibit an explicit smooth ($C^\infty$ or real-analytic) example of a Liouville integrable system on a compact symplectic manifold whose restriction to the singular locus $\Sigma$ has positive topological entropy; if it is impossible, prove the corresponding rigidity theorem.
status_search_result: The question of how complicated (and in particular how chaotic) the dynamics of a Liouville integrable Hamiltonian system can be on its singular locus appears to be an open research problem. Bolsinov–Taimanov constructed real-analytic integrable geodesic flows whose singular set carries positive topological entropy, showing chaotic-type behavior on singular subsets is possible in specific examples, but a general description of the constraints that integrability imposes on the dynamics restricted to the singular submanifold, and a complete answer to whether arbitrary chaotic behavior may appear on arbitrarily small singular submanifolds, has not been established.

original_question: Construct a hierarchy of higher helicity-type invariants for divergence-free vector fields so that when all lower invariants vanish, the first nonzero invariant gives a lower bound for the field's energy.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian 3-manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{V}(M)$ denote the space of smooth divergence-free vector fields on $M$ that are tangent to the boundary. For $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$, define its energy by
$$E(v) = \int_M \|v(x)\|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}(x),$$
and its helicity by
$$\mathcal{H}(v) = \int_M \langle v, \operatorname{curl}^{-1} v \rangle \, d\mathrm{vol},$$
where $\operatorname{curl}^{-1} v$ is a vector potential $A$ with $\operatorname{curl} A = v$. Arnold's classical inequality states that there exists a constant $C(M) > 0$ such that $E(v) \geq C(M)\, |\mathcal{H}(v)|$ for all $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$.

Construct a sequence of functionals $\{I_n : \mathcal{V}(M) \to \mathbb{R}\}_{n \geq 1}$, with $I_1 = \mathcal{H}$, having the following properties:

(i) each $I_n$ is invariant under the action of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ (i.e., is a higher-order helicity-type invariant);

(ii) for every $v \in \mathcal{V}(M)$ and every $n \geq 1$, if $I_1(v) = I_2(v) = \cdots = I_{n-1}(v) = 0$ but $I_n(v) \neq 0$, then there exists a constant $C_n(M) > 0$ (independent of $v$) and an exponent $\alpha_n > 0$ such that
$$E(v) \geq C_n(M)\, |I_n(v)|^{\alpha_n}.$$

In particular, vanishing of all lower invariants forces the first nonzero invariant to bound the energy of the field from below.
status_search_result: The problem, originating in Arnold–Khesin's topological hydrodynamics, remains open in full generality. Partial progress exists: cubic ("third-order") asymptotic helicity-type invariants and certain higher analogs of the asymptotic Hopf invariant have been constructed (e.g., Bodnar/Komendarczyk-Vela-Vick), and a related rigidity result shows helicity is the only regular integral invariant under mild assumptions. However, no general hierarchy giving energy lower bounds when lower invariants vanish has been established.

original_question: Describe the differential geometry of shape spaces carrying the nonlocal H^{-1/2} metrics that arise from dynamic free boundaries or vortex sheets in hydrodynamics.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote a shape space of smooth closed hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (for instance, the space $\mathrm{Emb}(M,\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ of unparametrized embeddings of a closed manifold $M$), and consider on $\mathcal{S}$ the family of nonlocal Riemannian metrics of fractional Sobolev order $H^{-1/2}$ that arise naturally in hydrodynamics: namely, the metrics induced on the space of dynamic free boundaries or on the space of vortex sheets by the kinetic energy of the surrounding incompressible fluid (where, for a normal velocity field $a$ on a hypersurface $\Gamma$, the squared norm is $\|a\|_{H^{-1/2}(\Gamma)}^2 = \int_\Gamma a\, \mathcal{N}^{-1} a\, dS$ with $\mathcal{N}$ the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, or analogously a vortex-sheet kinetic-energy norm).

Develop the differential geometry of $(\mathcal{S}, g_{H^{-1/2}})$: in particular, determine the geodesic equation, the Levi-Civita connection, sectional curvature, completeness properties (metric and geodesic), existence of minimizing geodesics, the structure of the exponential map, and the relationship of these geodesics to the free-boundary Euler equations and to the Birkhoff–Rott vortex-sheet evolution.
status_search_result: No comprehensive treatment of the differential geometry of shape spaces equipped with the nonlocal $H^{-1/2}$ metrics arising from free-boundary/vortex-sheet hydrodynamics appears in the literature. Related work (e.g., vortex-sheet motion as groupoid Euler–Arnold geodesics for an $L^2$ metric, and Sobolev metrics of nonnegative order on shape spaces) is available, but the specific $H^{-1/2}$ shape-space geometry is posed as a research direction and seems to remain open.

original_question: Explain the correspondence between bouncing-droplet dynamics and quantum-particle behavior by combining averaging arguments with the Madelung transform.
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider the hydrodynamic pilot-wave system describing a millimetric droplet bouncing on the surface of a vertically vibrated fluid bath above the Faraday threshold. In a standard model, the in-plane position $X(t)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ of the droplet satisfies a stroboscopic equation of motion of the form
$$ m\ddot X(t) + \gamma \dot X(t) = -\nabla h(X(t),t), $$
where the underlying wave field $h(x,t)$ is generated by the cumulative impacts of the droplet,
$$ h(x,t) = \sum_{n: t_n\le t} A\, e^{-(t-t_n)/T_F}\, W\!\big(|x-X(t_n)|\big), $$
with $W$ a Bessel-type Faraday wave kernel of wavelength $\lambda_F$, $T_F$ a memory time, and $\{t_n\}$ the bouncing times.

Separately, recall the Madelung transform: a wavefunction $\psi(x,t) = \sqrt{\rho(x,t)}\, e^{iS(x,t)/\hbar}$ solving the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = -\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta\psi + V\psi$ is equivalent to the hydrodynamic system
$$ \partial_t \rho + \nabla\!\cdot(\rho\, v) = 0, \qquad m(\partial_t v + (v\cdot\nabla)v) = -\nabla\!\left(V + Q[\rho]\right), $$
with $v = \nabla S/m$ and quantum potential $Q[\rho] = -\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\,\Delta\sqrt{\rho}/\sqrt{\rho}$.

Problem. Derive, by a combination of (i) a multi-scale averaging procedure applied to the fast bouncing/Faraday oscillations of the droplet–wave dynamics described above, and (ii) the Madelung transform, an effective continuum description of the long-time statistics of the droplet position whose evolution coincides with (or rigorously approximates) that of a Schrödinger-type equation for an emergent wavefunction $\psi$. In particular:

(a) Identify a small parameter $\varepsilon$ (e.g. ratio of Faraday period to memory time, or ratio of de Broglie-like wavelength to bath wavelength) and perform an averaging of the droplet equation over the fast time scale to obtain a closed evolution for the slowly-varying density $\rho(x,t)$ and mean velocity $v(x,t)$ of the droplet.

(b) Show that the averaged system can be put, via the inverse Madelung transform $\psi = \sqrt{\rho}\,e^{iS/\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}}$, into the form of a Schrödinger equation with an effective Planck constant $\hbar_{\mathrm{eff}}$ expressible in terms of the physical parameters $(m,\gamma,A,T_F,\lambda_F)$, and identify the effective potential induced by external boundaries or applied forces.

(c) Establish in what regime (memory, impact phase, geometry) this droplet–quantum-particle correspondence is exact, and quantify the corrections beyond that regime.
status_search_result: The proposed derivation—obtaining a Schrödinger-type description of bouncing-droplet dynamics by combining multi-scale averaging with the Madelung transform—does not appear to have been carried out rigorously. Partial correspondences (e.g., the Durey–Milewski–Bush statistical correspondence between droplet position distributions and time-averaged wave fields, and analogies via de Broglie's double-solution / quantum thermostat) are established in limited regimes, and recent work extends these statistical correspondences empirically, but a complete averaging-plus-Madelung derivation of the droplet–quantum particle correspondence is still being sought.

original_question: Determine whether a mechanism analogous to the proposed chamber-and-damper apparatus can explain cascades in real hydrodynamics, and whether one can choose the parameters n_i, m_i, and r_i so that the model functions as intended, ideally with an analogue in two-dimensional ideal fluid flow.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following idealized mechanical "chamber-and-damper" apparatus intended to model an energy cascade. The device consists of a finite collection of coupled chambers, indexed by i, each equipped with three positive real parameters: an integer mode number n_i (interpreted as a characteristic wavenumber or number of internal degrees of freedom), a mass parameter m_i, and a damping (or coupling) coefficient r_i. The dynamics among the chambers are designed so that energy injected at one scale is transferred, through the chain of couplings, toward chambers with smaller n_i (a large-scale, or "inverse," cascade), in a manner formally analogous to inverse energy cascade phenomena.

(a) Determine whether a mechanism of this type can be made to faithfully describe energy cascades occurring in real (viscous, three-dimensional) hydrodynamics.

(b) Decide whether one can explicitly choose the parameters {n_i}, {m_i}, {r_i} so that the apparatus actually exhibits the intended cascade behavior, and exhibit such a choice if it exists.

(c) Establish a rigorous link between such a mechanical device and a heat-engine-type model, in particular constructing an analogue of Maxwell's demon within this framework.

(d) Most importantly, construct an analogue of this mechanism within the dynamics of a two-dimensional ideal (Euler) incompressible fluid on a bounded domain or torus, and use it to give a mathematically rigorous mechanism producing inverse energy cascade in 2D ideal hydrodynamics.
status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent open problem list concerning mechanical/Hamiltonian models of cascades in 2D hydrodynamics. No published resolution providing a rigorous mechanism for inverse energy cascade in the 2D Euler equation along these lines has been located; the question is generally regarded as open.

paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
context_brief: Local stability of endemic equilibria for SIR-PH variants
original_question: For SIR-PH epidemic models and their SIR-PH-FA and SIR-PH-IA approximations with linear births, vaccination, loss of immunity, and disease-induced mortality, does R0>1 always imply local asymptotic stability of the endemic equilibrium whenever such a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium exists?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a SIR-PH epidemic model defined as follows. Let the population be split into a susceptible compartment $S$, a vector of "disease" (infectious/exposed) compartments $\mathbf{I}\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$ governed by a phase-type structure, and a removed compartment $R$. The disease compartments follow $\dot{\mathbf{I}} = (\boldsymbol{\beta}^\top \mathbf{I})\,S\,\boldsymbol{\alpha} + \mathbf{I}^\top A$, where $\boldsymbol{\alpha}\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$ with $\sum_i\alpha_i=1$ is the initial distribution among disease states, $\boldsymbol{\beta}\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$ is a vector of infection rates, and $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is a sub-generator (Markovian transition matrix among disease states with absorption). The full SIR-PH system also incorporates:
- a linear birth rate (constant inflow into $S$),
- natural mortality at rate $\mu>0$ for every compartment,
- vaccination of susceptibles (transferring mass into $R$) and loss of immunity (transferring mass from $R$ into $S$),
- disease-induced mortality from the $\mathbf{I}$ compartments (an extra removal rate vector $\boldsymbol{\nu}\ge 0$),
- vaccination-induced mortality.

Define the basic reproduction number $R_0$ via the next-generation matrix construction of van den Driessche and Watmough applied to this model. A disease-free equilibrium (DFE) is an equilibrium with $\mathbf{I}=0$; an endemic equilibrium (EE) is an equilibrium with $\mathbf{I}\ne 0$ whose coordinates are biologically feasible (all non-negative).

Consider also two simplifications used in the literature:
- The SIR-PH-FA approximation, in which the total population is replaced by its equilibrium value in the force-of-infection term (frequency-dependent transmission with fixed total population $N$).
- The SIR-PH-IA approximation, an "incidence approximation" obtained by linearizing certain mass-action terms around the DFE.

Question. Is the following statement true: for every SIR-PH model (and likewise for every SIR-PH-FA and SIR-PH-IA approximation) with parameters as above, whenever $R_0>1$ and a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium exists, that endemic equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable?
status_search_result: The conjecture that $R_0>1$ implies local asymptotic stability of the endemic equilibrium for SIR-PH models (and their FA/IA approximations) is stated explicitly as an open problem. It has been verified in numerous special cases via Routh–Hurwitz or Lyapunov methods, but no general proof or counterexample appears to have been published; subsequent literature on SIR-PH models still treats it as conjectural.

paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
context_brief: Possible stable periodic solutions outside known SEIRS global-stability regimes
original_question: For the vaccinated varying-population SEIRS/SAIRS model in which existing theorems prove global stability of a unique endemic point only under certain parameter restrictions, can stable periodic solutions occur outside those proven global-stability cases?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a varying-population SEIRS/SAIRS compartmental epidemic model with vaccination, where the population is partitioned into Susceptible (S), Exposed/Asymptomatic (E or A), Infectious (I), and Recovered (R) compartments, governed by the system of ODEs

  S' = Λ − μ S − β S I / N − ν S + γ R,
  E' = β S I / N − (μ + σ) E,
  I' = σ E − (μ + α + δ) I,
  R' = δ I + ν S − (μ + γ) R,

with N = S + E + I + R, all parameters Λ, μ, β, ν, γ, σ, α, δ > 0, and where vaccination moves susceptibles directly to R at rate ν and immunity is lost at rate γ. Suppose that global asymptotic stability of the unique endemic equilibrium (when the basic reproduction number R₀ > 1) has been proved only under a restricted set of parameter conditions. 

Question: Outside those known parameter regimes in which the endemic equilibrium is proved globally asymptotically stable, do there exist parameter values for which the system admits a stable periodic (limit-cycle) solution? Equivalently, does the model exhibit Hopf bifurcation leading to attracting periodic orbits in some region of parameter space?
status_search_result: A targeted search did not locate a definitive proof or disproof of the existence of stable periodic solutions for vaccinated varying-population SEIRS/SAIRS models in the regimes outside the known global-stability conditions. Related literature on SAIRS and SEIRS models with vaccination indicates this remains a conjectural/open direction.

paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
context_brief: Global stability for the constant-population SAIRS model beyond beta_e<gamma
original_question: For the eight-parameter constant-population SAIRS model obtained by setting the disease-induced death rate delta to zero, with vaccination, loss of immunity, exposed/asymptomatic transmission beta_e, and infective transmission beta_i, can global stability of the unique endemic equilibrium be proved beyond the currently resolved case beta_e<gamma?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following SAIRS-with-vaccination compartmental epidemic model on a constant total population (normalized to 1), with compartments S (susceptible), A (exposed/asymptomatic infectious), I (symptomatic infectious), R (recovered/immune). With nonnegative parameters Λ (birth rate equal to natural death rate μ so the population is constant), β_e (transmission rate from asymptomatic), β_i (transmission rate from symptomatic), α (rate of progression A→I), γ (recovery rate from I), γ_A (recovery rate from A), ν (vaccination rate S→R), and ρ (loss-of-immunity rate R→S), the dynamics are

   dS/dt = Λ − (β_e A + β_i I) S − (μ + ν) S + ρ R,
   dA/dt = (β_e A + β_i I) S − (α + γ_A + μ) A,
   dI/dt = α A − (γ + μ) I,
   dR/dt = γ_A A + γ I + ν S − (μ + ρ) R,

with S + A + I + R = 1.

Define the basic reproduction number R_0 in the usual next-generation way. Assume R_0 > 1 so that a unique endemic equilibrium E* with all coordinates positive exists in the simplex.

Problem. Prove that the endemic equilibrium E* is globally asymptotically stable in the positively invariant region {(S,A,I,R) : S,A,I,R ≥ 0, S+A+I+R = 1, (A,I) ≠ (0,0)} whenever R_0 > 1, without the additional restriction β_e < γ (under which restriction global asymptotic stability is already known). Equivalently, remove the parameter restriction β_e < γ from the known global stability result.
status_search_result: The conjecture that the endemic equilibrium of the SAIRS model with vaccination is globally asymptotically stable whenever R_0 > 1 without additional parameter restrictions appears to remain open. Recent works (Ottaviano–Sensi–Sottile 2021/2022 and the multi-group extension 2022/2023) explicitly state that they can only establish global stability under restrictions such as β_e < γ (or equal recovery rates for A and I), and numerical simulations suggest the unrestricted statement holds but has not been proved.

paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
context_brief: Extension of the endemic/disease-free determinant formula to SIR-PH models
original_question: For SIR-PH models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease-induced mortality, can the determinant identity Det(J_ee)=-Det(J_dfe), established for lower-dimensional SAIR first-approximation cases, be extended by exploiting the block partition of the scaled-model Jacobian into the susceptible coordinate and disease-coordinate block?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an SIR-PH compartmental epidemic model with phase-type-distributed infectious period, linear (constant-rate) birth, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease-induced mortality. The state is partitioned into a scalar susceptible coordinate s and a vector of "disease" coordinates i (comprising the infectious phases and possibly removed/vaccinated compartments). After non-dimensional scaling, the model has two equilibria: a disease-free equilibrium (DFE) and an endemic equilibrium (EE), and an associated basic reproduction number R0. Let J_dfe and J_ee denote the Jacobians of the scaled vector field at the DFE and EE, respectively, and write each Jacobian in block form according to the partition into the susceptible coordinate and the disease-coordinate block.

For low-dimensional SAIR (susceptible–asymptomatic–infectious–removed) first-approximation models with no disease-induced mortality (δ=0), the following identity is known:
   Det(J_ee) = Λ v0 v1 v2 (1 − R0) = − Det(J_dfe),
where Λ is the birth rate and v0, v1, v2 are explicit coefficients arising from the model parameters.

Problem. Determine whether this determinant identity Det(J_ee) = − Det(J_dfe) extends to general SIR-PH models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease-induced mortality, by exploiting the susceptible/disease block partition of the scaled-model Jacobian. If so, provide a general proof and an explicit formula for the common value of ±Det(J_ee) in terms of the model parameters and R0; otherwise, identify the obstructions and characterize the subclass of SIR-PH models for which the identity does hold.
status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a published proof or refutation extending the determinant identity Det(J_ee) = −Det(J_dfe) from the SAIR first-approximation case to general SIR-PH models with vaccination and disease-induced mortality. The question appears to remain an open research direction; status is recorded as unknown.

paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
context_brief: Scaled model as perturbation of the first approximation
original_question: Can the scaled epidemic model with linear births and disease-induced fatalities be rigorously analyzed as a perturbation of the first approximation model, for example using slow-fast, singular-perturbation, or homogenization techniques, so that conclusions about endemic equilibria and stability can transfer from the approximation to the scaled model?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a compartmental SIR-type epidemic model with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease- and vaccination-induced fatalities, whose total population N(t) is not constant. Concretely, let the state be a vector (S, I, R) (or, more generally, (S, \mathbf{I}, R) with a phase-type infectious compartment \mathbf{I} \in \mathbb{R}_+^n) evolving according to a system of ODEs of the form

  S' = \Lambda - \beta(N) S \mathbf{e}^\top \mathbf{I} - (\mu + \nu) S + \gamma R,
  \mathbf{I}' = (\beta(N) S \mathbf{e}^\top \mathbf{I}) \mathbf{a} + A \mathbf{I} - \mu \mathbf{I},
  R' = \mathbf{b}^\top \mathbf{I} + \nu S - (\mu + \gamma) R,

where \Lambda>0 is a constant birth (recruitment) rate, \mu>0 the natural death rate, \nu \ge 0 the vaccination rate, \gamma \ge 0 the loss-of-immunity rate, \mathbf{a} \in \mathbb{R}_+^n a probability vector, A a sub-generator matrix and \mathbf{b} = -(A+ \text{diag}(\text{death rates}))\mathbf{1} the recovery-rate vector, and where disease-induced and vaccination-induced fatalities cause N = S + \mathbf{e}^\top \mathbf{I} + R to be non-constant. Rescale this "full scaled model" by setting s = S/N, \mathbf{i} = \mathbf{I}/N, r = R/N, and let (\mathcal{S}) denote the resulting ODE system in the simplex variables.

The "first approximation" (FA) model (\mathcal{S}_0) is obtained from (\mathcal{S}) by dropping the additional terms in (\mathcal{S}) that arise from disease/vaccination fatalities and from the non-constancy of N — recovering a classical fixed-population SIR-PH-type system whose endemic equilibria and their local/global stability are well understood in terms of a basic reproduction number R_0.

Problem: Develop a rigorous perturbation theory that realizes (\mathcal{S}) as a small perturbation of (\mathcal{S}_0), using slow-fast / geometric singular perturbation theory, averaging, or homogenization methods, identifying a natural small parameter \varepsilon (e.g. encoding the ratio of fatality and demographic rates to the dominant epidemic timescales) such that (\mathcal{S}_\varepsilon) \to (\mathcal{S}_0) as \varepsilon \to 0. Using such a framework, prove that for sufficiently small \varepsilon:

(i) every hyperbolic endemic equilibrium of the FA model (\mathcal{S}_0) persists as a nearby equilibrium of the scaled model (\mathcal{S}_\varepsilon), with the same local stability type;
(ii) the basic reproduction number, endemic equilibrium coordinates, and Lyapunov/stability conclusions for (\mathcal{S}_0) transfer to (\mathcal{S}_\varepsilon) with quantitative O(\varepsilon) error bounds;
(iii) global asymptotic stability properties (where available for (\mathcal{S}_0)) are inherited by (\mathcal{S}_\varepsilon) on appropriate invariant regions.

original_question: Let A352991 be the OEIS sequence obtained by listing, in increasing order, all decimal concatenations coming from distinct permutations of the first m positive integers for varying m. If a term A352991(n) is a perfect power and is greater than 1, must it always be a perfect square and never a higher-order perfect power c^k with k >= 3? Equivalently, are there no nontrivial cubes, fourth powers, or other higher perfect powers anywhere in A352991?
self_contained_problem:
For each integer $m\ge 1$, consider all permutations $(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_m)$ of the set $\{1,2,\dots,m\}$, and form the decimal concatenation $\overline{a_1 a_2 \cdots a_m}$ obtained by writing each $a_i$ in base $10$ (without leading zeros) one after another. Let $S$ be the set of all positive integers obtained in this way as $m$ ranges over $\mathbb{N}_{\ge 1}$ and the permutation ranges over all $m!$ permutations of $\{1,\dots,m\}$. Arrange $S$ in strictly increasing order as a sequence $s_1<s_2<s_3<\cdots$.

Prove or disprove: for every $n\ge 2$ such that $s_n>1$ is a perfect power (i.e., $s_n=c^k$ for some integers $c\ge 2$ and $k\ge 2$), one must have $k=2$. Equivalently, show that the sequence $(s_n)$ contains no integer of the form $c^k$ with $c\ge 2$ and $k\ge 3$.
status_search_result: The conjecture remains open. It has been verified computationally for all terms below 10111121314151617181920212223456789 with no counterexample, and a partial theoretical result rules out perfect powers when m ≡ 2, 3, 5, 6 (mod 9), but no full proof or disproof is known.

context_brief: Ill-posedness degree of the composite Hausdorff moment operator
original_question: Let J: L2(0,1) -> L2(0,1) be the integration operator [Jx](s) = integral_0^s x(t) dt for 0 <= s <= 1, and let A := B^(H) o J: L2(0,1) -> l2. Is the inverse problem Ax = y moderately ill-posed, in the sense that there exist constants C > 0 and kappa > 0 such that C i^(-kappa) <= sigma_i(A) for all i in N, or is it instead exponentially ill-posed?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L^2(0,1)$ denote the Hilbert space of (equivalence classes of) square-integrable real-valued functions on $(0,1)$ with its standard inner product, and let $\ell^2$ denote the Hilbert space of square-summable real sequences indexed by $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$.

Define the integration operator
$$J:L^2(0,1)\to L^2(0,1),\qquad [Jx](s)=\int_0^s x(t)\,dt,\quad 0\le s\le 1,$$
and the Hausdorff moment operator
$$B^{(H)}:L^2(0,1)\to\ell^2,\qquad B^{(H)}x=\Bigl(\int_0^1 t^{i-1}\,x(t)\,dt\Bigr)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}.$$
Both operators are bounded and linear; $J$ is compact, while $B^{(H)}$ is bounded but non-compact. Consider their composition
$$A:=B^{(H)}\circ J:L^2(0,1)\to\ell^2,$$
which is a compact linear operator with non-closed range. Let $\sigma_1(A)\ge\sigma_2(A)\ge\cdots>0$ denote the singular values of $A$ arranged in non-increasing order.

Call the equation $Ax=y$ moderately ill-posed of degree at most $\kappa$ if there exist constants $C>0$ and $0<\kappa<\infty$ such that
$$C\,i^{-\kappa}\;\le\;\sigma_i(A)\qquad\text{for all }i\in\mathbb{N},$$
and severely ill-posed otherwise; the typical behaviour in the severely ill-posed case being exponential decay $\sigma_i(A)\lesssim e^{-ci}$ for some $c>0$.

Question: Is the equation $Ax=y$ moderately ill-posed (i.e. is there a polynomial lower bound $C\,i^{-\kappa}\le\sigma_i(A)$ for some finite $\kappa$), or is it exponentially (severely) ill-posed?
category_tag: Ill-posed inverse problems and singular value decay
status_search_result: Subsequent work studying compositions of the Hausdorff moment operator with the integration operator established two-sided bounds $e^{-\bar c\, i}\le\sigma_i(A)\le \bar c\, i^{-3/2}$ for large $i$, but explicitly states that it remains unresolved whether the composition is moderately ill-posed or exponentially ill-posed. No publication appears to definitively settle the dichotomy.

context_brief: Singular functions of the composite operator
original_question: For the composite operator A = B^(H) o J : L2(0,1) -> l2, what are the singular functions u_i(A) in L2(0,1) and v_i(A) in l2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $J: L^2(0,1) \to L^2(0,1)$ be the simple integration operator
$$ (Jf)(x) = \int_0^x f(t)\,dt, \qquad x \in (0,1), $$
and let $B^{(H)}: L^2(0,1) \to \ell^2$ be the Hausdorff moment operator
$$ B^{(H)} f = \Bigl( \int_0^1 t^{k-1} f(t)\, dt \Bigr)_{k=1}^{\infty}. $$
Consider the composite operator
$$ A = B^{(H)} \circ J : L^2(0,1) \to \ell^2, $$
so that $(A f)_k = \int_0^1 t^{k-1}\!\left(\int_0^t f(s)\,ds\right) dt$ for $k \ge 1$. The operator $A$ is a compact, injective bounded linear operator with non-closed range, and therefore admits a singular system $\{\sigma_i(A), u_i(A), v_i(A)\}_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, where $\{u_i(A)\} \subset L^2(0,1)$ and $\{v_i(A)\} \subset \ell^2$ are complete orthonormal systems and $\sigma_i(A) > 0$ satisfy
$$ A u_i(A) = \sigma_i(A)\, v_i(A), \qquad A^* v_i(A) = \sigma_i(A)\, u_i(A). $$
Determine the singular functions $u_i(A) \in L^2(0,1)$ and $v_i(A) \in \ell^2$ of $A$ in explicit form.
category_tag: Singular value decomposition of compact operators
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open question concerning the singular system of the composition of the simple integration operator with the Hausdorff moment operator. No closed-form expression for the singular functions of this composite operator appears to be available in the literature; published follow-up work discusses the (still conjectural) decay rate of its singular values rather than explicit eigenfunctions.

context_brief: Operator-norm gap between Hilbert matrix and truncations
original_question: Let H = (1/(i+j-1))_(i,j=1)^infinity be the infinite Hilbert-matrix operator on l2, and let H_n be the n x n Hilbert-matrix truncation extended to an operator on l2 by filling the remaining rows and columns with zeros. How does the operator norm ||H - H_n||_(L(l2,l2)) behave as n increases?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell^2$ denote the Hilbert space of square-summable complex sequences. Consider the infinite Hilbert matrix
$$H = \left(\frac{1}{i+j-1}\right)_{i,j=1}^{\infty},$$
which defines a bounded (non-compact) operator $H : \ell^2 \to \ell^2$ with operator norm $\|H\| = \pi$. For each integer $n \geq 1$, let $H_n$ be the operator on $\ell^2$ whose matrix is obtained by keeping the entries $1/(i+j-1)$ for $1 \le i, j \le n$ and setting all other entries to $0$; in particular $H_n$ has finite rank (hence is compact), so $\|H - H_n\|_{\mathcal{L}(\ell^2,\ell^2)}$ does not tend to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of
$$\|H - H_n\|_{\mathcal{L}(\ell^2,\ell^2)}$$
as a function of $n$. In particular, find explicit upper and lower bounds, and if possible the precise asymptotics or limit, of this operator-norm distance from $H$ to its $n \times n$ principal truncation as $n \to \infty$.
status_search_result: The problem is explicitly stated as an open question in the source. A web search did not surface any published resolution determining the asymptotic behavior of the operator-norm gap between the infinite Hilbert matrix on $\ell^2$ and its $n \times n$ zero-padded principal truncation. Related work concerns norms of (finite) Hilbert matrices and Hilbert matrix operators on analytic function spaces, but not this specific truncation gap.

context_brief: left stones two bones diagonal formula
original_question: Let T012(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T012(3n, 3n) = 2^n n! for every n >= 1?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the (a,b)-benzel, a hexagonal-style region in the triangular lattice depending on positive integers a,b. The allowed prototiles are: a "left stone" and a "right stone" (two shapes of 2-cell tiles), together with "bones," which come in three possible orientations (each a 3-cell straight tribone, one per direction of the triangular lattice). For 0 ≤ i,j ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ k ≤ 3, let T_{ijk}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel using prototiles from the set that includes the right stone iff i=1, the left stone iff j=1, and exactly k of the three bone orientations (one specifies which k of the three are allowed; the count T_{ijk} sums over the symmetry-equivalent classes as conventionally defined).

In the case (i,j,k) = (0,1,2): right stones are forbidden, left stones are allowed, and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Prove or disprove:
$$T_{012}(3n,3n) = 2^n\, n!\quad\text{for every integer } n \geq 1.$$
status_search_result: The conjecture was resolved by Defant, Li, Propp, and Young in subsequent work on benzel tilings (developed via the abacus bijection and generalized compression methods). The original problem statement was annotated as solved, and follow-up papers (arXiv:2209.05717 "Tilings of Benzels via the Abacus Bijection" and arXiv:2403.07663 "Tilings of Benzels via Generalized Compression") establish the relevant enumeration formulas.

original_question: Let T013(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which left stones are allowed, right stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel is negative or zero, must a type-013 tiling exist?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Work in the triangular grid in the plane and consider the associated hexagonal regions called benzels. For positive integers $a,b$, the $(a,b)$-benzel is the region obtained from a centrally symmetric hexagon in the triangular lattice by removing certain corner triangles; concretely, it is the union of unit triangles whose centroids $(x,y)$ satisfy
$$a < x+y < 2b, \qquad a < y+z < 2b, \qquad a < z+x < 2b,$$
where $(x,y,z)$ are barycentric-type coordinates on the triangular grid (so that the region is the standard $(a,b)$-benzel of Propp).

Prototiles. There are two kinds of prototiles:
- Stones: a stone is a tile covering three unit triangles meeting at a common vertex (so it has the shape of a small rhombus-like trio). Stones come in two chiralities, called the left stone and the right stone.
- Bones: a bone (tribone) covers three unit triangles in a row; there are three rotational orientations of the bone.

For $i,j\in\{0,1\}$ and $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ denote the number of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel by prototiles in which the right stone is allowed iff $i=1$, the left stone is allowed iff $j=1$, and exactly $k$ of the three bone orientations are allowed. Such a tiling is called an $(i,j,k)$-tiling.

The Conway–Lagarias invariant $\mathrm{CL}(a,b)$ is the integer invariant of the boundary word of the $(a,b)$-benzel defined (as in Conway–Lagarias) as the signed count obtained from the combinatorial-group-theoretic reduction of the boundary word relative to the relations imposed by the tribones; equivalently, it equals the signed area enclosed by the shadow path associated with the boundary.

Question. Is it true that for every pair $(a,b)$ of positive integers for which $\mathrm{CL}(a,b)\le 0$, there exists at least one $(0,1,3)$-tiling of the $(a,b)$-benzel, i.e. $T_{013}(a,b)\ge 1$?
status_search_result: Propp's benzel problems page lists Problem 4 as "Open" (status updated as of June 2025). Subsequent works on benzel tilings (Kim–Propp pentagonal number theorem; Defant–Li–Propp–Young abacus/compression bijections; the generalized compression paper) address related enumeration questions but do not resolve the existence question for type (0,1,3) tilings whenever the Conway–Lagarias invariant is non-positive.

original_question: Let T103(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which right stones are allowed, left stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T103(n, 2n-3) = (3n+3)(3n-7)!/((n-5)! (2n-1)!) for every n >= 5, with the same formula also yielding 0 for n = 3 and n = 4 if one formally interprets 1/(-1)! and 1/(-2)! as 0?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider the triangular lattice and the unit hexagonal cells dual to it. For positive integers $a,b$ with appropriate parity, the $(a,b)$-benzel is a specific finite, three-fold-symmetric region in the hexagonal grid (it is the union of all unit hexagons whose centers $(x,y,z)$, in a suitable oblique coordinate system on the triangular lattice with $x+y+z=0$, satisfy the three inequalities $\lceil a/3\rceil \le y-z \le b-\lceil a/3\rceil$ together with the two cyclic rotations of this inequality). 

Two kinds of prototiles are considered:
- "Stones": rhombi composed of two adjacent unit hexagons. Up to rotation there are two chiralities, called the right stone and the left stone.
- "Bones" (tribones): three unit hexagons in a straight line; up to rotation there are three orientations.

For $i,j\in\{0,1\}$ and $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ denote the number of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel by prototiles drawn from the set that contains the right stone iff $i=1$, contains the left stone iff $j=1$, and contains exactly $k$ of the three bone orientations (the specific subset of bone orientations being fixed by convention when $k\in\{1,2\}$, all three when $k=3$).

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every integer $n\ge 5$,
$$T_{103}(n,\,2n-3) \;=\; \frac{(3n+3)\,(3n-7)!}{(n-5)!\,(2n-1)!}.$$
Show moreover that, with the convention that $1/(-1)!=1/(-2)!=0$, the same right-hand side correctly evaluates $T_{103}(n,2n-3)=0$ for $n=3$ and $n=4$.

About half of the twenty problems in the list have been resolved by various authors (Defant, Li, Propp, Young, Byun, Ciucu, Lee), but Problem 6 — the conjectured closed form for $T_{103}(n,2n-3)$ — is not among the resolved ones. - three "bones," each a different orientation of another trimer (covering three unit triangles).

original_question: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T112(n+2, 2n+1) equals the nth large Schroder number for every n >= 1?
self_contained_problem:
Fix the triangular lattice in the plane and consider its three families of unit rhombi (lozenges), called "stones" of two chiralities (left stone and right stone) and "bones" of three orientations (horizontal, rising, and falling). For positive integers a, b, the (a,b)-benzel is a certain hexagonally-symmetric region in the triangular lattice (the standard benzel region parameterized by a and b) which can be tiled by combinations of stones and bones.

For 0 ≤ i, j ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ k ≤ 3, define T_{ijk}(a,b) to be the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel using prototiles drawn from the following allowed set:
- the right stone is allowed iff i = 1,
- the left stone is allowed iff j = 1,
- exactly k of the three bone orientations are allowed (with the chosen k orientations specified by the context defining T_{ijk}).

In particular, T_{1,1,2}(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which both stone orientations and exactly two of the three bone orientations are permitted.

The n-th large Schröder number S_n is defined by S_0 = 1 and the generating function
   ∑_{n≥0} S_n x^n = (1 - x - √(1 - 6x + x²)) / (2x),
giving the sequence 1, 2, 6, 22, 90, 394, ….

Prove or disprove: for every integer n ≥ 1,
   T_{1,1,2}(n + 2, 2n + 1) = S_n.

context_brief: unique all-tiles tiling when a+b=1 mod 3
original_question: Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever a+b is congruent to 1 modulo 3, is it true that T113(a,b) = 1, so that the region has exactly one tiling?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of planar regions known as benzels, defined as follows. Working in the triangular grid in the plane, the (a,b)-benzel (for positive integers a,b) is a hexagonal-like region obtained by intersecting suitable half-planes; concretely it is composed of unit triangles and admits tilings by certain prototiles. The allowed prototiles are of two types:
 - Stones: small rhombic tiles of two chiralities, the "right stone" and the "left stone".
 - Bones: elongated tiles in three possible orientations.

For 0 ≤ i, j ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ k ≤ 3, let T_{ijk}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone if and only if i = 1, contains the left stone if and only if j = 1, and contains exactly k of the three bone orientations.

In particular, T_{113}(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel where both stone chiralities and all three bone orientations are permitted.

Prove or disprove: whenever a + b ≡ 1 (mod 3), one has T_{113}(a,b) = 1; that is, the (a,b)-benzel admits exactly one tiling, which necessarily uses only right-pointing stones (since in this congruence class the Conway–Lagarias invariant equals the area of the region).
status_search_result: The problem has been resolved affirmatively. A subsequent paper proves (as its Theorem 1.1) that when a+b ≡ 1 (mod 3), the (a,b)-benzel admits a unique tiling, consisting entirely of right-pointing stones. This corresponds to the case where the Conway–Lagarias invariant matches the region's area, forcing a unique tiling.

original_question: Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $a,b\ge 1$ and consider the $(a,b)$-benzel, a hexagonal-grid region defined as follows. Place a regular triangular grid in the plane and consider the set of unit upward and downward triangles whose centroids lie in a certain trapezoidal/hexagonal region parameterized by $(a,b)$ (the "$(a,b)$-benzel"). The allowed prototiles are:
- two "stones": the right stone and the left stone, each a rhombus formed by gluing two unit triangles in one of two reflected orientations;
- three "bones": tribones (each a connected union of three unit triangles in a straight or bent shape) in their three possible orientations.

For $i,j\in\{0,1\}$ and $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ denote the number of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel by prototiles drawn from the set that contains the right stone iff $i=1$, contains the left stone iff $j=1$, and contains exactly $k$ of the three bone orientations.

Define the sequence
$$f(n) = T_{113}(n,\, 2n-3), \qquad n\ge 4,$$
which counts tilings of the $(n,2n-3)$-benzel when both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed.

A function $f:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is said to be $2$-adically continuous if it extends to a continuous function $\mathbb{Z}_2\to\mathbb{Z}_2$ with respect to the $2$-adic metric; equivalently, for every $r\ge 0$ there exists $M\ge 0$ such that $n\equiv n'\pmod{2^M}$ implies $f(n)\equiv f(n')\pmod{2^r}$.

Question: Is $f(n)=T_{113}(n,2n-3)$ a $2$-adically continuous function of $n\ge 4$?

original_question: Let T113(a,b;3) denote the weighted sum of all tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations and all three bone orientations are allowed, where a tiling with m stones has weight 3^m. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3; 3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of "benzel" regions in the triangular lattice indexed by pairs of positive integers $(a,b)$. A benzel can be tiled using two kinds of pieces: "stones" (with two possible orientations) and "bones" (with three possible orientations). For nonnegative integers $i,j,k \in \{0,1\}$ (with at least one nonzero), let $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ denote the set of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel that use stones in (any of) the orientations indicated by $i$ and $j$ and bones in the orientations indicated by $k$ (so $T_{113}(a,b)$ allows both stone orientations and all three bone orientations).

For a positive integer parameter, define the weighted tiling count
$$T_{113}(a,b;3) \;=\; \sum_{\tau} 3^{m(\tau)},$$
where the sum runs over all tilings $\tau$ of the $(a,b)$-benzel that use both stone orientations and all three bone orientations, and $m(\tau)$ is the number of stones in $\tau$.

A function $f:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is said to be \emph{$2$-adically continuous} if it extends to a continuous function from $\mathbb{Z}_2$ to $\mathbb{Z}_2$; equivalently, for every $k\ge 0$ there exists $M$ such that whenever $n\equiv n'\pmod{2^M}$ (with $n,n'\ge N$), one has $f(n)\equiv f(n')\pmod{2^k}$.

Question: Is the sequence $\bigl(T_{113}(n,2n-3;3)\bigr)_{n\ge 4}$ $2$-adically continuous as a function of $n$?

context_brief: 2-adic limit for stone tilings of triangular regions
original_question: Let T_n be the triangular region of hexagonal cells with n cells on each side. When stones alone are used as tiles, Conway, Lagarias, and Thurston showed that T_n is tileable exactly for n congruent to 0, 2, 9, or 11 modulo 12. As n tends to infinity through those congruence classes, does the number of stone tilings of T_n converge 2-adically to 0?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the triangular hexagonal region $T_n$ defined as follows: $T_n$ is the union of unit regular hexagonal cells arranged so that the region has the shape of an equilateral triangle with $n$ hexagonal cells along each side. A "stone" (also called a $T_2$ tile) is the shape obtained by gluing three hexagonal cells together so as to form a small triangular region with two cells on each side (there are two orientations, "left-pointing" and "right-pointing"). A "stone tiling" of $T_n$ is a tiling of $T_n$ using only stones (in either orientation), with no other tile shapes allowed.

It is known that $T_n$ admits a stone tiling if and only if $n \equiv 0, 2, 9,$ or $11 \pmod{12}$. For each such $n$, let $a(n)$ denote the number of distinct stone tilings of $T_n$.

For an integer $m \ne 0$, let $v_2(m)$ denote the 2-adic valuation of $m$ (the largest $k$ such that $2^k \mid m$), and define the 2-adic absolute value by $|m|_2 = 2^{-v_2(m)}$ and $|0|_2 = 0$. We say a sequence of integers converges 2-adically to $0$ if its 2-adic absolute values tend to $0$, equivalently if $v_2$ of its terms tends to $\infty$.

Question: As $n \to \infty$ ranging over positive integers with $n \equiv 0, 2, 9,$ or $11 \pmod{12}$, does $a(n) \to 0$ in the 2-adic metric? Equivalently, does $v_2(a(n)) \to \infty$?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a list of unsolved tiling problems by Propp. Related 2-adic conjectures about tilings (e.g., for Aztec diamonds and benzels) are actively studied, but no proof or disproof of this specific 2-adic convergence statement for stone tilings of T_n was located. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
original_question: How can model selection for biological systems be made statistically principled and computationally tractable when alternative models may have different effective parameter subspaces, many models can be nearly indistinguishable on available data, and the space of plausible models may not have any clear finite upper bound?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{M} = \{M_i\}_{i \in I}$ be a (possibly countably infinite) collection of candidate probabilistic models for a biological system. Each model $M_i$ specifies a parameter space $\Theta_i$ (which may have different dimensions and structure for different $i$) and a likelihood $p(D \mid \theta_i, M_i)$ for observed data $D$, together with a prior $\pi_i(\theta_i)$ on $\Theta_i$. A Bayesian model-selection procedure assigns prior probabilities $\{P(M_i)\}_{i \in I}$ with $\sum_i P(M_i) = 1$ and produces posterior probabilities
$$P(M_i \mid D) \;=\; \frac{P(M_i)\, \int_{\Theta_i} p(D\mid \theta_i, M_i)\, \pi_i(\theta_i)\, d\theta_i}{\sum_{j\in I} P(M_j)\, \int_{\Theta_j} p(D\mid \theta_j, M_j)\, \pi_j(\theta_j)\, d\theta_j}.$$
Three obstacles arise simultaneously:
(i) the index set $I$ has no natural finite upper bound and may need to be taken infinite;
(ii) different models may have effective parameter subspaces of differing dimensions, so that marginal likelihoods involve integrals over spaces that are not directly comparable;
(iii) on the data $D$ actually available, many models in $\mathcal{M}$ may yield nearly identical likelihoods, making them practically indistinguishable.

Devise a model-selection framework — specifying the choice of model prior $\{P(M_i)\}$, the within-model priors $\pi_i$, and an algorithm for computing or approximating the posterior $P(M_i\mid D)$ — that is (a) statistically principled (consistent and calibrated under reasonable assumptions on the data-generating process, and invariant under natural reparametrizations of $\Theta_i$), (b) computationally tractable for realistic biological data sets, and (c) robust to near-indistinguishability of models, in the sense that it explicitly quantifies and reports the resulting uncertainty rather than collapsing it onto a single model. Prove guarantees (e.g.\ consistency, contraction rates, or risk bounds) for the proposed framework.
status_search_result: Bayesian model selection over potentially infinite model spaces with non-nested parameter subspaces and near-indistinguishable alternatives is a longstanding foundational problem in Bayesian statistics. No general principled and computationally tractable solution is known; existing techniques (RJMCMC, nonparametric Bayes, ABC model choice, stacking, Bayesian model averaging) address parts of the problem but each has known limitations. The problem remains open as posed.

paper_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
original_question: How can biological model-development pipelines automatically generate, update, and compare large families of candidate models starting from a seed model while keeping the process reproducible and keeping parameter estimation and trans-dimensional model selection computationally feasible at each step?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an iterative pipeline for constructing mathematical models of biological systems. The pipeline starts from a seed model M(0) (for example a small system of ordinary or stochastic differential equations, a reaction network, or an agent-based rule set describing a biological process) and at each step i produces a family of candidate successor models {M(i+1,k)} by applying a set of symbolic rewriting operations (such as adding/removing species, splitting/merging variables, refining kinetic laws, or coupling submodels). Each candidate model has its own parameter space Θ(i+1,k) of possibly different dimension, and is to be fitted to a fixed corpus of experimental data D via a likelihood or approximate-likelihood L(D | M, θ).

Design an algorithmic framework that, simultaneously:

1. Automatically generates and updates large families of such candidate models from the seed M(0) under explicit rewriting rules, in a reproducible way (i.e. the same inputs and random seeds reproduce the same sequence of model families).

2. Performs parameter estimation for each candidate model at each step in a way whose total computational cost grows sub-exponentially with the depth i of the pipeline and with the size of the candidate family, despite the fact that conventional per-model maximum-likelihood or fully Bayesian fitting would be prohibitive.

3. Performs trans-dimensional model selection, i.e. statistical comparison between successive models M(i) and M(i+1,k) whose parameter spaces differ in dimension, with well-defined and consistent selection criteria (e.g. generalisations of reversible-jump Bayes factors, marginal likelihoods, or information criteria) whose computation remains feasible at each step.

Specifically: produce such a framework and prove, under stated regularity assumptions on the rewriting rules, the data-generating process, and the priors, (a) convergence or consistency guarantees for the model-selection procedure as data accumulate; (b) explicit computational complexity bounds per pipeline step; and (c) a notion of reproducibility making the entire automated trajectory of model families a deterministic functional of the seed model, the data, the rewriting rules, and the random seeds.
category_tag: automated model development and trans-dimensional model selection
status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad open challenge for the field of mathematical/systems biology: there is active research on automated model discovery (e.g. SINDy, symbolic regression, equation learning, ABC and reversible-jump MCMC for model selection), but no framework is known that simultaneously achieves reproducible automated model rewriting, scalable parameter estimation, and rigorous trans-dimensional model comparison with the guarantees requested. No publication appears to claim a complete resolution.

paper_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
original_question: How can submodels for gene regulation, metabolism, the cell cycle, mechanics, electrophysiology, and transport be linked into modular multiscale or whole-cell models that remain thermodynamically consistent across interfaces, especially when conservation laws and bond-graph structure must be respected?
self_contained_problem:
Develop a mathematical framework for coupling submodels of distinct cellular processes — gene regulation, metabolism, the cell cycle, mechanics, electrophysiology, and transport — into a single multiscale or whole-cell model that satisfies the following requirements:

(i) Each submodel is described as an open dynamical system that exchanges energy and matter with its environment through well-defined interface variables (effort/flow pairs in the sense of bond graphs, e.g., chemical potential and molar flow, voltage and current, force and velocity).

(ii) Each submodel is individually thermodynamically consistent: its constitutive relations derive from a free-energy (or entropy) potential so that, in isolation, it satisfies the first and second laws of thermodynamics and respects mass, charge, and energy conservation laws.

(iii) When any finite collection of these submodels is interconnected by identifying compatible interface variables, the resulting composite system is again thermodynamically consistent and continues to respect all conservation laws — i.e., consistency is preserved under composition (modularity).

(iv) The construction must accommodate the multiple time scales (fast biochemical kinetics, slower regulatory dynamics, cell-cycle and mechanical scales) and the heterogeneous formalisms (ODE chemical kinetics, stoichiometric/flux-balance models, continuum mechanics, cable/Hodgkin–Huxley type equations, reaction–diffusion transport) found across the submodels, possibly via principled model-reduction operations that themselves preserve thermodynamic consistency.

Problem: Construct such a compositional, thermodynamically-consistent modular framework (specifying admissible interfaces, composition rules, and reduction operations), and prove that arbitrary interconnections of submodels drawn from the above classes yield whole-cell models obeying the first and second laws together with all relevant conservation laws.
status_search_result: Recent work on bond-graph approaches to systems biology (e.g., Gawthrop, Pan, Crampin and collaborators, 2021–2025) has established modular, thermodynamically consistent formulations that unify stoichiometry, thermodynamics and kinetics for biochemical networks, and has begun coupling gene-regulation submodels to metabolic submodels with built-in resource competition and retroactivity. However, a fully general framework spanning all listed domains (cell cycle, mechanics, electrophysiology, transport) within a single whole-cell model, together with consistency-preserving reductions across scales, remains an active research goal rather than a completed result.

paper_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
original_question: What mathematically adequate genotype-to-phenotype maps are needed to explain how genes, gene expression, and their interactions produce phenotypes and complex diseases, especially when evolutionary dynamics combine deterministic selection, stochastic effects, and potentially omnigenic inheritance?
self_contained_problem:
Develop a mathematically rigorous framework for genotype-to-phenotype (GP) maps with the following requirements. Let $G$ denote a space of genotypes (e.g., sequences over a finite alphabet, or vectors of allele states across many loci), let $E$ denote an environment space, and let $P$ denote a phenotype space (which may be high-dimensional, continuous, or include disease states). A GP map is a (possibly stochastic) map $\varphi: G 	imes E 	o \mathcal{P}(P)$, where $\mathcal{P}(P)$ is the space of probability measures on $P$, that should incorporate:

1. Gene expression dynamics: an intermediate transcriptomic/proteomic layer $T$ with maps $G 	imes E 	o \mathcal{P}(T) 	o \mathcal{P}(P)$ encoding regulatory networks and gene–gene interactions (epistasis).
2. Omnigenic inheritance: the contribution to a typical complex phenotype is spread across a very large fraction of loci, so the map must remain well-defined and tractable when essentially all coordinates of $G$ contribute non-trivially to $\varphi$.
3. Evolutionary dynamics: a stochastic process $(G_t)_{t \ge 0}$ on $G$ combining deterministic selection driven by a fitness functional $F: \mathcal{P}(P) 	o \mathbb{R}$ pulled back through $\varphi$, together with stochastic effects (mutation, recombination, genetic drift in finite populations).

Problem: Construct such a class of GP maps $\varphi$, together with the associated evolutionary stochastic dynamics, satisfying the following properties:
(a) Identifiability/learnability from realistic genomic and phenotypic data.
(b) Predictive power for the distribution of complex phenotypes and disease risks given $G$ and $E$.
(c) Compatibility with omnigenic architectures (i.e., the model class does not collapse or become statistically vacuous when the number of contributing loci is comparable to the genome size).
(d) A rigorous limit theorem describing the long-time behavior of the induced phenotype distribution under the combined deterministic selection and stochastic mutation/drift dynamics.

Provide either an explicit construction meeting (a)–(d) or prove obstructions showing that no such GP map class can simultaneously satisfy them.
status_search_result: This is a broad foundational research direction in mathematical and evolutionary biology rather than a precisely formulated conjecture. No construction or impossibility result is known that simultaneously satisfies identifiability, predictive power for complex traits, compatibility with omnigenic architectures, and a rigorous limit theorem under combined deterministic and stochastic evolutionary dynamics; the question remains an active open problem.

paper_title: Open Problems in Mathematical Biology
original_question: What general theory of life can supply a mathematical definition of life together with general concepts and principles for living systems, rather than leaving biology with isolated descriptions that do not amount to a unified account of life as such?
self_contained_problem: Formulate a general mathematical theory of life. Specifically: provide a rigorous mathematical definition of "life" (i.e., a precise mathematical predicate, structure, or class of objects within some specified ambient formalism—such as dynamical systems, stochastic processes, information-theoretic structures, category-theoretic objects, or other—that distinguishes living systems from non-living ones), together with a coherent collection of general concepts, axioms, and principles from which the qualitative and quantitative properties of living systems can be derived. The theory should be universal in the sense that it applies to all living systems (not tied to terrestrial biochemistry), and it should unify biological phenomena under a single account rather than leaving them as a collection of isolated descriptive models.
status_search_result: No accepted general mathematical theory or definition of life exists. Multiple frameworks (autopoiesis, (M,R)-systems, assembly theory, free-energy principle, autocatalytic-set theory) propose partial answers, but none has been generally accepted as supplying a unified mathematical definition with derivable principles. Recent surveys and the assembly-theory literature continue to treat the problem as open.

original_question: How can mathematical biology reach the level of mathematical maturity needed for living systems by developing rigorous biological definitions, using theorem-proof style arguments where appropriate, and creating genuinely new mathematical theory rather than relying mainly on imported or ad hoc methods?
self_contained_problem: Develop a programmatic framework for raising the mathematical maturity of the study of living systems. Specifically, propose how to: (i) formulate rigorous, intrinsically biological definitions (of objects such as cell, organism, population, fitness, function, regulation, adaptation) suitable to serve as primitive notions in a definition–theorem–proof style theory; (ii) identify settings within mathematical biology in which theorem–proof arguments can replace heuristic or simulation-based reasoning, and exhibit prototypical theorems with complete proofs; and (iii) construct genuinely new mathematical theory tailored to biological phenomena, rather than relying on the direct importation of techniques from physics, engineering, or other established fields.
