original_question: When a non-reduced scheme X occurs as the eigenscheme of a tensor, what degrees can the irreducible components of X have, and which schemes can appear as such irreducible components?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space of dimension $n+1$ and let $T \in \mathrm{Sym}^d(V^*) \otimes V$ (equivalently, a partially symmetric tensor, or a homogeneous polynomial map $\mathbb{C}^{n+1} \to \mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ of degree $d-1$ in each coordinate). An eigenvector of $T$ is a nonzero $v \in V$ such that $T(v,\ldots,v) = \lambda v$ for some scalar $\lambda$. The eigenscheme $X = X(T) \subset \mathbb{P}(V) = \mathbb{P}^n$ is the projective subscheme defined by the $2\times 2$ minors of the $(n+1)\times 2$ matrix whose columns are the coordinate vector and $T(v,\ldots,v)$; equivalently, the scheme cut out by the polynomials $v_i\, T(v,\ldots,v)_j - v_j\, T(v,\ldots,v)_i$ for all $i,j$.

Suppose the eigenscheme $X$ is non-reduced. Determine:

(a) the possible degrees that an irreducible component of $X$ may have;
(b) which projective subschemes of $\mathbb{P}^n$ can occur as an irreducible component of such a non-reduced eigenscheme $X$.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about the structure of non-reduced eigenschemes of tensors. Web searches did not surface a published resolution classifying the possible degrees or schemes appearing as irreducible components of non-reduced eigenschemes. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Given real vector spaces V1,...,Vd with dim(Vi)=ni+1, does there exist a tensor T ∈ V1⊗···⊗Vd such that all c(n) critical points (equivalently singular tuples in the cited setup) are real?
self_contained_problem:
Let $V_1,\dots,V_d$ be real vector spaces with $\dim V_i = n_i+1$, and write $\mathbf{n}=(n_1,\dots,n_d)$. Equip each $V_i$ with the standard inner product, and equip $V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_d$ with the induced inner product. A singular vector tuple (equivalently, a critical rank-one tuple) of a tensor $T\in V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_d$ is a tuple of nonzero vectors $(v_1,\dots,v_d)\in V_1\times\cdots\times V_d$, considered up to simultaneous rescaling, that is a critical point of the function $(v_1,\dots,v_d)\mapsto \langle T,\,v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_d\rangle$ restricted to the product of unit spheres $S(V_1)\times\cdots\times S(V_d)$. For a generic tensor $T$ over the complex numbers, the number of complex singular vector tuples is a finite constant $c(\mathbf{n})$ depending only on $\mathbf{n}$, given by an explicit formula of Friedland–Ottaviani.

Question: Does there exist a real tensor $T\in V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes V_d$ all of whose $c(\mathbf{n})$ singular vector tuples are real (i.e., such that every complex critical point is in fact defined over $\mathbb{R}$)?
status_search_result: The question of total reality of singular vector tuples of tensors (analogous to real eigenvalue problems / real enumerative geometry) appears to be an active open question in tensor decomposition / applied algebraic geometry. Recent works (e.g., on decomposing tensors via rank-one approximations and on the span of singular tuples) treat related aspects but do not report a resolution of whether a real tensor with all $c(\mathbf{n})$ singular tuples real exists in general formats.

context_brief: ED degree of secant rational normal curve
original_question: Compute EDdeg(σ_2(v_d(P^1))), i.e., the Euclidean distance degree of the secant variety of the rational normal curve in P^d.
self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 3$ be an integer and let $v_d \colon \mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^d$ denote the degree-$d$ Veronese embedding, whose image $C_d = v_d(\mathbb{P}^1) \subset \mathbb{P}^d$ is the rational normal curve of degree $d$. Define the second secant variety
$$\sigma_2(C_d) \;=\; \overline{\bigcup_{p,q \in C_d} \overline{pq}} \;\subset\; \mathbb{P}^d,$$
i.e., the Zariski closure of the union of all (projective) lines spanned by two points of $C_d$.

For an affine cone $X \subset \mathbb{C}^{d+1}$ over a projective variety in $\mathbb{P}^d$, and a generic point $u \in \mathbb{C}^{d+1}$, the Euclidean distance degree $\mathrm{EDdeg}(X)$ is the number of complex critical points of the squared-distance function $x \mapsto \sum_{i=0}^{d}(x_i - u_i)^2$ on the smooth locus of $X$.

Determine, as an explicit function of $d$, the Euclidean distance degree
$$\mathrm{EDdeg}\bigl(\sigma_2(v_d(\mathbb{P}^1))\bigr).$$
category_tag: Euclidean distance degree of secant varieties

Kayser scheduled for January 2026 is titled "Euclidean distance degrees of secant varieties to the rational normal curve," indicating the problem is being actively studied. A December 2025 preprint proves an ED-degree formula for curves parametrized by rational functions and could in principle apply, but its abstract does not explicitly resolve this case. No definitive solution is verified.

original_question: Determine whether the border Waring class is contained in the border Chow class; more modestly, prove non-trivial upper bounds for border Waring rank RV(f) in terms of border Chow rank RCh(f).
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, and let $f \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_d$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $d \ge 1$.

Define the Waring rank $R_V(f)$ to be the minimal integer $r$ such that there exist linear forms $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_r \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_1$ with
$$ f = \ell_1^d + \ell_2^d + \cdots + \ell_r^d. $$
Define the Chow rank $R_{Ch}(f)$ to be the minimal integer $s$ such that there exist linear forms $\ell_{i,j} \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_1$ ($1\le i\le s,\,1\le j\le d$) with
$$ f = \sum_{i=1}^{s} \prod_{j=1}^{d} \ell_{i,j}. $$

The border Waring rank $\underline{R}_V(f)$ is the smallest $r$ such that $f$ lies in the Zariski closure of the set of degree-$d$ forms of Waring rank at most $r$; equivalently, the smallest $r$ such that there exist linear forms $\ell_i(\varepsilon)$ depending polynomially on $\varepsilon$ with
$$ f = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \sum_{i=1}^{r} \ell_i(\varepsilon)^d $$
(or, equivalently, $\varepsilon^N f(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{r} \ell_i(\varepsilon,x)^d$ modulo $\varepsilon^{N+1}$ for some $N$). The border Chow rank $\underline{R}_{Ch}(f)$ is defined analogously, replacing $d$-th powers $\ell_i^d$ by products $\prod_{j=1}^{d}\ell_{i,j}$.

Let
$$ \mathcal{V}_{\text{Waring}} = \{\,f : \underline{R}_V(f) < \infty \text{ with bound polynomial in the input size}\,\}, \qquad \mathcal{V}_{\text{Chow}} = \{\,f : \underline{R}_{Ch}(f) < \infty \text{ with bound polynomial in the input size}\,\} $$
be the corresponding complexity classes of polynomial sequences with polynomially bounded border Waring rank and border Chow rank, respectively.

(a) Determine whether $\mathcal{V}_{\text{Waring}} \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{\text{Chow}}$.

(b) More modestly, prove non-trivial upper bounds for $\underline{R}_V(f)$ in terms of $\underline{R}_{Ch}(f)$ (or vice versa) for an arbitrary degree-$d$ homogeneous polynomial $f$.
status_search_result: Recent work on debordering Waring rank (e.g., bounds of the form WR(f) ≤ d·r^{O(√r)} improving earlier d·4^r and d^r bounds) addresses Waring vs border-Waring rank, but does not establish the inclusion of the border Waring class in the border Chow class nor give non-trivial bounds of border Waring rank in terms of border Chow rank. No source found resolves the comparison of these two border-complexity classes, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Apply and develop the geometric complexity theory (GCT) representation-theoretic obstruction framework for the variety IMMr,V of small algebraic branching programs.
self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and let $r \ge 1$. Consider the space $V^{\otimes d}$ (or, more generally, the affine space of tensors/polynomials computed by width-$r$ algebraic branching programs over $V$). An algebraic branching program (ABP) of width $r$ computing a polynomial $f$ is a directed acyclic layered graph with a source and a sink, in which each edge is labelled by an affine linear form in the variables of $V$ and each internal layer has at most $r$ vertices; the polynomial computed is the sum over source-to-sink paths of the product of the edge labels. Equivalently, width-$r$ ABPs of length $d$ compute the (1,1)-entry of an iterated product $A_1 A_2 \cdots A_d$ of $r \times r$ matrices whose entries are affine linear forms.

Define the variety
$$\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V} \;:=\; \overline{\{\, f \in \mathrm{Sym}^d V^* : f \text{ is computed by some width-}r \text{ ABP over } V\,\}} \;\subseteq\; \mathrm{Sym}^d V^*,$$
where the closure is taken in the Zariski topology. The group $\mathrm{GL}(V)$ acts naturally on $\mathrm{Sym}^d V^*$, and the coordinate ring $\mathbb{C}[\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}]$ decomposes as a direct sum of irreducible $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-modules indexed by partitions $\lambda$, with multiplicities $m_\lambda(\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V})$.

A representation-theoretic obstruction to a polynomial $g \in \mathrm{Sym}^d V^*$ lying in $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$ is a partition $\lambda$ such that the multiplicity of the irreducible $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-module $S_\lambda V^*$ in the coordinate ring of the $\mathrm{GL}(V)$-orbit closure of $g$ strictly exceeds $m_\lambda(\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V})$.

Problem. Develop and carry out the geometric complexity theory (GCT) program for the variety $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$: determine, or give effectively computable bounds on, the multiplicities $m_\lambda(\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V})$ for all partitions $\lambda$, and use these to exhibit representation-theoretic obstructions separating explicit polynomial families (such as the permanent or other hard polynomials) from $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$ for suitable values of $r$.
status_search_result: The GCT program for the iterated matrix multiplication / small-width ABP variety remains an active open research direction. Geometric and representation-theoretic properties of IMM have been investigated (e.g. its symmetry group, dual variety, and Jacobian loci), and occurrence obstructions have been studied — with the Occurrence Obstruction Conjecture for permanent vs. determinant having been refuted, in part via results showing that partitions occurring in the IMM coordinate ring also occur for the permanent. However, no full implementation of the GCT obstruction framework for $\mathrm{IMM}_{r,V}$ yielding super-polynomial VP vs. VNP-type lower bounds is known.

original_question: Study the geometry of the variety of uniform (translation-invariant) matrix product states with periodic boundary conditions, and systematically derive families of equations using properties of the trace algebra.
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $d, D \geq 2$ and $n \geq 1$. For matrices $A_1, \dots, A_d \in \mathrm{Mat}_{D \times D}(\mathbb{C})$, define the uniform (translation-invariant) matrix product state with periodic boundary conditions as the tensor
$$T(A_1,\dots,A_d) \;=\; \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_n=1}^{d} \operatorname{tr}(A_{i_1} A_{i_2} \cdots A_{i_n})\, e_{i_1} \otimes e_{i_2} \otimes \cdots \otimes e_{i_n} \;\in\; (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes n},$$
where $\{e_1,\dots,e_d\}$ is the standard basis of $\mathbb{C}^d$. Let $\mathrm{uMPS}_{d,D,n} \subseteq (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes n}$ denote the Zariski closure of the image of the map $(A_1,\dots,A_d) \mapsto T(A_1,\dots,A_d)$, viewed as an algebraic variety.

Recall that the trace algebra is the ring of $\mathrm{GL}_D$-invariant polynomial functions on $\mathrm{Mat}_{D\times D}(\mathbb{C})^{\oplus d}$ under simultaneous conjugation, generated by traces of words in the matrices $A_1,\dots,A_d$ (by results of Procesi and Sibirskii), with relations described by the trace ideal.

Problem: Investigate the geometry of the variety $\mathrm{uMPS}_{d,D,n}$ — including its dimension, singular locus, identifiability properties, and ideal of defining equations — and develop systematic methods, based on the structure of the trace algebra and the relations among trace monomials, for producing families of polynomial equations vanishing on $\mathrm{uMPS}_{d,D,n}$.
status_search_result: The problem is an active research program. Partial progress has been made (e.g., Czaplinski–Michalek–Seynnaeve studied topology, defining equations, and identifiability for uMPS; earlier work by Critch–Morton connected trace algebras to MPS), but a complete description of the variety and a systematic derivation of all its defining equations via the trace algebra remains open.

original_question: Determine the border subrank of a generic tensor, and characterize conditions under which a tensor has border subrank strictly higher than the generic value.
self_contained_problem:
Let $T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$ be a $d$-way tensor over the complex numbers. The subrank $Q(T)$ is the largest integer $r$ such that the diagonal tensor $\langle r \rangle := \sum_{i=1}^r e_i^{\otimes d}$ can be obtained from $T$ by applying linear maps $A_1, \ldots, A_d : \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^r$ in each tensor factor, i.e., $(A_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d)\, T = \langle r \rangle$. The border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ is the largest integer $r$ such that $\langle r \rangle$ lies in the Euclidean (equivalently Zariski) closure of the set of tensors obtainable from $T$ in this way; equivalently, $\underline{Q}(T) \geq r$ if there exist families of linear maps $A_i(\varepsilon)$ depending polynomially on $\varepsilon$ with $\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0}(A_1(\varepsilon) \otimes \cdots \otimes A_d(\varepsilon))\,T = \langle r \rangle$.

(a) Determine the exact value of the border subrank $\underline{Q}(T)$ for a generic tensor $T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$, as a function of $n$ and $d$.

(b) Give explicit (algebraic or geometric) conditions on a tensor $T \in (\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$ that characterize when $\underline{Q}(T)$ is strictly greater than this generic value.
status_search_result: Recent work (2024) established that the generic border subrank of a tensor in $(\mathbb{C}^n)^{\otimes d}$ has growth rate $\Theta(n^{1/(d-1))})$, matching the generic subrank asymptotically, via a generalized Hilbert–Mumford criterion. However, an exact closed-form value for the generic border subrank for all $n, d$ and explicit conditions characterizing tensors of strictly higher border subrank are not yet fully established, so the problem remains only partially solved.

original_question: Establish non-trivial lower bounds for the generic stabilizer rank stabR_d (the least r such that the relevant symmetric space lies in the span of r stabilizer states).
self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ and consider the $n$-qubit Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_n=(\mathbb{C}^2)^{\otimes n}$. A stabilizer state in $\mathcal{H}_n$ is a unit vector (up to scalar) of the form $U|0\rangle^{\otimes n}$ where $U$ is an element of the $n$-qubit Clifford group; equivalently, it is a joint eigenvector of a maximal abelian subgroup of the Pauli group on $n$ qubits. Denote by $\mathrm{Stab}_n\subset\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{H}_n)$ the (finite) set of stabilizer states. For a vector $v\in\mathcal{H}_n$, the stabilizer rank of $v$ is
$$\chi(v)=\min\Bigl\{r\;:\;v=\sum_{i=1}^r c_i\,s_i,\ c_i\in\mathbb{C},\ s_i\in\mathrm{Stab}_n\Bigr\}.$$

Now fix a degree $d\ge 1$ and consider instead the space $S^d\mathbb{C}^m$ of symmetric tensors of order $d$ on $\mathbb{C}^m$, embedded in the appropriate $n$-qubit (or qudit) tensor space via the standard symmetrization. Define the generic stabilizer rank
$$\mathrm{stabR}_d := \min\bigl\{r\;:\; \text{a generic point of } S^d\mathbb{C}^m \text{ lies in the linear span of } r \text{ stabilizer states}\bigr\},$$
i.e. the least integer $r$ such that the $r$-th secant-like variety obtained as the linear span of $r$ stabilizer states fills (a Zariski-dense subset of) the symmetric space.

Problem. Establish non-trivial lower bounds on $\mathrm{stabR}_d$ as a function of $d$ (and $m$); in particular, prove a lower bound that grows faster than any bound obtainable from elementary dimension-counting arguments.
status_search_result: The problem of obtaining non-trivial lower bounds on stabilizer rank (including its generic/asymptotic forms) remains an active area of research. Recent works (Peleg–Shpilka–Volk 2021; Labib 2022; Lovitz–Steffan 2022; Mehraban–Tahmasbi 2023) have established lower bounds of the form Ω(n) for n-fold tensor products of single-qubit magic states and quadratic lower bounds for approximate stabilizer rank, but the question of non-trivial lower bounds for the generic stabilizer rank in the symmetric setting is still considered open.

paper_title: Private Information Retrieval and Its Applications: An Introduction, Open Problems, Future Directions
original_question: How can private read-write schemes for PRUW and PSU-based FSL be designed so that, in addition to preserving the intended private reading, private writing, and client-side privacy properties of those settings, they remain robust against adversaries and/or eavesdroppers?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a distributed storage system consisting of N non-colluding servers, each storing (coded) copies of a database organized into M sections (submodels). A client wishes to perform a private read-update-write (PRUW) operation: in each round the client (i) downloads the content of a chosen section θ ∈ {1,…,M}, (ii) computes an update, and (iii) writes the update back to section θ, while satisfying:

  (R1) Private reading: each individual server learns nothing about θ from the queries used to read.
  (R2) Private writing: each individual server learns nothing about θ from the uploaded update, and learns nothing about the value of the update itself.
  (R3) Storage consistency: after the write, the stored database equals the previous database with section θ replaced by its updated value.

In the federated submodel learning (FSL) variant, multiple clients participate; the scheme is additionally required to satisfy client-side privacy via private set union (PSU) combined with symmetric PIR (SPIR): the servers should learn only the union of submodel indices updated by the set of clients (or the aggregate of updates to those submodels), and nothing about any individual client's chosen index or update.

Now introduce adversarial parties: a subset A of up to a (out of N) servers may be Byzantine, returning arbitrarily corrupted responses and arbitrarily deviating from the protocol, and an external eavesdropper may observe the transmissions to/from up to e servers. 

Problem: Design PRUW schemes, and PSU+SPIR–based private FSL schemes, that simultaneously
  (a) preserve properties (R1)–(R3) (and, for FSL, client-side privacy as above) against any T-subset of colluding honest-but-curious servers,
  (b) allow the client(s) to correctly recover the desired reads and produce correct updates to the database despite the actions of any a Byzantine servers,
  (c) guarantee that an eavesdropper observing any e of the communication links learns nothing (in the information-theoretic sense) about θ, the read content, or the update,
and characterize the optimal read and write communication rates (capacities) of such schemes as functions of (N, T, a, e, M).
status_search_result: The question is posed as a future research direction for combining adversarial/eavesdropper robustness with PRUW and PSU-based private FSL. While individual robust/Byzantine/eavesdropper PIR results exist, no general capacity-achieving construction for robust PRUW and robust PSU+SPIR-based FSL is established. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Private Information Retrieval and Its Applications: An Introduction, Open Problems, Future Directions
context_brief: Simultaneous private access to multiple FSL submodels
original_question: In federated submodel learning, where a central learning model is divided into multiple submodels so each client downloads and updates only submodels relevant to that client’s local data, if a user has data for training multiple submodels at the same time, is there a private read/write method that lowers the total communication cost of reading and writing multiple submodels simultaneously compared with running the PRUW process separately for each submodel?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a federated submodel learning (FSL) system in which a global machine learning model is partitioned into M disjoint submodels W_1, …, W_M, each W_i consisting of L parameters taking values in a finite field F_q. The submodels are stored across N non-colluding databases using a (possibly coded) storage scheme. Users participate in training as follows: a user with locally available training data relevant to a subset S ⊆ {1, …, M} of the submodels wishes to (a) download the current values of all submodels W_i for i ∈ S (the read phase) and (b) upload an additive update Δ_i ∈ F_q^L to each W_i for i ∈ S so that the storage is updated to W_i + Δ_i (the write phase).

Privacy requirement (Private Read–Update–Write, PRUW). The protocol must guarantee that, from the messages exchanged with any single database, the database learns nothing (in the information-theoretic sense) about: (i) the index set S of submodels the user accesses, and (ii) the values of the uploaded updates {Δ_i : i ∈ S}.

Cost. Let C_read(|S|) and C_write(|S|) denote, respectively, the total number of symbols of F_q downloaded and uploaded by the user during the read and write phases of a PRUW protocol that serves a request of size |S|. Let C_PRUW^single denote the read+write communication cost of the best known PRUW protocol that handles a single submodel (|S| = 1).

Question. Does there exist a PRUW protocol that, when used by a single user to read and update |S| submodels simultaneously, achieves total read+write communication cost strictly less than |S| · C_PRUW^single — i.e., strictly less than the cost of running the single-submodel PRUW protocol |S| separate times — while still satisfying the information-theoretic privacy requirements above? Equivalently, characterize the optimal per-submodel communication rate (or capacity region) for simultaneous PRUW of |S| submodels and determine whether it improves upon the |S|-fold repetition baseline.
status_search_result: Existing PRUW literature (communication-efficient PRUW with/without sparsification, rate–distortion tradeoffs, heterogeneous databases, storage-constrained databases) all addresses the single-submodel-per-user setting. No published work was found that designs or characterizes the capacity of simultaneous PRUW for a user requesting multiple submodels at once, so the question of whether this beats |S|-fold repetition appears to remain open.

paper_title: Private Information Retrieval and Its Applications: An Introduction, Open Problems, Future Directions
context_brief: Writing cost in private epidemiological data collection
original_question: For private epidemiological data collection, a PRUW-related setting with users, databases, and a data collector and with both reading and writing components among those parties, what is the optimal writing cost, meaning the users’ upload cost, complementing prior work that considered the data collector’s download or reading cost?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a private epidemiological data collection system involving three classes of parties: a set of users, a set of N non-colluding databases, and a single data collector. The system stores epidemiological records distributed across the N databases. The protocol proceeds in rounds with two phases:

(Reading phase.) The data collector privately retrieves aggregated information from the databases concerning a chosen statistic, without revealing to any single database which statistic is being queried.

(Writing phase.) Each user privately uploads an update (e.g., an individual epidemiological record or an update to a stored value) to a chosen section/index of the distributed storage across the N databases, in such a way that no single database learns
 (a) the index of the section that is being updated, nor
 (b) the value of the update being written.

For one round of the writing phase, define the writing cost (the users' upload cost) as the total number of symbols (normalized by the size L of one section's update vector, as L → ∞) that the users must transmit to the N databases in order to perform one private update while satisfying the above privacy constraints together with the correctness constraint that, after the writing phase, each database stores the correct (updated) function of the section's contents.

Problem. Determine the information-theoretically optimal (minimum achievable) writing cost in this three-party private epidemiological data collection setting, as a function of the number of databases N and the relevant storage/code parameters, and exhibit a scheme that attains this minimum together with a matching converse.
status_search_result: The question is posed as a future research direction: prior work in this three-party private epidemiological data collection setting analyzed the data collector's download (reading) cost, while the user upload (writing) cost was left as an open problem. A web search did not locate any subsequent work establishing the optimal writing cost in this specific setting, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Can the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms of a given closed manifold be classified up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants, and is topological conjugacy a Borel equivalence relation on that space?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)$ denote the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of $M$ ($r\ge 1$), endowed with the $C^r$ topology (a Polish space). A diffeomorphism $f\in\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)$ is called Kupka–Smale if (i) every periodic point of $f$ is hyperbolic, and (ii) for every pair of periodic points $p,q$ of $f$, the stable manifold $W^s(p)$ and the unstable manifold $W^u(q)$ intersect transversely. Let $\mathrm{KS}(M)\subset\mathrm{Diff}^r(M)$ denote the set of Kupka–Smale diffeomorphisms, with the induced Polish topology. Define the topological conjugacy relation on $\mathrm{KS}(M)$ by
$$f\sim_{\mathrm{top}} g \iff \exists\,h\in\mathrm{Homeo}(M)\ \text{with}\ h\circ f = g\circ h.$$

Answer the following:
(a) Does there exist a complete classification of $(\mathrm{KS}(M),\sim_{\mathrm{top}})$ by Borel-measurable invariants taking values in a standard Borel space — i.e., a Borel map $\Phi:\mathrm{KS}(M)\to X$ into a standard Borel space $X$ such that $f\sim_{\mathrm{top}} g$ if and only if $\Phi(f)=\Phi(g)$?
(b) Is $\sim_{\mathrm{top}}$, viewed as a subset of $\mathrm{KS}(M)\times\mathrm{KS}(M)$, a Borel set?
status_search_result: Recent anti-classification work shows that on closed manifolds of dimension at least 5, topological conjugacy on $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is not a Borel equivalence relation, suggesting strong obstructions to a Borel classification by complete invariants. However, the question as posed specifically for the Kupka–Smale subspace (and for low-dimensional manifolds) does not appear to have been fully resolved in the literature, so it remains at least partially open.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: What is the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of the topological-conjugacy relation for Axiom A dynamical systems?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold and let $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ denote the Polish space of $C^\infty$-diffeomorphisms of $M$. A diffeomorphism $f\in\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ is said to satisfy Smale's Axiom A if its non-wandering set $\Omega(f)$ is hyperbolic and the periodic points of $f$ are dense in $\Omega(f)$. Two diffeomorphisms $f,g\in\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ are topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h\colon M\to M$ with $h\circ f = g\circ h$. This determines an equivalence relation $\cong_{TC}$ on the Borel subset $A(M)\subseteq\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ of Axiom A diffeomorphisms.

Determine the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of the equivalence relation $\cong_{TC}$ on $A(M)$ in the sense of Borel reducibility: in particular, locate this equivalence relation within the hierarchy of Borel/analytic equivalence relations (e.g., whether it is Borel, classifiable by countable structures, reducible to an orbit equivalence relation of a Polish group action, or universal among such relations).
status_search_result: Recent work has determined the Borel complexity of topological conjugacy in related settings — Cantor minimal systems, Toeplitz subshifts, invertible chaotic systems on the Cantor space, and diffeomorphisms on manifolds of dimension at least 2 (shown not classifiable by countable structures). However, no source located pinpoints the precise Borel-reducibility complexity of topological conjugacy specifically restricted to the class of Axiom A systems, so the status of this specific question appears unresolved.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Is the topological-conjugacy relation on the class of all Cantor minimal systems a Borel equivalence relation?
self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ denote the Cantor space (a compact, metrizable, totally disconnected, perfect topological space). A Cantor dynamical system is a pair $(C,T)$ where $T\colon C\to C$ is a homeomorphism. Such a system is called minimal if every orbit $\{T^n(x):n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$ is dense in $C$. Two Cantor dynamical systems $(C,T)$ and $(C,S)$ are topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h\colon C\to C$ such that $h\circ T=S\circ h$.

The space $H(C)$ of all homeomorphisms of $C$, equipped with the uniform convergence topology, is a Polish space, and the set $M(C)\subseteq H(C)$ of minimal homeomorphisms is a Borel (in fact, $G_\delta$) subset. Topological conjugacy defines an equivalence relation $\sim_c$ on $M(C)$, viewed as a subset of $M(C)\times M(C)$.

Question: Is $\sim_c$ a Borel subset of $M(C)\times M(C)$?
status_search_result: Recent work by Deka, García-Ramos, Kasprzak, Kunde, and Kwietniak (announced in 2024) shows that the topological conjugacy relation on Cantor minimal systems is not Borel, thereby answering Gao's question in the negative. Talks and lecture notes from 2024 (e.g., a McGill DDC seminar by K. Deka titled "The topological conjugacy of Cantor minimal systems is not Borel") corroborate this resolution.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: For all minimal subshifts, is topological conjugacy hyperfinite, or is it instead a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let $A$ be a finite alphabet with the discrete topology, and let $A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ be the space of bi-infinite sequences over $A$ with the product topology, on which the shift map $\sigma:A^{\mathbb{Z}}\to A^{\mathbb{Z}}$, $\sigma(x)(n)=x(n+1)$, acts as a homeomorphism. A subshift is a nonempty closed subset $X\subseteq A^{\mathbb{Z}}$ with $\sigma(X)=X$. A subshift $X$ is called minimal if it has no proper nonempty closed shift-invariant subset; equivalently, every $\sigma$-orbit in $X$ is dense in $X$. Two subshifts $(X,\sigma)$ and $(Y,\sigma)$ (possibly over different finite alphabets) are topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h:X\to Y$ with $h\circ\sigma=\sigma\circ h$.

Fix a way of coding minimal subshifts (over varying finite alphabets) as elements of a standard Borel space $\mathcal{M}$ — for example, by coding each minimal subshift via its language, viewed as a closed subset of $\bigcup_{k\geq 1}\bigcup_{n\geq 1}\{1,\dots,k\}^n$. Let $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ be the equivalence relation on $\mathcal{M}$ given by topological conjugacy. Then $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ is a countable Borel equivalence relation.

Recall that a countable Borel equivalence relation $E$ on a standard Borel space $X$ is hyperfinite if $E=\bigcup_n F_n$ where $F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots$ is an increasing sequence of Borel equivalence relations each having finite classes. A countable Borel equivalence relation $E_\infty$ is universal if every countable Borel equivalence relation $F$ Borel reduces to $E_\infty$, i.e., there is a Borel map $f$ with $x\,F\,y\iff f(x)\,E_\infty\,f(y)$.

Question. Is $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ hyperfinite, or is it a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?
category_tag: Descriptive set theory; countable Borel equivalence relations
status_search_result: The problem appears still open. Recent works establish hyperfiniteness only for restricted subclasses (e.g., Toeplitz subshifts with separated holes, generalized Oxtoby subshifts), and surveys explicitly state that for minimal subshifts in general the conjugacy relation is known to be non-smooth but it is not known whether it is hyperfinite or universal.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
context_brief: Almost Borel classification with metric entropy
original_question: Does an analogue of the stated almost-Borel classification remain true when one discards only sets of zero Lebesgue measure and uses metric entropy instead of topological entropy, at least in dimension 2?
self_contained_problem:
Background. A Borel dynamical system is a pair $(X,T)$ where $X$ is a standard Borel space and $T:X\to X$ is a Borel automorphism. Two Borel systems $(X,T)$ and $(Y,S)$ are said to be almost Borel isomorphic modulo a class $\mathcal N$ of "negligible" invariant Borel sets if there exist invariant Borel sets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$ with $X\setminus X_0,\,Y\setminus Y_0\in\mathcal N$ and a Borel bijection $\phi:X_0\to Y_0$ with $\phi\circ T=S\circ\phi$. For a Borel system, the topological entropy refers to the supremum of Kolmogorov–Sinai (metric) entropies $h_\mu(T)$ taken over all $T$-invariant Borel probability measures $\mu$, and the metric entropy refers to $h_\mu(T)$ for a specified invariant measure class.

There is a known almost Borel classification theorem for sufficiently regular (e.g.\ smooth) dynamical systems in which one discards sets that are universally null (negligible for every invariant probability measure) and the invariant under consideration is the topological entropy; this classification realizes such systems, up to almost Borel isomorphism, as universal models built from Bernoulli shifts of prescribed entropies.

Problem. Let $f:M\to M$ be a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a compact smooth surface $M$ (so $\dim M=2$), and equip $M$ with its Lebesgue (smooth volume) measure class. Does there exist an almost Borel classification of such systems, analogous to the one described above, in which:
(i) the negligible class $\mathcal N$ consists only of invariant Borel sets of Lebesgue measure zero (rather than universally null sets), and
(ii) the entropy invariant used is the metric entropy with respect to invariant probability measures (rather than the topological entropy)?

Equivalently, can every $C^\infty$ surface diffeomorphism be classified, up to Borel isomorphism after removing an invariant Borel set of Lebesgue measure zero, by its collection of ergodic invariant measures together with their metric entropies, in the spirit of the existing almost Borel classification?
category_tag: almost Borel classification of smooth dynamics
status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture by Buzzi. While recent work of Buzzi–Crovisier–Sarig provides strong ergodic and measure-theoretic results for $C^\infty$ surface diffeomorphisms (proving Viana's conjecture in dimension 2), no search result indicates that an almost Borel classification modulo Lebesgue-null sets using metric entropy has been established. The status appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Is the measure-isomorphism relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations of the unit interval bi-reducible with the maximal Polish group action?
self_contained_problem:
Let $([0,1], \lambda)$ denote the unit interval equipped with Lebesgue measure. Let $\mathrm{MPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ be the Polish group of (equivalence classes mod null sets of) invertible measure-preserving transformations of $([0,1],\lambda)$, endowed with the weak topology, and let $\mathrm{EMPT}([0,1],\lambda) \subseteq \mathrm{MPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ be the subset of ergodic transformations. Two transformations $S, T \in \mathrm{EMPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ are said to be measure-isomorphic, written $S \cong T$, if there exists $\varphi \in \mathrm{MPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ such that $\varphi \circ S = T \circ \varphi$ almost everywhere; this defines an analytic equivalence relation on $\mathrm{EMPT}([0,1],\lambda)$.

Recall that for analytic equivalence relations $E$ on a Polish space $X$ and $F$ on a Polish space $Y$, $E$ is Borel reducible to $F$, written $E \le_B F$, if there exists a Borel map $f \colon X \to Y$ such that $x \mathrel{E} x' \iff f(x) \mathrel{F} f(x')$. The relations $E$ and $F$ are Borel bi-reducible, $E \sim_B F$, when $E \le_B F$ and $F \le_B E$. An equivalence relation is called a maximal (or universal) orbit equivalence relation induced by a Polish group action if every orbit equivalence relation arising from a continuous action of a Polish group on a Polish space Borel reduces to it; such a maximal relation exists and is unique up to Borel bi-reducibility (e.g., realized by the action of the homeomorphism group of $[0,1]^{\mathbb{N}}$ on a suitable space).

Question: Is the measure-isomorphism equivalence relation on $\mathrm{EMPT}([0,1],\lambda)$ Borel bi-reducible with the maximal orbit equivalence relation induced by a Polish group action?
category_tag: Borel equivalence relations in ergodic theory
status_search_result: Recent work (2025) by Le Maître and Sabok and others has shown partial negative results about reducibility of the isomorphism relation of ergodic measure-preserving transformations to certain Polish group actions (e.g., it is not Borel reducible to the conjugacy action of the full group on itself), but these results do not resolve whether the relation is Borel bi-reducible with the maximal Polish group action. The question appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: For integers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, what is the descriptive complexity of the set CPE^k(T^n) of C^k self-maps of the n-torus with completely positive entropy?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$ and $k \geq 1$ be integers, and let $\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{R}^n / \mathbb{Z}^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional torus. Equip the space $C^k(\mathbb{T}^n, \mathbb{T}^n)$ of $C^k$ self-maps of $\mathbb{T}^n$ with the standard $C^k$ topology, making it a Polish space.

For a continuous self-map $f : X \to X$ of a compact metric space, the topological entropy $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$ is defined in the usual way. A topological factor of $(X,f)$ is a pair $(Y,g)$ with $g : Y \to Y$ continuous on a compact metric space together with a continuous surjection $\pi : X \to Y$ satisfying $\pi \circ f = g \circ \pi$. The factor is called trivial if $|Y| = 1$. The map $f$ is said to have completely positive entropy if every non-trivial topological factor of $(X,f)$ has strictly positive topological entropy.

Define
$$\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n) := \{ f \in C^k(\mathbb{T}^n, \mathbb{T}^n) : f \text{ has completely positive entropy} \}.$$

Determine the descriptive set-theoretic complexity of $\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n)$ as a subset of the Polish space $C^k(\mathbb{T}^n, \mathbb{T}^n)$. In particular, locate this set precisely within the Borel/projective hierarchy (e.g., determine whether it is Borel, and if not, whether it is complete coanalytic).
status_search_result: Related work by Darji and García-Ramos ("Local entropy theory and descriptive complexity", arXiv:2107.09263) shows that for many classes of compact spaces the set of dynamical systems with completely positive entropy is complete coanalytic (hence not Borel), with specific results for the circle, torus and certain compact orientable manifolds in the continuous category. The precise descriptive complexity of $\mathrm{CPE}^k(\mathbb{T}^n)$ within $C^k(\mathbb{T}^n,\mathbb{T}^n)$ for arbitrary $k \geq 1$ and $n \geq 1$ does not appear to have been fully resolved in the literature, and the question is posed as an open problem.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
context_brief: Measures of maximal entropy on T^2
original_question: For every smooth mixing map f ∈ C∞(T^2, T^2), is the measure of maximal entropy fully supported?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^2 = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$ denote the two-dimensional torus, and let $f: \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{T}^2$ be a smooth (i.e. $C^\infty$) map. Recall that $f$ is said to be topologically mixing if for every pair of non-empty open sets $U, V \subseteq \mathbb{T}^2$ there exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $f^{-n}(U) \cap V \neq \emptyset$ for all $n \geq N$. The topological entropy $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$ is defined as usual, and a measure of maximal entropy is an $f$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{T}^2$ with measure-theoretic entropy $h_\mu(f) = h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$. Such a measure $\mu$ is said to be fully supported if $\operatorname{supp}(\mu) = \mathbb{T}^2$.

Question: Is it true that for every smooth topologically mixing map $f \in C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^2, \mathbb{T}^2)$, every measure of maximal entropy of $f$ is fully supported?

original_question: Is the conjugation action of Aut(X, μ) on itself a complete orbit equivalence relation, meaning that every orbit equivalence relation induced by a Borel action of a Polish group on a standard Borel space is Borel reducible to it?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mu)$ be a standard atomless probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish group of measure-preserving automorphisms of $(X,\mu)$ modulo equality almost everywhere, equipped with the weak topology. Consider the conjugation action of $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ on itself, $(g,h)\mapsto g h g^{-1}$, and let $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ be the orbit equivalence relation it induces on $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$.

Recall that for Borel equivalence relations $E$ and $F$ on standard Borel spaces $Y$ and $Z$, $E$ is Borel reducible to $F$ (written $E\le_B F$) if there is a Borel map $f:Y\to Z$ such that $y_1\mathbin{E}y_2 \iff f(y_1)\mathbin{F}f(y_2)$. An orbit equivalence relation $F$ (induced by a Borel action of a Polish group on a standard Borel space) is called a complete orbit equivalence relation if $E\le_B F$ for every orbit equivalence relation $E$ arising from a Borel action of a Polish group on a standard Borel space.

Question: Is $E_{\mathrm{conj}}$ a complete orbit equivalence relation?

- $\sim_{\mathrm{Aut}}$ on $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$: $S \sim_{\mathrm{Aut}} T$ iff there exists $R \in \mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ with $RSR^{-1} = T$;
- $\sim_{[T_0]}$ on $[T_0]$: $U \sim_{[T_0]} V$ iff there exists $W \in [T_0]$ with $WUW^{-1} = V$.

Let $(I,\lambda)$ denote the unit interval equipped with Lebesgue measure, and for each integer $n\ge 1$ let $(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ denote the $n$-dimensional torus equipped with Lebesgue measure. Denote by $\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)$ the standard Borel space of Lebesgue measure-preserving automorphisms of $I$ that have finite Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, and by $\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ the standard Borel space of $C^\infty$ Lebesgue measure-preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}^n$.

$$G:\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)\;\longrightarrow\;\bigsqcup_{n\ge 1}\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$$
such that for every $T\in\mathrm{Auth}^{<\infty}(I,\lambda)$, if $G(T)\in\mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n)$ then the measure-preserving systems $(I,\lambda,T)$ and $(\mathbb{T}^n,\lambda^n,G(T))$ are measure-theoretically isomorphic?

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: If a measure-preserving dynamical system is Kakutani realizable by a smooth toral system, must it also be realizable up to measure isomorphism?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ be an invertible measure-preserving dynamical system on a standard probability space. Recall:

- Two measure-preserving systems $(X,\mu,T)$ and $(Y,\nu,S)$ are said to be *measure isomorphic* if there exist full-measure invariant subsets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$ and a measurable bijection $\phi:X_0\to Y_0$ with $\phi_*\mu=\nu$ and $\phi\circ T=S\circ\phi$ on $X_0$.
- Two systems are *Kakutani equivalent* if each is measure isomorphic to a measurable induced (first-return) transformation of the other on some positive-measure subset; equivalently, they admit isomorphic suspension flows up to time change.
- A measure-preserving system $(X,\mu,T)$ is said to be *smoothly realizable on the torus* (isomorphically) if there exist $d\geq 1$, a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $f:\mathbb{T}^d\to\mathbb{T}^d$, and an $f$-invariant Borel probability measure $\nu$ on $\mathbb{T}^d$ such that $(\mathbb{T}^d,\nu,f)$ is measure isomorphic to $(X,\mu,T)$.
- It is said to be *Kakutani realizable on the torus* if such an $f$ exists with $(\mathbb{T}^d,\nu,f)$ Kakutani equivalent to $(X,\mu,T)$.

Question: If a measure-preserving dynamical system on a standard probability space is Kakutani realizable by a smooth diffeomorphism of some torus equipped with an invariant Borel probability measure, must it also be isomorphically realizable by a smooth diffeomorphism of some torus with an invariant Borel probability measure?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem attributed to F. Rodriguez Hertz in a 2023 survey on open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems. A web search did not surface any subsequent work resolving the smooth-toral Kakutani-vs-isomorphic realization question; related rigidity and realization work by Rodriguez Hertz and collaborators addresses different aspects (e.g., smooth rigidity of Anosov maps), so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
original_question: Which families of dynamical systems are universal in the sense discussed in the paper?
self_contained_problem:
Work in the setting of Borel dynamics. A Borel dynamical system is a pair (X,T) where X is a standard Borel space and T:X→X is a Borel automorphism. For an invariant Borel probability measure μ on (X,T), let h_μ(T) denote the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy. A Borel system (Y,S) is said to embed into (X,T) on a μ-full set if there is a Borel injection π:Y'→X, defined on a T-invariant Borel set Y'⊆Y with μ(Y')=1, that conjugates S|_{Y'} to T|_{π(Y')}.

Following Hochman, call a free Borel system (X,T) universal if for every free Borel system (Y,S) and every S-invariant ergodic Borel probability measure μ on Y with h_μ(S) strictly less than the Borel entropy h(X,T) := sup{h_ν(T) : ν an ergodic T-invariant Borel probability measure on X}, the system (Y,S) embeds into (X,T) on a μ-full set. More generally, for t∈(0,∞], call (X,T) t-universal if it is free, carries no ergodic invariant measure of entropy ≥t, and contains an s-universal subsystem for every s<t.

Problem. Characterize, as broadly as possible, the families of Borel (respectively topological or smooth) dynamical systems that are universal in this sense. In particular, identify natural dynamical, geometric, or combinatorial properties (e.g., specification-type conditions, hyperbolicity, partial hyperbolicity, expansiveness) that imply universality, and determine which classes of systems—beyond mixing shifts of finite type, mixing sofic shifts, mixing positive-recurrent countable-state Markov chains, β-shifts, synchronized subshifts, and Axiom A diffeomorphisms restricted to their basic sets—are universal.
status_search_result: The question is a broad research program in Borel/topological dynamics initiated by Hochman (building on Krieger's generator theorem). Universality has been established for several specific classes (mixing SFTs, mixing sofic shifts, mixing positive-recurrent countable-state Markov chains, β-shifts, synchronized subshifts, Axiom A diffeomorphisms; also systems with the weak specification property, by Burguet and others). However, a complete characterization of which families are universal remains open, with ongoing research extending universality to broader classes.

paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
context_brief: Maps into the free part of ergodic toral automorphisms
original_question: Let (T^d, R) be a toral automorphism that is ergodic for Lebesgue measure, and let (Y, S) be a homeomorphism of a Polish space with no invariant probability measure. Does there exist an equivariant Borel map from (Y, S) into the free part of (T^d, R)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 1$ and let $R \colon \mathbb{T}^d \to \mathbb{T}^d$ be a toral automorphism (induced by some $A \in \mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{Z})$) which is ergodic with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{T}^d$. Denote by $\mathrm{Free}(\mathbb{T}^d, R) = \{x \in \mathbb{T}^d : R^n x \neq x \text{ for all } n \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}\}$ the free part of the $\mathbb{Z}$-action generated by $R$.

Let $Y$ be a Polish space and $S \colon Y \to Y$ a homeomorphism such that the dynamical system $(Y, S)$ admits no $S$-invariant Borel probability measure on $Y$.

A Borel map $\varphi \colon Y \to \mathbb{T}^d$ is called equivariant if $\varphi \circ S = R \circ \varphi$.

Question: Does there always exist an equivariant Borel map $\varphi \colon Y \to \mathbb{T}^d$ whose image is contained in $\mathrm{Free}(\mathbb{T}^d, R)$?
category_tag: Borel dynamics and descriptive set theory
status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a survey on descriptive set theory and dynamical systems. Related work by Chandgotia–Meyerovitch identifies a "property F" on $\mathbb{Z}^d$-subshifts under which any free Borel system maps equivariantly into the free part, but no resolution for general ergodic toral automorphisms appears in available sources.

paper_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
original_question: For each fixed integer k ≥ 1, let C_k be the limiting correlation C_k = lim_{R→∞} (1/K(R)) ∑_{j=1}^{K(R)} (A_R(λ_j)·A_R(λ_{j+k}) - 1/4), where the lattice points λ_j in the annulus of width √2 around the circle of radius R are ordered by polar angle and A_R(λ) is the area of the unit square centered at λ that lies inside B(R). Do these limiting correlations vanish as the angular-index separation grows, i.e. is lim_{k→∞} C_k = 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $B(R)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:\|x\|\le R\}$ and let $\mathcal{L}(R)=\mathbb{Z}^2\cap\{x:|\,\|x\|-R\,|\le \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\}$ be the set of integer lattice points lying in the closed annulus of width $\sqrt2$ centered on the circle of radius $R$. Order the points of $\mathcal{L}(R)$ as $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{K(R)}$ by increasing polar angle (with indices taken cyclically modulo $K(R)$), where $K(R)=|\mathcal{L}(R)|$. For each lattice point $\lambda$, let $A_R(\lambda)$ denote the area of the intersection of $B(R)$ with the closed unit square centered at $\lambda$ (with sides parallel to the coordinate axes).

For each fixed integer $k\ge 1$, define the limiting correlation (assumed to exist)
$$C_k \;=\; \lim_{R\to\infty}\frac{1}{K(R)}\sum_{j=1}^{K(R)}\Bigl(A_R(\lambda_j)\,A_R(\lambda_{j+k})-\tfrac{1}{4}\Bigr).$$

Prove or disprove: $\displaystyle\lim_{k\to\infty} C_k = 0.$
status_search_result: The Vanishing Correlation Conjecture is explicitly stated as unsettled by Lester and Wigman, who only prove supporting results (e.g., that the C_k vanish on average and that well-separated lattice points behave independently). The work was published in J. London Math. Soc. (2024); no subsequent resolution appears in the literature as of May 2026.

paper_title: Around the Gauss circle problem: Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles
original_question: Fix an angle θ and a shift parameter r in the tilted-and-shifted semi-infinite rectangle model R_{r,θ}. If one orders the lattice points of Z^2 ∩ R_{r,θ} by projection onto the long side of the rectangle and then projects them onto the short side, can one prove equidistribution of those short-side projections in [-1/√2, 1/√2] without averaging over the index ℓ, while instead exploiting averaging over r? The paper identifies establishing exactly this stronger equidistribution statement as the major challenge toward proving the vanishing-correlation conjecture.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\theta \in [0, 2\pi)$ be a fixed angle and let $r \in \mathbb{R}$ be a shift parameter. Consider the tilted-and-shifted semi-infinite rectangle
$$R_{r,\theta} = \{(x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : (x,y) = r\,(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) + s\,(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) + t\,(-\sin\theta, \cos\theta),\ s \geq 0,\ t \in [-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}]\},$$
i.e. an infinite strip of width $\sqrt{2}$ along the direction $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$, starting at the offset $r$ along that direction. Enumerate the lattice points $\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \dots$ of $\mathbb{Z}^2 \cap R_{r,\theta}$ in increasing order of their projection $\langle \kappa_\ell, (\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\rangle$ onto the long side of the rectangle. Let
$$p_\ell(r,\theta) = \langle \kappa_\ell, (-\sin\theta, \cos\theta)\rangle \in I := [-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}]$$
denote the projection of $\kappa_\ell$ onto the short side.

It is known that for a set of $\theta$ of full measure (those whose direction is badly approximable by rationals), the sequence $\{p_\ell(r,\theta)\}_{\ell}$ is equidistributed in $I$ on average over $\ell$.

Problem. For generic $\theta$, prove (or disprove) equidistribution of $p_\ell(r,\theta)$ in $I$ without averaging over the index $\ell$, by instead exploiting averaging over the shift parameter $r$. Concretely: show that for almost every $\theta$, there exists a set of shifts $r$ of full density along which, for each fixed $\ell$, the values $p_\ell(r,\theta)$ become equidistributed in $I$ as $r$ varies.
status_search_result: The problem is identified as the major remaining challenge toward proving the associated vanishing-correlation conjecture in the work on Hardy's conjecture and the distribution of lattice points near circles (published in the Journal of the London Mathematical Society, 2024). The equidistribution on average over the index is established, but the stronger statement using averaging over the shift parameter remains open; no subsequent resolution was found.

original_question: Let G be a connected graph. Must min{s+(G), s-(G)} always be at least n - 1, where s+(G) and s-(G) are the sums of the squares of the positive and negative adjacency eigenvalues of G and n is the number of vertices? More strongly, for an arbitrary graph with k connected components, must min{s+(G), s-(G)} be at least n - k?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A(G)$. Let $\lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_n$ be the eigenvalues of $A(G)$. Define
$$s^+(G) = \sum_{\lambda_i > 0} \lambda_i^2, \qquad s^-(G) = \sum_{\lambda_i < 0} \lambda_i^2.$$

(a) Prove or disprove: if $G$ is connected, then
$$\min\{s^+(G),\, s^-(G)\} \;\geq\; n - 1.$$

(b) (Stronger form.) Prove or disprove: if $G$ is an arbitrary graph having exactly $\kappa$ connected components, then
$$\min\{s^+(G),\, s^-(G)\} \;\geq\; n - \kappa.$$
status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in general. It has been verified for several graph classes (bipartite, regular, complete multipartite, line/claw-free graphs, graphs with small order after blow-up). Recent partial progress includes Shengtong Zhang's 2024 result establishing $\min\{s^+(G), s^-(G)\} \geq n - \gamma(G) \geq n/2$ (where $\gamma$ is the domination number), and a 2025 preprint resolving the claw-free case via a "gluing lemma". No counterexamples are known and no proof of the full conjecture has appeared.

original_question: Let G be a graph with m edges and clique number omega(G). Must the two largest adjacency eigenvalues satisfy lambda_1(G)^2 + lambda_2(G)^2 <= 2(1 - 1/omega(G))m?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with $m$ edges. Let $A(G)$ be its adjacency matrix, and let $\lambda_1(G) \geq \lambda_2(G) \geq \cdots$ denote the eigenvalues of $A(G)$ in non-increasing order. Let $\omega(G)$ denote the clique number of $G$, i.e., the size of the largest complete subgraph of $G$ (with the convention $1 - 1/\omega(G) = 0$ when $G$ has no edges).

Prove or disprove: for every such graph $G$,
$$\lambda_1(G)^2 + \lambda_2(G)^2 \;\leq\; 2\!\left(1 - \frac{1}{\omega(G)}\right) m.$$

A 2025 result shows it holds asymptotically almost surely for random graphs, and weaker-constant versions are known for all graphs.

original_question: Among all planar graphs on n >= 9 vertices, is the graph K_2 joined with the path P_{n-2} always the one with maximum spectral radius?

Let K_2 denote the complete graph on 2 vertices and P_{n-2} denote the path on n-2 vertices.

Prove or disprove: for every integer n ≥ 9, among all planar graphs on n vertices, the graph K_2 ∨ P_{n-2} attains the maximum spectral radius.

original_question: Suppose a graph G satisfies |E(H)| <= c|V(H)|^2 for every subgraph H of G. Does it follow that lambda(G) <= 2c|V(G)|? More generally, what bound should replace this when the exponent 2 is replaced by another constant less than 2?

Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with vertex set $V(G)$ and edge set $E(G)$, and let $\lambda(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of the adjacency matrix of $G$. Fix a constant $c>0$ and suppose that $G$ has the hereditary edge-density property
$$|E(H)| \le c\,|V(H)|^{2}$$
for every (not necessarily induced) subgraph $H$ of $G$.

(a) Does it follow that $\lambda(G) \le 2c\,|V(G)|$?

(b) More generally, suppose that for some constant $\alpha$ with $1<\alpha<2$ and some constant $c>0$, the graph $G$ satisfies $|E(H)| \le c\,|V(H)|^{\alpha}$ for every subgraph $H$ of $G$. original_question: Let k be a fixed positive integer and let G be a sufficiently large graph with m edges and no isolated vertices. If lambda(G) >= (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1))/2, must G contain a cycle of every length t <= 2k + 2 unless G is isomorphic to S_{m/k + (k+1)/2, k}?

original_question: Let G be a connected graph on n vertices with minimum degree delta, and let mu_1 >= ... >= mu_n be the Laplacian eigenvalues. Must the toughness satisfy t(G) >= mu_{n-1}/(mu_1 - delta)?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite, simple, connected graph on n ≥ 2 vertices with minimum degree δ. The toughness of G is defined by
  t(G) = min { |S| / c(G − S) : S ⊆ V(G), c(G − S) ≥ 2 },
where c(H) denotes the number of connected components of a graph H, and the minimum is over all vertex subsets S whose removal disconnects G (with t(G) = +∞ for complete graphs). Let L(G) = D(G) − A(G) be the Laplacian matrix of G, where D(G) is the diagonal degree matrix and A(G) is the adjacency matrix, and let its eigenvalues be ordered as
  μ_1 ≥ μ_2 ≥ … ≥ μ_{n−1} ≥ μ_n = 0.

Prove or disprove: for every such connected non-complete graph G,
  t(G) ≥ μ_{n−1} / (μ_1 − δ).

original_question: Find a spectral version of Mubayi's theorem for color-critical graphs, and in the special case q = 1 determine the sharp spectral analog when the forbidden color-critical graph F is a specific graph such as a triangle, clique, book, odd cycle, or even wheel.
self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A graph $F$ is called color-critical if there exists an edge $e \in E(F)$ such that $\chi(F-e) < \chi(F)$, where $\chi$ denotes the chromatic number. For an integer $r \ge 2$ and an integer $n \ge r$, let $T_{n,r}$ denote the Turán graph: the complete $r$-partite graph on $n$ vertices whose part sizes differ by at most one. Write $t_r(n) = e(T_{n,r})$.

Mubayi's theorem (supersaturation form). Let $F$ be a color-critical graph with $\chi(F) = r+1 \ge 3$. There exists $n_0 = n_0(F)$ such that for every integer $q$ with $1 \le q \le n/2$ and every $n \ge n_0$, every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with
$$e(G) \ge t_r(n) - q + 1$$
contains at least $q \cdot c(F,n)$ copies of $F$, where $c(F,n)$ denotes the minimum number of copies of $F$ that an edge of $T_{n,r}$ can be added to obtain (the standard Mubayi counting function). Equality is achieved by adding $q-1$ edges inside one part of $T_{n,r}$.

Let $\lambda(G)$ denote the spectral radius (largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix) of a graph $G$.

Problem. 

(i) (General spectral Mubayi.) Establish a spectral analogue of Mubayi's theorem. Specifically, for a color-critical graph $F$ with $\chi(F) = r+1 \ge 3$, determine the smallest function $\phi(F,n,q)$ such that for every integer $q$ with $1 \le q \le n/2$ and every sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with
$$\lambda(G) \ge \lambda(T_{n,r}) - \phi(F,n,q)$$
contains at least $q \cdot c(F,n)$ copies of $F$, and characterize the extremal graphs.

(ii) (Critical case $q=1$.) For each of the following specific color-critical graphs $F$, determine the sharp threshold $\lambda^\ast(F,n)$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\lambda(G) > \lambda^\ast(F,n)$ contains strictly more copies of $F$ than the minimum supersaturation count (equivalently, more than $c(F,n)$ copies), and identify all extremal graphs:
  (a) $F$ is the triangle $K_3$;
  (b) $F$ is a clique $K_{r+1}$ with $r \ge 3$;
  (c) $F$ is a book $B_k$ (the graph consisting of $k$ triangles sharing a common edge);
  (d) $F$ is an odd cycle $C_{2k+1}$ with $k \ge 2$;
  (e) $F$ is an even wheel $W_{2k}$ (the join of a vertex with $C_{2k}$).
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made. The triangle case (q=1) was resolved by Ning–Zhai and extended in subsequent works; further results on books, theta graphs, and disjoint color-critical graphs have appeared. A December 2025 preprint "Spectral supersaturation for color-critical graphs" claims to resolve the general Ning–Zhai problem, providing a spectral counterpart to Mubayi's and Pikhurko–Yilma's supersaturation results, though full peer-reviewed confirmation is pending. Hence the problem is partially solved, with the general case very recently addressed.

original_question: For each fixed Delta and all sufficiently large n, if G maximizes the spectral radius among connected nonregular n-vertex graphs with maximum degree Delta, must G have degree sequence (Delta, ..., Delta, delta) where delta equals Delta - 1 when Delta is odd and n is odd, equals 1 when Delta is odd and n is even, and equals Delta - 2 when Delta is even?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{G}(n,\Delta)$ denote the family of connected nonregular graphs on $n$ vertices whose maximum vertex degree is exactly $\Delta$. For a graph $G$, let $\lambda_1(G)$ denote its spectral radius (the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix). Fix an integer $\Delta \ge 3$, and for each sufficiently large $n$ let $G^*=G^*(n,\Delta) \in \mathcal{G}(n,\Delta)$ be a graph that maximizes $\lambda_1$ over $\mathcal{G}(n,\Delta)$.

Prove or disprove: for every fixed $\Delta \ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the degree sequence of $G^*$ has the form $(\Delta,\Delta,\dots,\Delta,\delta)$ with exactly one vertex of degree $\delta < \Delta$, where
- $\delta = \Delta-1$ if $\Delta$ is odd and $n$ is odd,
- $\delta = 1$ if $\Delta$ is odd and $n$ is even,
- $\delta = \Delta-2$ if $\Delta$ is even.
status_search_result: The conjecture has been confirmed for $\Delta = 3$ and $\Delta = 4$, where extremal graphs were shown to have a specific path-like block structure consistent with the predicted degree sequence. For general $\Delta \ge 5$ the conjecture appears to remain open.

original_question: Let G be a connected n-vertex m-edge graph of minimum spectral radius, and let r satisfy e(T_{n,r-1}) < m <= e(T_{n,r}). Is there a constant alpha > 0 such that G must be r-colorable whenever m = Omega(n^alpha)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $T_{n,r}$ denote the Turán graph on $n$ vertices with $r$ parts (the complete $r$-partite graph on $n$ vertices whose part sizes differ by at most one), and let $e(T_{n,r})$ denote its number of edges. For positive integers $n$ and $m$ with $m \le \binom{n}{2}$, let $\mathcal{H}(n,m)$ be the set of connected graphs with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The spectral radius $\rho(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

Let $G \in \mathcal{H}(n,m)$ be a connected graph attaining the minimum spectral radius among all graphs in $\mathcal{H}(n,m)$, and let $r$ be the unique integer satisfying
$$e(T_{n,r-1}) < m \le e(T_{n,r}).$$

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $\alpha > 0$ such that whenever $m = \Omega(n^{\alpha})$, the graph $G$ is $r$-colorable.
status_search_result: The conjecture is stated as an open problem in a recent compendium of unsolved problems in spectral graph theory. No published resolution was found in a web search; related work concerns spectral Turán-type problems and minimum spectral radius of saturated graphs but does not settle this modified Guiduli conjecture.

original_question: Let G be a nontrivial graph with maximum degree Delta. Does there always exist an edge signing sigma such that the signed graph has spectral radius strictly less than 2*sqrt(Delta - 1)?
self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $(G,\sigma)$ where $G=(V,E)$ is a finite simple graph and $\sigma:E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a function called a signature (or edge signing). The adjacency matrix $A(G,\sigma)$ of $(G,\sigma)$ is the symmetric $|V|\times|V|$ matrix with entries $A(G,\sigma)_{uv}=\sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise. The spectral radius $\rho(G,\sigma)$ is the largest absolute value of an eigenvalue of $A(G,\sigma)$.

Let $G$ be a nontrivial graph (i.e., having at least one edge) with maximum degree $\Delta$. Does there always exist a signature $\sigma:E(G)\to\{+1,-1\}$ such that
$$\rho(G,\sigma) < 2\sqrt{\Delta-1}\,?$$
status_search_result: The conjecture, attributed to Gregory, is listed among open problems in the spectral theory of signed graphs. Recent surveys and papers (2019–2023) describe it as still open, with related partial results (e.g., for regular graphs via Bilu–Linial-type constructions and for graphs with bounded maximum degree) but no full resolution.

original_question: For the d-dimensional hypercube Q_d and an integer m with 1 <= m <= 2^d, what is the maximum possible largest eigenvalue of the induced subgraph Q_d[U] over all vertex sets U of size m?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q_d$ denote the $d$-dimensional hypercube graph, whose vertex set is $\{0,1\}^d$ and in which two vertices are adjacent if and only if they differ in exactly one coordinate. For a subset $U \subseteq \{0,1\}^d$, let $Q_d[U]$ denote the subgraph of $Q_d$ induced by $U$, and let $\lambda_1(Q_d[U])$ denote its largest eigenvalue (i.e., the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix). For each integer $m$ with $1 \le m \le 2^d$, determine
$$f(d,m) := \max\{\lambda_1(Q_d[U]) : U \subseteq \{0,1\}^d,\ |U| = m\}.$$
That is, find a closed-form expression (or sharp characterization) for the maximum possible largest eigenvalue of an induced subgraph of $Q_d$ on exactly $m$ vertices, together with the extremal sets $U$ achieving this maximum.
category_tag: Spectral graph theory of the hypercube
status_search_result: The problem (attributed to Fink, with a weaker form by Friedman–Tillich) appears to remain open in general. Partial results are known: Bollobás and Lee showed that for an induced subgraph on $n \le d$ vertices with $n \ge 105$, the largest eigenvalue is at most $\sqrt{n-1}$, achieved by stars; and Hamming balls of radius $o(d)$ achieve a largest eigenvalue within $1+o(1)$ of the conjectured maximum. No complete solution for arbitrary $m$ has been published.

original_question: Given a graph F, what is the minimum possible spectral radius of an n-vertex F-saturated graph?
self_contained_problem:
Let F be a fixed graph. A graph G is said to be F-saturated if G does not contain F as a subgraph, but for every pair of non-adjacent vertices u,v in G, the graph G + uv contains a copy of F. For a graph G, let λ(G) denote the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix (the largest eigenvalue, which is real since the matrix is symmetric).

For a given graph F and a positive integer n, determine

    sat_λ(n, F) := min { λ(G) : G is an F-saturated graph on n vertices }.

In particular, characterize the extremal F-saturated graphs on n vertices that attain this minimum spectral radius, for general F.
status_search_result: The problem is open in general. It is posed as a broad research problem in spectral graph theory. Partial progress exists for specific families F: a conjecture of Kim–Kim–Kostochka–O addresses F = K_{r+1} (with the star-like graph S_{n,r-1} conjectured to be extremal), proved for r = 2,3 and recently extended for r = 4,5; sharp results have also been obtained for F = tP_3, tP_4, and K_5. No general answer is known.

original_question: For every graph G of order n and every k in {1, 2, ..., n}, does S_k(G) <= e(G) + binom(k+1, 2) hold with equality exactly for the graphs G_{k,r,s} described by Li and Guo?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices with edge set $E(G)$, and let $e(G)=|E(G)|$. Denote by $\mu_1(G)\ge\mu_2(G)\ge\cdots\ge\mu_n(G)=0$ the eigenvalues of the Laplacian matrix $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, where $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix and $D(G)$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees. For each integer $k$ with $1\le k\le n$, set
$$S_k(G)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\mu_i(G).$$

For integers $k\ge 1$, $r\ge 1$, $s\ge 0$ with $n=k+r+s$, define the graph $G_{k,r,s}$ as follows. Its vertex set is partitioned into three parts: a clique $K_k$ on $k$ vertices, an independent set $I_r$ on $r$ vertices, and an independent set $I_s=\{v_1,\dots,v_s\}$ on $s$ vertices. Every vertex of $I_r$ is adjacent to every vertex of $K_k$, and there are no edges between $I_r$ and $I_s$ nor inside $I_r$ or $I_s$. For each $v_i\in I_s$, its neighborhood $N(v_i)$ is a proper subset of $V(K_k)$, and the neighborhoods are nested: $N(v_{i+1})\subseteq N(v_i)$ for $1\le i\le s-1$.

Prove or disprove: for every graph $G$ of order $n$ and every $k\in\{1,2,\dots,n\}$,
$$S_k(G)\;\le\;e(G)+\binom{k+1}{2},$$
with equality if and only if $G\cong G_{k,r,s}$ for some $r\ge 1$ and $s\ge 0$.
status_search_result: The full Brouwer conjecture due to Li and Guo is known to hold for k∈{1,2} and k∈{n−3,n−2,n−1}, and has been verified by computer for graphs of order at most 9. Recent work (2025) further establishes it for split graphs, complete split graphs, and c-cyclic graphs with c∈{0,1,2}, but it remains open for general k.

original_question: Among all trees of order n, is the adjacency spectral gap minimized by some double comet C(k, ell)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $T$ be a simple undirected tree on $n$ vertices, and let $A(T)$ denote its adjacency matrix. Order the eigenvalues of $A(T)$ as $\lambda_1(T) \geq \lambda_2(T) \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_n(T)$. The (adjacency) spectral gap of $T$ is defined as $\lambda_1(T) - \lambda_2(T)$.

For integers $k \geq 1$ and $\ell \geq 1$ with $k + \ell + (n - k - \ell) = n$, the double comet $C(k, \ell)$ is the tree obtained from a path $P_{n-k-\ell}$ on $n-k-\ell$ vertices by attaching $k$ pendant edges to one endpoint of the path and $\ell$ pendant edges to the other endpoint.

Question: For every integer $n \geq 4$, is the minimum of the spectral gap $\lambda_1(T) - \lambda_2(T)$ over all trees $T$ on $n$ vertices attained by some double comet $C(k, \ell)$?
status_search_result: The conjecture, due to Jovović, Koledin, and Stanić (Ars Mathematica Contemporanea, 2018), is supported by computer verification for trees with at most 20 vertices, and partial theoretical results about double comets are known, but no general proof appears in the literature. The problem is still considered open.

original_question: For every graph G whose adjacency matrix is nonsingular, with maximum degree Delta and minimum degree delta, must the graph energy satisfy E(G) >= Delta + delta, with equality only for complete graphs?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix A(G). The energy of G is defined as
  E(G) = sum_{i=1}^{n} |λ_i|,
where λ_1, …, λ_n are the eigenvalues of A(G). Let Δ(G) and δ(G) denote the maximum and minimum vertex degrees of G, respectively. Assume that A(G) is nonsingular (i.e., 0 is not an eigenvalue of A(G)).

Prove or disprove: for every such graph G,
  E(G) ≥ Δ(G) + δ(G),
with equality if and only if G is a complete graph.
status_search_result: The conjecture has been verified for several restricted graph classes (including regular graphs, bipartite graphs, planar graphs, threshold graphs, triangle-free graphs, and quadrangle-free graphs), but it remains open in full generality. It is still listed as an open conjecture in recent surveys of unsolved problems in spectral graph theory.

context_brief: Powers third and fourth eigenvalue problem
original_question: If G is a graph of order n, must the third and fourth largest adjacency eigenvalues satisfy lambda_i(G) <= floor(n/i) for i = 3 and i = 4?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n$, and let $A(G)$ denote its adjacency matrix. Order the eigenvalues of $A(G)$ as $\lambda_1(G) \ge \lambda_2(G) \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n(G)$. Determine whether the following inequalities hold for every simple graph $G$ of order $n$:
$$\lambda_3(G) \le \left\lfloor \tfrac{n}{3} \right\rfloor \quad \text{and} \quad \lambda_4(G) \le \left\lfloor \tfrac{n}{4} \right\rfloor.$$
status_search_result: The case i=3 (whether λ₃(G) ≤ n/3) remains open in general, with partial affirmative results known for strongly regular graphs, regular line graphs, and Cayley/semi-Cayley graphs on abelian groups. The case i=4 has been disproved: Linz showed a construction with λ₄(G)/n ≥ (1+√5)/12 ≈ 0.2697 > 1/4, so the bound λ₄(G) ≤ n/4 fails.

original_question: If G is a planar subcubic graph, must its HL-index R(G) always be at most 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\lambda_1(G) \ge \lambda_2(G) \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n(G)$ denote the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. Define the two median eigenvalues of $G$ as $\lambda_H(G) = \lambda_{\lceil n/2 \rceil}(G)$ and $\lambda_L(G) = \lambda_{\lceil (n+1)/2 \rceil}(G)$, and define the HL-index of $G$ by
\[ R(G) = \max\bigl(|\lambda_H(G)|,\ |\lambda_L(G)|\bigr). \]
A graph is called subcubic if every vertex has degree at most $3$, and planar if it can be embedded in the plane without edge crossings.

Prove or disprove: for every planar subcubic graph $G$, one has $R(G) \le 1$.
status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Mohar) appears to still be open in general. It is known that R(G) ≤ √2 for every subcubic graph (Mohar), with equality only for the Heawood graph, and recent work has verified Mohar's conjecture for K₄-minor-free subcubic graphs and other sparse subclasses, but the full planar case remains unresolved as of recent (2024–2025) papers.

original_question: Among all connected graphs on n vertices, does the lollipop graph P_{n-3} · K_4 minimize the l1-norm of the principal eigenvector?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A(G)$. By the Perron–Frobenius theorem, $A(G)$ has a unique (up to positive scaling) positive unit eigenvector $x = (x_1,\dots,x_n)$ associated with its largest eigenvalue; this $x$ is called the principal eigenvector of $G$. Normalize $x$ so that $\|x\|_2 = 1$ (Euclidean unit norm), and define the $\ell_1$-norm of the principal eigenvector by $\|x\|_1 = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i$.

For $n \ge 7$, let $P_{n-3}\cdot K_4$ denote the lollipop graph obtained from a complete graph $K_4$ and a path $P_{n-3}$ on $n-3$ vertices by identifying one endpoint of the path with a single vertex of $K_4$ (so the resulting graph has $n$ vertices and is connected).

original_question: For each dimension d, what is the greatest possible volume of a pair of spherical orbifolds of dimension d that are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric?
self_contained_problem:
A spherical orbifold of dimension d is a quotient S^d/Γ, where S^d denotes the unit round sphere in R^{d+1} and Γ is a finite subgroup of the orthogonal group O(d+1) acting on S^d. Two such orbifolds are said to be Laplace-isospectral if the Laplace–Beltrami operators on their smooth parts have the same spectrum (with multiplicities), and they are isometric if there is a volume- and metric-preserving bijection between them; equivalently, S^d/Γ and S^d/Γ' are isometric iff Γ and Γ' are conjugate in O(d+1). The volume of S^d/Γ equals vol(S^d)/|Γ|.

For each integer d ≥ 2, determine

or equivalently, determine the smallest possible order of Γ admitting such an isospectral non-isometric partner in dimension d.
status_search_result: The problem is generally open. It has been conjectured that the largest-volume isospectral non-isometric pairs of spherical space forms are lens spaces, and this conjecture has been verified in dimensions n ≡ 2,3,4,5,6,7 (mod 9). Known constructions yield lower bounds such as vol(S^d)/8 (using almost-conjugate (Z/2Z)^3 subgroups) and vol(S^{2n-1})/11 in infinitely many odd dimensions, but the exact maximum is not known in general.

original_question: Whenever a pair of spherical space forms of a fixed dimension has the largest possible volume among all isospectral non-isometric pairs in that dimension, must that extremal pair always be a pair of lens spaces?
self_contained_problem:
A spherical space form is a Riemannian manifold of the form $\Gamma\backslash S^n$, where $S^n$ is the unit round sphere of dimension $n$ and $\Gamma$ is a finite subgroup of $O(n+1)$ acting freely on $S^n$ by isometries, equipped with the quotient metric. Two such space forms are said to be isospectral if the spectra of their Laplace–Beltrami operators (counted with multiplicity) coincide, and isometric if there exists a Riemannian isometry between them. A lens space is a spherical space form of odd dimension $2m-1$ obtained as $L\backslash S^{2m-1}$ for some cyclic subgroup $L$ of $O(2m)$ acting freely.

Fix a dimension $n \geq 2$. Among all unordered pairs $(M_1, M_2)$ of $n$-dimensional spherical space forms which are isospectral but not isometric, suppose that the common volume $\mathrm{vol}(M_1) = \mathrm{vol}(M_2)$ attains the maximum possible value over all such pairs (assuming such a maximum is attained in dimension $n$).

Question: Must every such volume-maximizing pair consist of two lens spaces?
status_search_result: The question has been addressed for odd dimensions: in dimension $2n-1$, the maximum-volume isospectral non-isometric pair is known to consist of lens spaces for all $3 \le n \le 1000$ except possibly $n = 144$ and $n = 935$, with general partial results bounding volumes (e.g., pairs of volume $\ge \mathrm{vol}(S^{2n-1})/10$ are isometric). The general question across all dimensions remains open.

context_brief: Orbifolds covered by compact symmetric spaces
