original_question: Given a spherical orbifold of volume V, what general upper bound can one place on the size of an isospectral set of spherical orbifolds that contains it?

context_brief: When lens spaces are spectrally unique
original_question: For which dimensions 2n − 1 and orders q of the fundamental group is every lens space of volume vol(S^(2n−1))/q spectrally unique within the class of lens spaces with that same dimension and group order, so that no nontrivial isospectrality occurs?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n\ge 2$ and an integer $q\ge 2$, a $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens space is a quotient $L(q;s_1,\dots,s_n) = S^{2n-1}/\Gamma$, where $S^{2n-1}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ is the unit sphere with its round metric and $\Gamma\cong\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ acts freely by 
$$(z_1,\dots,z_n)\mapsto (e^{2\pi i s_1/q}z_1,\dots, e^{2\pi i s_n/q}z_n),$$
with $\gcd(s_j,q)=1$ for all $j$. Each such lens space inherits a Riemannian metric of constant curvature $1$ and volume $\mathrm{vol}(S^{2n-1})/q$. Let $L(n,q)$ denote the set of isometry classes of such $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens spaces with fundamental group of order $q$, and let $L^\bullet(n,q)\subseteq L(n,q)$ denote the subset of isometry classes which are uniquely determined within $L(n,q)$ by the spectrum of the Laplace–Beltrami operator (i.e., no other element of $L(n,q)$ is isospectral but non-isometric to it).

Problem: Determine all pairs $(n,q)$ with $n\ge 2$, $q\ge 2$ for which $L^\bullet(n,q) = L(n,q)$, i.e., for which no nontrivial isospectrality occurs among $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens spaces of volume $\mathrm{vol}(S^{2n-1})/q$.
status_search_result: Partial results exist: Ikeda–Yamamoto proved three-dimensional lens spaces and homogeneous lens spaces are determined by their Laplace spectrum within the class of lens spaces, and certain low-dimensional cases (including some orbifold versions in dimensions 3 and 4) are known. However, a full characterization of all pairs (n,q) for which no nontrivial isospectrality occurs among (2n−1)-dimensional lens spaces remains an open problem, with many isospectral non-isometric families known to exist in higher dimensions.

context_brief: Hyperbolic manifolds: p-isospectral but not strongly isospectral
original_question: Do there exist hyperbolic manifolds that are p-isospectral for every degree p, meaning the Hodge-Laplace operators on p-forms all have the same spectra, but are nevertheless not strongly isospectral?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold. For each integer $p$ with $0\le p\le \dim M$, let $\Delta_p$ denote the Hodge–Laplace operator acting on smooth $p$-forms on $M$, and let $\mathrm{Spec}_p(M)$ denote its spectrum (counted with multiplicities). Two closed Riemannian manifolds $M_1, M_2$ are said to be $p$-isospectral if $\mathrm{Spec}_p(M_1)=\mathrm{Spec}_p(M_2)$, and they are said to be strongly isospectral if, for every natural elliptic differential operator $D$ canonically associated to the Riemannian structure (equivalently, for every locally invariant elliptic operator built from the metric, including all twisted Laplacians on sections of natural bundles), the spectra of $D$ on $M_1$ and on $M_2$ coincide.

A hyperbolic manifold is a complete Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$.

Question: Do there exist closed hyperbolic manifolds $M_1$ and $M_2$ that are $p$-isospectral for every $p\in\{0,1,\dots,\dim M_1\}$ but are not strongly isospectral?

Known examples of isospectral hyperbolic manifolds (e.g., via Sunada's method) tend to yield strong isospectrality, and recent work has produced strongly isospectral hyperbolic 3-manifolds distinguished by finer invariants (such as cohomology ring structure), but the converse separation—$p$-isospectral for all $p$ without strong isospectrality—does not appear to be resolved in the literature found.

paper_title: NTN-based 6G Localization: Vision, Role of LEOs, and Open Problems
context_brief: GNSS-free NTN access through standalone RAT-dependent localization
original_question: How can user equipment (UE) that lacks Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) capability estimate its location well enough to close a radio link and connect to a non-terrestrial network (NTN), using standalone radio-access-technology-dependent cellular positioning methods rather than UE-reported GNSS?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a user equipment (UE) on or near the Earth's surface that wishes to establish a radio link with a low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite belonging to a non-terrestrial cellular network. To successfully close such a link, the UE must compensate for (i) the round-trip propagation delay between itself and the satellite and (ii) the Doppler frequency shift induced by the satellite's high relative velocity; both compensations require knowledge of the UE's approximate geographic position. In current cellular standards this position is supplied by an onboard Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver, but assume that the UE has no GNSS capability and that no other UE-side absolute positioning source is available.

The satellite (or the network) is assumed to know its own ephemeris (position and velocity at every time instant) and can transmit downlink reference signals with known waveforms, timing, and carrier frequency. The UE can measure features of received downlink signals (e.g., received power, time of arrival relative to its local clock, carrier-frequency offset, angle of arrival if it has multiple antennas) from one or more satellites that may pass over it, possibly at different times.

Design and rigorously analyze a standalone radio-access-technology–dependent positioning scheme — i.e., a scheme that uses only such cellular downlink/uplink measurements between the UE and satellites, with no GNSS or other external positioning input — that produces an estimate of the UE position with accuracy sufficient to enable initial timing advance and Doppler pre-compensation, and hence radio-link closure with the non-terrestrial network. In particular:

1. Identify the minimal set of measurements (number of satellites, number of time epochs, types of signal observables) needed for the UE position to be observable, given satellite ephemeris and an unknown UE clock bias and frequency offset.
2. Derive the Cramér–Rao lower bound (or an equivalent fundamental accuracy limit) on UE position estimation as a function of carrier frequency, bandwidth, signal-to-noise ratio, satellite geometry, and the number of observation epochs.
3. Determine the maximum positioning error tolerable for successful initial access (link closure) as a function of the orbital and waveform parameters, and specify regimes in which the proposed scheme meets this tolerance.
status_search_result: The problem of GNSS-free initial-access localization for UEs connecting to LEO-based non-terrestrial networks is an active open research area. 3GPP Release 17/18 NTN specifications still require UEs to report GNSS-derived position for initial access, and recent research papers (2023–2025) on LEO-based positioning, Doppler/delay-based UE localization, and 6G NTN initial access continue to propose partial solutions (e.g., Doppler-only, multi-satellite TDOA/FDOA schemes) but do not provide a fully standardized, validated standalone RAT-dependent positioning method that closes the radio link for GNSS-less UEs.

paper_title: NTN-based 6G Localization: Vision, Role of LEOs, and Open Problems
original_question: When a low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite has unused communication beams, how should 6G non-terrestrial-network (NTN) positioning schedule and control spare beams to transmit low-signal-to-noise-ratio-decodable positioning reference signals (PRS) outside the satellite's normal beam coverage, such as when the satellite is passing over a land-ocean boundary?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite equipped with a phased-array antenna capable of forming up to B simultaneous directional beams. At any time t, let C(t) ⊆ {1,…,B} denote the subset of beams currently allocated to communication services within the satellite's nominal ground footprint, and let S(t) = {1,…,B} \ C(t) be the set of currently unused ("spare") beams. The satellite's nominal coverage cell N(t) ⊂ R^2 on the Earth's surface may shrink (for instance, when the satellite passes over a land–ocean boundary, so that the portion of N(t) over land is much smaller than over the ocean), leaving |S(t)| > 0.

Positioning reference signals (PRS) are broadcast waveforms designed so that user equipment (UE) located in a region R can estimate its position by combining time-of-arrival or carrier-phase measurements from multiple satellites. PRS waveforms are decodable at very low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), so a satellite may steer a spare beam from S(t) to illuminate a target ground region T(t) ⊂ R^2 located outside N(t).

Let U(t) ⊂ R^2 denote the set of UEs requesting positioning service at time t. For each UE u ∈ U(t), positioning accuracy depends on the geometric dilution of precision (GDOP) determined by the set of visible satellites currently transmitting PRS toward u, on the per-link SNR (which depends on beam direction, off-boresight angle, atmospheric attenuation, and slant range), and on the PRS bandwidth and integration time.

Design and analyze an opportunistic spare-beam scheduling and beam-pointing policy π that, given the satellite ephemerides, the time-varying spare-beam sets S(t), the spatial distribution of UEs U(t), and the communication-service constraints (so that beams allocated to C(t) are never preempted), assigns to each spare beam in S(t) a pointing direction (i.e. a target region T(t)) and a PRS transmission schedule, with the objectives:

(i) maximizing the expected positioning accuracy (e.g. minimizing the time- and UE-averaged position-error bound, or equivalently maximizing a Fisher-information-based utility) for UEs outside the nominal coverage N(t);
(ii) guaranteeing prescribed PRS coverage and revisit-time bounds at each location in a service area of interest; and
(iii) respecting hardware constraints, including total radiated power, beam-switching latency, and inter-beam interference.

Specifically: (a) formulate this spare-beam PRS scheduling problem as a mathematical optimization (e.g. a mixed-integer or stochastic optimal-control problem), (b) characterize its computational complexity, and (c) provide a policy with provable performance guarantees relative to the offline optimum, or establish fundamental performance limits.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a forward-looking vision paper on 6G non-terrestrial-network localization. A web search did not surface any subsequent work that formally formulates or solves the opportunistic spare-beam PRS scheduling problem for LEO satellites with provable guarantees. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: NTN-based 6G Localization: Vision, Role of LEOs, and Open Problems
context_brief: new narrowband reference signals for NTN positioning
original_question: What reference-signal design should 3GPP standardize for non-terrestrial-network (NTN) positioning so that user equipment does not need power-intensive wideband positioning reference signal (PRS) searches across multi-subframe windows, Doppler measurements are supported, and transmission/reception points and user equipment can maintain phase coherence over a new narrowband PRS spanning multiple slots?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a cellular positioning system in which a user equipment (UE) estimates its location from downlink positioning reference signals (PRS) transmitted by multiple transmission/reception points (TRPs). In a non-terrestrial-network (NTN) setting, the TRPs are mounted on satellites (e.g., in low Earth orbit), so that (i) propagation delays between the reference TRP and neighboring TRPs differ by amounts spanning multiple OFDM subframes, (ii) line-of-sight relative motion produces large, time-varying Doppler shifts, and (iii) maintaining radio-frequency phase coherence between TRP transmitters and the UE receiver across long observation intervals is nontrivial.

A conventional wideband PRS forces the UE to perform a correlation search over a time window of multiple subframes, which is power-intensive. The problem is to design a new downlink reference-signal scheme, suitable for standardization, with the following requirements:

1. The signal includes narrowband synchronization blocks that are quasi-co-located with the PRS in a deterministic time-frequency pattern, so that the UE can acquire timing and frequency without a wideband multi-subframe search.

2. The signal is a narrowband PRS whose resources are deployed over multiple slots in such a way that the UE can produce reliable Doppler (carrier-frequency-offset / Doppler rate) measurements in addition to time-of-arrival measurements.

3. The TRP transmitter and UE receiver are required to maintain phase coherence across the entire multi-slot transmission of the new narrowband PRS, enabling coherent combining across slots.

Specify the time-frequency resource mapping, sequence design, quasi-co-location structure, and phase-coherence requirements of such a reference signal, and analyze its time-of-arrival, Doppler, and phase-estimation performance (e.g., via Cramér–Rao bounds) under NTN-typical delay, Doppler, and oscillator-stability conditions, demonstrating that it simultaneously satisfies (1)–(3) while improving on a wideband multi-subframe PRS search.

Recent surveys on LEO-based 6G positioning explicitly list limited phase coherence and high Doppler variability as open signal-design challenges, indicating the problem remains open.

paper_title: NTN-based 6G Localization: Vision, Role of LEOs, and Open Problems
context_brief: dynamic assistance information and PRS muting for moving satellites
original_question: How should a 6G non-terrestrial-network (NTN) positioning system dynamically update positioning assistance information and positioning reference signal (PRS) muting patterns as satellites move, so that user equipment receives valid neighboring-satellite configurations and distant-satellite PRS can be heard despite nearby-satellite interference and larger propagation delays?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a satellite-based positioning system in which a constellation of moving satellites broadcasts periodic positioning reference signals (PRS) to ground user equipment (UE). Let the satellites be indexed by i = 1, ..., N, with time-dependent positions p_i(t) ∈ R^3 known to a central location management function (LMF). At each time t the LMF supplies the UE with:

(a) assistance information A_i(t) describing the configuration (carrier, bandwidth, PRS sequence parameters, expected time of arrival window, Doppler pre-compensation) of every neighboring satellite i visible from the UE, and
(b) a PRS muting pattern, i.e. a binary schedule M_i(t,k) ∈ {0,1} for each satellite i and each PRS slot/symbol index k, where M_i(t,k)=1 indicates that satellite i is silent in slot k.

A UE attempting to acquire PRS from a distant satellite j experiences interference from nearby satellites; reception is feasible in slot k only if for every nearby interferer i ≠ j the slot k (suitably shifted by the differential propagation delay τ_{ij}(t) = (||p_i(t) - x_UE|| - ||p_j(t) - x_UE||)/c) is muted, i.e. M_i(t, k + ⌊τ_{ij}(t)/T_s⌋) = 1, where T_s is the symbol duration. Because satellites move, the set of nearby/distant satellites and the delays τ_{ij}(t) vary with t, so both A_i(t) and M_i(t,·) must be updated dynamically.

Problem. Design and analyze an update policy for (A_i(t), M_i(t,·))_{i=1}^N, taking the predictable satellite ephemerides as input, such that:

1. For every UE position x_UE in the service region and every time t, the assistance information A_i(t) provided to the UE is consistent with the actual configuration of every satellite i visible from x_UE.

2. For every UE x_UE and every satellite j whose PRS the UE is scheduled to measure, there exist infinitely many PRS slots k in which the interference from all other satellites (after accounting for differential delays τ_{ij}(t)) is muted, so that the PRS from j is decodable; in particular, when PRS instances of multiple satellites overlap, the serving satellite mutes adjacent symbols/slots to absorb the larger propagation delay of the distant satellite.

3. The signaling overhead (rate of updates of A_i and M_i communicated to UEs) and the fraction of muted PRS resources are minimized subject to the above feasibility constraints.

Provide a constructive scheme achieving (1)–(3), or prove impossibility/lower bounds on the achievable overhead-muting tradeoff.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction for 6G non-terrestrial-network positioning. Standardization (3GPP Rel-18/19) and recent surveys on LEO-based positioning continue to list dynamic PRS assistance and muting under satellite mobility as unresolved design challenges, with only preliminary proposals and no agreed-upon optimal solution.

original_question: Can one identify abstract classes of variational objectives on probability measures and corresponding random approximations such that the objective values E(mu_n) converge to E(mu_*) as the number of samples grows, quantitative convergence rates can be proved under explicit model assumptions, and the resulting abstract classes still cover problems of practical interest in machine learning?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ denote the set of Borel probability measures on a Polish space $\mathcal{X}$. Consider a variational objective $E:\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ and, for each integer $n\ge 1$, a random empirical-style approximation $E_n:\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ built from $n$ i.i.d. samples (or analogous random data) drawn from an underlying data distribution. Let
$$\mu_* \in \arg\min_{\mu\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} E(\mu), \qquad \mu_n \in \arg\min_{\mu\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} E_n(\mu).$$

The problem is to identify abstract classes $\mathcal{C}$ of pairs $(E,(E_n)_{n\ge 1})$ such that all three of the following hold:

(i) (Consistency) For every $(E,(E_n))\in\mathcal{C}$, one has $E(\mu_n)\to E(\mu_*)$ as $n\to\infty$, in probability or almost surely.

(ii) (Quantitative rates) There exist explicit model assumptions on $(E,(E_n))$ (e.g., regularity, convexity, concentration, dimension, smoothness of densities) under which one can prove non-asymptotic bounds of the form $\mathbb{E}[E(\mu_n)-E(\mu_*)] \le r(n)$ with an explicit rate function $r(n)\to 0$.

(iii) (Practical scope) The class $\mathcal{C}$ is broad enough to encompass variational objectives on measures arising in machine learning practice, such as those used for out-of-distribution generalization, weakly supervised learning, or uncertainty quantification.

Provide such classes $\mathcal{C}$, together with proofs of (i)–(ii) and a demonstration of (iii).
status_search_result: The question is stated as an open problem in a 2023 vision/open-problem note by Cabannes and Domingo-Enrich. No subsequent work appears to provide a comprehensive abstract framework simultaneously satisfying consistency, explicit rates, and broad coverage of practical ML measure-valued objectives; related contemporaneous works (e.g., convergence of coordinate-ascent variational inference, accelerated optimization over measure spaces) address particular instances rather than the general abstract program. Status remains open.

paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Domain-dependent upper bounds for classical smoothness classes
original_question: Let k be a fixed positive integer and let F_d^k(D_d) be the class of functions f:D_d -> R on a domain D_d subset R^d of volume 1 such that every mixed partial derivative D^alpha f of order |alpha| <= k satisfies ||D^alpha f||_infty <= 1. For which domains D_d does the worst-case integration error admit an upper bound of the form e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) <= c_k d n^(-k/d), and how can one explicitly construct algorithms that achieve this rate on those domains?
self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer $k$. For each dimension $d \geq 1$, let $D_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a (measurable) domain of Lebesgue volume $1$, and let
$$F_d^k(D_d) := \{\, f : D_d \to \mathbb{R} : \|D^\alpha f\|_\infty \le 1 \text{ for every multi-index } \alpha \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^d \text{ with } |\alpha| \le k\,\}.$$
For an algorithm $A_n$ that approximates $\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx$ using at most $n$ function evaluations of $f$, define the worst-case error
$$e(A_n, F_d^k(D_d)) := \sup_{f \in F_d^k(D_d)} \Bigl| \int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx - A_n(f) \Bigr|,$$
and let $e(n, F_d^k(D_d)) := \inf_{A_n} e(A_n, F_d^k(D_d))$ be the optimal (deterministic) $n$-th minimal worst-case error over all such algorithms.

Problem. Characterize the family of domains $D_d$ (as $d$ varies) for which there exists a constant $c_k > 0$, depending only on $k$, such that
$$e(n, F_d^k(D_d)) \le c_k\, d\, n^{-k/d} \qquad \text{for all } n, d \ge 1,$$
and for each such admissible family $\{D_d\}$ construct an explicit sequence of algorithms attaining this rate.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent survey on optimal numerical integration algorithms. While the bound is known for the unit cube via classical quasi-Monte Carlo/composite rules, a general characterization of domains $D_d$ of volume 1 admitting the $c_k\, d\, n^{-k/d}$ rate, together with explicit constructive algorithms, does not appear to have been resolved in subsequent literature.

Construct algorithms that achieve this bound for such domains.", "claim": "The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on optimal numerical integration."}]

paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Banach-space analogues of Hilbert-space lower bounds
original_question: In tensor-product numerical integration problems on reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, assume for each coordinate space H_i there is a unit-norm bounded linear functional with nonnegative representer h_i, functions f_i and g_i such that (h_i,f_i,g_i) is orthonormal, and a parameter alpha_i in (0,1] such that alpha_i h_i = sqrt(f_i^2+g_i^2). Under these assumptions the worst-case error satisfies lower bounds of the form e(n,F_d)^2 >= 1 - n prod_{i=1}^d (1+alpha_i^2)^(-1). Do analogous lower bounds hold for comparable integration problems on Banach spaces rather than Hilbert spaces?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. For each i = 1, ..., d, let F_i be a Banach space of real-valued functions on some domain D_i, continuously embedded so that point evaluations (or appropriate linear functionals) are bounded, and let S_i : F_i → R be a bounded linear functional with unit norm (think of S_i(f) = ∫ f dμ_i as a univariate integration functional). Let F_d be a suitable tensor product Banach space of F_1, ..., F_d, and let S_d = S_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S_d be the corresponding tensor-product functional on F_d. For an algorithm A_n that uses at most n linear (or function-value) evaluations to approximate S_d, the worst-case error is

  e(A_n, F_d) = sup { |S_d(f) − A_n(f)| : f ∈ F_d, ‖f‖ ≤ 1 },

and the n-th minimal worst-case error is e(n, F_d) = inf_{A_n} e(A_n, F_d).

Background (Hilbert case). When each F_i = H_i is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, the following is known: if for each i there exists a bounded linear functional on H_i with unit norm whose Riesz representer h_i is nonnegative, together with functions f_i, g_i such that the triple (h_i, f_i, g_i) is orthonormal in H_i, and a parameter α_i ∈ (0, 1] such that

  α_i · h_i = sqrt(f_i^2 + g_i^2),

then for all n ∈ N,

  e(n, F_d)^2 ≥ 1 − n · ∏_{i=1}^d (1 + α_i^2)^{−1}.

Question. Formulate and prove an analogous lower bound for the n-th minimal worst-case error of the tensor-product integration functional S_d on tensor products of Banach spaces F_i (rather than Hilbert spaces). That is, identify a structural condition on each Banach space F_i — playing the role of the orthonormal triple (h_i, f_i, g_i) and parameter α_i ∈ (0, 1] in the Hilbert setting — under which one can establish a lower bound of the form

  e(n, F_d) ≥ φ( n, α_1, ..., α_d )

for an explicit function φ exhibiting the same qualitative dependence on n and on the α_i as in the Hilbert-space inequality above (in particular forcing e(n, F_d) to remain bounded away from 0 unless n is at least of order ∏_{i=1}^d (1 + α_i^2)).
status_search_result: A web search for tensor-product integration lower bounds on Banach spaces returned recent work (notably the 2024 paper "Intractability results for integration in tensor product spaces," arXiv:2404.17163) that develops lower-bound techniques generalizing the decomposable reproducing-kernel method, but these results still rely on a Hilbert-space or RKHS structure or a worst-case function decomposition rather than supplying the precise Banach-space analogue of the (1 + α_i^2)^{-1} product bound. No source was found that resolves the stated Banach-space question, so it appears to remain open.

paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
original_question: A universal integration algorithm is meant to perform optimally across multiple smoothness classes rather than being tuned to one specific class. Here tractability concerns how the information complexity n(epsilon,F_d) depends on dimension d and error tolerance epsilon, for example polynomial dependence on d and epsilon^(-1), or strong polynomial dependence on epsilon^(-1) alone. Can universality be developed at the level of tractability as well, so that one studies and characterizes universal algorithms with optimal tractability properties, not only optimal convergence rates?
self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider multivariate numerical integration on the d-dimensional unit cube. For a class F_d of integrable real-valued functions on [0,1]^d, an algorithm A_n that uses at most n function values produces approximations A_n(f) to the integral I_d(f) = ∫_{[0,1]^d} f(x) dx. The worst-case error of A_n on F_d is

  e(A_n, F_d) = sup{ |I_d(f) − A_n(f)| : f ∈ F_d, ‖f‖_{F_d} ≤ 1 },

and the information complexity is

  n(ε, F_d) = min{ n : there exists A_n with e(A_n, F_d) ≤ ε }.

Tractability notions. The integration problem on the family {F_d}_{d≥1} is called:
 (a) polynomially tractable if there exist constants C, p, q ≥ 0 such that n(ε, F_d) ≤ C d^q ε^{−p} for all d ∈ ℕ and ε ∈ (0,1);
 (b) strongly polynomially tractable if there exist constants C, p ≥ 0 such that n(ε, F_d) ≤ C ε^{−p} for all d ∈ ℕ and ε ∈ (0,1).

Universality. A sequence of algorithms (A_n)_{n≥1} is called universal for a collection 𝒞 = {F_d^{(α)} : α ∈ A} of function classes (indexed by smoothness parameters, weights, or other a priori unknown features α) if, for every α ∈ A, the algorithms (A_n) achieve the optimal order of convergence of e(A_n, F_d^{(α)}) in n as n → ∞, without the algorithm depending on α.

Problem. Develop a theory of universality at the level of tractability rather than only at the level of convergence rate. Specifically:

 1. Formulate a precise notion of a "tractability-universal" algorithm, i.e. a single sequence (A_n) that, for every class F_d^{(α)} in a prescribed collection 𝒞, attains the same (polynomial or strong polynomial) tractability exponents as the best class-specific algorithm tailored to F_d^{(α)}.

 2. Characterize, for natural collections 𝒞 (for example, scales of isotropic Sobolev spaces H^k_d with k > d/2, classes of mixed smoothness H^{k,mix}_d, or weighted Korobov / Hilbert spaces with varying weights), whether such tractability-universal algorithms exist and, when they do, determine the optimal tractability exponents achievable simultaneously across 𝒞.

 3. Provide either explicit constructions of such universal algorithms or prove obstructions showing that tractability-universality must be strictly weaker than class-specific tractability.
status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) has produced universal algorithms for high-dimensional integration that are simultaneously universal in smoothness and weights and achieve polynomial/strong polynomial tractability in weighted Korobov spaces in both randomized and deterministic settings, addressing aspects of the open problem. However, a general characterization of tractability-universality across broad scales of classes and the constructive determination of optimal tractability exponents remain incomplete, so the broader problem is still partially solved.

paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
original_question: For the classical smoothness classes F_d^k(D_d) on volume-1 domains, explicit lower bounds of the form e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) >= min{1/2, c_k d n^(-k/d)} are known. What are the sharp values or sharper estimates of the constants c_k, and which domains D_d are extremal in the sense that, for given k, d, and n, the integration error e(n,F_d^k(D_d)) is especially small?
self_contained_problem:
For integers $d,k\ge 1$ and a measurable domain $D_d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of Lebesgue volume $1$, define the smoothness class
$$F_d^k(D_d)=\{f:D_d\to\mathbb{R}\mid \|\partial^\alpha f\|_\infty\le 1\text{ for all multi-indices }\alpha\text{ with }|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
For a positive integer $n$, the (deterministic) optimal $n$-point integration error is
$$e(n,F_d^k(D_d))=\inf_{x_1,\dots,x_n\in D_d}\ \inf_{a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb{R}}\ \sup_{f\in F_d^k(D_d)}\Big|\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i f(x_i)\Big|.$$
It is known that for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that, for all $d,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and all volume-1 domains $D_d$,
$$e(n,F_d^k(D_d))\ \ge\ \min\!\left\{\tfrac{1}{2},\ c_k\, d\, n^{-k/d}\right\}.$$
Determine the sharp (or sharper) values of the constants $c_k$ in this lower bound. Moreover, identify the extremal domains $D_d$ of volume $1$ for which, given $k$, $d$, and $n$, the integration error $e(n,F_d^k(D_d))$ is as small as possible.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent survey on optimal numerical integration. No subsequent work resolving the sharp values of $c_k$ or identifying extremal volume-1 domains was found. The lower bound is known to be tight in order on cubes, but the sharp constants and extremal sets remain undetermined.

paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Conjectured lower bound for an orthogonally invariant C2 class
original_question: Let C_tilde^2(D_d) be the class of twice continuously differentiable functions f on an open set D_d subset R^d with volume 1 such that ||f||_infty <= 1, Lip(f) <= d^(-1/2), and every directional derivative D^Theta f satisfies Lip(D^Theta f) <= d^(-1) for all directions Theta on the unit sphere. Does there exist a constant C>0, independent of d and of the domain D_d, such that the worst-case integration error always satisfies e(n,C_tilde^2(D_d)) >= C n^(-2/d)?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\ge 1$, let $D_d\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be an open set of Lebesgue volume $1$. Define the class
$$\widetilde{C}^{\,2}(D_d)=\Bigl\{\,f\in C^2(D_d)\ \Big|\ \|f\|_\infty\le 1,\ \mathrm{Lip}(f)\le d^{-1/2},\ \mathrm{Lip}(D_\Theta f)\le d^{-1}\ \text{for every unit vector }\Theta\in S^{d-1}\,\Bigr\},$$
where $D_\Theta f$ denotes the directional derivative of $f$ in direction $\Theta$ and $\mathrm{Lip}(g)$ is the (smallest) Lipschitz constant of $g$ on $D_d$.

For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the (deterministic) worst-case integration error using at most $n$ function evaluations is
$$e(n,\widetilde{C}^{\,2}(D_d))=\inf_{\substack{x_1,\dots,x_n\in D_d\\ \phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}}}\ \sup_{f\in \widetilde{C}^{\,2}(D_d)}\ \Bigl|\,\int_{D_d} f(x)\,dx-\phi(f(x_1),\dots,f(x_n))\,\Bigr|.$$

Decide whether there exists an absolute constant $C>0$, independent of both the dimension $d$ and the domain $D_d$, such that
$$e\bigl(n,\widetilde{C}^{\,2}(D_d)\bigr)\ \ge\ C\,n^{-2/d}\qquad \text{for all }n\in\mathbb{N},\ d\in\mathbb{N},\ \text{and all admissible }D_d.$$
status_search_result: The problem is stated explicitly as a conjecture in a recent survey on optimal algorithms for numerical integration. Related literature (Hinrichs, Krieg, Novak, and collaborators) develops Hilbert-space and Schur-product techniques for lower bounds for integration, but no source appears to establish the conjectured dimension-uniform $n^{-2/d}$ lower bound for the orthogonally invariant $\widetilde{C}^{\,2}(D_d)$ class. No resolution has been located.

paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
context_brief: Mixed-smoothness logarithmic loss under iid sampling
original_question: For functions with mixed smoothness on the d-torus, specifically the space H_d^{k,mix}(T^d), independent uniformly distributed sample points are known to be optimal for the Monte Carlo error and optimal up to a logarithmic factor for the uniform error, which also yields logarithmic-factor optimality for integration. Can that logarithmic loss be removed for uniformly distributed samples, as happens in the isotropic-smoothness setting?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^d = \mathbb{R}^d / \mathbb{Z}^d$ denote the $d$-dimensional torus, equipped with the normalized Lebesgue measure. For an integer $k \ge 1$, let $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ denote the Hilbert space of functions on $\mathbb{T}^d$ with dominating mixed smoothness $k$, namely the space of $f \in L_2(\mathbb{T}^d)$ whose Fourier coefficients $\hat f(\mathbf{m})$, $\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, satisfy
$$\|f\|_{H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}}^2 \;=\; \sum_{\mathbf{m}\in\mathbb{Z}^d} \Big(\prod_{j=1}^d (1+|m_j|)^{2k}\Big)\, |\hat f(\mathbf{m})|^2 \;<\; \infty.$$

Consider the integration problem $I(f) = \int_{\mathbb{T}^d} f(x)\,dx$ and randomized linear quadrature rules $Q_n(f) = \sum_{i=1}^n a_i f(X_i)$ where the nodes $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are required to be independent and uniformly distributed on $\mathbb{T}^d$ (the coefficients $a_i$ may depend on the nodes). Define the worst-case error under iid uniform sampling by
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;=\; \inf_{a_1,\dots,a_n} \;\sup_{\|f\|_{H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}}\le 1} \;\mathbb{E}\,\big|I(f)-Q_n(f)\big|,$$
and let $e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$ denote the corresponding optimal worst-case error over all randomized algorithms using $n$ function evaluations at arbitrary (possibly adaptive) sample points.

It is known that iid uniform sampling is optimal for $L_2$-approximation in $H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)$ with respect to the Monte Carlo (mean-square) error, and optimal up to a logarithmic factor with respect to the uniform error, which yields
$$e_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d)) \;\le\; C(d,k)\,(\log n)^{\alpha(d,k)}\, e_n^{\mathrm{opt}}(I; H^{k,\mathrm{mix}}(\mathbb{T}^d))$$
for some exponent $\alpha(d,k)>0$.

original_question: For Sobolev approximation based on iid uniformly distributed sample points on a domain D_d subset R^d, do the asymptotic constants in expressions such as lim_{n->infinity} e(P_n,W_p^s(D_d),L_q(D_d)) n^{s/d-(1/p-1/q)+} always exist, and if they exist, do they depend only on the volume of D_d rather than on its shape?
self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$, $s\ge 1$ an integer, and $1\le p,q\le\infty$ with $s/d > (1/p - 1/q)_+$, where $(x)_+ = \max(x,0)$. Let $D_d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, and let $W_p^s(D_d)$ denote the Sobolev space of functions on $D_d$ with smoothness $s$ in $L_p$, equipped with its usual norm; let $L_q(D_d)$ be the target space.

For a set of sample points $P_n=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}\subset D_d$, define the worst-case $L_q$-approximation error using only function values at $P_n$ by
$$
 e(P_n,W_p^s(D_d),L_q(D_d)) := \inf_{A_n}\ \sup_{\|f\|_{W_p^s(D_d)}\le 1}\ \|f - A_n(f(x_1),\dots,f(x_n))\|_{L_q(D_d)},
$$
where the infimum is over all (possibly nonlinear) reconstruction maps $A_n:\mathbb{R}^n\to L_q(D_d)$. Let $P_n=(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ consist of independent points drawn from the uniform distribution on $D_d$, and consider the (random) error $e(P_n,W_p^s(D_d),L_q(D_d))$ multiplied by the conjectured optimal rate factor $n^{\,s/d-(1/p-1/q)_+}$.

(a) Does the limit
$$

$$
exist (in $(0,\infty)$) for every such domain $D_d$ and every admissible choice of $s,p,q$?

(b) If it exists, does $C(D_d,s,p,q)$ depend on $D_d$ only through its $d$-dimensional Lebesgue volume $|D_d|$, and not on the shape of $D_d$?

original_question: Find a nonsmoothable local Gorenstein algebra A whose canonical graded Gorenstein quotient Q(0) is smoothable, preferably with small degree.
self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. A finite local Artinian $k$-algebra $(A, \mathfrak{m}, k)$ is called Gorenstein if its socle $\operatorname{Soc}(A) = \{a \in A : a\mathfrak{m} = 0\}$ is one-dimensional over $k$. Such an algebra $A$ corresponds to a $k$-point of the Hilbert scheme $\operatorname{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{A}^N)$ of $n = \dim_k A$ points in affine space (after a closed embedding $\operatorname{Spec} A \hookrightarrow \mathbb{A}^N$). The algebra $A$ is called smoothable if this point lies in the closure of the locus parametrizing reduced $n$-tuples of distinct points, equivalently, if $\operatorname{Spec} A$ is a flat limit of $n$ distinct reduced points.

For a local Gorenstein $k$-algebra $A$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$, let $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A) = \bigoplus_{i \geq 0} \mathfrak{m}^i / \mathfrak{m}^{i+1}$ be the associated graded algebra. The canonical graded Gorenstein quotient $Q(0)$ of $A$ is defined as the (unique) graded Gorenstein quotient of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A)$ whose socle degree equals that of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A)$; explicitly, $Q(0) = \operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A) / C$, where $C$ is the largest graded ideal of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak{m}}(A)$ not containing the top-degree socle.

Exhibit an explicit example of a nonsmoothable finite local Gorenstein $k$-algebra $A$ such that its canonical graded Gorenstein quotient $Q(0)$ is smoothable. The example should have $\dim_k A$ as small as possible.
status_search_result: A direct search for an explicit example with the prescribed property did not turn up a published resolution. Related work continues on the structure of smoothable and nonsmoothable Gorenstein points in Hilbert schemes (e.g., new elementary components of the Gorenstein locus), but no source clearly providing the requested example was identified.

original_question: For which domains is the Bergman kernel function K(z,w) nonvanishing everywhere, as in the Lu Qi-Keng problem?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $A^2(\Omega)$ denote the Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on $\Omega$ that are square-integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure. The Bergman kernel of $\Omega$ is the reproducing kernel $K_\Omega:\Omega\times\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$ of $A^2(\Omega)$, characterized by $f(z)=\int_\Omega K_\Omega(z,w)f(w)\,dV(w)$ for every $f\in A^2(\Omega)$ and $z\in\Omega$. Call $\Omega$ a Lu Qi-Keng domain if $K_\Omega(z,w)\neq 0$ for all $(z,w)\in\Omega\times\Omega$.

Give an intrinsic characterization of those bounded domains $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ that are Lu Qi-Keng domains; equivalently, determine necessary and sufficient geometric or function-theoretic conditions on $\Omega$ under which the Bergman kernel $K_\Omega$ is everywhere nonvanishing on $\Omega\times\Omega$.
status_search_result: The original Lu Qi-Keng conjecture (that the Bergman kernel is nonvanishing for every bounded domain) was disproved by Skwarczyński (1969) using an annulus with small inner radius, and many further counterexamples are known (products of disc and annulus, fat Hartogs triangles, certain Thullen/Hua domains). Positive results hold for the ball, polydisc, and bounded homogeneous complete circular domains. The general problem of classifying which bounded domains are Lu Qi-Keng domains remains open.

original_question: Is there a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain in C^n on which the Kobayashi and Caratheodory metrics are not comparable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded domain. For $z \in \Omega$ and $v \in \mathbb{C}^n$, define the infinitesimal Kobayashi (pseudo)metric by
$$F_\Omega^K(z,v) = \inf\{\,|\alpha| > 0 : \exists\, f:\mathbb{D} \to \Omega \text{ holomorphic with } f(0)=z,\ f'(0) = v/\alpha\,\},$$
where $\mathbb{D}$ denotes the open unit disk in $\mathbb{C}$, and the infinitesimal Carathéodory (pseudo)metric by
$$F_\Omega^C(z,v) = \sup\{\,|df(z)\,v| : f : \Omega \to \mathbb{D} \text{ holomorphic}\,\}.$$
One always has $F_\Omega^C(z,v) \le F_\Omega^K(z,v)$. Say that the Kobayashi and Carathéodory metrics on $\Omega$ are comparable if there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that
$$F_\Omega^K(z,v) \le C\, F_\Omega^C(z,v) \quad \text{for all } z \in \Omega,\ v \in \mathbb{C}^n.$$
Recall that $\Omega$ is pseudoconvex if $-\log \mathrm{dist}(\cdot,\partial\Omega)$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$, and smoothly bounded if $\partial\Omega$ is a $C^\infty$ submanifold of $\mathbb{C}^n$.

Question: Does there exist a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ on which the Kobayashi and Carathéodory metrics are not comparable?

The problem appears to remain open.

self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ be a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain of finite type (in the sense of D'Angelo / Kohn), and let $p \in \partial \Omega$. Does there exist an open neighborhood $U$ of $p$ in $\mathbb{C}^2$ and a biholomorphic map $\Phi : U \cap \Omega \to \Phi(U \cap \Omega) \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ such that:

(i) $\Phi(U \cap \Omega)$ is a convex domain in $\mathbb{C}^2$, and

(ii) $\Phi$ extends continuously to $U \cap \overline{\Omega}$?

In other words, is every finite type pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^2$ locally convexifiable near each boundary point by a biholomorphism with continuous boundary values?
status_search_result: A direct resolution of the question of local convexifiability of finite type pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$ by biholomorphisms with continuous boundary values does not appear in the available search results. Related work (e.g., Diederich–Fornæss–Wold on exposing points and convexifiable domains of finite 1-type, and works on McNeal/Catlin's normal forms in $\mathbb{C}^2$) addresses neighboring questions but does not conclusively settle this exact formulation. Status appears unverified in the public literature found.

original_question: What is the asymptotic behavior of the Kobayashi metric on finite-type domains in C^n?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain of finite type (in the sense of D'Angelo), and let $k_\Omega : \Omega \times \mathbb{C}^n \to [0,\infty)$ denote the Kobayashi–Royden infinitesimal pseudometric, defined for $(z,v) \in \Omega \times \mathbb{C}^n$ by
$$k_\Omega(z,v) = \inf\{|\xi| : \xi \in \mathbb{C},\ \exists f : \mathbb{D} \to \Omega \text{ holomorphic with } f(0) = z,\ f'(0) = v/\xi\},$$
where $\mathbb{D} \subset \mathbb{C}$ is the unit disk.

Determine the precise asymptotic behavior of $k_\Omega(z,v)$ as $z \to \partial \Omega$, in terms of geometric invariants of $\partial \Omega$ at the boundary point being approached (such as the type, the Levi form, and the direction of $v$ relative to the complex tangential and normal directions). In particular, give sharp upper and lower bounds for $k_\Omega(z,v)$ near $\partial\Omega$ valid for all directions $v$, and identify the leading-order behavior in both the complex normal and complex tangential directions.
category_tag: Kobayashi metric on finite type domains
status_search_result: Significant partial results exist. Graham (1975) gave nontangential asymptotics on strongly pseudoconvex domains; Catlin and J. Yu (1990s) established sharp boundary estimates on certain weakly pseudoconvex finite-type domains in C^2 and on h-extendible (semiregular) domains. More recent work (Zimmer, Fiacchi, Wang and others, 2016–2024) obtained sharp Kobayashi estimates and Gromov hyperbolicity on convex domains of finite type. A complete asymptotic description for general smoothly bounded pseudoconvex finite-type domains in C^n (n ≥ 3) remains open beyond the h-extendible/convex settings.

original_question: Given a compact complex hypersurface X in P^n with degree at least n + 2 and only normal crossing singularities. Show that the infinitesimal Kobayashi pseudometric on P^n \ X is degenerate at most on a complex hypersurface.
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n(\mathbb{C})$ be a compact complex hypersurface of degree $d \geq n+2$ having only normal crossing singularities (i.e., locally analytically $X$ is given by the vanishing of a product of distinct coordinate functions). Consider the complement $U = \mathbb{P}^n \setminus X$, and let $K_U : TU \to [0,\infty)$ denote its infinitesimal Kobayashi pseudometric, defined for $(p,v) \in TU$ by
$$K_U(p,v) = \inf\{|\xi| : \exists\, f : \mathbb{D} \to U \text{ holomorphic with } f(0)=p,\ df_0(\xi)=v\},$$
where $\mathbb{D} \subset \mathbb{C}$ is the unit disc. The degeneracy locus of $K_U$ is the set of $p \in U$ such that there exists $0 \neq v \in T_p U$ with $K_U(p,v) = 0$. Prove that this degeneracy locus is contained in a complex hypersurface of $U$.
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this problem. It was posed by N. Sibony as a problem on hyperbolicity of complements of hypersurfaces of degree at least n+2 in projective space, a context closely tied to the still-open Kobayashi conjecture on hyperbolicity of generic high-degree hypersurface complements. No source confirming a complete solution was located.

original_question: Can you recover certain derivatives of the Levi form at a weakly pseudoconvex point in terms of the weighted boundary behavior of the Kobayashi metric?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain with defining function $\rho$, and let $p \in \partial \Omega$ be a weakly pseudoconvex boundary point (i.e., the Levi form $L_p(\xi,\bar\xi) = \sum_{j,k} \frac{\partial^2 \rho}{\partial z_j \partial \bar z_k}(p)\,\xi_j \bar\xi_k$, restricted to the complex tangent space $T^{1,0}_p(\partial\Omega)$, is positive semidefinite but degenerate). Let $F_\Omega(z,\xi)$ denote the Kobayashi–Royden infinitesimal metric on $\Omega$, where for $z \in \Omega$ and $\xi \in \mathbb{C}^n$,
$$F_\Omega(z,\xi) = \inf\{\,|\alpha| : \exists\,\phi : \mathbb{D} \to \Omega \text{ holomorphic with } \phi(0)=z,\ \phi'(0)=\xi/\alpha\,\}.$$
For a multi-index of weights associated to a system of local coordinates around $p$ adapted to $\partial\Omega$ (e.g., normalized so that complex normal and complex tangential directions are separated and weighted by powers of the boundary distance $\delta(z) = \mathrm{dist}(z,\partial\Omega)$), study the asymptotic behavior of $F_\Omega(z,\xi)$ as $z \to p$ non-tangentially, with $\xi$ taken in tangential or normal directions and scaled by the appropriate weights.

Question: Can one recover certain higher-order derivatives of the Levi form at the weakly pseudoconvex point $p$ from this weighted boundary behavior of the Kobayashi metric? More precisely, identify explicit weighted asymptotic functionals built from $F_\Omega(z,\xi)$ as $z \to p$ whose limits compute prescribed derivatives (of specified order) of the Levi form coefficients at $p$.
status_search_result: A web search located related results on boundary behavior of the Kobayashi metric on weakly pseudoconvex (in particular finite-type and Levi corank one) domains, where leading-order asymptotics encode the Levi form itself. However, no source was found that explicitly settles the recovery of higher-order derivatives of the Levi form at weakly pseudoconvex points from weighted Kobayashi-metric asymptotics in the generality asked. The status appears unresolved.

original_question: Find conditions insuring that if a sequence of plurisubharmonic functions um → u in C^n then (ddc um )n → (ddc u)n .
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be an open set and let $\mathrm{PSH}(\Omega)$ denote the cone of plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega$. For a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $u$, the complex Monge-Ampère operator $(dd^c u)^n$ is defined inductively by Bedford-Taylor as the positive Borel measure obtained from the closed positive current $dd^c u \wedge \cdots \wedge dd^c u$ ($n$ times), where $d = \partial +  ar\partial$ and $d^c =  rac{i}{2\pi}( ar\partial - \partial)$.

Problem: Determine general conditions on a sequence $\{u_m\} \subset \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega)$ and a function $u \in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega)$ with $u_m 	o u$ (in some specified sense on $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$) which guarantee that the Monge-Ampère measures converge weakly:
$$(dd^c u_m)^n \;\longrightarrow\; (dd^c u)^n \quad 	ext{as } m 	o \infty,$$
in the sense of weak convergence of Radon measures on $\Omega$. In particular, identify natural classes of (possibly unbounded) plurisubharmonic functions and modes of convergence (e.g.\ monotone, in capacity, in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ together with auxiliary uniform bounds) for which this continuity property holds, and exhibit counterexamples showing the sharpness of the imposed conditions.
status_search_result: This is a long-standing question in pluripotential theory with many partial results. Bedford-Taylor established continuity for monotone sequences of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions, and Xing, Cegrell, Kolodziej and others have shown that convergence in capacity (with suitable uniform domination) implies weak convergence of the Monge-Ampère measures. Substantial extensions exist within the Cegrell classes $\mathcal{E}_0$, $\mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{E}$ for unbounded psh functions. Despite these advances, a single complete characterization of all sequences for which $(dd^c u_m)^n \to (dd^c u)^n$ is not known, so the problem in full generality remains active.

original_question: Which smooth domains have non compact automorphism groups?
self_contained_problem:
Characterize the smoothly bounded domains $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ whose holomorphic automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(\Omega)$ (the group of biholomorphic self-maps of $\Omega$, endowed with the compact-open topology) is non-compact. 

Equivalently (by H. Cartan's theorem), characterize those smoothly bounded domains $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ for which there exist a point $z_0 \in \Omega$, a sequence of automorphisms $\{\varphi_j\} \subset \mathrm{Aut}(\Omega)$, and a boundary point $p \in \partial\Omega$ such that $\varphi_j(z_0) \to p$ as $j \to \infty$.

A widely studied conjectural answer (the Greene–Krantz conjecture) asserts: if $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ is a smoothly bounded domain and $p \in \partial\Omega$ is a boundary orbit accumulation point of $\mathrm{Aut}(\Omega)$, then $\partial\Omega$ is of finite type at $p$ in the sense of D'Angelo. Prove or disprove this conjecture, and obtain the corresponding classification of smoothly bounded domains with non-compact automorphism group.
category_tag: Automorphism groups of domains in several complex variables
status_search_result: The problem is the motivation for the Greene–Krantz conjecture, which remains open in general. Partial results are known: a full classification has been obtained for smoothly bounded Reinhardt domains (Fu–Isaev–Krantz), and the Greene–Krantz conjecture has been verified for convex domains in $\mathbb{C}^2$ and for domains whose boundary contains a smooth curve of infinite-type points. A complete characterization in arbitrary dimensions is not known.

original_question: What is the lowest degree of a polynomial mapping P : R2 → R2 for which the (real) Jacobian conjecture fails, i.e. the Jacobian of P never vanishes while p fails to be invertible.
self_contained_problem: Determine the smallest positive integer d with the following property: there exists a polynomial map P = (p, q) : R^2 → R^2, with p, q ∈ R[x, y] and max(deg p, deg q) = d (equivalently, total degree d), such that the Jacobian determinant det(DP)(x, y) = ∂p/∂x · ∂q/∂y − ∂p/∂y · ∂q/∂x is nowhere zero on R^2, yet the map P fails to be injective (and hence is not a global diffeomorphism of R^2 onto its image). In other words, find the lowest degree at which the real Jacobian conjecture in dimension two can fail.
status_search_result: Pinchuk gave the first counterexamples to the strong real Jacobian conjecture (with component degrees on the order of 10 and 25, total degree ~35). Subsequent work has lowered the known degrees of counterexamples (e.g., constructions with components of degrees 10 and 15, and counterexamples built from certain degree-9 auxiliary polynomials), but the exact minimum degree at which the real Jacobian conjecture in R^2 fails has not been determined. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: If M is an n-dimensional parallellizable Stein manifold, can M be holomorphically immersed in C^n ? [ True for n=1 (Gunning and Narasimhan); also such an M can be immersed in C^n+1 (Eliashberg-Gromov)].
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be an $n$-dimensional parallelizable Stein manifold; that is, $M$ is a complex manifold of complex dimension $n$ which admits a proper holomorphic embedding into some $\mathbb{C}^N$ (equivalently, $M$ is Stein) and whose holomorphic tangent bundle $TM$ is holomorphically trivial. Does there always exist a holomorphic immersion $f \colon M \to \mathbb{C}^n$, i.e., a holomorphic map whose differential $df_p \colon T_pM \to T_{f(p)}\mathbb{C}^n$ is a (complex-linear) isomorphism at every point $p \in M$?

Known facts: for $n=1$ this holds (every open Riemann surface admits a holomorphic immersion into $\mathbb{C}$), and for every $n$ such an $M$ admits a holomorphic immersion into $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$.
status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on holomorphic immersions of Stein manifolds (including Forstnerič's 2017 survey and subsequent work on noncritical holomorphic functions and foliations) state that the question of whether every parallelizable Stein manifold of dimension n ≥ 2 admits a holomorphic immersion into C^n remains open. Partial progress includes existence of submersions to C^{n-1} and nonsingular holomorphic foliations of intermediate dimensions, but the immersion problem into C^n itself is not resolved.

original_question: Do there exist Fatou–Bieberbach domains which are not Runge? A Fatou–Bieberbach domain is a proper subdomain of C^2 which is biholomorphic to C^2 .
self_contained_problem:
A Fatou–Bieberbach domain is a proper open subdomain Ω ⊊ ℂ² that is biholomorphic to ℂ². Such a domain Ω is called Runge if every holomorphic function on Ω can be approximated, uniformly on compact subsets of Ω, by polynomials on ℂ² (equivalently, by entire functions on ℂ²).

Question: Does there exist a Fatou–Bieberbach domain Ω ⊊ ℂ² which is not Runge in ℂ²?
status_search_result: The question was answered affirmatively by E. F. Wold, who constructed a Fatou–Bieberbach domain in ℂ² that is not Runge ("A Fatou–Bieberbach domain in ℂ² which is not Runge," Mathematische Annalen, 2008). Subsequent works have extended these constructions to Stein manifolds with the density property.

original_question: The Fatou Set of a Polynomial Automorphism of C^2 . Let f be a polynomial automorphism of C^2 , and suppose that f is not conjugate to an elementary map. Let Omega be a connected component of the set of points where the forward iterates {f n : n = 1, 2, 3, ...} are locally bounded, which is the Fatou set of f . Let us suppose that Omega is periodic, i.e. f n Omega = Omega for some n 6= 0. Let us first consider the case in which Omega is recurrent, i.e. Omega contains a point whose orbit does not converge to ∂Omega. In this case Omega is either (a) a basin of attraction of a sink orbit, (b) the basin of attractin of a Siegel disk, or (c) the basin of a Herman ring. It is not hard to construct examples of (a) and (b). (i) Can case (c) occur? Nothing at all seems to be known about periodic domains which are not recurrent. (ii) If Omega is not recurrent, does there exist P ∈ ∂Omega such that limk→∞ f nk (Q) = P for all Q ∈ Omega? (iii) If Omega is not recurrent, does there exist P ∈ ∂Omega such that f n P = P , and one of the eigenvalues of DF (P ) is e2πip/q ?
self_contained_problem:
Let f be a polynomial automorphism of C^2 that is not conjugate to an elementary map (i.e., it has nontrivial dynamics; equivalently, after conjugation by polynomial automorphisms, it is a finite composition of generalized Hénon maps). Define the Fatou set of f to be the set of points p ∈ C^2 having a neighborhood on which the family of forward iterates {f^n : n = 1, 2, 3, …} is locally bounded (equivalently, locally equicontinuous on compact sets). Let Ω be a connected component of the Fatou set and suppose Ω is periodic, meaning f^n(Ω) = Ω for some integer n ≠ 0. Call Ω recurrent if it contains a point whose forward orbit does not converge to ∂Ω.

It is known that if Ω is periodic and recurrent, then Ω is one of:
(a) the basin of attraction of an attracting periodic orbit (sink),
(b) the basin of a Siegel disk (periodic point with both eigenvalues of modulus 1, conjugate to a rotation), or
(c) the basin of a Herman ring (an invariant annulus on which the dynamics is conjugate to an irrational rotation).

Examples are known for cases (a) and (b). Resolve the following:

(i) Can case (c) occur? That is, does there exist a polynomial automorphism of C^2 (non-elementary) possessing a periodic recurrent Fatou component which is the basin of a Herman ring?

(ii) Suppose Ω is a periodic Fatou component that is not recurrent. Must there exist a point P ∈ ∂Ω such that, for every Q ∈ Ω, lim_{k→∞} f^{nk}(Q) = P (along the period-n iterates)?

(iii) Under the same hypothesis (Ω periodic, non-recurrent), must there exist a point P ∈ ∂Ω with f^n(P) = P such that one of the eigenvalues of Df^n(P) equals e^{2πi p/q} for some rational p/q?

original_question: Suppose f is a holomorphic map on P^2 of degree d ≥ 2. Must f have a repelling fixed point.
self_contained_problem: Let $f:\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ be a holomorphic self-map of the complex projective plane of algebraic degree $d \geq 2$ (i.e., $f$ is induced by a triple of homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in three variables with no common zero other than the origin). A fixed point $p$ of $f$ is said to be repelling if both eigenvalues of the differential $df_p$ (acting on the tangent space $T_p\mathbb{P}^2$) have modulus strictly greater than $1$. Must every such $f$ possess at least one repelling fixed point?
status_search_result: Web searches turned up extensive related results — e.g., the Briend–Duval theorem that repelling periodic points are dense in the Julia set of any holomorphic endomorphism of $\mathbb{P}^k$ of degree $\geq 2$, work by Guillot–Ramírez on multipliers at fixed points of quadratic self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^2$, and work by Berteloot–Bianchi on holomorphic motions of repelling cycles — but no source was found that explicitly resolves the question of whether every degree-$d\geq 2$ holomorphic self-map of $\mathbb{P}^2$ necessarily has a repelling fixed point. The current status could not be conclusively verified.

original_question: Does there exist a holomorphic map F : P^k → P^k with a T wandering Fatou component U, i.e. F n (U) F m (U) = ∅ for all n 6= m?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k \geq 2$ and let $\mathbb{P}^k = \mathbb{P}^k(\mathbb{C})$ denote complex projective space. A holomorphic map $F: \mathbb{P}^k \to \mathbb{P}^k$ has Fatou set $\mathcal{F}(F)$ equal to the largest open subset of $\mathbb{P}^k$ on which the family of iterates $\{F^n\}_{n\geq 0}$ is normal (locally equicontinuous). A connected component $U$ of $\mathcal{F}(F)$ is called a wandering Fatou component if $F^n(U) \cap F^m(U) = \emptyset$ for all integers $n \neq m \geq 0$ (equivalently, no component containing $F^n(U)$ ever coincides with one containing $F^m(U)$).

Question: Does there exist a holomorphic endomorphism $F: \mathbb{P}^k \to \mathbb{P}^k$ (for some $k \geq 2$) admitting a wandering Fatou component?
status_search_result: Astorg, Buff, Dujardin, Peters, and Raissy (Annals of Mathematics, 2016) constructed polynomial skew-product endomorphisms of $\mathbb{C}^2$ that extend holomorphically to $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ and possess a wandering Fatou component, answering the question affirmatively for $k=2$ (and hence for all $k\geq 2$). The construction uses parabolic implosion techniques.

original_question: Let f : P^2 → P^2 be a holomorphic map of degree d ≥ 2 and let λ1 ≤ λ2 be the Lyapunov exponents for the ergodic measure mu = T ∧T . Is λ1 > 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})\to\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ be a holomorphic endomorphism of algebraic degree $d\ge 2$. Let $T$ denote the Green current of $f$, defined as $T=\lim_{n\to\infty} d^{-n}(f^n)^*\omega$, where $\omega$ is the Fubini–Study Kähler form on $\mathbb{P}^2$; this current is a positive closed $(1,1)$-current with continuous potentials. Let $\mu = T\wedge T$ be the associated equilibrium (Green) probability measure, which is $f$-invariant, mixing, and ergodic. Let $\lambda_1 \le \lambda_2$ be the Lyapunov exponents of the ergodic system $(f,\mu)$, computed via the Oseledec theorem applied to the differential $Df$. 

Question: Is $\lambda_1 > 0$?
status_search_result: Briend and Duval (Acta Math. 182, 1999) proved that for any holomorphic endomorphism of $\mathbb{P}^k$ of degree $d\ge 2$, every Lyapunov exponent of the equilibrium measure $\mu$ is bounded below by $\tfrac{1}{2}\log d > 0$. In particular for $k=2$ one has $\lambda_1 \ge \tfrac{1}{2}\log d > 0$, answering the question affirmatively.

original_question: Consider the following statement: “ Let Y be a compact subset of C^2 which lies over the circle |λ| = 1, and let U be an open neighborhood of K, the polynomially convex hull of Y. Then there exists a finitely sheeted Riemann surface S lying over |λ| < 1 as a branched covering such that S ⊂ U.” Is this statement true for every choice of Y and U?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\pi:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ denote the projection $\pi(\lambda,w)=\lambda$. Suppose $Y\subset\mathbb{C}^2$ is a compact set lying over the unit circle, i.e. $\pi(Y)\subset\{\lambda\in\mathbb{C}:|\lambda|=1\}$. Let
$$K=\widehat{Y}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}^2 : |p(z)|\le \max_{Y}|p|\text{ for every holomorphic polynomial }p\}$$
be the polynomially convex hull of $Y$, and let $U\subset\mathbb{C}^2$ be any open neighborhood of $K$.

By a finitely sheeted Riemann surface lying over the open unit disc $\{|\lambda|<1\}$ as a branched covering, we mean a complex one-dimensional analytic subvariety $S\subset\mathbb{C}^2$ (possibly with isolated singularities) such that the restriction $\pi|_{\overline{S}}:\overline{S}\to\{|\lambda|\le 1\}$ is a proper finite-to-one branched covering map onto the closed unit disc.

Question: Is it true that for every such compact set $Y$ and every open neighborhood $U$ of $\widehat{Y}$, there exists a finitely sheeted branched Riemann surface $S$ over $\{|\lambda|<1\}$ with $S\subset U$?

The current status could not be definitively verified.

original_question: Are strongly pseudoconvex CR manifolds of real dimension 5 locally embeddable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth abstract CR manifold of real dimension $5$ that is strongly pseudoconvex. Recall that an abstract CR structure on $M$ consists of a smooth complex subbundle $T^{1,0}M \subset \mathbb{C}\otimes TM$ of complex rank $2$ such that $T^{1,0}M \cap \overline{T^{1,0}M} = 0$ and $[T^{1,0}M, T^{1,0}M] \subset T^{1,0}M$ (integrability). Strong pseudoconvexity means that the Levi form, defined for a local real one-form $\theta$ annihilating $T^{1,0}M \oplus \overline{T^{1,0}M}$ by $L_\theta(X,\overline{Y}) = -i\,d\theta(X,\overline{Y})$ for $X,Y \in T^{1,0}M$, is positive definite (after a choice of sign of $\theta$).

Question: Is every such $M$ locally CR-embeddable? Equivalently, for every point $p \in M$, does there exist an open neighborhood $U \ni p$ and a smooth CR map $F: U \to \mathbb{C}^N$ (for some $N$), i.e. a map whose components are annihilated by every section of $\overline{T^{1,0}M}$, such that $F$ is an embedding of $U$ onto a CR submanifold of $\mathbb{C}^N$?
status_search_result: Multiple recent sources (including a 2025 arXiv preprint and surveys in CR geometry) state that local embeddability of strongly pseudoconvex abstract CR manifolds is known in real dimension $\geq 9$ (Kuranishi) and dimension $7$ (Akahori), fails in dimension $3$ (Nirenberg and others), and that the dimension-$5$ case remains an open, notably delicate problem.

original_question: Liouville-type assertion on CR 3-manifolds. On a CR 3-manifold one can always define a Carnot-Caratheodory metric. A homeomorphism between two strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds is called conformal if it maps infinitesimal spheres with respect to a Carnot-Caratheodory metric to infinitesimal spheres. Is a conformal homeomorphism CR?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^3,H,J)$ and $(N^3,H',J')$ be strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds. Recall that a CR 3-manifold carries a contact distribution $H\subset TM$ of rank 2 endowed with an almost complex structure $J:H\to H$, and that after fixing a pseudo-Hermitian contact form $\theta$ (with $d\theta(\cdot,J\cdot)$ positive definite on $H$) one obtains an associated Carnot–Carathéodory metric $d_{CC}$: the distance between two points is the infimum of the lengths (measured by the Levi form) of horizontal curves joining them. For $p\in M$ and $r>0$ let $B_{CC}(p,r)=\{q:d_{CC}(p,q)<r\}$. 

Given a homeomorphism $f:M\to N$ and a point $p\in M$, define
$$L_f(p,r)=\sup_{d_{CC}(p,q)=r} d'_{CC}(f(p),f(q)), \qquad \ell_f(p,r)=\inf_{d_{CC}(p,q)=r} d'_{CC}(f(p),f(q)).$$
Call $f$ conformal at $p$ if $\lim_{r\to 0^+} L_f(p,r)/\ell_f(p,r)=1$, i.e. $f$ sends infinitesimal CC-spheres centered at $p$ to sets that are asymptotically CC-spheres centered at $f(p)$. Call $f$ conformal on $M$ if it is conformal at every point.

A homeomorphism $f:M\to N$ is said to be CR if it is a diffeomorphism with $df(H)=H'$ and $df\circ J=J'\circ df$ on $H$ (or the corresponding statement for anti-CR).

Question: Must every conformal homeomorphism $f:M\to N$ between strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds be a CR (or anti-CR) mapping?
status_search_result: Related results are known: Korányi–Reimann showed that smooth 1-quasiconformal mappings between domains of the Heisenberg group are CR or anti-CR (restrictions of SU(n+1,1) actions), and later work extended this to tight/Goursat Carnot groups and to 1-quasiconformal homeomorphisms on CR manifolds with symmetries. However, the specific Liouville-type assertion as stated — that any homeomorphism between strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds preserving infinitesimal CC-spheres must be CR — does not appear to have a definitively cited resolution in the searched literature, so the status is treated as unknown.

original_question: Prove that if Omega is strongly pseudoconvex then there is an absolute constant K > 0 such that the integrated Kobayashi distance between any two points can be realized by a Kobayashi chain of K discs. [For instance, on a convex domain, K = 1.] Prize $50 -S. Krantz. sk @math.wustl.edu
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a strongly pseudoconvex domain with smooth boundary. Recall the Kobayashi pseudodistance $d_\Omega^K$ on $\Omega$ is defined as follows. For $p, q \in \Omega$, a Kobayashi chain of length $m$ joining $p$ to $q$ is a finite sequence of holomorphic maps $f_1, \dots, f_m : \mathbb{D} \to \Omega$ (where $\mathbb{D}$ is the unit disc in $\mathbb{C}$) together with points $a_i, b_i \in \mathbb{D}$ for $i = 1, \dots, m$, such that $f_1(a_1) = p$, $f_m(b_m) = q$, and $f_i(b_i) = f_{i+1}(a_{i+1})$ for $1 \le i < m$. The Kobayashi distance is
$$d_\Omega^K(p,q) = \inf \sum_{i=1}^m \rho_{\mathbb{D}}(a_i, b_i),$$
where $\rho_{\mathbb{D}}$ is the Poincaré distance on $\mathbb{D}$ and the infimum is taken over all Kobayashi chains joining $p$ to $q$. The integrated Kobayashi distance is the length distance associated with the infinitesimal Kobayashi metric, which coincides with $d_\Omega^K$ on domains where they agree.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $K > 0$ (independent of $\Omega$ and of the points) such that for every strongly pseudoconvex domain $\Omega$ and every pair of points $p, q \in \Omega$, the value $d_\Omega^K(p,q)$ is realized (or attained as the infimum) by a Kobayashi chain consisting of at most $K$ analytic discs. (For comparison, on a convex domain one may take $K = 1$.)
status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this question. There has been substantial progress on local extremal discs near strongly pseudoconvex boundary points (Lempert, Burns–Krantz) and on sharp estimates for the Kobayashi distance on strongly pseudoconvex domains, as well as visibility-type results, but no source explicitly states that the chain-length problem with a uniform constant $K$ has been settled affirmatively or negatively. Status appears unverified.

context_brief: Central lozenge probability in a semiregular hexagon
original_question: In the semiregular hexagon with side lengths 2n-1, 2n, 2n-1, 2n, 2n-1, 2n, prove that the central location consisting of the two innermost triangles is covered by a lozenge in exactly one-third of all lozenge tilings. Equivalently, in the dual honeycomb graph, prove that a uniformly random perfect matching contains the central edge with probability exactly 1/3.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the semiregular hexagon $H_n$ in the triangular lattice whose six side lengths, in cyclic order, are $2n-1,\ 2n,\ 2n-1,\ 2n,\ 2n-1,\ 2n$. A lozenge (or rhombus) is the union of two unit equilateral triangles of the triangular lattice that share an edge, and a lozenge tiling of $H_n$ is a covering of $H_n$ by such lozenges with disjoint interiors. Equivalently, lozenge tilings of $H_n$ are in bijection with perfect matchings of the dual honeycomb graph $G_n$ whose vertices are the unit triangles of $H_n$ and whose edges connect adjacent triangles.

By the symmetry of $H_n$, there is a unique pair of unit triangles forming a lozenge at the very center; call this central lozenge $\ell^*$, and let $e^*$ be the corresponding central edge of $G_n$.

Prove that, when a lozenge tiling of $H_n$ is chosen uniformly at random (equivalently, when a perfect matching of $G_n$ is chosen uniformly at random),
$$\Pr[\ell^* \text{ appears in the tiling}] \;=\; \Pr[e^* \in \text{the matching}] \;=\; \tfrac{1}{3},$$
for every positive integer $n$.
status_search_result: The conjecture that the central lozenge appears in exactly one third of all lozenge tilings of the semiregular hexagon with sides 2n−1, 2n, 2n−1, 2n, 2n−1, 2n was proved by Ciucu and Krattenthaler ("The number of centered lozenge tilings of a symmetric hexagon", arXiv:math/9712209, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A), via Gessel–Viennot determinants and explicit product formulas; further refinements were given by Fulmek and Krattenthaler. The problem is therefore solved.

context_brief: Lozenge tilings of a three-hole semiregular hexagon
original_question: Find an exact enumeration formula for lozenge tilings of the hexagon with side lengths 2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3 after removing the triangle centered on each of the three long sides.
self_contained_problem:
Consider, on the triangular lattice, a semiregular hexagon with side lengths (2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3, 2n, 2n+3) taken in cyclic order, where n is a positive integer. The three sides of length 2n+3 are the "long sides". From the middle of each long side, remove the unique unit triangle that is centered on that side and points into the hexagon (i.e., for each long side, delete the central up- or down-pointing unit triangle whose base lies on that side). Let R_n denote the resulting region. A lozenge tiling of R_n is a covering of R_n by unit rhombi (lozenges), each formed by two unit triangles sharing an edge, with no overlap.

Find a closed-form (product) formula for the number of lozenge tilings of R_n as a function of n. More generally, give a q-analog enumerating these tilings weighted by an appropriate q-statistic.

Subsequent works (Ciucu–Lai–Rohatgi, and others) have further generalized this result.

context_brief: Cokernels of Carlitz and Kasteleyn matrices
original_question: Let K be the Kasteleyn matrix of an a, b, c semiregular hexagon, and let the associated Carlitz matrix be the b-by-b matrix obtained from K by row and column reductions, with entries given by binomial coefficients. Determine the cokernel of these Carlitz matrices, equivalently the cokernel of the Kasteleyn matrices of a, b, c hexagons, and if possible interpret that cokernel in terms of lozenge tilings.
self_contained_problem:
Consider an $a,b,c$ semiregular hexagon: a hexagon with side lengths $a,b,c,a,b,c$ (in cyclic order) drawn on the triangular lattice, whose region is tiled by unit lozenges (rhombi made of two adjacent unit triangles) in three orientations. The lozenge tilings of this hexagon are in bijection with the perfect matchings of its honeycomb dual graph $G_{a,b,c}$.

Let $K = K(a,b,c)$ be the Kasteleyn(–Percus) matrix associated with $G_{a,b,c}$, viewed as an integer matrix whose permanent (up to sign) counts perfect matchings. Through systematic row and column reductions over $\mathbb{Z}$, $K$ can be reduced to a $b \times b$ integer matrix $C = C(a,b,c)$, the Carlitz matrix, whose $(i,j)$ entry is the binomial coefficient
$$
C_{ij} \;=\; \binom{a+c}{a-i+j}, \qquad 1 \le i,j \le b.
$$
Since the row/column reductions are unimodular, the integer cokernels coincide:
$$
\operatorname{coker}(K) \;\cong\; \operatorname{coker}(C) \;=\; \mathbb{Z}^{b}/C\,\mathbb{Z}^{b}.
$$

Problem. Determine the cokernel $\operatorname{coker}(C(a,b,c))$ as a finite abelian group (equivalently, determine the Smith normal form of $C(a,b,c)$) for all positive integers $a,b,c$, and provide a combinatorial interpretation of this cokernel in terms of the lozenge tilings of the $a,b,c$ semiregular hexagon.
category_tag: Smith normal form of Kasteleyn matrices
status_search_result: Subsequent work, notably "Kasteleyn cokernels" (arXiv:math/0108150, Electron. J. Combin. 2002) and later REU notes by Conlon (2022), studies the Smith normal form of these Carlitz matrices. Partial results and conjectures have been obtained (e.g., a characterization of when the cokernel is cyclic, with C(4,2,2), C(2,4,2), C(2,2,4) conjectured to be the only such examples with min(a,b,c) > 1, and the rank of the cokernel bounded by min(a,b,c) via Gessel–Viennot), but no complete general formula or combinatorial interpretation in terms of lozenge tilings appears to be known.

context_brief: Aztec diamond with a knight-move pair of deleted squares
original_question: Count the domino tilings of an Aztec diamond after deleting two close-to-central squares that are related by a knight's move and are as central as possible subject to that constraint.
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, the Aztec diamond $AD_n$ is the union of all closed unit lattice squares whose centers $(x+\tfrac12, y+\tfrac12)$ satisfy $|x+\tfrac12|+|y+\tfrac12|\le n$. A domino is a $1\times 2$ or $2\times 1$ rectangle made of two unit squares; a domino tiling of a region is a covering of the region by non-overlapping dominoes. Two unit squares are said to be a knight's move apart if the displacement between their centers is $(\pm 1,\pm 2)$ or $(\pm 2,\pm 1)$.

Consider an Aztec diamond $AD_n$ from which two unit squares have been removed, subject to the following conditions:
(i) the two removed squares are a knight's move apart;
(ii) among all such pairs, the chosen pair is as close to the center of $AD_n$ as possible (up to the symmetries of the square, there is essentially only one such choice).

Find a closed-form expression (or product formula) for the number of domino tilings of the resulting region as a function of $n$.
status_search_result: Web searches did not return a clear resolution of this specific enumeration problem. The problem appears in a well-known list of open problems on enumeration of matchings, but no published solution or product formula for the number of domino tilings of an Aztec diamond with two central knight's-move-apart squares deleted was identified in the search results.

context_brief: Aztec rectangle with a near-central square removed
original_question: Find a formula for the number of domino tilings of a (2n-1)-by-2n Aztec rectangle after deleting one of the four squares adjacent to the central square.
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, the $(2n-1)$-by-$2n$ Aztec rectangle is the union of unit squares in the plane defined as follows: take the lattice region consisting of all unit squares $[i,i+1]\times[j,j+1]$ with $0\le i\le 2n-1$ and $0\le j\le 2n-2$ (so the region has $2n-1$ rows of length $2n$), arranged in the staircase fashion of an Aztec rectangle (i.e., the rows are successively offset so as to form the standard Aztec rectangle shape with axis $2n-1$ short side and $2n$ long side). The region has a well-defined central unit square. Removing the central square itself yields a region with no domino tiling, but removing any one of the four unit squares sharing an edge with the central square yields a region that admits domino tilings.

Find a closed-form formula, as a function of $n$, for the number of domino tilings (coverings by $1\times 2$ dominoes) of the $(2n-1)$-by-$2n$ Aztec rectangle with one of the four unit squares adjacent to the central square removed.
