paper_title: Open Problems in Number Theory
original_question: Let S be a finite set of rational primes, and let X(S) be the set of rational numbers x in Q such that both x and 1−x are S-units. The source asks for lower bounds on the size of X(S), or on the maximum of |X(S)| over all sets S with |S|=s. Does there exist a lower bound that grows faster than any polynomial in s?
self_contained_problem:
For a finite set $S$ of rational primes, a nonzero rational number is called an $S$-unit if every prime appearing (with nonzero exponent) in its factorization belongs to $S$. Define
$$X(S) = \{ x \in \mathbb{Q} : x \text{ and } 1-x \text{ are both } S\text{-units}\},$$
and let
$$N(s) = \max_{|S|=s} |X(S)|,$$
where the maximum is taken over all finite sets $S$ of rational primes of cardinality $s$.

Determine whether there exists a lower bound for $N(s)$ that grows faster than every polynomial in $s$; that is, does there exist a function $f(s)$ with $f(s)/s^k \to \infty$ as $s \to \infty$ for every fixed $k \ge 1$, such that $N(s) \ge f(s)$ for all sufficiently large $s$?
status_search_result: Erdős, Stewart and Tijdeman (Compositio Math. 66 (1988), 37–56) proved that there exist arbitrarily large sets $S$ of $s$ primes for which the $S$-unit equation $x+y=1$ has at least $\exp((4+o(1))(s/\log s)^{1/2})$ solutions, which grows faster than every polynomial in $s$. This gives an affirmative answer to the question. Konyagin–Soundararajan and Evertse–Moree–Stewart–Tijdeman later refined and generalized such bounds.

paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
original_question: In the multiserver job model, where jobs may request different numbers of servers and may have different service-time distributions, what is the exact stability region beyond the currently understood special cases such as identical exponential durations or the two-class exponential case?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a continuous-time multiserver-job queueing model defined as follows. There are k servers and J classes of jobs. Class-j jobs arrive according to independent Poisson processes with rates λ_j (j = 1, ..., J), each class-j job requires simultaneous use of exactly s_j ∈ {1, ..., k} servers for the entire duration of its service, and class-j service times are i.i.d. samples from a distribution F_j with mean 1/μ_j. Jobs are served in first-come-first-served (FCFS) order: the head-of-line job waits until s_j servers become simultaneously available, and jobs may pass one another only when blocked by capacity. A job in service cannot be preempted, and idle servers cannot work on waiting jobs that need more servers than currently available.

Define the system to be stable if the number-in-system process is positive recurrent. Determine, in closed form, the exact stability region — that is, the set of arrival-rate vectors (λ_1, ..., λ_J) for which the system is stable — as a function of (k, {s_j}, {F_j}, {μ_j}), in the general setting of arbitrarily many classes J ≥ 2 with possibly distinct server requirements s_j and possibly non-exponential service-time distributions F_j.

(Known special cases include: (i) all classes share a common exponential service-time distribution but may have different server requirements; (ii) J = 2 classes with class-dependent exponential service-time distributions. The problem asks for the characterization in the remaining general cases.)
status_search_result: Recent work by Grosof, Harchol-Balter, and Scheller-Wolf ("New Stability Results for Multiserver-Job Models via Product-form Saturated Systems", MAMA/SIGMETRICS PER, 2023) extends stability characterizations beyond the two-class exponential case using product-form saturated systems, but a fully general closed-form characterization for arbitrary numbers of classes with distinct (and possibly non-exponential) service distributions is not yet available. The problem remains open in full generality, with active partial progress.

paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
original_question: Suppose jobs arrive over time to a system with a fixed number n of servers, all jobs share the same concave, sublinear speedup function s(k), and each job's inherent size is unknown at arrival but is drawn from a non-exponential distribution. What server-allocation policy minimizes mean response time in this setting?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a queueing system with a fixed number $n$ of identical servers. Jobs arrive over time according to some stochastic arrival process. Each job $j$ has an inherent (sequential) size $X_j$ that is unknown at the time of arrival; the sizes $X_j$ are i.i.d. samples from a known distribution $F$ that is not exponential (and in particular need not be memoryless). All jobs share a common speedup function $s:\{1,2,\dots,n\}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ which is concave and sublinear (i.e., $s(k+1)-s(k)$ is non-increasing in $k$ and $s(k)<k\,s(1)$ for $k\ge 2$). If at a given instant a job is allocated $k$ servers, then it processes its remaining inherent work at rate $s(k)$. Allocations may be changed continuously over time, subject to the constraint that the total number of servers allocated to active jobs is at most $n$ (and jobs may be served in parallel, preempted, and reallocated at no cost). The response time of a job is the time between its arrival and its completion.

Determine the server-allocation policy (a mapping from the system state, namely the set of jobs in the system and their ages, to an allocation of the $n$ servers among them) that minimizes the mean response time in steady state.
category_tag: Parallel job scheduling in queueing theory
status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2026) have advanced the theory of optimal scheduling for parallelizable jobs with concave speedup functions, including the Consistent Derivative Ratio rule and SmartFill / General Water-Filling algorithms for known sizes, and ServerFilling-Gittins for unknown sizes in related multiserver-job models. However, none of these works appears to give a definitive solution for the specific setting of unknown inherent sizes drawn from a general (non-exponential) distribution with a common concave sublinear speedup on a fixed number of servers. The status thus appears unresolved in full generality.

original_question: When all jobs are present at time 0 and share a common speedup function that is neither of the form s(k)=k^p nor a simple threshold-based speedup function, what is the optimal way to allocate the n servers across jobs to minimize mean response time or mean slowdown?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a system with $n$ identical servers and $m$ jobs, all present at time $0$. Each job has an inherent (sequential) size $X_i>0$. There is a common speedup function $s:\{1,2,\dots,n\}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ with $s(1)=1$ that is the same for every job: if a job is currently allocated $k$ servers, its remaining size decreases at rate $s(k)$. A scheduling policy is a (possibly time-varying) assignment of nonnegative integers $k_1(t),\dots,k_m(t)$ to the alive jobs at each time $t\ge 0$, subject to $\sum_i k_i(t)\le n$. Let $T_i$ denote the completion time of job $i$ under a given policy. Define the mean response time $\overline{T}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m T_i$ and the mean slowdown $\overline{S}=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m T_i/X_i$.

Known special cases. When $s(k)=k^p$ for some $p\in(0,1]$, and when $s$ is a "threshold" speedup of the form $s(k)=k$ for $k\le k^\ast$ and $s(k)=s(k^\ast)$ for $k\ge k^\ast$, optimal allocation policies minimizing $\overline{T}$ (and $\overline{S}$) are known explicitly.

Problem. For an arbitrary speedup function $s$ that is neither a power law $s(k)=k^p$ nor a threshold function of the above form, determine the policy that allocates the $n$ servers to the $m$ jobs over time so as to minimize the mean response time $\overline{T}$, and separately the policy minimizing the mean slowdown $\overline{S}$, given that all jobs are present at time $0$.
status_search_result: Recent work (heSRPT and follow-ups) explicitly solves the cases $s(k)=k^p$ and threshold speedups, and recent papers on the Core Allocation to Malleable jobs problem state that, for general concave speedup functions, optimizing mean response time with known job sizes "is still largely an open problem." No general solution for arbitrary speedup functions appears to be known.

paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
original_question: For a system where directed-acyclic-graph jobs arrive over time, each job consists of tasks with precedence constraints, and the scheduler must choose both which jobs to run and which tasks within each job to run on n servers, what is the optimal allocation policy for minimizing mean job response time?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a queueing system with $n$ identical servers. Jobs arrive over time according to a stochastic arrival process (for concreteness, take a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$). Each arriving job is a directed acyclic graph (DAG) whose vertices are tasks and whose directed edges encode precedence constraints: a task may begin processing only after all of its predecessor tasks have completed. Each task has a (random) service requirement drawn from a known distribution, and at most one task may be processed on a server at a time; a server processes at most one task at a time, and tasks are non-preemptive (or, equivalently, preemptive — both variants are of interest). The DAG structure and task sizes of each job are revealed upon arrival.

A scheduling policy must, at every moment, decide (a) which of the currently present jobs to work on and (b) which eligible tasks (those whose predecessors have completed) of each chosen job to assign to which of the $n$ servers. Let $T$ denote the response time of a job (the time from its arrival until the completion of its final task), and let $\mathbb{E}[T]$ denote the long-run mean response time over all jobs.

Problem. Determine the scheduling policy that minimizes $\mathbb{E}[T]$, and characterize the resulting optimal value as a function of $n$, the arrival rate, and the joint distribution of DAG structure and task sizes.
status_search_result: The problem of optimally scheduling DAG-structured jobs across multiple servers to minimize mean response time is widely regarded as an open problem in queueing theory; even simplified versions (fixed DAG, identical task sizes) remain unresolved. No general optimal policy is known; recent work focuses on heuristics and approximation guarantees.

original_question: In the limited fork-join model with n distributed queues and jobs that create only k much smaller than n tasks, how large can k grow while the queues still exhibit asymptotic independence as n tends to infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the limited fork-join queueing model defined as follows. There are $n$ parallel server stations, each with its own FIFO queue and a single server with unit service rate (service times are i.i.d. from some distribution, e.g. exponential). Jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\Lambda(n)$. Upon arrival, each job splits into $k = k(n) \le n$ tasks, which are dispatched to $k$ distinct stations chosen uniformly at random; a job is considered complete only when all of its $k$ tasks have finished service. Assume the per-server load $\rho = \Lambda(n)\, k(n)/n$ is held in $(0,1)$.

We say the system exhibits asymptotic independence (in the regime $n \to \infty$) if, for any fixed integer $m$, the joint stationary distribution of the workloads at any $m$ of the $n$ queues converges to the product of $m$ copies of the stationary workload distribution of a single M/G/1 queue with load $\rho$. More generally, one may ask for joint independence of $k(n)$ queues (with $k(n)$ growing with $n$).

It is known that asymptotic independence of any $k(n)$ queues holds whenever $k(n) = o(n^{1/4})$.

Problem. Determine the largest growth rate of $k(n)$ (as a function of $n$) for which asymptotic independence of the queues continues to hold in this limited fork-join model. In particular, does asymptotic independence persist for $k(n)$ growing faster than $n^{1/4}$, and what is the sharp threshold?
status_search_result: Existing work establishes asymptotic independence of the queues in the limited fork-join model under the condition $k(n) = o(n^{1/4})$, generalizing earlier results that handled only a fixed number of queues. The sharp growth rate of $k(n)$ for which asymptotic independence persists has not been determined, and improving the $n^{1/4}$ threshold remains open.

paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
original_question: For the stochastic M/G/k queue with arrivals over time, outside the heavy-traffic regime typical optimality results do not apply. Under what conditions is SRPT-k actually optimal for minimizing mean response time?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an M/G/k queueing system: jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate λ and have i.i.d. service requirements drawn from a general distribution G, served by k identical parallel servers (each of unit speed). Job sizes are known to the scheduler upon arrival, and the scheduler may preempt jobs at any time without cost. The SRPT-k policy assigns the k servers, at every instant, to the (at most) k jobs in the system with the smallest remaining processing requirements.

Let ρ = λ E[G]/k denote the system load, and let E[T] denote the steady-state mean response time (time from arrival to completion).

Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on the service-time distribution G, the number of servers k, and the load ρ — outside the heavy-traffic limit ρ → 1 — under which the SRPT-k policy minimizes the steady-state mean response time E[T] over all (possibly preemptive, size-aware) scheduling policies. In particular, decide whether SRPT-k is optimal for minimizing mean response time in the M/G/k queue at low or moderate load, and if not, characterize the gap to optimality.
status_search_result: The problem appears to be open. Stochastic bounds and asymptotic optimality of SRPT-k in the heavy-traffic limit (ρ → 1) have been established (Grosof, Scully, Harchol-Balter), and an explicit open problem on M/G/k/SRPT under medium load was posed in Stochastic Systems (2020). Subsequent work (e.g., SIGMETRICS 2024) provides improved bounds and shows that SRPT-k can be strictly improved upon under moderate load, but the question of when SRPT-k is exactly optimal for minimizing mean response time outside heavy traffic remains unresolved.

original_question: In a distributed load-balancing system with multiple server queues and SRPT scheduling within each server, what dispatching policy minimizes mean response time outside the heavy-traffic limit?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a distributed service system consisting of $k \ge 2$ identical server stations. Jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$, and each job has an i.i.d. size drawn from a general distribution $G$ with finite mean (so total load $\rho = \lambda \mathbb{E}[G] < k$). Let $\mathbb{E}[T^\pi]$ denote the steady-state mean response time (sojourn time) under dispatching policy $\pi$. A related explicit open problem on M/G/k/SRPT under medium load was posed in Stochastic Systems (2019).

paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
original_question: For the multi-server M/G/k queue when job sizes are not known a priori and the Gittins rank policy is extended to run the k jobs with lowest Gittins ranks, is Gittins-k optimal outside of heavy traffic?
self_contained_problem:
Consider an M/G/k queue: jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$ to a system with $k$ identical servers (each of unit speed), and job sizes (service requirements) are i.i.d. samples from a general distribution $S$ with finite mean, so that the system load is $\rho = \lambda \mathbb{E}[S]/k < 1$. Job sizes are not known to the scheduler a priori; instead, for each job in the system, the scheduler observes only the amount of service the job has received so far (its attained service / age). 

For a job of age $a$, define its Gittins rank as
$$ \mathrm{rank}(a) \;=\; \inf_{\Delta > 0} \frac{\mathbb{E}[\min(S-a, \Delta) \mid S > a]}{\mathbb{P}(S - a \le \Delta \mid S > a)}, $$
i.e. the smallest possible ratio of expected additional service to probability of completion within an additional service quantum. The Gittins-$k$ policy is the preemptive scheduling rule that, at every moment, serves the (up to) $k$ jobs in the system whose current Gittins ranks are smallest, one on each server.

Question: Is the Gittins-$k$ policy optimal for minimizing the mean response time (expected sojourn time) in the M/G/k queue with unknown job sizes for all loads $\rho \in (0,1)$, and not merely in the heavy-traffic limit $\rho \to 1$?
status_search_result: Gittins-k has been proven asymptotically optimal for mean response time in the M/G/k under heavy traffic (Scully, Grosof, and Harchol-Balter, 2020; Grosof's 2023 thesis), but its optimality outside the heavy-traffic regime remains an open question. Even existence of an optimal policy for the M/G/k with unknown job sizes in general load conditions is not established.

paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
original_question: For the Drop-The-Larger-Hopeless policy, which keeps First-Come-First-Served queue order except that on an infeasible arrival it may drop a larger queued job instead of the new smaller job, how close is this policy to the true optimum for minimizing deadline misses?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue serving jobs that arrive over time. Each arriving job $j$ has a known size (service requirement) $s_j > 0$ and a known deadline $d_j$ (a time by which its service must be completed). At any moment, given the current set of queued jobs (with their remaining sizes and deadlines) and the current time, call a set of jobs "feasible" if there exists a schedule that completes every job in the set by its deadline; otherwise it is "infeasible." A job that cannot be completed by its deadline under any continuation is called "hopeless."

Define the Drop-The-Larger-Hopeless (DTLH) admission/scheduling policy as follows. The server serves jobs in First-Come-First-Served order. Whenever a new job arrives such that admitting it would render the queue infeasible, DTLH compares the new job's size with the sizes of currently queued jobs: if some queued job has size strictly larger than the new arrival's size and dropping that larger job restores feasibility, then DTLH drops such a larger queued job and admits the new (smaller) one; otherwise DTLH drops the new arrival. Jobs that are not dropped must be completed by their deadlines; dropped jobs count as deadline misses.

Let $\mathrm{Miss}_{\mathrm{DTLH}}(\omega)$ denote the number (or long-run rate) of dropped jobs under DTLH on an arrival instance $\omega$, and let $\mathrm{Miss}_{\mathrm{OPT}}(\omega)$ denote the corresponding minimum over all online (non-clairvoyant beyond knowing each job's size and deadline upon arrival) policies, or equivalently over all admissible causal policies in the chosen stochastic or adversarial model.

Problem: Determine the worst-case (or, in a specified stochastic arrival model, the typical) ratio or additive gap between $\mathrm{Miss}_{\mathrm{DTLH}}$ and $\mathrm{Miss}_{\mathrm{OPT}}$. In particular, find tight bounds on
$$\sup_{\omega}\,  rac{\mathrm{Miss}_{\mathrm{DTLH}}(\omega)}{\mathrm{Miss}_{\mathrm{OPT}}(\omega)},$$
and characterize how close DTLH is to optimal for minimizing the number (or rate) of deadline misses.
status_search_result: No published results were located that quantify the optimality gap of the Drop-The-Larger-Hopeless policy for minimizing deadline misses; the question is posed as an explicit open problem in the queueing-theory open-problems literature and no resolution appears in subsequent literature.

original_question: In the same null-recurrent renewal-process setting, where D_t = X_{N_t} is the total life at time t, does there exist a non-decreasing function φ such that D_t / φ(t) converges in distribution, as t → ∞, to a non-degenerate random variable D_φ? $$N_t = \sup\{n \ge 0 : S_n \le t\}, \qquad t \ge 0.$$
Define the total life at time $t$ by
$$D_t = X_{N_t + 1} = A_t + B_t,$$
where $A_t = t - S_{N_t}$ is the age and $B_t = S_{N_t+1} - t$ is the residual life.

Assume that $F$ is null recurrent in the sense that $E[X_1] = \infty$ (so that $D_t \to \infty$ in distribution as $t \to \infty$).

Question: Does there exist a non-decreasing function $\varphi : (0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)$ and a non-degenerate random variable $D_\varphi$ such that
$$\frac{D_t}{\varphi(t)} \xrightarrow{\;d\;} D_\varphi \qquad \text{as } t \to \infty\,?$$
In particular, can one take $\varphi(t) = E[\min(X_1, t)]$?
status_search_result: The general question appears to remain open. A partial answer is known in the regularly-varying regime: when the inter-arrival distribution is regularly varying with index $\alpha \in (0,1)$, scaling-limit results for the age, residual life and total life have been established (e.g., Blanchet–Glynn–Thorisson and subsequent work on the limiting ratio of current age to total life for null-recurrent renewal processes). Beyond regularly varying tails, no general non-degenerate scaling limit has been established.

paper_title: Open problems in renewal, coupling and Palm theory
original_question: Let S = (S_n)_{n≥0} be a random walk on ℝ starting at 0 with i.i.d. step lengths X_1, X_2, …, and let S' = (S'_n)_{n≥0} be the version started at x ∈ ℝ. Say that the two walks admit exact coupling if they can be constructed on one probability space with an almost surely finite random time T such that S_n = S'_n for all n ≥ T. If the common step-length distribution is neither discrete nor spread out, for which starting offsets x do the two walks admit exact coupling?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ that is neither discrete (not supported on a countable set) nor spread out (no convolution power $\mu^{*n}$ has a nontrivial absolutely continuous component with respect to Lebesgue measure). Let $X_1, X_2, \dots$ be i.i.d. random variables with common distribution $\mu$, and define the random walks
$$S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n X_k, \qquad S'_n = x + \sum_{k=1}^n X_k', \quad n \ge 0,$$
where $(X_k')_{k\ge 1}$ is an independent copy with the same distribution $\mu$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Say that $S$ and $S'$ admit an exact coupling if there exists a probability space carrying processes $(\tilde S_n)_{n\ge 0}$ and $(\tilde S'_n)_{n\ge 0}$ with the same laws as $S$ and $S'$ respectively, and an almost surely finite random time $T$ such that $\tilde S_n = \tilde S'_n$ for all $n \ge T$.

Characterize the set of starting offsets $x \in \mathbb{R}$ for which $S$ and $S'$ admit an exact coupling.
status_search_result: A 2017 preprint (arXiv:1706.06968, "Exact Coupling of Random Walks on Polish Groups") explicitly states that it solves Thorisson's problem and provides the characterization: the random walk started at 0 admits a successful exact coupling with the version started at x if and only if there exists $n \ge 1$ with $\mu^{*n} \wedge \mu^{*n}(x + \cdot) \ne 0$ (i.e., the n-fold convolutions have a common component after shifting by x). The paper also gives convergence rates depending on the order of x.

paper_title: Open problems in renewal, coupling and Palm theory
original_question: If the answer to the previous question is negative, what coupling property exactly characterizes the setwise convergence P(θ_n X ∈ A) → P(X' ∈ A) for all measurable sets A in the path-space sigma-field?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(E,\mathcal{E})$ be a measurable space and let $E^{\mathbb{N}}$ denote the space of $E$-valued sequences equipped with the product $\sigma$-field $\mathcal{E}^{\infty}$. Let $\theta:E^{\mathbb{N}}\to E^{\mathbb{N}}$ be the shift map defined by $(\theta x)_k = x_{k+1}$, and write $\theta_n = \theta^n$ for its $n$-fold iterate. Let $X=(X_0,X_1,\dots)$ and $X'=(X'_0,X'_1,\dots)$ be random elements of $E^{\mathbb{N}}$ defined on some probability space, and consider the setwise convergence condition
$$P(\theta_n X \in A) \to P(X' \in A) \quad \text{as } n \to \infty, \text{ for every } A \in \mathcal{E}^{\infty}. \qquad (\ast)$$
A coupling of $\theta_n X$ and $X'$ is, for each $n$, a pair $(\hat X^{(n)}, \hat X'^{(n)})$ of random elements of $E^{\mathbb{N}}$ defined on a common probability space such that $\hat X^{(n)} \stackrel{d}{=} \theta_n X$ and $\hat X'^{(n)} \stackrel{d}{=} X'$.

Assuming that setwise convergence $(\ast)$ is strictly stronger than the total variation / coupling-in-the-distributional-sense convergence (i.e.\ it cannot be characterized by the existence of couplings $(\hat X^{(n)},\hat X'^{(n)})$ with $P(\hat X^{(n)} \neq \hat X'^{(n)}) \to 0$), determine a property of couplings $(\hat X^{(n)},\hat X'^{(n)})_{n\ge 1}$ (or of an appropriate shift-coupling type construction) which holds if and only if the setwise convergence $(\ast)$ holds.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem by Thorisson in his list of open probability problems on coupling, renewal, and Palm theory. No published resolution of this specific coupling characterization of setwise convergence under shifts was located.

paper_title: Open problems in renewal, coupling and Palm theory
original_question: Let ξ be a diffuse random measure on a locally compact second countable Abelian group G, and let X be a random element in a G-space. Mass-stationarity means that the origin is a typical location in the mass of ξ, and for simple point processes it is characterized by the shift-invariance condition θ_−T(X, ξ) ≐ (X, ξ) for every measurable shift T = π(X, ξ) induced by a preserving allocation. When ξ is diffuse, is mass-stationarity of (X, ξ) already equivalent to this condition (4.1) without adjoining an extra stationary random field Y independent of (X, ξ)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a locally compact second countable Abelian group with Haar measure $\lambda$, acting measurably on a measurable space $(\Omega, \mathcal{F})$ by shifts $\{\theta_t : t \in G\}$. Let $\xi$ be a random measure on $G$ defined on $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$, and let $X$ be a random element taking values in a measurable $G$-space, so that $(X, \xi)$ carries a natural shift action $\theta_t(X, \xi)$.

Assume $\xi$ is diffuse (i.e.\ $\xi(\{t\}) = 0$ almost surely for every $t \in G$).

A measurable map $\pi$ from the state space of $(X, \xi)$ to $G$ is called a preserving allocation if it produces shifts $T = \pi(X, \xi)$ that preserve the joint distribution in the appropriate balanced sense (the shift $\theta_{-T}$ moves the origin to a point of $\xi$-mass selected in a translation-equivariant way).

Consider the condition
$$\theta_{-T}(X, \xi) \stackrel{d}{=} (X, \xi) \qquad \text{for every shift } T = \pi(X, \xi) \text{ induced by a preserving allocation.} \tag{$\ast$}$$

The pair $(X, \xi)$ is called mass-stationary if, for every relatively compact Borel set $C \subset G$,
$$(\theta_{-V_C}(X, \xi),\, V_C + U_C) \stackrel{d}{=} ((X, \xi),\, U_C),$$
where $U_C$ is uniformly distributed on $C$ independently of $(X, \xi)$ and $V_C$ is sampled from $\xi(\cdot \cap (U_C + C)) / \xi(U_C + C)$ on the event $\{\xi(U_C + C) \in (0, \infty)\}$.

It is known that, when one adjoins a stationary random field $Y$ on $G$ independent of $(X, \xi)$, mass-stationarity of $(X, \xi)$ is equivalent to condition $(\ast)$ holding for $((X, Y), \xi)$.

Question: If $\xi$ is diffuse, is mass-stationarity of $(X, \xi)$ already equivalent to condition $(\ast)$ for $(X, \xi)$ itself, without the auxiliary independent stationary field $Y$?
status_search_result: Searches surface foundational work by Last and Thorisson on mass-stationarity and invariant transports, and subsequent papers on stationary and mass-stationary random measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and on transportation of diffuse random measures, but none explicitly announce a resolution of the specific question of whether, for diffuse $\xi$, mass-stationarity is equivalent to the shift-invariance condition under preserving allocations without an auxiliary independent stationary field. The status appears to remain unresolved in the indexed literature.

paper_title: Open problems in some competition models
original_question: Consider the two-species Ricker competition system x_{n+1}=x_n e^{K-x_n-a y_n}, y_{n+1}=y_n e^{L-y_n-b x_n} on the positive quadrant, where K,L>0 are carrying capacities and a,b∈(0,1) are competition parameters. Its coexistence fixed point is ((aL-K)/(ab-1),(bK-L)/(ab-1)). Assume the local stability inequality 4(ab-1)+2(1-a)L+2(1-b)K ≤ (aL-K)(bK-L) < (1-a)L+(1-b)K holds. Is this coexistence fixed point globally asymptotically stable in the positive first quadrant for every parameter pair satisfying that inequality?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-species Ricker competition system on the positive quadrant $\mathbb{R}_+^2$:
$$x_{n+1} = x_n\, e^{K - x_n - a y_n}, \qquad y_{n+1} = y_n\, e^{L - y_n - b x_n},$$
where $K, L > 0$ are the carrying capacities and $a, b \in (0,1)$ are the competition parameters. Assume the coexistence fixed point
$$(x^*, y^*) = \left( \frac{aL - K}{ab - 1},\ \frac{bK - L}{ab - 1} \right)$$
lies in the open positive quadrant, and that the parameters satisfy the local stability inequality
$$4(ab - 1) + 2(1 - a)L + 2(1 - b)K \;\le\; (aL - K)(bK - L) \;<\; (1 - a)L + (1 - b)K.$$
Prove or disprove: for every quadruple $(K, L, a, b)$ satisfying these conditions, the coexistence fixed point $(x^*, y^*)$ is globally asymptotically stable in the open positive quadrant; that is, every orbit starting in $\mathbb{R}_+^2$ with $x_0, y_0 > 0$ converges to $(x^*, y^*)$.
status_search_result: The conjecture that local asymptotic stability of the coexistence fixed point implies global asymptotic stability for the planar Ricker competition model remains open in full generality. Partial results exist: Ryals and Sacker, and later work by Bilgin, Gyllenberg, Jiang, Niu, and others, have established global asymptotic stability under additional technical assumptions, but the conjecture as stated has not been fully proved.

paper_title: Open problems in some competition models
context_brief: Logistic competition second boundary fixed point
original_question: Consider the logistic competition system x_{n+1}=a x_n(1-x_n)/(1+c y_n), y_{n+1}=b y_n(1-y_n)/(1+d x_n), where x,y∈[0,1], c,d∈(0,1), and a,b∈(0,4]. Determine the stability type of the boundary fixed point (0,(b-1)/b) in the parameter case b=3 and a=1+c(b-1)/b.

Consider the planar discrete-time logistic competition system
   x_{n+1} = a x_n (1 - x_n) / (1 + c y_n),
   y_{n+1} = b y_n (1 - y_n) / (1 + d x_n),
with state space (x_n, y_n) ∈ [0,1]×[0,1] and parameters c, d ∈ (0,1), a, b ∈ (0,4]. The point (0, (b-1)/b) is a boundary fixed point of this map (lying on the y-axis) whenever b > 1.

   b = 3,    a = 1 + c(b-1)/b = 1 + 2c/3,
with c, d ∈ (0,1) arbitrary. In this critical case the standard linearization at (0, (b-1)/b) becomes non-hyperbolic (one eigenvalue equals 1, the other equals -1, the latter coming from b = 3 at the logistic fixed point (b-1)/b).

paper_title: Open Problems in Stringology
original_question: For a fixed pattern x, consider the deterministic finite automaton suggested as a way to augment the Boyer-Moore string-search procedure so that it remembers which comparisons need not be repeated after a mismatch and shift. What is the exact number of states required by such a "Boyer-Moore dfa", or at least what are close upper and lower bounds on that state count as a function of the pattern?
self_contained_problem:
Fix a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ and a pattern $x = x_1 x_2 \cdots x_m \in \Sigma^m$. Recall the Boyer–Moore string-matching procedure: when searching for $x$ inside a text $t \in \Sigma^*$, the pattern is aligned with a window of the text and characters are compared from right to left; on a mismatch (or full match) the window is shifted to the right according to the standard Boyer–Moore shift rules. After such a shift, some positions in the new window have already been compared during the previous alignment, so their values relative to $x$ are known and the corresponding comparisons need not be repeated.

Define the "Boyer–Moore DFA for $x$" as the deterministic finite automaton over the input alphabet $\Sigma$ that simulates this enhanced search exactly: each state encodes the complete information accumulated by the algorithm so far (current alignment of $x$ against the text and the set of window positions whose contents, relative to $x$, are already known together with what is known about them), and on reading the next text character the automaton performs the rightmost not-yet-resolved comparison, applies all forced Boyer–Moore shifts and bookkeeping updates, and moves to the resulting state. Let $S(x)$ denote the number of states of this minimal automaton.

Determine $S(x)$ exactly as a function of the pattern $x$, or give matching (or near matching) upper and lower bounds on $S(x)$ in terms of $m = |x|$ and $|\Sigma|$.
status_search_result: The problem of determining the exact state complexity of a Boyer–Moore DFA was posed as an open question in stringology. Subsequent work (e.g., Blumer–Blumer–Ehrenfeucht–Haussler–Chen–Seiferas style automata theory, and specifically papers titled "On Boyer-Moore automata" in Algorithmica and "About the Size of Boyer-Moore Automata") has produced upper and lower bounds on the size of such automata and efficient construction algorithms, but a closed-form exact count $S(x)$ for arbitrary patterns does not appear to be established. The problem is therefore best described as partially solved (bounds known, exact formula not known in general).

paper_title: Open Problems in the Dynamics of the Expression of Gene Interaction Networks
context_brief: General inverse problem for gene-network dynamics
original_question: Consider a gene-interaction system in which the state vector x_n records the expression levels of a set of genes at time step n, and the dynamics are given by x_{n+1} = A(x_n), where the interaction rule A and the initial state x_0 are both unknown. Suppose experimental data typically reveal only a final attractor state x_f satisfying x_f = lim_{n→∞} A^n(x_0), or at most limited partial observations of intermediate states. What mathematical properties of the unknown interaction rule A can be determined from the observed attractor x_f alone, or from x_f together with such limited time-step data, even though A itself cannot be uniquely reconstructed?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A : \mathbb{R}^d 	o \mathbb{R}^d$ be an (unknown) map modeling the interaction rule of a network of $d$ genes, and let $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be an (unknown) initial state representing the gene-expression levels at time $0$. Define the discrete-time trajectory by $x_{n+1} = A(x_n)$ for $n \geq 0$, and assume that the limit
$$x_f \;=\; \lim_{n 	o \infty} A^n(x_0)$$
exists in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (so that $x_f$ is a fixed point of $A$ on the orbit closure of $x_0$ and represents an experimentally observed attractor state).

Suppose that the only data available about the system are either:
(i) the attractor state $x_f$ alone, or
(ii) $x_f$ together with the values $x_{n}$ at a small finite collection of intermediate times $n \in S \subset \mathbb{N}$.

Because many distinct pairs $(A, x_0)$ can produce the same $x_f$ (and even the same partial orbit data), the map $A$ cannot be uniquely reconstructed from such observations. The problem is to identify and characterize mathematical invariants of $A$ that are nevertheless determined by the data:

1. Determine which properties of $A$ (for example, structural features such as the support pattern of its Jacobian at $x_f$, its local linearization spectrum, its monotonicity class, Lipschitz constants, fixed-point index, the topology or combinatorics of its basin of attraction, or other suitably defined invariants) are uniquely determined by $x_f$ alone.

2. Determine which additional properties of $A$ become uniquely determined when $x_f$ is augmented with partial intermediate-state observations $\{x_n : n \in S\}$.

3. Define, where necessary, new invariants of $A$ and of $x_f$ that make precise the correspondence between observable features of the attractor (or partial trajectory) and recoverable structural properties of the underlying interaction rule, and prove rigorous identifiability theorems linking the two.
category_tag: inverse problems for discrete dynamical systems
status_search_result: The question is posed as a broad open inverse problem about which properties of an unknown discrete-time dynamical rule on a gene network can be inferred from a single attractor state (and limited intermediate observations). It is a general programmatic problem rather than a single sharp conjecture, and no comprehensive resolution appears in the literature; related work in network inference, identifiability of Boolean networks, and reverse-engineering of regulatory networks gives only partial answers in restricted settings.

paper_title: Open Problems in the Dynamics of the Expression of Gene Interaction Networks
original_question: Assume each gene influences the expression of another gene through a nonlinear single-gene response rather than a linear additive term. In particular, for gene j affecting gene i, the contribution may be a Hill-type nonlinear function such as x_j^h / [1 + (x_j / x_{j0})^h] when gene j stimulates gene i, or 1 / [1 + (x_j / x_{j0})^h] when gene j inhibits gene i, where h is the Hill coefficient and x_{j0} is a constant. Given only experimentally observed attractor data x_f, and possibly limited intermediate observations x_n, what properties of the unknown nonlinear interaction rule A can be determined when A is a nonlinear function of the expression of each individual gene?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a gene regulatory network with N genes whose expression levels at time t are given by x(t) = (x_1(t), ..., x_N(t)) ∈ R^N_{≥0}. Suppose the dynamics are governed by a system of the form

  dx_i/dt = F_i(x_1, ..., x_N) - γ_i x_i,   i = 1, ..., N,

where γ_i > 0 are degradation rates and the interaction term F_i is built from single-gene nonlinear responses; specifically, assume there exist sign labels s_{ij} ∈ {+1, -1, 0} (stimulation, inhibition, no interaction) and constants h > 0, x_{j0} > 0 such that

  F_i(x) = A_i( f_{i1}(x_1), f_{i2}(x_2), ..., f_{iN}(x_N) ),

where

  f_{ij}(x_j) = x_j^h / (1 + (x_j / x_{j0})^h)   if s_{ij} = +1,
  f_{ij}(x_j) = 1 / (1 + (x_j / x_{j0})^h)        if s_{ij} = -1,
  f_{ij}(x_j) = 0                                   if s_{ij} = 0,

and A_i : R^N → R is an unknown (possibly nonlinear) combining rule. Assume that the only experimental data available are:

(i) a finite collection {x_f^{(k)}}_{k=1}^K ⊂ R^N_{≥0} of observed attractors (equilibrium states) of the system, and
(ii) possibly a limited collection {x_n^{(ℓ)}}_{ℓ=1}^L of intermediate (non-equilibrium) observations of trajectories.

Problem. Determine which structural and quantitative properties of the unknown nonlinear interaction rule {A_i}_{i=1}^N — for instance, the sign pattern (s_{ij}), the Hill coefficient h, the thresholds x_{j0}, the functional form of A_i (additive, multiplicative, or other composition of the f_{ij}), and the identifiability of A_i up to equivalence — can be recovered from the data in (i) and (ii). In particular, give necessary and sufficient conditions on the attractor set, and on the size/nature of the intermediate observations, under which A is uniquely identifiable, and otherwise characterize the equivalence class of nonlinear rules A consistent with the data.
status_search_result: The problem is posed explicitly as an open problem about identifying nonlinear (Hill-type) single-gene interaction rules from attractor data in gene regulatory network dynamics. No comprehensive resolution of identifiability for general nonlinear A from attractor data is reported; related work on inference of Hill-type GRNs continues to address only special or restricted cases.

paper_title: Open problems in the theory of fuzzy metric spaces
context_brief: Separability of the fuzzy Gromov-Hausdorff space of compact fuzzy metric spaces.
original_question: Let CFM be the set of isometry classes of compact fuzzy metric spaces, where a fuzzy metric space is a triple (X, M, *) consisting of a set X, a continuous t-norm * on [0,1], and a function M on X^2 × (0,∞) satisfying positivity, identity of indiscernibles, symmetry, a triangle-type inequality M(x,y,t) * M(y,z,s) ≤ M(x,z,t+s), and continuity in the time variable. When CFM is endowed with the fuzzy Gromov-Hausdorff metric, is CFM a separable fuzzy metric space?

paper_title: Open problems in the theory of fuzzy metric spaces
context_brief: Completeness/completion of the fuzzy Gromov-Prokhorov space of compact fuzzy mm-spaces.
original_question: For the fuzzy metric space of all compact fuzzy metric-measure spaces, equipped with the fuzzy Gromov-Prokhorov distance M_GP defined from the Prokhorov fuzzy metric on probability measures and common isometric embeddings into a fuzzy metric space, is that fuzzy metric space completable?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. A fuzzy metric space (in the sense of George–Veeramani) is a triple $(X,M,\ast)$, where $X$ is a nonempty set, $\ast$ is a continuous t-norm, and $M:X\times X\times(0,\infty)\to(0,1]$ satisfies, for all $x,y,z\in X$ and $s,t>0$:
(i) $M(x,y,t)>0$; (ii) $M(x,y,t)=1\iff x=y$; (iii) $M(x,y,t)=M(y,x,t)$; (iv) $M(x,y,t)\ast M(y,z,s)\le M(x,z,t+s)$; (v) $M(x,y,\cdot):(0,\infty)\to(0,1]$ is continuous. The topology induced by $M$ is generated by the open balls $B(x,r,t)=\{y:M(x,y,t)>1-r\}$.

A fuzzy metric-measure space (fuzzy mm-space) is a triple $\mathcal X=(X,M,\mu)$, where $(X,M,\ast)$ is a compact fuzzy metric space and $\mu$ is a Borel probability measure on $X$ with $\operatorname{supp}\mu=X$. Two fuzzy mm-spaces $(X,M_X,\mu_X)$ and $(Y,M_Y,\mu_Y)$ are identified if there exists a fuzzy isometry $\varphi:X\to Y$ (i.e., a bijection with $M_Y(\varphi(x),\varphi(x'),t)=M_X(x,x',t)$ for all $x,x'\in X$, $t>0$) such that $\varphi_\ast\mu_X=\mu_Y$.

Given a fuzzy metric space $(Z,M_Z,\ast)$, the Prokhorov fuzzy metric $P_{M_Z}$ on the set $\mathcal P(Z)$ of Borel probability measures on $Z$ is defined by
$$P_{M_Z}(\mu,\nu,t)=\sup\{1-\varepsilon\in(0,1]:\mu(A)\le \nu(A^{\varepsilon,t})+\varepsilon\text{ and }\nu(A)\le \mu(A^{\varepsilon,t})+\varepsilon\ \forall A\text{ Borel}\},$$
where $A^{\varepsilon,t}=\{z\in Z:\exists a\in A,\ M_Z(z,a,t)>1-\varepsilon\}$.

The fuzzy Gromov–Prokhorov distance between two compact fuzzy mm-spaces $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Y$ is
$$M_{GP}(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,t)=\sup\bigl\{P_{M_Z}\bigl(\varphi_\ast\mu_X,\psi_\ast\mu_Y,t\bigr)\bigr\},$$
where the supremum is taken over all fuzzy metric spaces $(Z,M_Z,\ast)$ and all isometric embeddings $\varphi:X\hookrightarrow Z$, $\psi:Y\hookrightarrow Z$. Let $\mathfrak{FM}$ denote the resulting fuzzy metric space of (isomorphism classes of) compact fuzzy mm-spaces equipped with $M_{GP}$.

Problem. Is $(\mathfrak{FM},M_{GP},\ast)$ completable, i.e., does there exist a complete fuzzy metric space into which it embeds isometrically as a dense subspace?

paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
original_question: Does there exist a nuclear F-space that is locally pseudo-convex but not locally convex?
self_contained_problem:
Recall the following definitions. A topological vector space $X$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ is called an F-space if its topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric. A subset $U$ of $X$ is called $p$-convex (for some $0 < p \le 1$) if for all $x, y \in U$ and all scalars $\alpha, \beta \ge 0$ with $\alpha^p + \beta^p = 1$ one has $\alpha x + \beta y \in U$. The space $X$ is called locally pseudo-convex if it has a base of neighborhoods of $0$ each of which is $p$-convex for some $p \in (0,1]$ (the value of $p$ may depend on the neighborhood). It is locally convex if it has a base of convex (i.e. $1$-convex) neighborhoods of $0$. A locally pseudo-convex space $X$ is called nuclear if for every continuous $p$-homogeneous seminorm $q$ on $X$ there exists a continuous $r$-homogeneous seminorm $\tilde q \ge q$ (with $0 < p, r \le 1$) such that the canonical map between the associated local quasi-Banach spaces is nuclear in the appropriate $p$-normed sense.

Question: Does there exist a nuclear F-space that is locally pseudo-convex but not locally convex?
status_search_result: The problem was resolved in the negative shortly after being posed: J.-P. Ligaud proved that every nuclear locally pseudo-convex space is locally convex, so no such F-space exists.

for vectors $v_i$ in a suitable filtration of $E^c(x)$; these are the central Lyapunov exponents. (b) Must $f$ be stably ergodic, i.e., must every $C^2$-small $C^2$ volume-preserving perturbation of $f$ also be ergodic?

paper_title: Open problems in the theory of non-uniform hyperbolicity
context_brief: Full-measure basin for a non-uniformly hyperbolic SRB measure
original_question: Assume a non-uniformly hyperbolic SRB measure μ supported on a topological attractor Λ exists. Under what conditions does the basin of attraction B(μ) have full measure in the trapping region U?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f:M\to M$ be a $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphism of a compact Riemannian manifold $M$. Suppose $U\subset M$ is an open set with $\overline{f(U)}\subset U$ (a trapping region), and let $\Lambda=\bigcap_{n\ge 0} f^n(U)$ be the corresponding topological attractor. Recall that an $f$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ supported on $\Lambda$ is called a non-uniformly hyperbolic SRB measure if all of its Lyapunov exponents are nonzero $\mu$-almost everywhere and its conditional measures on unstable manifolds are absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure induced on those unstable manifolds. The basin of attraction of $\mu$ is
$$B(\mu)=\Big\{x\in M : \tfrac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\delta_{f^k(x)}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{w^*}\mu\Big\}.$$
Assume such a non-uniformly hyperbolic SRB measure $\mu$ supported on $\Lambda$ exists.

self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold and let $f : M \to M$ be a $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphism. A nonempty open set $U \subset M$ is called a trapping region for $f$ if $\overline{f(U)} \subset U$. Denote by $m$ the normalized Lebesgue (Riemannian volume) measure on $M$, and for each $n \ge 1$ consider the empirical averages
$$\mu_n \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f_*^k m\big|_U .$$
For $x \in M$ and $0 \neq v \in T_x M$ define the upper Lyapunov exponent
$$\chi_+(x,v) \;=\; \limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n}\log \|D_x f^n(v)\|.$$
Say that the pair $(f,U)$ satisfies condition (H) if $\chi_+(x,v) \neq 0$ for Lebesgue-almost every $x \in U$ and every nonzero $v \in T_x M$.

An invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $M$ is called a physical measure for $f$ if the set of points $x \in M$ for which $\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\delta_{f^k(x)} \to \mu$ in the weak-$*$ topology has positive Lebesgue measure. The measure $\mu$ is called hyperbolic if all its Lyapunov exponents are nonzero almost everywhere, and it is an SRB (Sinai–Ruelle–Bowen) measure if it has at least one positive Lyapunov exponent almost everywhere and its conditional measures on local unstable manifolds are absolutely continuous with respect to the Riemannian volume on those manifolds.

No general resolution providing sufficient additional conditions (beyond nonvanishing Lyapunov exponents on a positive Lebesgue measure set) guaranteeing hyperbolicity or the SRB property of accumulation measures of the Cesàro averages of Lebesgue measure is known; only partial results in specific settings (e.g. partially hyperbolic systems, dominated splittings) exist.

original_question: In the planar case of tensegrities on 10 labeled points, describe every possible type of stratum that can occur in the configuration-space stratification by sign-preserving equivalence classes of self-stress fibers.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and edge set $E$. A tensegrity framework realizing $G$ in the plane is a configuration $p=(p_1,\dots,p_n)\in(\mathbb{R}^2)^n$ together with the straight-line edges $\overline{p_ip_j}$ for $\{i,j\}\in E$. A self-stress on $(G,p)$ is an assignment $w:E\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for every vertex $i$,
$$\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0.$$
The set of self-stresses forms a real vector space $W(G,p)$, called the self-stress fiber at $p$. Fix the graph $G$ and consider the configuration space $\mathcal{C}(G)=(\mathbb{R}^2)^n$ minus the locus where the dimension of $W(G,p)$ jumps; on its open part $B_d(G)$ where $\dim W(G,p)=d$, declare two configurations $p,q$ equivalent if there is a linear isomorphism $W(G,p)\to W(G,q)$ that preserves the sign of every edge weight (sign-preserving equivalence of fibers). A stratum is a maximal connected component of $B_d(G)$ consisting of configurations all of which are mutually equivalent in this sense.

Problem. For $n=10$ labeled points in the plane, describe every possible type of stratum that can arise in this stratification, ranging over all graphs $G$ on $10$ vertices.

$$\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in E(G)} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0 \qquad \text{for every } i=1,\dots,n.$$

original_question: In the planar Cayley-algebra description of tensegrity strata, determine when two Cayley algebra systems define the same stratum or the same stratum condition; here the Cayley-algebra setting uses points and lines in the plane together with the join and meet operations to express geometric conditions.

Background. Work in the real projective plane (or affine plane) and consider the planar Cayley algebra whose objects are points and lines. It is equipped with two operations: the join, which to a pair of distinct points associates the line through them and to a point and a line produces incidence relations, and the meet, which to a pair of distinct lines associates their intersection point. By iterating joins and meets starting from a finite list of input points (the "free" generators), one builds compound expressions whose vanishing or incidence conditions translate into polynomial conditions on the coordinates of the inputs.

A Cayley algebra system is a finite collection of such Cayley-algebra expressions/conditions in a fixed set of input points. The zero locus of these conditions in the configuration space of the input points is called the stratum defined by the system; two systems are said to define the same stratum condition if they cut out the same subset of the configuration space (equivalently, the same closed condition up to the chosen notion of equivalence, e.g., set-theoretic equality of strata).

Problem. Give a complete description (e.g., a decision procedure, a normal form, or a set of generating syntactic moves) determining when two planar Cayley algebra systems, built from points and lines via the join and meet operations, define the same stratum, and equivalently when they define the same stratum condition.

paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
original_question: Develop a theory of geometric conditions that define or characterize strata for tensegrities in multidimensional Euclidean spaces, beyond the planar case.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph with vertex set $V=\{v_1,\dots,v_n\}$, and fix an integer $d\ge 2$. A configuration of $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a map $P:V\to\mathbb{R}^d$, $v_i\mapsto p_i$; the configuration space is identified with $(\mathbb{R}^d)^n$. A self-stress on $(G,P)$ is an assignment of weights $w_{ij}=w_{ji}\in\mathbb{R}$ to each edge $\{v_i,v_j\}\in E$ satisfying the equilibrium condition
$$\sum_{j:\{v_i,v_j\}\in E} w_{ij}(p_j-p_i)=0\qquad\text{for every } i=1,\dots,n.$$
A tensegrity supported on $G$ is a pair $(P,w)$ where $w$ is a nonzero self-stress. The set
$$W(G)=\{P\in(\mathbb{R}^d)^n : (G,P)\text{ admits a nonzero self-stress}\}$$
is naturally stratified according to the dimension of the space of self-stresses; its strata $W_k(G)=\{P:\dim\ker=k\}$ partition the configuration space.

In the planar case $d=2$, each stratum can be characterized by explicit geometric incidence conditions on the points $p_1,\dots,p_n$ (for example, classical conditions such as "six points lie on a conic" arising via Cayley-type meet-join expressions in the projective plane).

Problem: For arbitrary $d\ge 3$, develop a theory of geometric (incidence-type) conditions on configurations $P=(p_1,\dots,p_n)\in(\mathbb{R}^d)^n$ that define and characterize the strata $W_k(G)$ of the configuration space of tensegrities supported on $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. In particular, produce a system of geometric conditions, expressed via projective incidence operations among the points and the linear subspaces they span, that is necessary and sufficient for a generic configuration to admit a nonzero self-stress with prescribed combinatorial type, generalizing the known planar characterization to all higher dimensions.
status_search_result: The problem of describing strata of tensegrity configuration spaces by geometric conditions has been resolved in the planar case via Cayley/meet-join incidence conditions, but in dimensions d ≥ 3 essentially nothing is known. Recent literature on stresses in frameworks (e.g., the combinatorial geometry of stresses) addresses related questions but does not provide a general theory of geometric conditions for strata in higher dimensions, so the problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Find a decoding algorithm for quadratic residue codes, since the chapter states that no decoding algorithm was known for them.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be an odd prime such that $2$ is a quadratic residue modulo $p$, and let $\mathbb{F}_2$ denote the binary field. Let $Q \subset \mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$ be the set of nonzero quadratic residues modulo $p$, and let $\alpha$ be a primitive $p$-th root of unity in some extension field of $\mathbb{F}_2$. The (binary) quadratic residue code of length $p$ is the cyclic code $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^p$ whose generator polynomial is
$$g(x) = \prod_{i \in Q} (x - \alpha^i) \in \mathbb{F}_2[x].$$
Such codes have minimum distance $d$ satisfying $d^2 \geq p$ (the square-root bound) and the designed error-correcting capability $t = \lfloor (d-1)/2 \rfloor$.

Problem: Construct an explicit decoding algorithm that, given any received word $r = c + e \in \mathbb{F}_2^p$ where $c \in \mathcal{Q}$ and $e$ has Hamming weight at most $t$, recovers the error vector $e$ (and hence the codeword $c$). The algorithm should work for general primes $p$ in the above family, achieving the full error-correcting capability of the code up to half the minimum distance.
status_search_result: Since the late 1980s, many algebraic decoding algorithms have been developed for binary quadratic residue (QR) codes, including methods based on the Berlekamp–Massey algorithm, lookup tables, syndrome-weight decoding, and difference-of-syndromes techniques. These algorithms successfully decode binary QR codes up to half the minimum distance for code lengths up to roughly 113 (with explicit algorithms published for lengths 41, 47, 71, 73, 79, 89, 97, 113). However, decoding long binary QR codes and non-binary QR codes in full generality remains an active research problem.

Let $q$ be a prime power and $m\ge 1$ an integer. For an integer $r$ with $0\le r\le m(q-1)$, the generalized Reed–Muller code $\mathrm{GRM}_q(r,m)$ of order $r$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear code consisting of the evaluation vectors $(f(x))_{x\in\mathbb{F}_q^m}$ of all polynomials $f\in\mathbb{F}_q[X_1,\dots,X_m]$ of total degree at most $r$ in which each variable appears with degree at most $q-1$. Identify a codeword $c\in\mathrm{GRM}_q(r,m)$ with its associated polynomial $f$, and let $Z(f)\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^m$ be the zero set of $f$. This method has been shown to recover the description of the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathrm{GRM}_q(r,m)$ for certain orders $r$.

paper_title: Open problems on cyclic codes
original_question: Characterize which classical Goppa codes, extended or not, are cyclic.
self_contained_problem:
Let q be a prime power, m a positive integer, and let F = GF(q^m) be the finite field with q^m elements. Let L = (α_1, …, α_n) be a tuple of distinct elements of F (the support) and let g(x) ∈ F[x] be a polynomial (the Goppa polynomial) such that g(α_i) ≠ 0 for all i. The classical Goppa code Γ(L, g) is the GF(q)-linear code of length n consisting of all vectors (c_1, …, c_n) ∈ GF(q)^n satisfying

    Σ_{i=1}^{n} c_i / (x − α_i) ≡ 0  (mod g(x))

in F[x]/(g(x)). The extended Goppa code is obtained from Γ(L, g) by appending an overall parity-check coordinate.

A linear code C ⊆ GF(q)^N is called cyclic if it is invariant under the cyclic shift (c_1, c_2, …, c_N) ↦ (c_N, c_1, …, c_{N−1}) (after a suitable ordering of the coordinates).

Problem: Give a complete characterization of those triples (q, L, g) for which the classical Goppa code Γ(L, g) is (equivalent to) a cyclic code, and, separately, of those triples for which the extended classical Goppa code is (equivalent to) a cyclic code.
status_search_result: The problem of fully characterizing which classical Goppa codes (extended or not) are cyclic remains open. Numerous works (Berlekamp–Moreno, Tzeng–Zimmermann, Berger, and more recent papers including a 2024 preprint on generator polynomials of cyclic expurgated or extended Goppa codes) provide sufficient conditions and new families of cyclic (extended) Goppa codes, but no complete characterization has been established.

paper_title: Open problems on cyclic codes
original_question: Are all families of cyclic codes asymptotically bad, or do there exist asymptotically good cyclic linear codes?
self_contained_problem:
Work over a fixed finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. A linear code of length $n$ and dimension $k$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is a $k$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$; its minimum distance $d(C)$ is the minimum Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword. The code $C$ is called cyclic if it is invariant under the cyclic shift $(c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{n-1}) \mapsto (c_{n-1}, c_0, \dots, c_{n-2})$.

An infinite family $\{C_i\}_{i \ge 1}$ of linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, with parameters $[n_i, k_i, d_i]$ and $n_i \to \infty$, is called asymptotically good if
$$\liminf_{i \to \infty} \frac{k_i}{n_i} > 0 \quad\text{and}\quad \liminf_{i \to \infty} \frac{d_i}{n_i} > 0.$$
Otherwise it is called asymptotically bad.

Question: Does there exist an asymptotically good family of cyclic linear codes over some finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, or is every infinite family of cyclic linear codes (over every fixed finite field) asymptotically bad?
status_search_result: The question of whether the class of cyclic codes is asymptotically good is a long-standing open problem in coding theory and remains unresolved as of 2024. Partial results show certain subclasses (e.g., BCH codes, cyclic codes whose lengths use only finitely many primes) are asymptotically bad, while various generalized/additive cyclic code variants (Z_4Z_4Z_4-additive cyclic, SR-additive cyclic, F_2[u]F_2[u]-additive cyclic) have been shown to be asymptotically good. The original question for ordinary cyclic codes is still open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues 0 < λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ ···. For every integer m ≥ 2, must λₘ₊₁/λₘ be at most the ball value j_{p+1,1}² / j_{p,1}², where p = (n−2)/2 and j_{ν,k} is the k-th positive zero of J_ν? In dimension 2, this asks whether λₘ₊₁/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)_disk ≈ 2.5387 for all m ≥ 2.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain, and let $0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2\le\lambda_3\le\cdots$ denote the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u=\lambda u$ in $\Omega$. For a real number $\nu>-1$, let $j_{\nu,k}$ denote the $k$-th positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Set $p=(n-2)/2$.

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ and every integer $m\ge 2$,
$$\frac{\lambda_{m+1}(\Omega)}{\lambda_m(\Omega)}\;\le\;\frac{j_{p+1,1}^{\,2}}{j_{p,1}^{\,2}},$$
the value on the right-hand side being the ratio $\lambda_2/\lambda_1$ for a ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, when $n=2$, decide whether
$$\frac{\lambda_{m+1}(\Omega)}{\lambda_m(\Omega)}\le\left(\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}\right)_{\text{disk}}\approx 2.5387\quad\text{for all }m\ge 2.$$
status_search_result: The case m=1 is the classical Payne–Pólya–Weinberger conjecture, proved by Ashbaugh and Benguria in the 1990s. The extension to consecutive ratios λ_{m+1}/λ_m for m≥2 remains an open conjecture; partial results and related strengthenings exist (e.g., work on lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues and PPW-type results in symmetric spaces), but no full proof or counterexample for general bounded domains has appeared.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω vary over bounded domains in ℝⁿ, and let λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ··· be its Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues. For every pair of integers k, m ≥ 1, must one always have λ_{km}/λₘ ≤ sup_D λ_k(D)/λ₁(D), where the supremum is taken over bounded domains D?
self_contained_problem:
For a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, let $0 < \lambda_1(\Omega) \le \lambda_2(\Omega) \le \lambda_3(\Omega) \le \cdots$ denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u = 0$ on $\partial \Omega$.

For each integer $k \ge 1$, define
$$ R_k := \sup_{D} \frac{\lambda_k(D)}{\lambda_1(D)}, $$
where the supremum is taken over all bounded domains $D \subset \mathbb{R}^n$.

Prove or disprove: for every pair of integers $k, m \ge 1$ and every bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$,
$$ \frac{\lambda_{km}(\Omega)}{\lambda_m(\Omega)} \;\le\; R_k. $$
status_search_result: The question is part of a well-known circle of conjectures about universal bounds for ratios of Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues, going back to Payne–Pólya–Weinberger and Ashbaugh–Benguria. The base case k=2, m=1 is the PPW conjecture, proved by Ashbaugh–Benguria; the more general inequality λ_{km}/λ_m ≤ sup λ_k/λ_1 remains open, with only partial results known for small k and m.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ··· be its Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues. Must the ratio λₙ₊₂/λ₁ always be at most the corresponding ratio for the n-ball, namely j_{p+2,1}² / j_{p,1}² with p = (n−2)/2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain. Consider the Dirichlet eigenvalue problem
$$-\Delta u = \lambda u \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
whose spectrum consists of an increasing sequence $0 < \lambda_1(\Omega) \le \lambda_2(\Omega) \le \lambda_3(\Omega) \le \cdots$ of eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity). For an $n$-ball $B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, the eigenvalues are explicitly given in terms of zeros of Bessel functions: setting $p = (n-2)/2$ and letting $j_{\nu,k}$ denote the $k$-th positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$, one has $\lambda_1(B) = j_{p,1}^2/R^2$ and $\lambda_{n+2}(B) = j_{p+2,1}^2/R^2$, where $R$ is the radius of $B$. In particular, the ratio $\lambda_{n+2}(B)/\lambda_1(B) = j_{p+2,1}^2/j_{p,1}^2$ is scale-invariant.

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\frac{\lambda_{n+2}(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)} \;\le\; \frac{j_{p+2,1}^2}{j_{p,1}^2},$$
with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is (up to a set of measure zero) a ball.
status_search_result: This is part of the family of Ashbaugh–Benguria higher-order eigenvalue ratio conjectures. Recent work (e.g., arXiv:1810.09415 and subsequent papers on the PPW conjecture for higher eigenvalues) makes partial progress toward such isoperimetric bounds but does not establish the sharp bound $\lambda_{n+2}/\lambda_1 \le j_{p+2,1}^2/j_{p,1}^2$ for arbitrary bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ λ₃ ≤ ···. Must the reciprocal-gap sum ∑_{i=1}^n λ₁/(λ_{i+1}−λ₁) be at least the corresponding value for the n-ball, namely n / (j²_{p+1,1}/j²_{p,1} − 1) where p = (n−2)/2? In dimension 2 this is the inequality λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁) ≥ ((λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁))_disk) ≈ 1.2998.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $0 < \lambda_1 < \lambda_2 \leq \lambda_3 \leq \cdots$ denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e., the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nontrivial $u \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u = 0$ on $\partial \Omega$.

For real $\nu \geq 0$, let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Set $p = (n-2)/2$.

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_{i+1} - \lambda_1} \;\geq\; \frac{n}{\,j_{p+1,1}^{2}/j_{p,1}^{2} - 1\,},$$
the right-hand side being the corresponding quantity when $\Omega$ is an $n$-dimensional ball. Equivalently, in dimension $n=2$,
$$\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2 - \lambda_1} + \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_3 - \lambda_1} \;\geq\; \left( \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2 - \lambda_1} + \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_3 - \lambda_1} \right)_{\text{disk}} \approx 1.2998.$$
status_search_result: The conjecture is a strengthening of the Payne–Pólya–Weinberger / Ashbaugh–Benguria type isoperimetric inequalities involving sums of reciprocal gaps of low Dirichlet eigenvalues. Searches turned up related Ashbaugh–Benguria conjectures and recent work on PPW-type bounds, but no published proof of this particular reciprocal-gap-sum inequality bounded below by the ball value; it appears to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let λ₂, …, λₙ₊₁ be the first nontrivial Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues after λ₁. Must the scale-invariant sum |Ω|^{2/n}(λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁) be at least the corresponding n-ball value C_n^{2/n} n j_{p+1,1}²? In dimension 2, this is the conjecture A(λ₂ + λ₃) ≥ [A(λ₂ + λ₃)]_disk = 2π j_{1,1}².
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 2$) be a bounded domain, and let
$$0<\lambda_1(\Omega)<\lambda_2(\Omega)\le\lambda_3(\Omega)\le\cdots$$
denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e., the numbers $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u=\lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Let $|\Omega|$ denote the $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure of $\Omega$, and let $B\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a ball.

For $\nu\ge 0$, let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$. Set $p=n/2-1$, so that the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$ are given by squares of zeros of $J_{p+k}$ for $k\ge 0$, and in particular $\lambda_2(B)=\cdots=\lambda_{n+1}(B)$ all equal $j_{p+1,1}^2/R^2$ where $R$ is the radius of $B$. Writing $C_n=\omega_n j_{p,1}^n$ with $\omega_n$ the volume of the unit $n$-ball (so that $|B|^{2/n}\lambda_1(B)=C_n^{2/n}j_{p,1}^2$ in normalized form), the corresponding scale-invariant value for the ball $B^*$ of the same volume as $\Omega$ is
$$\bigl[\,|\Omega|^{2/n}\bigl(\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1}\bigr)\bigr]_{\text{$n$-ball}}=C_n^{2/n}\, n\, j_{p+1,1}^2.$$

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$|\Omega|^{2/n}\bigl(\lambda_2(\Omega)+\lambda_3(\Omega)+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1}(\Omega)\bigr)\;\ge\;C_n^{2/n}\, n\, j_{p+1,1}^2,$$
with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball.

In particular, in dimension $n=2$, show that for every bounded planar domain $\Omega$ with area $A=|\Omega|$,
$$A\bigl(\lambda_2(\Omega)+\lambda_3(\Omega)\bigr)\;\ge\;2\pi\, j_{1,1}^2,$$
the right-hand side being the value attained when $\Omega$ is a disk.
status_search_result: This is a Faber–Krahn-type lower bound for the scale-invariant sum of the eigenvalues $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{n+1}$, conjectured to be minimized by the ball. The analogous Faber–Krahn result for $\lambda_1$ is classical, and the Ashbaugh–Benguria-type ratio inequalities are known, but the lower bound for the sum $\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_{n+1}$ (and even the planar case $A(\lambda_2+\lambda_3)$) does not appear to be established in the literature. Recent surveys on shape optimization for Laplace eigenvalues continue to list this as an open problem; no proof or counterexample was located.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let 0 = μ₀ < μ₁ ≤ μ₂ ≤ ··· be the Neumann eigenvalues of the Laplacian, defined by −Δv = μv in Ω with ∂v/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω. Must the reciprocal sum |Ω|^{-2/n}(1/μ₁ + ··· + 1/μₙ) be at least the n-ball value n/(C_n^{2/n} p_{n/2,1}²), where p_{ν,1} is the first positive zero of the derivative of t^{1−ν}J_ν(t)? In dimension 2, this is the question whether (1/A)(1/μ₁ + 1/μ₂) ≥ [(1/A)(1/μ₁ + 1/μ₂)]_disk = 2/(π p_{1,1}²).
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth bounded domain, and let
$$0=\mu_0<\mu_1\le\mu_2\le\cdots$$
denote the Neumann eigenvalues of the Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the values $\mu$ for which there exists a nontrivial function $v$ satisfying $-\Delta v=\mu v$ in $\Omega$ and $\partial v/\partial n=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Write $|\Omega|$ for the Lebesgue measure of $\Omega$, let $C_n=\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2+1)$ denote the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $p_{\nu,1}$ denote the first positive zero of the derivative of $t^{1-\nu}J_\nu(t)$, where $J_\nu$ is the Bessel function of the first kind of order $\nu$.

Prove or disprove the following sharp isoperimetric inequality:
$$|\Omega|^{-2/n}\left(\frac{1}{\mu_1}+\frac{1}{\mu_2}+\cdots+\frac{1}{\mu_n}\right)\ \ge\ \frac{n}{C_n^{2/n}\,p_{n/2,1}^{\,2}},$$
with equality (in the limiting sense) when $\Omega$ is a ball. In particular, in dimension $n=2$, prove or disprove that for every smooth bounded planar domain of area $A$,
$$\frac{1}{A}\left(\frac{1}{\mu_1}+\frac{1}{\mu_2}\right)\ \ge\ \frac{2}{\pi\,p_{1,1}^{\,2}}.$$
status_search_result: Web search indicates this isoperimetric lower bound for the reciprocal sum of the first n nonzero Neumann eigenvalues remains open in general. Partial results exist (e.g. sharp bounds for the harmonic mean of low Neumann eigenvalues for simply connected planar domains, due to work in the Ashbaugh–Benguria line), but the inequality is not established for arbitrary smooth bounded planar domains or in higher dimensions.

original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with n ≥ 4. For the clamped plate eigenvalue problem Δ²w = Γw in Ω with boundary conditions w = 0 and ∂w/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω, must the lowest eigenvalue Γ₁ satisfy the Faber-Krahn-type inequality |Ω|^{4/n} Γ₁ ≥ (|Ω|^{4/n} Γ₁)_{n-ball}?

Let $n \geq 4$ and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain. Consider the clamped plate eigenvalue problem
$$\Delta^2 w = \Gamma\, w \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad w = 0,\ \ \frac{\partial w}{\partial \nu} = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega,$$
where $\Delta$ is the Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $\Delta^2$ the biharmonic operator, and $\nu$ the outward unit normal on $\partial\Omega$. $$|\Omega|^{4/n}\, \Gamma_1(\Omega) \ \geq \ |B|^{4/n}\, \Gamma_1(B),$$
with equality if and only if $\Omega$ is a ball.

original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ. Write λ₂(Ω), …, λₙ₊₁(Ω) for the second through (n+1)-st Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues of Ω, and Λ₁(Ω) for the lowest buckling eigenvalue. Is the stronger lower bound Λ₁(Ω) ≥ (1/n)(λ₂(Ω) + ··· + λₙ₊₁(Ω)) always true?

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain. Consider the Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalue problem
$$-\Delta u = \lambda u \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u=0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
whose eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, are $0<\lambda_1(\Omega)\le \lambda_2(\Omega)\le \lambda_3(\Omega)\le \cdots$. Consider also the buckling (clamped-plate) eigenvalue problem
$$\Delta^{2} v = -\Lambda\,\Delta v \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad v = \frac{\partial v}{\partial \nu}=0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
whose smallest eigenvalue is denoted $\Lambda_1(\Omega)$.

Decide whether the inequality
$$\Lambda_1(\Omega) \;\ge\; \frac{1}{n}\bigl(\lambda_2(\Omega) + \lambda_3(\Omega) + \cdots + \lambda_{n+1}(\Omega)\bigr)$$
holds for every bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ. What is the optimal lower bound for the scale-invariant product |Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)λ₂(Ω), where λ₁ and λ₂ are the first two Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues? Likewise, if Ω is convex, what is the optimal lower bound for |Ω|^{2/n} λ₂(Ω)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain, and let $0<\lambda_1(\Omega)\le\lambda_2(\Omega)\le\cdots$ denote the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian, i.e. the eigenvalues of the problem
$$-\Delta u=\lambda u\text{ in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\text{ on }\partial\Omega.$$
Write $|\Omega|$ for the $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure of $\Omega$. The quantities $|\Omega|^{4/n}\lambda_1(\Omega)\lambda_2(\Omega)$ and $|\Omega|^{2/n}\lambda_2(\Omega)$ are scale invariant.

(a) Determine the sharp constant
$$C_1(n)=\inf_{\Omega}\,|\Omega|^{4/n}\,\lambda_1(\Omega)\,\lambda_2(\Omega),$$
where the infimum is taken over all bounded domains $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, and identify the extremal domains (if any).

(b) Determine the sharp constant
$$C_2(n)=\inf_{\Omega\text{ convex}}\,|\Omega|^{2/n}\,\lambda_2(\Omega),$$
where the infimum is taken over all bounded convex domains $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, and identify the extremal domains (if any).
status_search_result: A web search did not locate a sharp lower bound for either of these scale-invariant quantities. While many related results exist (Faber–Krahn for $|\Omega|^{2/n}\lambda_1$, Ashbaugh–Benguria for the ratio $\lambda_2/\lambda_1$, Pólya-type lower bounds, and recent work on the Ashbaugh–Benguria conjectures), no reference establishing the optimal lower bound for $|\Omega|^{4/n}\lambda_1\lambda_2$ over general bounded domains or for $|\Omega|^{2/n}\lambda_2$ over convex domains was found, so the problems appear to remain open.

paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
original_question: Let λ_k and μ_k denote the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacian eigenvalues of a bounded planar domain Ω of area A, with μ₀ = 0. Do Pólya’s conjectures hold, namely μ_k < 4πk/A < λ_k for every k = 1, 2, ...? More generally, are Dirichlet eigenvalues always above, and Neumann eigenvalues always below, their Weyl asymptotic values in all dimensions?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded planar domain of area $A$. Denote by 
$$0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \lambda_3 \le \cdots$$
the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$ (i.e., $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ in $\Omega$, $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$), and by
$$0 = \mu_0 \le \mu_1 \le \mu_2 \le \cdots$$
the eigenvalues of the Neumann Laplacian on $\Omega$ (with vanishing normal derivative on $\partial\Omega$).

(a) Prove or disprove Pólya's conjectures: for every $k = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$,
$$\mu_k \;<\; \frac{4\pi k}{A} \;<\; \lambda_k.$$

(b) More generally, for a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) of volume $V$, let $\lambda_k$ and $\mu_k$ denote the corresponding Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacian eigenvalues. Let
$$W_k \;=\; \frac{(2\pi)^2 \, k^{2/n}}{(\omega_n V)^{2/n}},$$
where $\omega_n$ is the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, denote the leading Weyl asymptotic value. Is it true that
$$\mu_k \;<\; W_k \;<\; \lambda_k \qquad \text{for all } k \ge 1?$$
status_search_result: Pólya's conjectures are known for tiling domains (Pólya, 1961). Filonov, Levitin, Polterovich, and Sobolev (Inventiones, 2023; arXiv:2203.07696) proved the Dirichlet form of Pólya's conjecture for Euclidean balls in all dimensions and for planar disks and sectors; extensions to annuli appeared in 2025/2026 (arXiv:2505.21737), and to cylinders in 2025 (arXiv:2511.17050). The conjectures remain open for general bounded domains in any dimension.

paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
original_question: Let s(G) = lambda_1(G) - lambda_n(G) be the spectral spread of a connected graph G on n >= 3 vertices. Is it true that s(G) <= sqrt(4qn - 3q^2 - 2q + 1), where q = ceil(2n/3), with equality if and only if G is the complete split graph CS(n,q), meaning the graph whose vertex set is partitioned into a clique of size q and an independent set of size n-q = floor(n/3), with every clique vertex adjacent to every independent-set vertex?
self_contained_problem:
For a simple connected graph $G$ on $n\ge 3$ vertices, let $\lambda_1(G)\ge \lambda_2(G)\ge\cdots\ge \lambda_n(G)$ denote the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix, and define the spectral spread
$$s(G)=\lambda_1(G)-\lambda_n(G).$$
For integers $n\ge 3$ and $1\le q\le n-1$, let $CS(n,q)$ denote the complete split graph: the graph on $n$ vertices whose vertex set is partitioned into a clique of size $q$ and an independent set of size $n-q$, with every vertex of the clique adjacent to every vertex of the independent set. Set $q=\lceil 2n/3\rceil$ (so $n-q=\lfloor n/3\rfloor$).

Prove or disprove: for every connected graph $G$ on $n\ge 3$ vertices,
$$s(G)\le \sqrt{4qn-3q^2-2q+1},$$
with equality if and only if $G\cong CS(n,q)$.
status_search_result: Breen, Riasanovsky, Tait, and Urschel ("Maximum spread of graphs and bipartite graphs", arXiv:2109.03129, Comm. AMS 2022) proved the long-standing Gregory–Hershkowitz–Kirkland conjecture that the spread-maximizing $n$-vertex graph is the join of a clique of size $\lfloor 2n/3\rfloor$ and an independent set of size $\lceil n/3\rceil$ — a complete split graph — for all sufficiently large $n$. The conjecture remains open for all $n$, so the bound and equality case stated above are established only asymptotically.
