paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: For Stable Marriage instances with uncertain preferences in the lottery model, determine the computational complexity of SM HighestProbability: compute a matching with the highest probability of being stable when each agent has a probability distribution over strict preference lists.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with uncertain preferences in the lottery model, defined as follows. There are two disjoint finite sets of agents, men M and women W, with |M| = |W| = n. Each agent a ∈ M ∪ W is associated with a probability distribution P_a over the set of strict (linear) preference orders on the agents of the opposite side; the distributions of different agents are independent. A realization is obtained by independently sampling, for each agent a, a strict preference list according to P_a. Given a perfect matching μ between M and W, the matching is said to be stable in a realization if there is no blocking pair, i.e., no pair (m, w) ∈ M × W with μ(m) ≠ w such that m strictly prefers w to μ(m) and w strictly prefers m to μ(w) under the realized preferences. The stability probability of μ is the probability, over the random realization, that μ is stable.

Problem (SM-HighestProbability, lottery model): Given the distributions {P_a}_{a ∈ M ∪ W} as input, determine the computational complexity of the problem of computing a perfect matching μ that maximizes the stability probability. In particular, decide whether this optimization problem (or its natural decision version: given a rational threshold q, does there exist a matching whose stability probability is at least q?) is solvable in polynomial time, NP-hard, or of some other complexity.
status_search_result: The general complexity of SM-HighestProbability in the lottery model appears to remain open. Partial results are known: the problem is NP-hard in restricted settings (e.g., under certain transitivity/WST assumptions), and it is polynomial-time solvable when only a constant number of agents on the same side are uncertain. No full classification (polynomial-time algorithm or unconditional NP-hardness) for the general lottery model has been reported.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, determine the complexity and algorithmic structure of the model when exchanges are allowed to occur along cycles of length greater than 2, rather than only through swaps between two applicants.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following house allocation model on a social network. Let G=(V,E) be a simple undirected graph whose vertices V={1,...,n} represent applicants. Each applicant i initially owns a distinct house h_i and has a strict preference order ≻_i over the set H={h_1,...,h_n} of houses. Applicants may exchange houses only along cycles in G: for any simple cycle v_1, v_2, ..., v_k, v_1 in G (with k≥2), the applicants on the cycle may simultaneously rotate their currently held houses (each v_j passing its house to v_{j+1}, indices mod k), provided that every participating applicant strictly prefers the house they receive to the house they currently hold. An allocation is a permutation assigning each applicant a house; it is reachable from the initial endowment by a sequence of such cyclic exchanges.

The case k=2 (swaps along edges only) has been studied and its computational complexity is understood. The problem asks: when cyclic exchanges of arbitrary length k≥2 are permitted (with the cycle required to be a cycle in G), determine the computational complexity of the natural decision problems associated with this model — in particular, deciding whether a given target allocation is reachable from the initial endowment via a sequence of cyclic exchanges along cycles of G, deciding whether a Pareto-improving cyclic exchange exists, and computing a (core-)stable or Pareto-optimal reachable allocation. Provide algorithms or hardness results, and describe the algorithmic structure of the model.
status_search_result: Recent work (2023–2024) studies housing markets on networks with mechanisms such as "Swap With Neighbors", "Leave and Share", and "Connected Trading Cycles", and establishes NP-hardness for several core-related questions and for swap-reachability on cliques and caterpillars. However, no source in the search resolves the general complexity and algorithmic structure of network-restricted exchanges along cycles of length greater than 2 in the house allocation setting; the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: For the NP-hard cases of deciding whether a target matching is reachable from an initial matching, and of finding a Pareto-optimal matching, in house allocation via exchanges in a social network, determine whether these hard cases become tractable under useful parameters and develop a parameterized complexity theory for them.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following house allocation model with exchanges over a social network. There is a set of agents $A = \{a_1,\dots,a_n\}$ and a set of houses $H = \{h_1,\dots,h_n\}$. Each agent $a_i$ has a (possibly weak) preference order $\succeq_i$ over $H$. The social network is an undirected graph $G=(A,E)$ on the agents. A matching is a bijection $M: A \to H$. From a matching $M$, a swap between two adjacent agents $a_i, a_j$ (with $\{a_i,a_j\}\in E$) produces a new matching $M'$ in which $a_i$ and $a_j$ exchange their houses; the swap is allowed only if it is rational/Pareto-improving (each of $a_i, a_j$ weakly prefers the new house and at least one strictly prefers it). A matching $M^*$ is reachable from an initial matching $M_0$ if there is a finite sequence of allowed swaps transforming $M_0$ into $M^*$. A matching $M$ is Pareto-optimal if no other matching $M'$ is weakly preferred by all agents and strictly preferred by at least one.

The following two decision problems are known to be NP-hard in general:
(R) Given $(A,H,G,(\succeq_i)_{i\in A}, M_0, M^*)$, decide whether $M^*$ is reachable from $M_0$ by a sequence of allowed swaps along edges of $G$.
(P) Given $(A,H,G,(\succeq_i)_{i\in A}, M_0)$, find a Pareto-optimal matching reachable from $M_0$ (or decide existence of one with prescribed properties).

Identify natural structural or numerical parameters $k$ (e.g., treewidth of $G$, maximum degree, number of distinct preference profiles, number of houses any agent finds acceptable, size of symmetric difference between $M_0$ and $M^*$, etc.) under which these problems admit fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms with running time $f(k)\cdot \mathrm{poly}(n)$, and develop a parameterized complexity theory (FPT algorithms, $W[1]$/$W[2]$-hardness, kernelization lower and upper bounds) classifying the complexity of (R) and (P) with respect to these parameters.
category_tag: parameterized complexity of matchings under preferences
status_search_result: Follow-up work has addressed parts of this program. The MFCS 2021 paper "Maximum Votes Pareto-Efficient Allocations via Swaps on a Social Network" and subsequent works refine the complexity landscape of Pareto-efficient swap matchings on social networks (giving polynomial algorithms for path networks with strict preferences and NP-hardness for star networks with weak preferences). Parameterized complexity has been examined for related house-allocation problems (e.g., with lower/upper quotas), but a comprehensive parameterized complexity theory for the specific NP-hard cases of reachability and Pareto-optimality in the social-network swap model does not yet appear to be complete; the broader program remains partially open.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: Given a Stable Marriage instance I and a matching M_0, determine the computational complexity of deciding whether the divorce digraph D_I contains a directed path from the vertex v_{M_0} to a sink vertex, equivalently to some stable matching.
self_contained_problem:
Let I be an instance of the Stable Marriage problem: a set of n men and n women, each providing a strict, complete preference list over the members of the opposite sex. A matching M is a set of disjoint man–woman pairs that saturates everyone. A pair (m,w) ∉ M is a blocking pair of M if m prefers w to his partner in M and w prefers m to her partner in M; M is stable if it has no blocking pair.

Define the divorce digraph D_I as follows. Its vertices are all (perfect) matchings of I. For every matching M and every blocking pair (m,w) of M, place a directed arc from M to the matching M' obtained from M by "satisfying" (m,w), i.e., by pairing m with w and re-pairing their previous partners with each other (so M' differs from M only on these two pairs). The sinks of D_I are exactly the stable matchings of I.

Decision problem. Given as input a Stable Marriage instance I together with a (not necessarily stable) matching M_0 of I, determine the computational complexity of deciding whether D_I contains a directed path from the vertex M_0 to some sink, equivalently, whether some sequence of blocking-pair resolutions starting from M_0 reaches a stable matching.
status_search_result: Recent work on "paths to stability" for the stable marriage problem (including a 2023 paper on Improved Paths to Stability) continues to study reachability in the divorce digraph, but does not report a resolution of the complexity of deciding whether a given starting matching can reach a stable matching via blocking-pair resolutions. No source found that settles this decision problem; it appears still open.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: For 1s-max smti, where ties occur on only one side of the market, determine whether the current approximation upper bound can be reduced to 5/4.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with Ties and Incomplete lists, restricted so that ties occur on only one side of the market (1-sided SMTI). An instance consists of two disjoint finite sets, the men $U$ and the women $W$. Each man $u \in U$ has a strictly ordered preference list over a subset of $W$ (his acceptable partners). Each woman $w \in W$ has a preference list over a subset of $U$ (her acceptable partners) in which ties (groups of equally ranked men) are allowed. A matching $M$ is a set of pairwise disjoint man–woman pairs $(u,w)$ such that each pair is mutually acceptable. A pair $(u,w) \notin M$ is a blocking pair for $M$ if $u$ and $w$ find each other acceptable, $u$ is either unmatched in $M$ or strictly prefers $w$ to his $M$-partner, and $w$ is either unmatched in $M$ or strictly prefers $u$ to her $M$-partner or is indifferent between them. A matching $M$ is weakly stable if it admits no blocking pair. The problem MAX-SMTI with one-sided ties asks for a weakly stable matching of maximum cardinality.

For a constant $c \ge 1$, a polynomial-time algorithm is a $c$-approximation algorithm if, for every instance, it returns a weakly stable matching of cardinality at least $\mathrm{OPT}/c$, where $\mathrm{OPT}$ denotes the maximum cardinality of a weakly stable matching.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial-time $\tfrac{5}{4}$-approximation algorithm for MAX-SMTI with one-sided ties? Equivalently, can the best achievable polynomial-time approximation ratio for this problem be reduced to $5/4$?
status_search_result: The general one-sided-ties MAX-SMTI approximation ratio has been progressively improved (3/2, then 25/17 ≈ 1.4706 by Iwama–Miyazaki–Yanagisawa, then 22/15 ≈ 1.4667 by Huang–Kavitha, then 13/9 ≈ 1.444 by Bauckholt–Pashkovich–Sanità in 2018), but none reach 5/4. Lam and Plaxton later achieved the 5/4 bound only when tie lengths are bounded by 2 (and more generally an integrality-gap-matching bound for bounded tie size). For unbounded one-sided ties, no 5/4-approximation is known and the question appears to remain open, while 5/4 is the known UGC-hardness lower bound.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: Given an instance I of the Stable Marriage problem with ties, determine whether there exists an efficient output-sensitive algorithm for listing all stable matchings in time O(p(n) + |S_I| q(n)), where p and q are polynomial functions and S_I is the set of stable matchings of I.
self_contained_problem:
An instance I of the Stable Marriage problem with ties (SMT) consists of a set of n men and n women, together with, for each person, a preference list ranking some subset of the members of the opposite sex, where ties are allowed (i.e., a person may rank several alternatives as equally preferred). A matching M is a set of disjoint man–woman pairs. A pair (m,w) not in M is a (weakly) blocking pair for M if m and w each strictly prefer each other to their current partner under M (with unmatched persons treated as worst). A matching M is weakly stable if it admits no blocking pair. Let S_I denote the set of all weakly stable matchings of I, and let n denote the size of I.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given any instance I of SMT, outputs every matching in S_I (each exactly once) within total running time
  O(p(n) + |S_I| · q(n)),
where p and q are fixed polynomials? Equivalently, is there an output-sensitive polynomial-delay algorithm for enumerating all weakly stable matchings of an SMT instance?
status_search_result: A web search did not surface any algorithm that enumerates all weakly stable matchings of a stable marriage instance with ties in output-sensitive polynomial time O(p(n)+|S_I|q(n)). While polynomial-delay enumeration is known for the classical stable marriage problem (without ties) via Gusfield's method on the rotation poset, no analogous output-sensitive result for SMT appears in the literature, and the question is repeatedly cited as open in surveys on matching under preferences.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: For the general (a, b)-supermatch notion in Stable Marriage or Stable Roommates instances with incomplete lists, determine whether the decision problem “does there exist an (a, b)-supermatch?” belongs to NP.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider a Stable Marriage with Incomplete lists (SMI) instance, or more generally a Stable Roommates with Incomplete lists (SRI) instance: there is a finite set of agents, each of whom ranks a subset of the other agents in strict order of preference. A matching M is a set of acceptable pairs such that each agent appears in at most one pair. A pair (x,y) not in M blocks M if x and y find each other acceptable and each of x,y is either unmatched in M or strictly prefers the other to their current partner. M is stable if it has no blocking pair.

Given two nonnegative integers a and b, a stable matching M is called an (a,b)-supermatch if, for every subset S of at most a pairs in M, removing these pairs (so that the 2|S| agents involved become single) can be "repaired" by producing a new stable matching M' such that:
 (i) every agent in S is matched in M' (possibly to a different partner), and
 (ii) M' differs from M\S in at most b additional pairs (i.e., apart from the pairs in S being replaced, at most b other pairs of M are modified).

Question. Determine whether the following decision problem belongs to the complexity class NP: given an SMI (or SRI) instance and integers a, b, does there exist an (a,b)-supermatch?

Equivalently: is there a polynomial-size certificate, verifiable in polynomial time, witnessing the existence of an (a,b)-supermatch for arbitrary a (in particular a > 1)?
status_search_result: Published complexity studies on robust stable marriage establish NP-completeness of the (1,b)-supermatch decision problem, but for general a > 1 the membership of the (a,b)-supermatch existence problem in NP remains unresolved: no polynomial-time verifiable certificate is known. The problem is NP-hard but not known to be in NP.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: Develop a theory of robust stable matchings for the Stable Roommates problem, including robustness notions analogous to those studied for Stable Marriage and incomplete-list variants, since robust stability in SR appears not to have been studied in those senses.
self_contained_problem:
Stable Roommates setting. Let $A=\{a_1,\dots,a_n\}$ be a finite set of agents with $n$ even. A preference profile $P$ assigns to each agent $a\in A$ a strict total order $\succ_a$ over $A\setminus\{a\}$ (the complete-list case), or a strict total order over some subset of $A\setminus\{a\}$ representing acceptable partners (the incomplete-list case). A matching is a partition $M$ of $A$ into pairs (and, in the incomplete-list case, possibly singletons). A pair $\{a,b\}\notin M$ is blocking if $a$ and $b$ each prefer the other to their partner in $M$ (with being unmatched ranked below every acceptable partner). $M$ is stable if it admits no blocking pair.

Two notions of robust stability have been studied for the Stable Marriage problem:

(i) Robustness to errors / swaps in preferences (Mai–Vazirani style). Given a preference profile $P$ and an integer $d\geq 0$, define the $d$-neighbourhood $N_d(P)$ to consist of all profiles $P'$ obtainable from $P$ by performing at most $d$ adjacent swaps in the preference lists (over all agents in total, or per agent, depending on the variant). A stable matching $M$ for $P$ is called $d$-robust if $M$ is stable in every $P'\in N_d(P)$, or, in a weaker variant, if for every $P'\in N_d(P)$ there exists a stable matching $M'$ for $P'$ that is "close" to $M$ in a prescribed sense (e.g. small symmetric difference).

(ii) Robustness to changes in preferences (Chen et al. style). Here one studies how stable matchings adapt to bounded modifications of the profile, parameterized by combinatorial measures of change, and asks for matchings simultaneously stable, or simultaneously "almost stable", across a set of profiles.

Task. Develop an analogous theory of robust stable matchings for the Stable Roommates problem, both with complete and with incomplete preference lists. In particular:

(a) Formulate precise definitions of $d$-robust stable matchings for Stable Roommates in the senses of (i) and (ii), accounting for the fact that some Stable Roommates instances admit no stable matching at all.

(b) Determine the computational complexity of deciding, given an instance $(A,P)$ of Stable Roommates and an integer $d$, whether a $d$-robust stable matching exists, and of finding one if it does.

(c) Establish structural results (existence guarantees, lattice or poset structure of robust stable matchings, characterizations of instances admitting robust stable matchings, bounds on the size of $d$ for which they exist) parallel to those known in the Stable Marriage case.

Provide such definitions, algorithms, hardness results, and structural theorems for Stable Roommates and its incomplete-list variants.
status_search_result: A web search for robust stable matchings in the Stable Roommates problem returned no work developing the Mai–Vazirani or Chen et al. notions of robustness specifically for Stable Roommates. Existing robustness work (Mai–Vazirani ESA 2018; Chen et al.; Gangam's dissertation work) focuses on Stable Marriage / bipartite settings. A separate line of work introduces "stability against robust deviations" for the roommate problem, but this is a different notion (weakening stability via deviation depth), not the input-perturbation robustness asked for here. The problem therefore appears still open.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
context_brief: least unpopular matchings in house allocation
original_question: In the House Allocation problem with strict or tied applicant preferences, can one obtain a better approximation algorithm for finding a matching of minimum unpopularity factor or minimum unpopularity margin, or alternatively prove tighter inapproximability bounds for these optimization problems?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the House Allocation problem: an instance consists of a set $A$ of applicants and a set $H$ of houses, together with, for each applicant $a \in A$, a preference list over a subset of $H$ that is either strictly ordered or may contain ties (so each list is a weak ranking of acceptable houses). A matching is an assignment $M \subseteq A \times H$ in which each applicant is matched to at most one acceptable house and each house to at most one applicant.

For two matchings $M$ and $M'$, let $\phi(M,M')$ be the number of applicants who strictly prefer their partner in $M$ to their partner in $M'$ (an applicant unmatched in one and matched in the other prefers the matched one; unacceptable assignments are not allowed). Define:
- the unpopularity factor of $M$ as
$$u(M) = \max_{M' : \phi(M',M) > 0} \frac{\phi(M',M)}{\phi(M,M')},$$
- the unpopularity margin of $M$ as
$$g(M) = \max_{M'} \bigl(\phi(M',M) - \phi(M,M')\bigr).$$
A matching is popular if $u(M) \le 1$ (equivalently $g(M) \le 0$).

The optimization problems Min-Unpopularity-Factor and Min-Unpopularity-Margin ask, given an instance, for a matching minimizing $u(M)$ and $g(M)$ respectively.

Problem: Design an approximation algorithm for Min-Unpopularity-Factor or for Min-Unpopularity-Margin in the House Allocation setting (with strict preferences, or with ties) whose approximation guarantee improves on currently known ratios; or, conversely, establish stronger inapproximability lower bounds for these problems than those currently known.
status_search_result: Recent work (2023–2025) has produced new approximation results for related unpopularity problems, notably tight approximations for the related Graphical House Allocation and improved unpopularity-factor bounds for (3,3)-hypergraph matchings with one-sided preferences. However, no work appears to have closed the approximability gap for Min-Unpopularity-Factor or Min-Unpopularity-Margin in the classical House Allocation problem, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
context_brief: highest-probability stable matching under lottery uncertainty
original_question: Under the lottery model of uncertain preferences, what is the computational complexity of computing a matching with the highest probability of being stable in a Stable Marriage instance?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with n men and n women. In the classical setting, each agent has a strict linear preference order over the agents of the opposite sex, and a perfect matching M is called stable if there is no man–woman pair (m, w) such that m prefers w to his partner in M and w prefers m to her partner in M.

In the lottery model of uncertain preferences, the input is a probability distribution P_a over strict linear orders over the opposite sex for each agent a, and these distributions are mutually independent. A preference profile is sampled by drawing each agent's preference order independently from its distribution. The stability probability of a perfect matching M is the probability, taken over a random preference profile sampled from these independent distributions, that M is stable.

Problem. Determine the computational complexity of the following decision/search problem: given such a lottery-model instance (the n × n probability distributions, encoded as explicit lists of (linear order, probability) pairs with rational probabilities), compute a perfect matching M* whose stability probability is maximum among all perfect matchings (equivalently, decide, given a rational threshold q, whether some perfect matching has stability probability at least q). In particular, is this problem NP-hard, and does it belong to NP, to PP, or to some other natural complexity class?
status_search_result: According to the work introducing the lottery model for stable matching with uncertain linear preferences (Aziz, Biró, Gaspers, de Haan, Mattei, Rastegari; Algorithmica 2020), computing a matching with the highest stability probability in the lottery model is explicitly listed as an open problem. It is known to be solvable in polynomial time only in restricted cases (e.g., when only a constant number of agents are uncertain and one side of the market has certain preferences). No subsequent resolution of the general case has been located.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: After the complexity gaps in Table 1 are resolved for Pareto-optimal and stable matchings under uncertain preferences, determine the analogous complexity of computing or reasoning about rank-maximal matchings when agents' preferences are uncertain.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a bipartite matching market with a finite set of agents A and a finite set of items (or another set of agents) B, where each agent a ∈ A has a strict preference order over an acceptable subset of B. A matching M is rank-maximal if it has the maximum number of agents matched to their first choice, subject to that the maximum number matched to their second choice, and so on lexicographically over the rank-distribution vector.

Now suppose the preferences are uncertain, given in one of the standard uncertainty models:
(i) Lottery model: for each agent a, a probability distribution over linear orders of that agent's acceptable partners is given.
(ii) Compact indifference model: each agent provides a partial order (e.g., a weak order with ties), and the true preference is any linear extension chosen uniformly at random.
(iii) Joint probability model: a probability distribution over complete preference profiles is given explicitly.

For each uncertainty model, determine the computational complexity of the following decision/search problems:
1. (Possibly rank-maximal) Given a matching M, decide whether there exists a realization of the preferences under which M is rank-maximal.
2. (Necessarily rank-maximal) Given a matching M, decide whether M is rank-maximal under every realization of positive probability.
3. (Probability of rank-maximality) Compute the probability that a given matching M is rank-maximal.
4. (Most likely rank-maximal) Compute a matching maximizing the probability of being rank-maximal.

Classify each problem as polynomial-time solvable, NP-hard, #P-hard, or otherwise, in each of the three uncertainty models.
status_search_result: A search indicates that rank-maximal matchings have been studied extensively under classical and tied preferences, and uncertain-preference frameworks have been analyzed for stable, Pareto-optimal, popular, and dominant matchings. However, a systematic complexity classification of rank-maximal matchings under the standard uncertain-preference models (lottery, compact indifference, joint probability) does not appear to have been carried out. The problem is highlighted as a future direction and appears to remain open.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, which exchange mechanisms are strategyproof, and under what structural restrictions on the network or exchange rules can strategyproofness be achieved?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following model of house allocation via exchanges on a social network. Let G = (N, E) be an undirected graph whose vertex set N = {1, ..., n} represents agents and whose edge set E encodes a social network (an edge {i, j} ∈ E means agents i and j are acquaintances). Each agent i ∈ N initially owns one indivisible house h_i, and has a strict preference order ≻_i over the set of houses {h_1, ..., h_n}. An exchange mechanism is a function f that takes as input the reported preference profile (≻_i)_{i ∈ N} (and possibly the network G) and outputs an allocation π : N → {h_1, ..., h_n} that is a permutation of the initial endowment, subject to the constraint that exchanges respect the network structure (for example, only agents connected by an edge, or lying in a common connected subset, may trade houses, or trading cycles must be subgraphs of G).

A mechanism f is strategyproof if for every agent i, every preference profile (≻_j)_{j ∈ N}, and every alternative report ≻'_i, the house assigned to i under truthful reporting is weakly preferred (under the true ≻_i) to the house assigned to i when i reports ≻'_i.

Problem. Characterize the exchange mechanisms on social networks that are strategyproof. In particular:
(a) Identify structural restrictions on the network G (e.g., trees, bounded degree, bipartite, complete) under which there exist nontrivial strategyproof exchange mechanisms satisfying additional desiderata such as individual rationality, Pareto efficiency (with respect to feasible exchanges), and non-wastefulness.
(b) Identify restrictions on the allowed exchange rules (e.g., bounded cycle length, only pairwise swaps, only swaps along edges, top trading cycles restricted to the network) under which strategyproofness can be guaranteed.
(c) Provide impossibility results delineating the boundary between settings admitting strategyproof exchange mechanisms and those in which strategyproofness is incompatible with the chosen efficiency/fairness criteria.
status_search_result: Subsequent work has made partial progress on this question. In particular, an AAMAS 2022 paper "Strategy-Proof House Allocation with Existing Tenants over Social Networks" proposes a modified YRMH-IGYT mechanism that is individually rational, strategy-proof, and weakly non-wasteful, and proves impossibility results (e.g., even on tree-structured networks, no strategy-proof and individually rational mechanism is non-wasteful). Further work on online housing markets and on strategy-proofness in network auctions continues to explore the boundary. A complete characterization of strategyproof network-exchange mechanisms remains open.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: For each instance size n of the Stable Marriage problem, determine the maximum possible number x_n of stable matchings over all size-n instances, or at least substantially narrow the remaining gap between the best known lower and upper bounds on x_n.
self_contained_problem:
An instance of the Stable Marriage problem of size n consists of n men and n women, where each person has a strict total order (preference list) ranking all n members of the opposite sex. A matching M is a bijection between the set of men and the set of women. A pair (m,w) with M(m) ≠ w is called a blocking pair for M if m prefers w to M(m) and w prefers m to M(w). A matching M is stable if it admits no blocking pair.

For each positive integer n, let x_n denote the maximum, taken over all Stable Marriage instances of size n, of the number of distinct stable matchings admitted by the instance.

Determine x_n exactly for every n, or otherwise substantially narrow the gap between the best known lower and upper bounds on x_n. In particular, the current best lower bound is of the form Ω(c₁^n) with c₁ ≈ 2.28 (via the Irving–Leather construction) and the current best upper bound is simply exponential of the form c₂^n for some constant c₂; close the gap between these two constants, or determine the precise exponential growth rate of x_n.
status_search_result: The problem remains open in its exact form. Karlin, Gharan, and Weber (STOC 2018, arXiv:1711.01032) established the first simply exponential upper bound c^n for the maximum number of stable matchings, improving on prior bounds of the form 2^(n log n - O(n)). The best lower bound, due to Irving and Leather, remains Ω(2.28^n). A gap between the bases of the exponents persists, and the exact growth rate of x_n is still unknown.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
context_brief: approximability gap for unrestricted max smti
original_question: For unrestricted Stable Marriage with Ties and Incomplete lists, close the approximability gap for finding a maximum-cardinality stable matching between the current best lower and upper bounds.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with Ties and Incomplete lists (SMTI). An instance consists of two disjoint finite sets, men M and women W, where each person p has a preference list that is a strict ranking of ties (equivalence classes) over a subset of the opposite side (the acceptable partners). A matching is a set of disjoint acceptable man–woman pairs. A pair (m,w), with m and w not matched to each other, is blocking for matching S if m and w find each other acceptable and each of them is either unmatched in S or strictly prefers the other to their current partner in S (ties are broken in favor of the current partner, i.e., indifference is not strict preference). A matching is stable if it admits no blocking pair. The MAX-SMTI problem asks for a stable matching of maximum cardinality.

It is known that MAX-SMTI is NP-hard and APX-hard. In the unrestricted setting (ties may appear on either or both sides, and arbitrary incomplete lists are allowed), let α* denote the infimum of constants α ≥ 1 such that there exists a polynomial-time α-approximation algorithm for MAX-SMTI, and let β* denote the supremum of constants β ≥ 1 such that MAX-SMTI cannot be approximated within β in polynomial time unless P = NP.

Determine α* exactly, and in particular close the gap between the best known polynomial-time approximation ratio (upper bound on α*) of 3/2 and the best known NP-hardness of approximation threshold (lower bound on β*) of 33/29.
status_search_result: The best known polynomial-time approximation ratio for unrestricted MAX-SMTI remains 3/2 (McDermid; Király; Paluch), and the best known inapproximability lower bound is 33/29 under P≠NP (with stronger bounds under UGC). No subsequent work has been identified that closes this gap; the problem is still considered open in the matching-under-preferences literature.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: When one or both sides of a Stable Marriage with Ties and Incomplete lists instance are derived from master lists, can those structural constraints be exploited to obtain better approximation guarantees for maximum-cardinality stable matching?
self_contained_problem:
An instance of the Stable Marriage problem with Ties and Incomplete lists (SMTI) consists of a set U of men and a set W of women. Each person p has a preference list that ranks an acceptable subset of the opposite side; the ranking is a weak order, i.e., it may contain ties (groups of equally preferred partners). Acceptability is symmetric: w appears on m's list if and only if m appears on w's list.

A matching M is a set of mutually acceptable pairs in which each person appears in at most one pair. A pair (m,w) not in M is a blocking pair (in the weak stability sense) if m and w find each other acceptable, and each of m,w is either unmatched in M or strictly prefers the other to their current partner in M. A matching is weakly stable if it admits no blocking pair. The MAX-SMTI problem asks for a weakly stable matching of maximum cardinality.

A master list for one side is a single weak order over all members of that side such that every preference list on the other side is the restriction of this master list to the acceptable partners. The instance is said to be derived from master lists on one (resp. both) sides if such a master list exists on that side (resp. on both sides).

It is known that MAX-SMTI is NP-hard and admits a polynomial-time 3/2-approximation algorithm in the general case, while no approximation ratio below 4/3 (and not below some smaller explicit constant such as roughly 21/19) is achievable under standard complexity assumptions.

Question: When the preferences on one side, or on both sides, are derived from a master list, does there exist a polynomial-time approximation algorithm for MAX-SMTI with approximation ratio strictly better than 3/2? More generally, determine the best possible polynomial-time approximation ratio for MAX-SMTI restricted to instances with a master list on one side, and restricted to instances with master lists on both sides.
status_search_result: Web searches surface the general 3/2-approximation for MAX-SMTI (Király) and hardness lower bounds (≈1.1052 unconditionally, 4/3 under UGC), as well as polynomial-time solvability of certain master-list variants of stable roommates, but did not surface any improved approximation algorithm for MAX-SMTI specifically exploiting one-sided or two-sided master lists. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
context_brief: solvability probability for random stable roommates
original_question: For a uniformly random Stable Roommates instance of size n, determine the probability p_n that the instance admits a stable matching, especially its asymptotic behavior as n grows large.
self_contained_problem: Consider the Stable Roommates problem of size n (with n even): there are n agents, and each agent has a strict preference ranking (a total order) over the other n−1 agents. A matching is a partition of the agents into n/2 disjoint unordered pairs. A pair of agents {a,b} that are not matched to each other forms a blocking pair if a strictly prefers b to its current partner and b strictly prefers a to its current partner. A matching is stable if it admits no blocking pair. An instance of size n is chosen uniformly at random from all ((n−1)!)^n possible profiles of preference lists (equivalently, each agent's preference list is an independent uniformly random permutation of the other n−1 agents). Let p_n denote the probability that such a uniformly random instance admits at least one stable matching. Determine p_n, and in particular determine the asymptotic behavior of p_n as n → ∞.
status_search_result: The problem of computing p_n exactly is classically open (Problem 8 of Gusfield–Irving). Pittel–Irving (1994) gave a non-trivial constant upper bound e^{1/2}/2 ≈ 0.8244 and a lower bound of order n^{-1/2}. A recent preprint ("The random stable roommates problem typically has no solution", arXiv:2601.07612) proves that p_n → 0 as n → ∞, confirming the Gusfield–Irving conjecture; however, the exact asymptotic rate (simulations suggest Θ(n^{-1/4})) and a closed-form for p_n remain undetermined.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
context_brief: approximability of minimizing b for supermatches
original_question: For a given Stable Roommates instance, what approximation guarantees are achievable for finding a (1,b)-supermatch that minimizes the repair parameter b?
self_contained_problem:
Let an instance of the Stable Roommates problem (SR) consist of a set of an even number of agents, where each agent ranks all other agents in a strict order of preference. A matching M is a partition of the agents into pairs. A pair {x,y} not in M is a blocking pair of M if x prefers y to its partner in M and y prefers x to its partner in M; M is stable if it admits no blocking pair.

Given a stable matching M and an integer b ≥ 0, M is called a (1,b)-supermatch if, for every pair {x, M(x)} in M, after removing that pair from M, the remaining matching on the other agents can be extended to a stable matching M' of the whole instance such that M and M' differ on at most b+1 pairs (equivalently, repairing the broken pair forces at most b further changes).

Problem: For a given SR instance, determine the best possible polynomial-time approximation ratio achievable for the optimization problem of finding a (1,b)-supermatch that minimizes b. In particular, establish either approximation algorithms with provable performance guarantees, or inapproximability lower bounds (e.g., under P ≠ NP or standard complexity assumptions), for this minimization problem.
status_search_result: Existing work provides metaheuristics (local search and genetic local search) and a polynomial-time verification procedure for (1,b)-supermatches in the Stable Roommates problem, but no theoretical approximability results for minimizing b appear in the literature. The problem remains open.

paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
original_question: Can the current O(N^5) upper bound for computing the weighted straight skeleton of a polygon be improved, perhaps by exploiting additional structure in the associated Stable Roommates instance used by the reduction?
self_contained_problem:
Background. The straight skeleton of a simple polygon P in the plane is the geometric structure traced out by the vertices of P as each edge of P is translated inward at unit speed in the direction of its inward normal (with edges shrinking, splitting, or merging according to the standard wavefront-propagation rules). In the weighted version, each edge e of P is assigned a positive real weight w(e), and during the propagation edge e moves inward with speed w(e); the trajectories of vertices over time then form the weighted straight skeleton of (P, w).

One known approach to computing the weighted straight skeleton of an n-vertex polygon reduces the problem to solving an associated Stable Roommates instance (an instance of the matching-under-preferences problem in which 2k agents must be paired up so that no two unmatched agents mutually prefer each other to their assigned partners) and yields an algorithm with running time O(N^5), where N is a polynomial-size parameter derived from the input polygon.

Problem. Improve the O(N^5) upper bound for computing the weighted straight skeleton of an arbitrary simple polygon in the plane. In particular, decide whether a deeper exploitation of the structural properties of the Stable Roommates instance produced by the reduction (for example, special structure in the agents' preference lists arising from the geometry of P) can be used to design an algorithm with worst-case running time asymptotically faster than O(N^5).
status_search_result: Recent work on weighted straight skeletons (including a 2020 predictor–corrector incremental algorithm and CGAL's 2023 implementation for positive weights) has produced practical improvements and special-case results (e.g., O(n log n) for monotone polygons with positive weights, O(n) for convex polygons), but I did not find a published worst-case improvement over the O(N^5)-type bound coming from the Stable Roommates reduction for arbitrary polygons with general (possibly negative) weights. The status of the specific question—whether the structure of the underlying SR instance can be exploited to beat O(N^5)—appears unresolved in the sources located.

paper_title: Solutions to Some Open Problems from Slaney
original_question: In the same positive sentential logic TW+[Ax L, AxTO], is the right-top-or schema (RTO), namely (A → B) ∨ (B → A), derivable?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the positive (negation-free) sentential relevance logic TW₊, whose language is built from propositional variables using the binary connectives → (implication), ∧ (conjunction), and ∨ (disjunction). The axioms and rules of TW₊ are:

Axioms:
 (A1) A → A
 (A2) (A → B) → ((C → A) → (C → B))
 (A3) (A → B) → ((B → C) → (A → C))
 (A4) (A ∧ B) → A,  (A ∧ B) → B
 (A5) ((A → B) ∧ (A → C)) → (A → (B ∧ C))
 (A6) A → (A ∨ B),  B → (A ∨ B)
 (A7) ((A → C) ∧ (B → C)) → ((A ∨ B) → C)
 (A8) (A ∧ (B ∨ C)) → ((A ∧ B) ∨ C)

Rules: modus ponens (from A and A → B infer B) and adjunction (from A and B infer A ∧ B).

Extend TW₊ by adding the following two axiom schemes:
 (Ax L) ((A → B) ∧ (C → D)) → ((A ∨ C) → (B ∨ D))
 (Ax TO) (A → B) ∨ (B → C)

Call the resulting system TW₊ + [Ax L, Ax TO].

The "right-top-or" schema (RTO) is the schema
 (RTO)  (A → B) ∨ (B → A).

Question: Is every instance of (RTO) derivable in TW₊ + [Ax L, Ax TO]?
status_search_result: According to the source's own theorem, (RTO) is derivable in TW₊+[Ax L, Ax TO] (an affirmative answer is established by showing the stronger schema (IO) is provable there, which yields RTO).

paper_title: Solutions to Some Open Problems from Slaney
context_brief: Derivability of AxK and AxC with fusion
original_question: Assume again that TW+[Ax L, AxTO] is extended by a fusion connective ◦ satisfying the residuation rule `(A ◦ B) → C` iff `A → (B → C)`. If this extension is not conservative over formulas built only from →, ∧, and ∨, does adding (Resid) to TW+[Ax L, AxTO] make both axiom schemata (AxK) and (AxC) derivable?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the relevance logic TW₊ (the positive contraction-less Ticket Entailment / weak relevance logic in the language with implication →, conjunction ∧, and disjunction ∨), extended with the two axiom schemata
  (Ax L)  ((A → B) ∧ (B → C)) → (A → C),
  (AxTO) ((A → B) ∧ (C → D)) → ((A ∧ C) → (B ∧ D)),
yielding the system TW₊[Ax L, AxTO]. Enrich the language by a binary fusion connective ∘ and add the residuation rule
  (Resid)  (A ∘ B) → C  is a theorem  iff  A → (B → C)  is a theorem.
Assume that this extension is not conservative over the {→, ∧, ∨}-fragment of TW₊[Ax L, AxTO] (i.e., adding ∘ together with (Resid) produces new theorems in the original language). Under this assumption, are both of the following axiom schemata derivable in TW₊[Ax L, AxTO] + (Resid):
  (AxK)  A → (B → A),
  (AxC) (A → (B → C)) → (B → (A → C)) ?
status_search_result: The problem is reported as solved: it is established that (AxK) and (AxC) are both provable in TW₊[Ax L, AxTO] + (Resid), giving a positive answer.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Let Ω be the unit disc in R^2 and, for ε>0, consider the Ginzburg–Landau Dirichlet problem -Δu=(1/ε^2)u(1-|u|^2) in Ω with boundary condition u(x)=x on ∂Ω. Let U_ε(x)=(x/|x|)f_ε(|x|) denote the radial solution obtained from the unique ODE solution f_ε with f_ε(0)=0 and f_ε(1)=1. Is U_ε the only solution of this boundary-value problem?
self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝ² denote the open unit disc, and for a parameter ε > 0 consider the Ginzburg–Landau Dirichlet boundary-value problem for maps u : Ω → ℝ²,

  −Δu = (1/ε²) u (1 − |u|²)  in Ω,
  u(x) = x  on ∂Ω.

The associated radial profile equation is the ODE
  −f''(r) − (1/r) f'(r) + f(r)/r² = (1/ε²) f(r)(1 − f(r)²),  r ∈ (0,1),
with boundary conditions f(0) = 0 and f(1) = 1, which is known to admit a unique solution f_ε. Define the radial vortex
  U_ε(x) = f_ε(|x|) · x/|x|,  x ∈ Ω \ {0}, U_ε(0) = 0.

Question: Is U_ε the only solution of the above boundary-value problem? Equivalently, prove or disprove that every solution u ∈ C²(Ω; ℝ²) of −Δu = ε⁻² u(1 − |u|²) in Ω with u(x) = x on ∂Ω must coincide with U_ε.
status_search_result: The two-dimensional uniqueness question for the radial Ginzburg–Landau vortex on the unit disc, originating from work of Bethuel–Brezis–Hélein and Brezis, is widely regarded as a long-standing open problem. Recent progress establishes uniqueness of the degree-one vortex in the unit ball B^N for dimensions N ≥ 7 (Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu and subsequent works), and partial minimality/symmetry results in dimensions N = 2,…,6 for restricted classes (e.g. gradient fields, vortex sheets), but the full uniqueness in the original 2D disc case is not resolved.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Let Ω be the unit disc in R^2, fix p>2, and consider the p-Ginzburg–Landau energy E_{ε,p}(u)=(1/p)∫_Ω|∇u|^p + (1/(4ε^2))∫_Ω(|u|^2-1)^2 on W^{1,p}_g(Ω;R^2) with boundary data g(x)=x on ∂Ω. If u_ε is any minimizer or any critical point of E_{ε,p}, does u_ε(x) converge to x/|x| on Ω\{0} as ε→0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit disc, and fix a real number $p > 2$. For $\varepsilon > 0$, define the $p$-Ginzburg–Landau energy
$$E_{\varepsilon,p}(u) = \frac{1}{p}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^p\,dx + \frac{1}{4\varepsilon^2}\int_\Omega (|u|^2 - 1)^2\,dx$$
for vector fields $u: \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^2$ in the Sobolev space $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$. Impose the boundary condition $u(x) = g(x) := x$ on $\partial\Omega$, and let $W^{1,p}_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$ denote the corresponding affine space of admissible maps.

Let $u_\varepsilon \in W^{1,p}_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$ be any minimizer of $E_{\varepsilon,p}$ (respectively, any critical point of $E_{\varepsilon,p}$ in $W^{1,p}_g(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$). 

Question: Does $u_\varepsilon(x) \to x/|x|$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, pointwise (or in suitable function-space sense) on $\Omega \setminus \{0\}$?
status_search_result: The question of asymptotic radial symmetry for minimizers/critical points of the planar $p$-Ginzburg–Landau energy with boundary data $g(x)=x$ when $p>2$ appears to remain open. Partial results exist: radially symmetric degree-one minimizers are shown to be locally stable for $2 < p \le 4$, and global minimizers for related $p$-GL problems on $\mathbb{R}^2$ have been constructed, but a full proof that arbitrary minimizers (let alone critical points) converge to $x/|x|$ on $\Omega\setminus\{0\}$ has not been found in the literature.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Let Ω=B^3 be the unit ball in R^3, let g:∂Ω≈S^2→S^2 be smooth with degree deg g=0, and consider weak harmonic maps u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2) satisfying Δu_i=u_i|∇u|^2 in Ω and u=g on ∂Ω. Does there always exist at least one solution that is continuous on the closed ball Ω̄?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit ball with boundary $\partial\Omega = S^2$. Let $g : S^2 \to S^2$ be a smooth map of topological degree $\deg g = 0$. Define the Sobolev space
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u(x)| = 1 \text{ a.e. in } \Omega,\ u = g \text{ on } \partial\Omega\}.$$
A map $u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ is called a weak harmonic map (into $S^2$) if it satisfies, in the sense of distributions, the system
$$\Delta u_i = u_i\, |\nabla u|^2 \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad i = 1,2,3,$$
together with the boundary condition $u = g$ on $\partial\Omega$.

Question: For every smooth $g : S^2 \to S^2$ with $\deg g = 0$, does there exist at least one weak harmonic map $u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ that is continuous on the closed ball $\overline{\Omega}$?
status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems. Even when the boundary degree vanishes (removing the obvious topological obstruction), energy-minimizing harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2 are known to develop singularities in general (Hardt–Lin gap phenomenon), and no general construction of a continuous harmonic extension is known. Recent literature (e.g., on the Lavrentiev gap for harmonic maps into spheres) continues to treat this as open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Let R(u) be the relaxed energy for maps u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2), where Ω=B^3, deg g=0, and R is defined by weak H^1 limits of continuous S^2-valued maps with the same boundary trace g. Are minimizers of the relaxed-energy problem min{R(u):u∈H^1_g(Ω;S^2)} continuous on Ω̄? At least, is one minimizer continuous?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and let $g : \partial\Omega \to S^2$ be a smooth boundary datum of topological degree zero. Consider the Sobolev space
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u(x)| = 1 \text{ a.e.}, \ u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \}.$$
For $u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$, define the relaxed Dirichlet energy
$$R(u) = \inf\Big\{ \liminf_{n\to\infty} \tfrac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u_n|^2\,dx : u_n \in C^0(\overline{\Omega}; S^2) \cap H^1(\Omega; S^2),\ u_n|_{\partial\Omega} = g,\ u_n \rightharpoonup u \text{ in } H^1 \Big\}.$$
Consider the minimization problem
$$\min\{ R(u) : u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) \}.$$
(a) Is every minimizer of this problem continuous on $\overline{\Omega}$?
(b) If not, does there always exist at least one minimizer that is continuous on $\overline{\Omega}$?

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: For 1<p≤2 and maps f∈W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1), does there exist a universal constant c such that |deg f|≤c(p-1)∫_{S^1}∫_{S^1}|f(x)-f(y)|^p/|x-y|^2\,dx\,dy?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle in $\mathbb{R}^2$, equipped with its standard arc-length measure. For $1<p\le 2$, the fractional Sobolev space $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ consists of measurable maps $f:S^1\to S^1\subset\mathbb{C}$ such that
$$[f]_{W^{1/p,p}}^p:=\int_{S^1}\int_{S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy<\infty,$$
where $|x-y|$ is the arc-length distance on $S^1$. Every such map $f$ has a well-defined integer topological degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ (defined via approximation by smooth maps, since $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)\hookrightarrow \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$ for $p>1$).

Question: Does there exist a universal constant $c>0$, independent of $p$ and $f$, such that for every $1<p\le 2$ and every $f\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$,
$$|\deg f|\;\le\; c\,(p-1)\int_{S^1}\int_{S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy\;?$$
category_tag: Fractional Sobolev maps and topological degree
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in Brezis's 2022/2024 collection of favorite open problems. Web searches did not surface a published resolution; related works (Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen estimates for the topological degree, Brezis–Mironescu's monograph on Sobolev maps to the circle) treat closely related estimates but do not appear to settle this specific uniform-in-$p$ inequality near $p=1$. Status appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Given a specific circle-valued map f∈C(S^1;S^1), or more generally f∈VMO(S^1;S^1), does there always exist some summation process (σ_{n,ε}) that may depend on f and for which lim_{ε→0}\sum_{n∈Z} n|a_n(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε}=deg f?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1 = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| = 1\}$. For a measurable map $f : S^1 \to S^1$, write its Fourier coefficients as
$$a_n(f) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(e^{i\theta})\,e^{-in\theta}\,d\theta, \qquad n \in \mathbb{Z}.$$
Recall that $\mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$ is the closure of $C^\infty(S^1;S^1)$ in the BMO seminorm, and that the topological degree $\deg f \in \mathbb{Z}$ is well-defined for $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ and, more generally, for $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$. For smooth $f : S^1 \to S^1$ one has the identity
$$\deg f \;=\; \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2,$$
but for merely continuous (or VMO) $f$ this series need not converge absolutely.

A summation process is a family $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})_{n\in\mathbb{Z},\ \varepsilon>0}$ of real (or complex) numbers such that, for each $\varepsilon>0$, $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \to 1$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$ for every fixed $n$, and the sums below make sense.

Question: Given any $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ (respectively, any $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$), does there exist a summation process $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})$, possibly depending on $f$, such that
$$\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0}\;\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \;=\; \deg f\ ?$$
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a list of favorite open problems by Brezis. A closely related work ("Winding numbers and Fourier series") addresses such formulas with specific summation methods, and a recent preprint claims to settle Brezis's "first" open problem, but no source found resolves this specific question about the existence of an $f$-dependent summation process realizing the degree for arbitrary $C$ or VMO maps. Status appears open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Distance between H1 homotopy classes on S2
original_question:
For homotopy classes E_d={f∈H^1(S^2;S^2):deg f=d}, define Dist_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})=\sup_{f∈E_{d_1}}\inf_{g∈E_{d_2}}\|
abla(f-g)\|_{L^2}. Is it true that Dist_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})^2=8π|d_1-d_2| for all integers d_1,d_2? Even more basically, is this distance symmetric in the two classes?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^2$ denote the standard unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^3$. For a map $f\in H^1(S^2;S^2)$ (i.e., $f\in H^1(S^2;\mathbb{R}^3)$ with $|f(x)|=1$ a.e.), the Brouwer degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ is well defined. For each $d\in\mathbb{Z}$ set
$$E_d=\{f\in H^1(S^2;S^2):\deg f=d\}.$$
For $d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{Z}$ define the (in general asymmetric) $H^1$-distance between homotopy classes by
$$\operatorname{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})=\sup_{f\in E_{d_1}}\inf_{g\in E_{d_2}}\|\nabla(f-g)\|_{L^2(S^2)}.$$

(a) Decide whether
$$\operatorname{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})^2=8\pi\,|d_1-d_2|\qquad\text{for all }d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{Z}.$$

(b) Decide the weaker symmetry question: is it true that
$$\operatorname{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_1},E_{d_2})=\operatorname{Dist}_{H^1}(E_{d_2},E_{d_1})\qquad\text{for all }d_1,d_2\in\mathbb{Z}?$$
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in the literature on distances between homotopy classes of Sobolev maps between spheres. Related results are known for $W^{1,p}(S^n;S^n)$ with $p>n$ (where the distance between distinct classes equals a universal positive constant), but the precise value $8\pi|d_1-d_2|$ and even the symmetry of $\operatorname{Dist}_{H^1}$ in the critical $H^1=W^{1,2}$ case on $S^2$ are not known to be resolved.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
context_brief: Unbounded extremal solutions in high dimension
original_question: Consider the extremal weak solution u* arising from the nonlinear Dirichlet problem -Δu=λf(u) in a bounded smooth domain Ω⊂R^N, with u>0 in Ω, u=0 on ∂Ω, and f:[0,∞)→(0,∞) smooth, increasing, convex, and superlinear at infinity. When N≥10, Ω is a bounded smooth convex domain, and f(u)=e^u, must the extremal solution u* be unbounded? If not for some convex Ω, can one choose another admissible convex increasing superlinear f, possibly depending on Ω, for which u* is unbounded?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N\ge 10$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth convex domain. For a function $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ that is smooth, increasing, strictly convex, and superlinear at infinity (i.e. $\lim_{t\to\infty} f(t)/t = +\infty$), consider the family of semilinear elliptic Dirichlet problems
$$ -\Delta u = \lambda\, f(u) \ \text{ in } \Omega,\qquad u>0 \ \text{ in } \Omega,\qquad u=0 \ \text{ on } \partial\Omega, \qquad (P_\lambda) $$
parametrized by $\lambda>0$. It is classical that there exists a critical value $\lambda^*=\lambda^*(\Omega,f)\in(0,\infty)$ such that:
(i) for every $\lambda\in(0,\lambda^*)$, $(P_\lambda)$ admits a minimal classical solution $u_\lambda$, and the family $\{u_\lambda\}$ is pointwise increasing in $\lambda$;
(ii) for $\lambda>\lambda^*$, $(P_\lambda)$ has no weak solution.
The pointwise limit $u^*(x):=\lim_{\lambda\uparrow\lambda^*} u_\lambda(x)$ is called the extremal solution; it is a weak solution of $(P_{\lambda^*})$ in an appropriate sense, and the question of whether $u^*\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ depends on $N$, $\Omega$, and $f$.

Question (two parts):
(a) Taking $f(u)=e^u$, must the extremal solution $u^*$ be unbounded (i.e. $u^*\notin L^\infty(\Omega)$) for every bounded smooth convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ with $N\ge 10$?
(b) If the answer to (a) is negative for some convex domain $\Omega$, does there nevertheless exist an admissible nonlinearity $f$ (smooth, increasing, strictly convex, and superlinear at infinity), possibly depending on $\Omega$, for which the corresponding extremal solution $u^*$ is unbounded?
category_tag: extremal solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
status_search_result: For general (not necessarily convex) bounded smooth domains, it is classical that singular extremal solutions exist when $N\ge 10$ (e.g., $\Omega$ the unit ball, $f(u)=e^u$, gives the explicit singular solution $-2\log|x|$). The Cabré–Figalli–Ros-Oton–Serra theorem (2020) established boundedness of stable/extremal solutions for general $\Omega$ and $f$ up to dimension $N\le 9$, which is sharp. However, in the convex case with $N\ge 10$ the question is whether convexity of $\Omega$ can force boundedness of $u^*$; this is still listed as an open problem and no example of a convex domain in dimension $\ge 10$ producing an unbounded extremal solution (for $f=e^u$ or any admissible $f$) is known.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: For functions on the N-dimensional torus T^N, N≥2, the paper proves a stronger phase-control estimate in H^{1/2}+W^{1,1} and explains that the same method would follow from the unresolved inequality ||φ-∫φ||_{H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}} ≤ C ||∇φ||_{H^{1/2}+L^1}. Does this estimate hold for every scalar function φ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N \ge 2$ and let $\mathbb{T}^N = (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^N$ denote the $N$-dimensional torus. For a scalar function $\varphi : \mathbb{T}^N \to \mathbb{R}$, denote by $\fint \varphi = \int_{\mathbb{T}^N} \varphi$ its mean value.

Recall the sum-space norms: for two Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ of distributions on $\mathbb{T}^N$, the space $X+Y$ is equipped with the norm
$$\|u\|_{X+Y} = \inf\{\|u_1\|_X + \|u_2\|_Y : u = u_1 + u_2,\ u_1 \in X,\ u_2 \in Y\}.$$
Here $H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)$ is the Sobolev space of order $1/2$, $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^N)$ is the Sobolev space of $L^1$ functions whose distributional gradient is in $L^1$, and $\|\nabla \varphi\|_{H^{1/2}+L^1}$ denotes the sum-space norm of the gradient considered componentwise (i.e.\ $\nabla \varphi = F + G$ with $F \in H^{1/2}$, $G \in L^1$, and one takes the infimum of $\|F\|_{H^{1/2}} + \|G\|_{L^1}$).

Does there exist a constant $C = C(N) > 0$ such that for every scalar function $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{T}^N$ one has
$$\Big\| \varphi - \fint \varphi \Big\|_{H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}} \le C\, \|\nabla \varphi\|_{H^{1/2}+L^1}\,?$$
status_search_result: A recent 2025 preprint resolves "Open Problem 1.1" from Brezis's list of favorite open problems (the Brezis–Nirenberg problem on the 3-ball), but does not address this sum-space estimate. No source located indicates a resolution of the inequality in $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ controlled by $\|\nabla\varphi\|_{H^{1/2}+L^1}$, which is recorded as undecided. It appears to remain open.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Let Ω be a smooth bounded connected domain in R^N, let p≥1, and for a measurable function u:Ω→R define Φ_{λ,p}(u)=meas{(x,y)∈Ω×Ω : |u(x)-u(y)|^p / |x-y|^{p+N} ≥ λ}. The paper proves that if λΦ_{λ,p}(u)→0 as λ→∞, then u is constant. Does the same conclusion still follow from the weaker condition liminf_{λ→∞} λΦ_{λ,p}(u)=0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a smooth bounded connected domain, and let $p \geq 1$. For a measurable function $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\lambda > 0$, define
$$\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u) \;=\; \operatorname{meas}\!\left\{(x,y) \in \Omega \times \Omega \;:\; \frac{|u(x) - u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{p+N}} \,\geq\, \lambda \right\},$$
where $\operatorname{meas}$ denotes the $2N$-dimensional Lebesgue measure on $\Omega \times \Omega$. It is known that if $\lim_{\lambda \to \infty} \lambda\, \Phi_{\lambda,p}(u) = 0$, then $u$ is constant almost everywhere on $\Omega$.

Question: Does the same conclusion (that $u$ is constant a.e. on $\Omega$) follow from the weaker hypothesis
$$\liminf_{\lambda \to \infty} \lambda\, \Phi_{\lambda,p}(u) \;=\; 0\,?$$

Recent work on characterizations of Sobolev norms and the BBM formula (e.g., Brezis–Seeger–Van Schaftingen–Yung and related papers from 2024–2025) addresses related constancy criteria for these nonlocal functionals, but the specific liminf strengthening does not appear to have been resolved in the literature found.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Do the functionals λΦ_{λ,p} Γ-converge, as λ→∞, to the Sobolev or BV energy: namely to u↦c_p||∇u||_{L^p}^p on W^{1,p}(Ω) and +∞ outside W^{1,p}(Ω) when p>1, and to u↦c_1||∇u||_M on BV(Ω) and +∞ outside BV(Ω) when p=1, for some positive constants c_p and c_1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $N\ge 1$, $p\ge 1$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded open set (or, more generally, a measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}^N$). Fix a real exponent $\gamma>0$ and set $b=\gamma/p$. For a measurable function $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ define the difference quotient
$$Q_b u(x,y)=\frac{u(x)-u(y)}{|x-y|^{\,1+b}},\qquad x,y\in\Omega,\ x\ne y,$$
the superlevel set
$$E_{\lambda,b,\Omega}(u)=\bigl\{(x,y)\in\Omega\times\Omega:\ |Q_b u(x,y)|>\lambda\bigr\},$$
the weighted measure
$$\nu_\gamma(E)=\iint_E |x-y|^{-N+\gamma}\,dx\,dy,$$
and the nonlocal "tail" functional
$$\Phi_{\lambda,p}(u)\ :=\ \lambda^{p}\,\nu_\gamma\!\bigl(E_{\lambda,b,\Omega}(u)\bigr),\qquad \lambda>0.$$

Consider the family $\{\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}\}_{\lambda>0}$ of functionals on $L^p(\Omega)$ (resp. $L^1(\Omega)$ when $p=1$), endowed with the strong $L^p$ topology.

Question. Do there exist positive constants $c_p$ (depending only on $N$ and $p$) and $c_1$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $p>1$, then $\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,p}\ \xrightarrow{\ \Gamma\ }\ \Psi_p$ as $\lambda\to\infty$, where
$$\Psi_p(u)=\begin{cases}c_p\,\|\nabla u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^{\,p}, & u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega),\\ +\infty, & \text{otherwise};\end{cases}$$
\item If $p=1$, then $\lambda\,\Phi_{\lambda,1}\ \xrightarrow{\ \Gamma\ }\ \Psi_1$ as $\lambda\to\infty$, where
$$\Psi_1(u)=\begin{cases}c_1\,\|Du\|_{\mathcal{M}(\Omega)}, & u\in BV(\Omega),\\ +\infty, & \text{otherwise}?\end{cases}$$
\end{enumerate}
Here $\|Du\|_{\mathcal{M}(\Omega)}$ denotes the total variation of the Radon measure $Du$.
status_search_result: Recent surveys and a 2025 preprint on characterizations of Sobolev norms and total variation via nonlocal functionals explicitly list the Γ-convergence of λΦ_{λ,p} to the Sobolev/BV energy as an open problem; only partial lower- and upper-bound results and pointwise limits are available, while the full Γ-convergence statement (with identification of the constants c_p, c_1) does not appear to be established.

paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Recent Development
original_question: Classify all hypersurfaces M in Euclidean space Eⁿ⁺¹ whose position vector field x has a finite spectral decomposition x = c + x₁ + ··· + x_k, where c is a constant vector, the x_i are non-constant Eᵐ-valued maps, and each satisfies Δx_i = λ_i x_i for some real eigenvalue λ_i. In particular, classify all such finite-type surfaces in E³.
self_contained_problem:
Let $x : M^n \to \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ be an isometric immersion of a connected hypersurface into Euclidean $(n+1)$-space, and let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the induced metric on $M$. The immersion (or the hypersurface) is said to be of finite type if its position vector field $x$ admits a finite spectral decomposition
$$x \;=\; c + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k,$$
where $c \in \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is a constant vector, each $x_i : M \to \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is a non-constant smooth $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$-valued map, and there exist real numbers $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_k$ such that
$$\Delta x_i = \lambda_i\, x_i, \qquad i = 1, \ldots, k.$$

(a) Classify, up to congruence, all finite-type hypersurfaces $M^n$ in $\mathbb{E}^{n+1}$.

(b) In particular, classify all finite-type surfaces $M^2$ in $\mathbb{E}^3$.

Related results exist in pseudo-Euclidean spaces, for surfaces with respect to other fundamental forms, and for restricted classes (ruled, factorable, quadric Gauss-map type), but the general problem and its hypersurface generalization are still open.

original_question: Study and classify all 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere of Eⁿ⁺², where 2-type means that the position vector field has a spectral decomposition x = c + x₁ + x₂ with Δx₁ = λ₁x₁ and Δx₂ = λ₂x₂ for two distinct eigenvalues λ₁ and λ₂. self_contained_problem:
Let $E^{n+2}$ denote the $(n+2)$-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard inner product and Laplacian $\Delta$ acting componentwise on vector-valued functions. Let $S^{n+1}\subset E^{n+2}$ be a round hypersphere, and let $x: M^n \to S^{n+1}\subset E^{n+2}$ be an isometric immersion of a connected orientable $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold as a hypersurface of $S^{n+1}$.

The immersion $x$ is said to be of $2$-type if the position vector field admits a spectral decomposition
$$x = c + x_1 + x_2,$$
where $c\in E^{n+2}$ is a constant vector and $x_1, x_2: M \to E^{n+2}$ are non-constant smooth maps satisfying
$$\Delta x_1 = \lambda_1 x_1, \qquad \Delta x_2 = \lambda_2 x_2,$$
for two distinct real eigenvalues $\lambda_1 \ne \lambda_2$.

Problem. Classify, up to rigid motions of $E^{n+2}$, all $2$-type hypersurfaces $M^n$ of $S^{n+1}\subset E^{n+2}$. In particular, give a complete classification of all $2$-type hypersurfaces of the unit $4$-sphere $S^4 \subset E^5$.
status_search_result: Partial results exist: 2-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere are known to have constant nonzero mean curvature and constant scalar curvature, and several local rigidity and partial classification theorems (including the classification of 2-type surfaces in S^3 as products of two circles of distinct radii) have been established. original_question: Are the only finite-type surfaces in S³ ⊂ E⁴ the minimal surfaces, the standard 2-spheres, and the products of two plane circles, where finite type means that the position vector field has a finite decomposition into Laplace eigenmaps?

$$x = x_0 + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k,$$
where $x_0 \in \mathbb{E}^m$ is a constant vector and $x_1, \ldots, x_k$ are non-constant $\mathbb{E}^m$-valued maps satisfying $\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i$ for some real numbers $\lambda_i$, with $\Delta$ the Laplace operator of $M$ acting componentwise.

(i) the minimal surfaces of $S^3$,
(ii) the standard (totally umbilical) 2-spheres in $S^3$, and
(iii) the products of two plane circles (i.e., flat tori $S^1(a) \times S^1(b) \subset S^3$ with $a^2 + b^2 = 1$).

paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Recent Development
original_question: Do there exist 2-type surfaces lying fully in S⁴ that are not mass-symmetric, where 2-type means that the position vector field has a spectral decomposition with exactly two distinct Laplace eigenvalues, and a spherical immersion x : M → S^(m−1)_c ⊂ Eᵐ is mass-symmetric when the center of gravity of M in Eᵐ coincides with the center c of the hypersphere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $E^m$ denote $m$-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard inner product, and let $S^{m-1}_c(r) \subset E^m$ be the hypersphere of radius $r$ centered at a point $c \in E^m$. For an isometric immersion $x : M \to E^m$ of a compact Riemannian manifold $M$, decompose the position vector field as
$$ x = x_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{\infty} x_t, \qquad \Delta x_t = \lambda_t x_t, $$
where $x_0 \in E^m$ is the center of gravity of $M$ in $E^m$, $\Delta$ is the Laplace–Beltrami operator of $M$ acting componentwise, and the $x_t$ are the nonzero $E^m$-valued eigencomponents corresponding to distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_t$. The immersion (and the submanifold) is said to be of $k$-type if exactly $k$ of the eigencomponents $x_t$ (with $t \geq 1$) are nonzero and their eigenvalues are mutually distinct. A spherical isometric immersion $x : M \to S^{m-1}_c(r) \subset E^m$ is called mass-symmetric if the center of gravity $x_0$ of $M$ in $E^m$ coincides with the center $c$ of the hypersphere.

Question: Does there exist a surface $M$ admitting an isometric immersion $x : M \to S^4_c(r) \subset E^5$ which is of 2-type, lies fully in $S^4_c(r)$ (i.e., is not contained in any totally geodesic 3-sphere of $S^4_c(r)$), and is not mass-symmetric?

original_question: Other than minimal submanifolds, which submanifolds of Euclidean space Eᵐ are biharmonic, where an immersion x : M → Eᵐ is biharmonic when Δ²x = 0, equivalently when its mean-curvature vector H satisfies ΔH = 0?
self_contained_problem:
Let $x: M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ be an isometric immersion of a (connected) submanifold $M$ into Euclidean $m$-space $\mathbb{E}^m$, and let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the induced Riemannian metric on $M$, acting componentwise on $\mathbb{E}^m$-valued functions. The immersion is called biharmonic if
$$\Delta^2 x \equiv 0,$$
which, by Beltrami's formula $\Delta x = -nH$ (where $n=\dim M$ and $H$ is the mean curvature vector of the immersion), is equivalent to
$$\Delta H \equiv 0.$$
A submanifold is called minimal if $H \equiv 0$; every minimal submanifold is trivially biharmonic.

Problem: Classify all biharmonic submanifolds $M$ of $\mathbb{E}^m$ that are not minimal. Equivalently, determine whether there exists a non-minimal biharmonic submanifold in some Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}^m$, and if so, describe all such submanifolds.
status_search_result: The problem is the well-known Chen biharmonic conjecture, which asserts that every biharmonic submanifold of Euclidean space is minimal. It remains open in general. Partial confirmations are known: for surfaces in E^3 (Chen, Jiang), for hypersurfaces in E^4, for hypersurfaces in E^5, for hypersurfaces with at most two or with three distinct principal curvatures in any dimension, and under various additional curvature or completeness assumptions. No non-minimal biharmonic submanifold of Euclidean space has been found.

paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Recent Development
original_question: Is every biharmonic submanifold of a Riemannian manifold with non-positive sectional curvature minimal? The source explicitly records that this conjecture was later disproved in general.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(N,h)$ be a Riemannian manifold and let $\phi:(M,g)\to(N,h)$ be an isometric immersion of a Riemannian manifold $M$ into $N$. The tension field of $\phi$ is $\tau(\phi)=\operatorname{tr}_g\nabla d\phi$, and the bitension field is $\tau_2(\phi)=-\Delta\tau(\phi)-\operatorname{tr}_g R^N(d\phi,\tau(\phi))d\phi$, where $\Delta$ is the rough Laplacian on sections of $\phi^{-1}TN$ and $R^N$ is the Riemann curvature tensor of $(N,h)$. The immersion $\phi$ (or the submanifold $M\subset N$) is called biharmonic if $\tau_2(\phi)\equiv 0$, and minimal if $\tau(\phi)\equiv 0$.

Question (Generalized Chen Conjecture): Is it true that every biharmonic submanifold of a Riemannian manifold with non-positive sectional curvature is minimal?
status_search_result: The generalized Chen conjecture has been disproved in general. Ou and Tang constructed proper biharmonic hyperplanes in certain conformally flat 5-manifolds of negative sectional curvature, giving explicit counterexamples; further counterexamples have appeared subsequently. The original Chen conjecture (ambient Euclidean space) and various restricted versions remain open, but the generalized version with non-positive sectional curvature is known to be false.

original_question: Is every complete biharmonic submanifold of a Euclidean space minimal, where biharmonic means that the immersion satisfies Δ²x = 0, equivalently ΔH = 0?

$$\Delta^2 x \equiv 0,$$
or equivalently $\Delta H \equiv 0$, where $H = \frac{1}{n}\Delta x$ (with $n = \dim M$) is the mean curvature vector field of the immersion. The immersion is called minimal if $H \equiv 0$.

paper_title: Some Open Problems Concerning Expansive Systems
context_brief: Persistence of semi-trajectories in expansive systems
original_question: Let f be an expansive homeomorphism of a compact metric space M. Say that the semi-trajectory of a point x is persistent in the future if for every epsilon > 0 there exists a C^0-neighborhood N_x of f such that, for every g in N_x, there is y in M with dist(f^n(x), g^n(y)) <= epsilon for all n >= 0; define persistence in the past analogously for n <= 0. Is every semi-trajectory of every expansive system persistent in the future and in the past?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,d)$ be a compact metric space and let $f\colon M\to M$ be a homeomorphism. We say $f$ is expansive if there exists a constant $c>0$ (an expansivity constant) such that for any $x,y\in M$ with $x\neq y$ there is some $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ with $d(f^n(x),f^n(y))>c$. Endow the space $H(M)$ of homeomorphisms of $M$ with the $C^0$ (uniform) topology, where a basic neighborhood of $f$ consists of all $g$ with $\sup_{x\in M}d(f(x),g(x))<\delta$ and $\sup_{x\in M}d(f^{-1}(x),g^{-1}(x))<\delta$.

For $x\in M$, the forward semi-trajectory of $x$ is the sequence $\{f^n(x)\}_{n\geq 0}$, and the backward semi-trajectory is $\{f^n(x)\}_{n\leq 0}$. Say that the forward semi-trajectory of $x$ is persistent in the future if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a $C^0$-neighborhood $\mathcal{N}_x$ of $f$ in $H(M)$ such that for every $g\in\mathcal{N}_x$ there exists $y\in M$ with
$$d(f^n(x),g^n(y))\leq\varepsilon\quad\text{for all }n\geq 0.$$
Persistence in the past for the backward semi-trajectory of $x$ is defined analogously, requiring the inequality to hold for all $n\leq 0$.

Question: Is it true that for every expansive homeomorphism $f$ of every compact metric space $M$, every point $x\in M$ has its forward semi-trajectory persistent in the future and its backward semi-trajectory persistent in the past?
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of the question of whether every semi-trajectory of every expansive homeomorphism is persistent in the future and in the past. While the broader area of expansive and measure-expansive systems is active, no source found explicitly settles this particular semi-trajectory persistence problem, so its current status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
original_question: For metric spaces or Banach spaces X and Y and C >= 1, let B_C(X,Y) be the set of all α in (0,1] such that every (K,α)-Hölder map from a subset of X into Y extends to a (CK,α)-Hölder map on all of X, and let B_C^e(X,Y) = intersection over ε > 0 of B_{C+ε}(X,Y). Is B(X,Y) = union over C >= 1 of B_C(X,Y) always closed? Is B_C^e(X,Y) always closed? If B_C^e(X,Y) is closed, must B_C^e(X,Y) = B_C(X,Y), or at least must B_C^e(X,Y) be contained in B_C(X,Y)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be metric spaces (or Banach spaces). For $K>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1]$, a map $f:A\to Y$ defined on a subset $A\subseteq X$ is called $(K,\alpha)$-Hölder if $d_Y(f(x),f(x'))\le K\,d_X(x,x')^{\alpha}$ for all $x,x'\in A$.

For $C\ge 1$, define
$$B_C(X,Y)=\{\alpha\in(0,1]:\text{every }(K,\alpha)\text{-Hölder map from any }A\subseteq X\text{ into }Y\text{ extends to a }(CK,\alpha)\text{-Hölder map }X\to Y\},$$
and set
$$B(X,Y)=\bigcup_{C\ge 1}B_C(X,Y),\qquad B_C^{e}(X,Y)=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}B_{C+\varepsilon}(X,Y).$$

Answer the following:

(a) Is $B(X,Y)$ always a closed subset of $(0,1]$?

(b) Is $B_C^{e}(X,Y)$ always a closed subset of $(0,1]$?

(c) Whenever $B_C^{e}(X,Y)$ is closed, must $B_C^{e}(X,Y)=B_C(X,Y)$, or at least $B_C^{e}(X,Y)\subseteq B_C(X,Y)$?
